Section: 11. Refuting <s>Uddyotakara</s>'s view, and stating that the effect-reason indicates [only
relative to place and the like.]

body.text:
yas tu manyate -- `yaḥ pradeśo 'gnisambandhī so 'pratyakṣo yas tu pratyakṣo nabhobhagarūpa ālokādyātmā[108]dhūmavat tayā dṛśyamāno na so 'gnimān ataḥ kathaṃ pradeśe dhūmasya pratyakṣataḥ prasiddhiḥ | [S. 22b.] tasmād dhūma eva dharmī yuktaḥ | sāgnir ayaṃ dhūmaḥ dhūmatvāt ity evaṃ sādhyasādhanabhāvaḥ' iti -- tasyāpi sāgneḥ dhūmāvayavasyā 'pratyakṣatvāt, paridṛśyamānasya corddhvabhāgavartino 'gninā sahāvṛtteḥ, kathaṃ dhūmasāmānyasya sādhyadharmiṇi pratyakṣataḥ prasiddhiḥ? | dhūmāvayavī pratyakṣa iti cet; na, avayavavyatirekeṇa [T. 219b.] tasy[h2]ābhāvāt | lokādhyavasāyatas tasyaikatve vā pradeśasyāpi
{p. 21.1} tāvataḥ kalpitam ekatvaṃ na nivāryate | pradeśe eva ca loko 'gniṃ pratipadyate, na dhūme | deśakālādyapekṣayaiva[109]ca kāryahetur ggamakaḥ | yad āha -

children.translated_text: 'It is accepted that even in the case of a contrary effect, there is dependence on place, time, and so forth;
and of uncreated-ness in the case of verbal testimony' —
[this is established] through the diversity of cognitions, etc., by inference.

body.translated_text: But he who thinks: 'The location that is connected with fire is imperceptible; but the [location] that is perceptible, having the nature of a portion of the sky with illumination and the like — being seen like smoke — that is not [the location] possessing fire. Therefore, how is there establishment from perception of smoke in the location? Hence smoke alone is the proper <s>dharmin</s>. "This smoke possesses fire, because of being smoke" — thus is the relation of <s>sādhya</s> and <s>sādhana</s>' — [we respond:] for him too, since the part of the smoke that is [connected] with fire is imperceptible, and since the visibly perceived upper portion does not co-occur with fire, how is there establishment from perception of smoke-in-general in the <s>sādhyadharmin</s>? If [one replies:] the smoke-whole (<s>dhūmāvayavin</s>) is perceptible — no, because it does not exist apart from its parts. Or, if by worldly conventional understanding its unity is [accepted], then the contrived unity of the location too, to the same extent, cannot be prevented. And indeed it is in the location that ordinary people cognize fire, not in smoke. And the effect-reason is indicative only with reference to place, time, and the like. As he has said —

body.text:
[ā] lokatam asī nabhaḥ
[109] dhūmakāle eva cāgniḥ sādhyate na bhasmakāle
[110] na kevalaṃ kāryahetau
body.translated_text:
[ā]<s>lokatam asī nabhaḥ</s>
[109] Fire is proved only at the time of smoke, not at the time of ashes.
[110] Not only in the case of the effect-reason —
Section: 12. Answer to <s>Kumārila</s>'s objection: how can non-conceptual [perception
grasp universals?]

body.text: atra yathopavarṇitaṃ pratyakṣataḥ [S. 23a.] pakṣadharmasya sādhyadharmiṇi prasiddhāv abhiprāyam apratipadyamānaḥkumārilaḥ-- `kathaṃ pratyakṣeṇa(ṇā)vikalpena sāmānyātmano liṅgasya dhūmādeḥ svrūpagra[haṇa]m api tāvad yujyate, dharmiṇo vā kuta eva tatsambandhagrahaṇam' -- iti pratyavatasthe | tena hi

children.translated_text: 'And because inference and the like are preceded by perception, [they have] no independent basis with respect to properties (<s>dharma</s>)'
— this is the <s>Bhāṣya</s> passage.
'How could inference and the like be preceded by perception,
when the cognition of a non-conceptual sense [faculty] is incapable of producing memory?' ||
'And of a non-conceptualized logical mark, likewise the apprehension of [its connection with] the property-bearer —'
'is [impossible].'
Having thus objected —
'But the non-apprehension of the logical mark and the like by perception, due to non-conceptualization —
that is not accepted, since conceptualization too assists the form of the object.' ||
'For there exists first a <s>ālocana</s> (bare sensory) cognition, which is non-conceptual (<s>nirvikalpaka</s>),

body.translated_text: Here, <s>Kumārila</s>, not understanding the intended sense regarding the establishment of the property of the thesis-subject (<s>pakṣadharma</s>) in the subject of the proof (<s>sādhyadharmin</s>) through perception as described above, [S. 23a.] objected: 'How can perception, being non-conceptual (<s>avikalpaka</s>), even apprehend the intrinsic nature of the logical mark (<s>liṅga</s>), which is of the nature of a universal (<s>sāmānya</s>), such as smoke and the like? — and how much less the apprehension of its connection with the property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>)?' — thus he stood his ground. For indeed —
similar to the cognition of infants, mutes, and the like, born of a pure object.' ||

children.translated_text: Then,
'afterwards, that which by means of properties such as genus (<s>jāti</s>) and the like, with respect to the object —'

body.translated_text: 'is determined by the intellect — that too is accepted as having the nature of perception.' ||

body.text: {p. 22.1}[h3]iti bruvatā -- `saugat[h4]ānām evāyaṃ liṅgadharmitatsambandhāgrāhaṇalakṣaṇo doṣo yeṣām avikalpakam eva pratyakṣaṃ, nāsmākaṃ savikalpam api pratyakṣam icchatām' [S. 23b.] ity uktaṃ bhavati | tatas tadupavarṇitadoṣapratividhānāyā ''ha --

children.translated_text: 'With smoke indeed' (<s>sadhūmaṃ hi</s>)

children.text: ityādi | ayam atra samudāyārthaḥ -- pratyakṣaṃ hi purovasthitam auttarādharyeṇa dhūmapradeśādikaṃ vidhirūpeṇa dhūmādisvalakṣaṇaṃ sakalasajātīyavijātīyavyāvṛttaṃ ca svasvabhāvavyavasthiteḥ sarvāsāmarthamātrāṇāṃ parasparam asaṃkīrṇarūpatvāt
children.translated_text: and so forth. Here the composite meaning is as follows: perception, being directly present, [apprehends] in sequential order the region of smoke and the like in the form of positive determination (<s>vidhi</s>), the particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>) of smoke and the like, and [its] exclusion from all homogeneous and heterogeneous [entities] — because of the establishment of each thing in its own nature, since all mere entities, being of mutually unmixed natures —

children.text:
tatsāmarthyabhāvi yathāsthānam[111]anukurvat pāścāttyavidhipratiṣedhavikalpadvayaṃ janayati yena dhūmapradeṣākhyau dharmadharmiṇau tayoś cauttarādharyam `evam etat nānyathā' iti vikalpayati | yathānubhavam abhyāsapāṭavādipratyayāntarasahakāriṇāṃ vikalpānām udayāt | tato dharmadharmiṇoḥ svarūpaniścayaḥ sambandhaniścayaś ca pratyakṣanibandhanaḥ
sampadyate | tathā hi -- ayam eva dhūmapradeśayoḥ sambandhasya niścayo yaḥ `ātrāyam' ity adhyavasāyaḥ | sa cāvikalpenāpi pratyakṣeṇa yathoktena prakāreṇa sampādita eva | na cauttarādharyāvasthitād vastudvayād anya [S. 24a.] eva kaścid ādhā[rādhe]yabhāvalakṣaṇaḥ sambandhaḥ yataḥ tasya [T. 220b.] pratyakṣeṇānanubhūtatvāt paścāda(d) vikalpanaṃ syāt | vastubhūtasya tasyānyatra niṣedhāt | tasmād ayaṃ tad eva tathāvasthitam[112]arthadvayam[113]āśritya kalpanāsamāropita eva | tena sambandhaḥ sambandhīti bhedāntarapratikṣepāpratikṣepābhyāṃ dharmadharmitayā vyavahāro loke na tu pāramārthikaḥ | sāmānyavyavahāro 'pi vijātīyavyāvṛttāneva bhāvānāsṛ(śri)tya kalpanāsamāropita eva pratanyate | teṣām eva bhinnānām apy anubhavadvāreṇa vijātīyavyāvṛttatayā prakṛtyaivaikākāraparāmarśapratyayahetutvāt tathā cāha -
children.translated_text:
by the power of that [perception], reproducing [the object] as it actually stands, it generates the subsequent pair of conceptual cognitions — positive and negative (<s>vidhipratiṣedhavikalpa</s>) — whereby it conceptualizes the two [things] called smoke and region as property (<s>dharma</s>) and property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>), and their sequential relation, [thinking] 'it is thus and not otherwise.' [This is] because of the arising of conceptual cognitions, with the assistance of other mental factors such as habitual familiarity from repeated experience and the like. From this, the ascertainment of the intrinsic nature of the property and property-bearer, as well as the ascertainment of their connection, is accomplished as grounded in perception.
For the following reason: this very ascertainment of the connection between smoke and the region is the determinate cognition 'this [smoke] is here [in the region].' And this is accomplished through non-conceptual perception itself in the manner described. Moreover, there is no connection characterized by a substratum-superstratum relation (<s>ādhārādheyabhāva</s>) that is something other than the two real entities standing in sequential relation — [S. 24a.] because, since that [connection] has not been experienced by perception, there could be no subsequent conceptualization of it [T. 220b.]. Because that which is real is denied elsewhere. Therefore, this [connection] is merely a conceptual superimposition (<s>kalpanāsamāropita</s>) based upon that very pair of real entities standing in that relation. Hence, the distinction between 'connection' and 'the connected,' the conventional usage as property and property-bearer through the non-exclusion and exclusion of other distinctions — that is [only] worldly convention, not ultimate reality. The usage of universals too, being based only on entities that are excluded from what is heterogeneous, is merely conceptual superimposition and proceeds [only] conventionally. Because those very [entities], though distinct, through the door of experience, being by their very nature excluded from what is heterogeneous, are causes of a cognitive apprehension of a single form. And thus [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>] says —
'Certain things, though different, are determined toward accomplishing a single purpose,
because of the cognition that apprehends them as one — by their own nature, like the sense faculties and the like.'

body.translated_text: By saying this — 'this defect, characterized by the non-apprehension of the logical mark, the property-bearer, and their connection, belongs to the Buddhists (<s>Saugata</s>) alone, for whom only the non-conceptual is perception, not to us who accept even the conceptual as perception' [S. 23b.] — this is what is stated. Therefore, in order to counter the defect described by him, [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>] says —

<s>puro 'vasthitārthasāmarthyabhāvipratyakṣa</s>-
[112] <s>auttarādharyāvasthitam</s>
[113] <s>dhūmapradeśalakṣaṇa</s>-

body.text: {p. 23.1} tataḥ sāmānyavi[kalpajananadvārā] [S.24b.] tatpratibhāsino dhūmākārasya vijātīyavyāvṛ[ttarūpasya sāmānyarūpatayā] pratyakṣeṇaiva gṛhītatvāt | na hi vijātīyavyāvṛttir vyāvṛttād anyaiva kācid yasyāḥ pratyakṣeṇāgrahaṇaṃ syāt | tasmād yathāparidṛṣṭaṃ dhūmādisvalakṣaṇam evānyato vyāvṛ[ttātmanā vi]kalpyata iti pratipattradhyavasāyavaśāt smṛtir eva | dvividho vikalpaḥ pratyakṣapṛṣṭhabhāvī vastutaḥ punar nirviṣaya eva | tato yad āha -- sāmānyasyānanubhūta tathā --

children.translated_text: 'If one were to say that this cognition is memorial, having the universal as its object without distinction —'

children.text: anumānagrāhyam eva | tatra cānavasthā liṅgagrāhiṇo 'py anumānasya tadanyaliṅgabalenotpatteḥ | tasya ca sāmānyarūpatayā [S. 25a.] tadanyānumānamānaviṣayatvāt tathā tadanyasyāpīti kasyacid ekasyāpi liṅginaḥ pratipattiḥ yugasahasrair api na sambhavati | kim aṅga punar ekena puruṣāyuṣkeṇeti | tathā cāha -

And in that case there would be an infinite regress, since the inference that apprehends the logical mark also arises by the force of another logical mark; and since that [other mark too], as having the form of a universal, is the object of yet another inference, and that [other inference requires] yet another — thus the comprehension of even a single logical subject would not be possible even in a thousand eons; how much less then within a single human lifetime! And thus [<s>Kumārila</s>] says —
'A universal is not cognized without inference,

body.translated_text: Therefore, through the door of generating the conceptualization of the universal, [S. 24b.] the smoke-form — which is excluded from what is heterogeneous — [is apprehended] as having the nature of a universal, precisely because it has been grasped by perception itself. For the exclusion from what is heterogeneous is nothing other than what is [already] excluded [from the heterogeneous], such that its non-apprehension by perception would be impossible. Therefore, the particular of smoke and the like, as it has been perceived, is itself conceptualized as having the nature of exclusion from other things — thus, by the force of the cognizer's determinate judgment, it is nothing but memory. Conceptualization is of two kinds: that which follows perception, and that which, in reality, has no [real] object whatsoever. Therefore, regarding what was said — 'the universal has not been experienced' — and likewise —
and inference does not operate without a logical mark.' ||
'And no one accepts that a non-universal is a logical mark;
nor does any unapprehended logical mark illuminate [anything].' ||

children.text: arthāntaraiḥ sajātīyavijātīyair viviktam asaṅkīrṇaṃ rūpam asyeti vigrahaḥ | sarvabhāvānāṃ svasvabhāvavyavasthiteḥ svabhāvasāṅkaryābhāvāt | anyathā sarvasya sarvatropayogād atiprasaṅgaḥ | [S. 26b.] anena pratiṣedhavikalpasya nimittam ākhyātam, sāmānyotprekṣāyāś ca bījam | taduktam -

Otherwise, since everything would be applicable to everything, there would be an unacceptable over-extension. [S. 26b.] By this, the cause of the negative conceptualization (<s>pratiṣedhavikalpa</s>) is stated, as well as the seed of the imputation of universals. As stated —

[He] begins the investigation of validity and invalidity of the [three kinds of] conceptualization: seeing (<s>darśana</s>), positive determination (<s>vidhi</s>), and negative exclusion (<s>pratiṣedha</s>).

—
occurring before the arising of conceptualization, hence:
'first' (<s>ādyam</s>)
— is declared.

— [means] having the particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>) as its object. That [bare] seeing —
'alone' (<s>eva</s>)

body.text:
pramāṇam, na vidhipratiṣedhavikalpāv api, tasyaiva pramāṇalakṣaṇayogād itarayoś ca tadasambhavāt. tathā hi -- anadhigataviṣayatvam arthakriyāsādhanaviṣayatvaṃ ca pramāṇalakṣaṇam.[117]tad darśanasyaivāsti.
tatra
body.translated_text:
— is a <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid cognition), not the positive and negative conceptualizations as well — because only that [seeing] possesses the defining characteristics of a <s>pramāṇa</s>, while the other two lack them. For the definition of a <s>pramāṇa</s> is: having a previously unattained object and having as its object that which is capable of causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyāsādhana</s>). That belongs only to [bare] seeing.
Among those,
'first' (<s>ādyam</s>)
— [the word] declares [the property of] being a cognition of a novel object, and
'having an uncommon object' (<s>asādhāraṇaviṣayam</s>)

— [declares the property of] having as its object that which is capable of causal efficacy, since only the particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>) is capable of causal efficacy. [Section: 15. Establishing the invalidity of negative conceptualization.]

body.text: prathamaviśeṣaṇāt pratiṣedhavikalpasyā'dhyavaseyārthakriyāsādhanaviṣayatve 'pi na prāmāṇyam | dvitīyāt tu dhidhivikalpasyānadhigatasāmānyaviṣayatve 'pi na prāmāṇyam
body.translated_text: By the first qualifier, even though the negative conceptualization has as its object something capable of causal efficacy through determinate judgment, it lacks validity. By the second [qualifier], even though the positive conceptualization has as its object a previously unattained universal, it too lacks validity.

body.text: tatra pratiṣedhavikalpasya tāvat pratyakṣagṛhītārthaviṣayatayā smṛtitvaṃ pratipādayann āha --

— uncommon,

— by that which arises from the power of [the object's] unmixed form,
'having been seen' (<s>dṛṣṭe</s>)

children.translated_text: For the following reason: even one who accepts the absence-portion (<s>abhāvāṃśa</s>) as distinct from the positive-portion (<s>bhāvāṃśa</s>) must posit the positive-portion as unmixed in nature by its own intrinsic character — otherwise, that very absence-portion would not be established. And —

children.text: svabhāvenāsaṅkīrṇarūpatāyām asatyāṃ pṛthagbhūtābhāvāṃśasadbhāve 'pi sā[119]yuktimatī, svahetubalāyātasya saṅkīrṇarūpasyākiñcitkarābhāvāṃśasambhave 'pi tyāgāyogāt. na[120]ca tenaiva tadvināśanam, vināśahetvayogasya pratipādayiṣyamāṇatvāt. tena saṅkīrṇarūpavināśane ca varaṃ svahetor eva svabhāvato 'saṅkīrṇarūpāṇāmudayo 'stu kiṃ parivrāṅmo[T. 223b.]dakanyāyopagamena? tasmāt svabhāvata eva bhāvānāṃ
children.translated_text: When the unmixed form is not present due to [its] essential nature, even though a separately existing absence-portion is present, that [argument] is rational, because even though the mixed-form [entity] produced by the force of its own cause may contain an inoperative absence-portion, there is no justification for abandoning [the entity as a whole]. And that [absence-portion] does not destroy it [the entity], since the absence of a cause of destruction is about to be explained. Therefore, rather than destroying the mixed-form [entity], let the arising of unmixed-form [entities] from their own cause's essential nature itself [be accepted] — what is the point of accepting the analogy of the monk and the maiden? Therefore, the entities' deficiency in the form of the other, which is the absence-portion, is due to their essential nature alone,

Exclusion (<s>vyāvṛtti</s>) from 'not-that' is <s>atad-vyāvṛtti</s>. That which has this as its object is so described. 'Just as observed, the difference from other things is imagined by me too' — thus it is said because of the determination by each cognizer. Ultimately, because [memory] is objectless. [S. 29b.] That [memory]
is not a valid means of cognition (<s>pramāṇa</s>)

children.text: nābhāvapramāṇaphalam[123]ity arthaḥ | na hi smṛtijanakatvena pramāṇatā yuktā | kasmāt na pramāṇam? | yathādṛṣṭasyākāro 'bhyāsapāṭavādipratyāyāntarasāpekṣo viśeṣas tasya grahaṇāt | na hi dṛṣṭam ity eva vikalpena gṛhyate, darśanāviśeṣāt sarvākāreṣu vikalpodayaprasaṅgāt, api tu kaścid evābhyāsādipratyayāpekṣa ity ākāragrahaṇenācaṣṭe |
children.translated_text: — meaning it is not the result of a means of cognition of absence — this is the meaning. For it is not justified that what generates memory should thereby have the status of a valid cognition. Why is it not a valid cognition? Because what is grasped is a particular aspect (<s>ākāra</s>) of the thing as observed, which is a special [feature] dependent on other conditions such as practice and skill. For what is observed is not grasped by conceptual cognition (<s>vikalpa</s>) merely as 'observed' — since, due to the non-specificity of observation, there would be the absurd consequence of conceptual cognition arising for all aspects. Rather, only some [aspect], dependent on conditions such as practice, [is grasped] — he indicates this through 'grasping of the aspect.'

children.text: bhavatu yathādṛṣṭā[T. 224a.]kāragrahaṇam[124]| pramāṇam tu kasmān na bhavatīti parasya[125]taduktapramāṇalakṣaṇavirahaṃ darśayann āha --
children.translated_text: Granted that there is grasping of the aspect as observed. But why is it not a valid cognition? — Showing the opponent the absence of the definition of valid cognition as stated by him [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>], he says —
'Previously' (<s>prāk</s>) —
{p. 27.1} at the time of the arising of the apprehending cognition (<s>ālocanā-jñāna</s>);
'uncommon' (<s>asādhāraṇa</s>) —

'of one who is expressing' (<s>abhilapataḥ</s>) —
of one who is conceptualizing (<s>vikalpayataḥ</s>);
'because the prohibitive conceptual cognition (<s>pratiṣedha-vikalpa</s>) does not cognize a previously unknown object' —

body.translated_text:
When mixed by essential nature
[119] Unmixed-form-ness
[120] [Objection:] 'The absence-portion is not inoperative, since it destroys the mixed-form-ness by that very [presence]' — to this he says
[121] 'The absence-portion is because the other-form is imagined' — T.
[122] 'Rather, it would be an inference'
[123] 'By the opponents, it has been thus explained because the observation of a real entity alone is said to be the means of cognition of absence, through generating the conceptual cognition of non-existence'
[124] 'By you too, as-' — T.
[125] 'Of the subsequent [cognition] after the apprehending cognition, or of <s>Kumārila</s>'

body.text: yadyuktena prakāreṇa pratiṣedhavikalpo na pramāṇaṃ, vidhivikalpas tarhi pramāṇaṃ bhaviṣyati. na hi tasyāpūrvārthavijñānatvābhāvaḥ sambhavati | tatpratibhāsino 'nugatasya sāmānyākārasyāsādhāranarūpāv alambinā darśanenānadhigamāt tat kuto 'syāprāmāṇyam | tad uktam --

children.translated_text: 'Then, subsequently, the real entity —'
ŚV <s>Pratyakṣa</s> 120

children.text: ityādi | tad etatkumārilavacanam āśaṅkya vidhivikalpasyāpi prāmāṇyam anupa(m apa)nudann āha --
children.translated_text: and so forth. Anticipating this statement of <s>Kumārila</s> and refuting the validity of affirmative conceptual cognition too, he says —
'Of that which accomplishes effective action (<s>arthakriyā-sādhana</s>)' —
of the particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>);
'because that which accomplishes effective action, which is not seen by the apprehending cognition (<s>ālocanā-jñāna</s>), again, that which accomplishes it' —
i.e., of the essential nature that accomplishes effective action;
'is not apprehended by conceptual cognition — [therefore] affirmative conceptual cognition is not a valid cognition.'

children.text: yady api[126]tenānadhigataṃ sāmānyam adhigamyata iti varṇyate, tathāpi tad arthakriyāsādhanaṃ na bhavati iti tad adhigantā taimirikādijñānaprakhyo vidhivikalpo na pramāṇam | [S. 30b.]
children.translated_text: Even though it is described that the universal, which is not apprehended by that [direct perception], is apprehended [by conceptual cognition], nevertheless, since that [universal] does not accomplish effective action, the affirmative conceptual cognition that apprehends it — resembling the cognition of one with an eye-disease (<s>taimirika</s>) seeing [non-existent] hairs and such — is not a valid cognition. [S. 30b.]

children.text: tataḥ[127] paraṃpunar vastu dharmair jātyādibhir yayā|
children.translated_text: 'Then, subsequently, the real entity, with properties such as class (<s>jāti</s>) and so forth, by which [cognition] —' even when there is apprehension, just as with the cognition of hairs [by one with eye-disease], there is no validity. For this very reason, since the universal, which lacks the capacity for effective action, has no contact (<s>saṃprayoga</s>) with the sense faculties, the status of being direct perception (<s>pratyakṣatā</s>) is also impossible. By the word 'and' (<s>ca</s>), [the reason] 'because it is memory (<s>smṛti</s>)' — thus the previously stated grounds are combined. And its character of being memory will be demonstrated later.

children.text: adhigame 'pi keśādijñānasyeva na prāmāṇyam | ata evārthakriyāsāmarthyavirahiṇā sāmānyenendriyāṇāṃ samprayogābhāvāt pratyakṣatā 'py asambhavinī | cakāreṇa smṛtitvāc ceti pūrvoktakāraṇasamucayaḥ | smṛtitvaṃ cāsyottaratra pratipādayiṣyate |

children.translated_text: 'Like inference (<s>anumāna</s>)' —

children.text:
iti vaidharmyadṛṣṭāntaḥ. yathā pratyakṣeṇārthakriyāsādhane pradeśākhye dharmiṇy adhigate 'py anadhigatasyāgner arthakriyāsādhanasyāsāmānyākāreṇa[128]parokṣasya svalakṣaṇākāreṇa pratipattum aśakyatvāt pratipattiḥ[129], naivaṃ vidhivikalpena sāmānyākāreṇānadhigatam arthakriyāsādhanam adhigamyate,[130]tasyālocanājñānenaivādhigamāt. [S. 31a.] tasmiṃ(smin) smṛtir evāsāv iti na pramāṇam iti |
[ section: 17. arthakriyāsādhanaviṣayajñānasyaiva prāmāṇyasamarthanam |]
children.translated_text:
this is a dissimilarity-example. Just as, even when the thesis-subject called 'location' (<s>pradeśa</s>), which accomplishes effective action, has been apprehended by direct perception, fire — which is imperceptible (<s>parokṣa</s>) and accomplishes effective action — cannot be apprehended by the form of the particular through the non-particular universal-form, [but rather] is apprehended [through inference] — not so does affirmative conceptual cognition apprehend what accomplishes effective action that has not been apprehended through the universal-form, since that [effective-action-accomplishing particular] has already been apprehended by the apprehending cognition alone. [S. 31a.] Regarding that, this [conceptual cognition] is merely memory — therefore it is not a valid cognition.
[Section: 17. Establishing that only cognition pertaining to what accomplishes effective action has validity.]

body.translated_text: If by the manner shown, prohibitive conceptual cognition is not a valid cognition, then affirmative conceptual cognition (<s>vidhi-vikalpa</s>) will be a valid cognition. For the absence of the character of cognizing a previously unknown object is not possible for it — since the universal-form (<s>sāmānyākāra</s>) that appears in it as a common [feature] is not apprehended by the observation that grasps the uncommon form. Then whence comes its invalidity? As has been said —

body.text: sāmānyamātraṃ vā vidhivikalpena gṛhyate tadviśiṣṭaṃ vā svalakṣaṇam, gatyantarābhāvāt | tatra pūrvapakṣe āha
body.translated_text: Either the universal alone is grasped by affirmative conceptual cognition, or the particular qualified by that — since there is no alternative. In the first alternative, he says
'Even though'

body.text:
ity ādi
[127] uttarasmin pakṣe āha
[128] -dhanasya sāmā- -- T.
[129] anumāneneti śeṣaḥ
[130] vastunaḥ
body.translated_text:
and so forth.
[127] In the second alternative, he says

children.translated_text: 'Only cognition pertaining to what accomplishes effective action (<s>arthakriyā-sādhana</s>) is a valid cognition'

children.text: , netarad iti kuta etat iti cet
children.translated_text: — 'and not the other'; whence is this? — if [one asks];
'For one desiring effective action' (<s>arthakriyārthī</s>) —
i.e., a person who desires the attainment and avoidance of the beneficial and harmful;
'every [person]' —
not just some [person] by the principle of the crow and the palm-fruit (<s>kākatālīya-nyāya</s>);
'one who takes sides' (<s>pakṣāvān</s>) —
one who acts deliberately (<s>buddhipūrvakārī</s>);
'valid cognition or invalid cognition' —

children.text: pramānād eva sarvadā pravarta(rte)ya apramāṇāt mā kadācit, vipralambhasambhavād,
children.translated_text: [seeks to] always proceed from valid cognition alone, and never from invalid cognition, because of the possibility of deception;
'investigates both' —

children.text: na vyasanitayā | tato 'yam arthakriyāsādhanaviṣayam eva pramāṇam bravīti, tasyārthakriyāsādhane pravṛttyaṅgatvāt | netarat, tadviparītatvāt | tathā hi -- pramāṇam avisaṃvādakam apratārakam ucyate loke 'pi | [T. 225a.] yac cārthakriyāsādhanam anadhigacchan na tatra pravartayati, kuta eva tat prāpayet tat katham avisaṃvādakatayā prekṣāpūrvakārī pramāṇam ācakṣīta? |
children.translated_text: not out of obsessiveness. Therefore, this person declares only cognition pertaining to what accomplishes effective action to be valid cognition, since it is a factor in engaging with what accomplishes effective action. Not the other, since it is the opposite of that. For indeed — a valid cognition (<s>pramāṇa</s>) is called non-deceptive (<s>avisaṃvādaka</s>), non-misleading (<s>apratāraka</s>), even in common usage. And that which, not apprehending what accomplishes effective action, does not prompt engagement therein — how then could it lead one to attain that? How then would a deliberate agent declare it a valid cognition on the grounds of being non-deceptive?

body.translated_text: Section: 18. Extensive demonstration that the universal is unreal.

body.text: yady evaṃ sāmānyam apy arthakriyāsādhanam eva tatas tadviṣayo vidhivikalpaḥ pramāṇaṃ bhaviṣyatīti ced, āha --
body.translated_text: If so, the universal too must accomplish effective action; in that case, the affirmative conceptual cognition pertaining to it would be a valid cognition — if [one objects]; he says —
'And not' (<s>na ca</s>) —
not at all;
'the universal [does not produce] any' —
any effective action — whether that which is accepted as accomplished by it, characterized by undifferentiated cognition and designation, or another [effective action] accomplished by the particular;
'[the universal] does not produce effective action.'
Of what kind [is this universal]?
'After the apprehension of the particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>)' —
after the apprehension of the particular, known as the apprehending cognition (<s>ālocanā-jñāna</s>);
'subsequent to' (<s>ūrdhvam</s>) —
i.e., in the later moment;
'grasped by conceptual cognition arising from the power of that [direct perception].'

body.text: iti | tacchabdena svalakṣaṇapratipattiḥ sambadhyate | `tataḥ paraṃ punar vastu' ity[131]ādiparair abhidhānād evaṃ bravīti darśanapṛṣṭhabhāvino vikalpasya pratyakṣapramāṇatāṃ nirākartum | sarvam eva tu sāmānyaṃ na kāñcid arthakriyām upakalpayati.
body.translated_text: By the word 'that' (<s>tat</s>), the apprehension of the particular is connected. He says this — quoting from the opponents' [statement] 'then, subsequently, the real entity' and so forth — in order to refute the status of the conceptual cognition that follows upon observation as a valid direct perception. But all universals whatsoever do not produce any effective action.

body.text: yat tu sāmānyam anumānavikalpagrāhyam, tat kāraṇavyāpakasambaddhaliṅganiścayadvārāyātaṃ sambaddhasambandhād anadhigatārthakriyāsādhanaviṣayām arthakriyām upakalpayatīti tadviṣayo vikalpaḥ pramāṇam | [S. 32a.] idaṃ tu naivam, adhigatatvād arthakriyāsādhanasyālocanājñāneneti | atrodāharaṇam
body.translated_text: However, that universal which is grasped by the conceptual cognition of inference, having come through the channel of the ascertainment of a mark connected by the relationship of cause or pervader, produces effective action pertaining to a previously unapprehended object that accomplishes effective action, through the connected relationship — therefore, the conceptual cognition pertaining to it is a valid cognition. [S. 32a.] But this [affirmative conceptual cognition following perception] is not so, because what accomplishes effective action has already been apprehended by the apprehending cognition. The example here is —
'For instance — having seen blue, in the cognition "[this is] blue"' —

body.text:
pratibhāsamānam iti śeṣaḥ | na sāmānyaṃ kāñcid arthakriyām upakalpayatīti prakṛtena sambandhaḥ |
  nanu ca liṅgavikalpapratibhāsi [T. 225b.] sāmānyaṃ prakṛtam tat kim anyad udāhriyate? | sarvasya darśanapṛṣṭhabhāvino vikalpasya paropagatāṃ pratyakṣapramāṇatāṃ tulyanyāyatayā nirākartum | kāṃ punar nīlam iti vikalpajñāne darśanapṛṣṭhabhāvini pratibhāsamānaṃ sāmānyam arthakriyāṃ nopakalpayati? | yadi vyaktisādhyām; tadā 'nyo 'pi padārtho 'nyadīyām arthakriyāṃ nopakalpayatīti tasyāpy anarthakriyāsādhanatvād avastutvaprasaṅgaḥ | atha svasādhyām; tad asiddham, abhinnajñānābhidhānalakṣaṇāyāḥ svasādhyāyāḥ karaṇād ity āśaṅkyāha --
body.translated_text: i.e., the universal appearing [therein] — this is the remainder. The connection with the topic is: 'the universal does not produce any effective action.' [Objection:] But is not the universal appearing in inferential conceptual cognition the topic? Why is another [case] illustrated? — In order to refute by equal reasoning the status of direct-perception-validity accepted by the opponent for all conceptual cognition following upon observation. And what effective action does the universal appearing in the conceptual cognition following observation, 'this is blue,' not produce? If [it does not produce] that accomplished by the particular — then another entity too does not produce the effective action belonging to yet another; hence, from its too not accomplishing effective action, there would be the absurd consequence of its unreality. Or if [it does not produce] that accomplished by itself — that is unestablished, since it does accomplish its own [effective action] characterized by undifferentiated cognition and designation. — Anticipating this, he says —
'That very [particular] indeed' —
that which was apprehended by the apprehending cognition [S. 32b.]
'the particular of blue (<s>nīla-svalakṣaṇa</s>)' —
the particular instance of blue;
'produces the effective action accomplished by such [a universal].'

body.text:
| tathāvidhaśabdena sāmānyam atrābhipretam, tādṛśaparyāyatvād asya, sādhāraṇarūpasya ca tādṛśatvāt | tena tathāvidhasādhyāṃ nīlasāmānyasādhyām abhinnajñānābhidhānalakṣaṇām
arthakriyāṃ kartuṃ śīlam asya svalakṣaṇasyeti tat tathoktam |
  evaṃ manyate -- yathā bhinnā api vyaktyaḥ kayācit pratyāsattyā tadekakāryapratiniyamalakṣaṇayā tadekam abhinnaṃ sāmānyam upakurvanti[132], tadaparasāmānyayogam antareṇāpi, anyathā 'navasthāprasaṅgāt, tathā 'bhinnajñānābhidhānātmikām apy arthakriyāṃ sādhayiṣyanti | kim apramāṇakena pramāṇabādhitena ca sāmānyenopagatena? | [T. 226a.] tathā hi -- anumānādike jñāne yathāvidham asyāspaṣṭaṃ rūpaṃ pratibhāsate na tathāvidhaṃ vyaktiṣu dṛśyamānās upalakṣayāmaḥ | ekam eva hi vyaktidarśanakāle spaṣṭam nīlādirūpaṃ vibhāvayāmaḥ | [S. 33a.]
body.translated_text: By the word 'such' (<s>tathāvidha</s>), the universal is meant here, since this [word] is a synonym for 'of that kind,' and since the common form is of such a kind. Therefore, 'produces' means: it is the nature of this particular to accomplish the effective action accomplished by 'such' — i.e., by the blue-universal — [the action] characterized by undifferentiated cognition and designation — thus it is so stated. He considers thus: Just as different particulars, by some proximity — defined as the restriction to producing a single [kind of] effect — contribute to a single undifferentiated universal, even without another universal of that universal — otherwise there would be the absurd consequence of infinite regress — so too they will accomplish effective action that is of the nature of undifferentiated cognition and designation. What need is there for a universal that is not established by any valid cognition and is refuted by valid cognition? For indeed, in inferential and other cognitions, the indistinct form of this [universal] that appears according to its nature — we do not observe such a form in the particulars. For at the time of observing a particular, we discern only a single vivid form such as blue and so forth. [S. 33a.]

body.text: tat katham adṛṣṭakalpanayā ''tmānaṃ svayam eva vipralabhe mahi? | vyaktirūpasaṃsargād ayogolakavahnivad avibhāvanam[133]iti cet; na, sarvatra bhedābhedavyavasthāyā abhāvaprasaṅgāt | asyottarasyānyatrāpi sulabhatvāt | na ca sāmānyasya dve rūpe staḥ spaṣṭam aspaṣṭaṃ ca, yenaikena darśane pratibhāseta anyenānumānādijñāne, padārthadvayopagamaprasaṅgāt, pratibhāsabhedasyaiva sarvatra bhāvabhedavyavasthānibandhanatvāt, sāmānyasyāparasāmānyaprasakter[134]niḥsāmānyasya cāsyopagamāt |
body.translated_text: Then how should we deceive ourselves by imagining what has not been observed? [Objection:] Due to the admixture with the form of the particular, [the universal's form] is not discerned, like fire [concealed] in an iron ball — [Reply:] No, because in that case the distinction between difference and non-difference could not be established anywhere — since the reply to this [objection] is easily available elsewhere as well. And the universal does not have two forms — one vivid and one indistinct — such that by one it would appear in direct perception and by the other in inferential cognition; [for this would lead to] the absurd consequence of accepting two entities; since the difference of appearance is itself the basis for establishing the distinction of real entities everywhere; because the universal leads to [the need for] another universal [ad infinitum]; and because this [universal] is accepted as lacking [its own] universal.

body.text:
kriyāviśeṣaṇamadaḥ
[132] anupakṛtasya tadādheyatvābhāvāt
[133] sāmānyasya
[134] dūṣaṇāntaram āha
body.translated_text:
'This is a qualifier of action'
[132] 'Because what is not assisted [by it] cannot be its substratum'
[133] 'Of the universal'
[134] 'He states another refutation'
Section: 19. Refutation of <s>Kumārila</s>'s dual-natured cognition (<s>dvyātmakabuddhi</s>)

body.text:
etenaitad api nirastam yad āha --
  sarvavastuṣu buddhiś ca vyāvṛttyanugamātmikā |
  jāyate dvyātmakatvena vinā sā ca na yujyate ||

children.translated_text: ŚV <s>ākṛti</s> 5

children.text:
na cātrānyatarā bhrāntirūpacāreṇa ceṣyate |
  dṛḍhatvāt[135]sarvadā buddher bhrāntis tadbhrāntivādinām ||
children.translated_text: 'And here, neither of the two is regarded as erroneous or as metaphorical; because of the firmness (<s>dṛḍhatva</s>) of cognition at all times — [the charge of] error belongs to those who assert its erroneousness.' ||
ŚV <s>ākṛti</s> 7

body.translated_text: By this, the following [position] too is refuted, which [<s>Kumārila</s>] states: 'And in all things, cognition arises as having a dual nature (<s>dvyātmakatva</s>), consisting of exclusion (<s>vyāvṛtti</s>) and positive concomitance (<s>anugama</s>); and without that [duality], it is not tenable.' ||
[i.e.,] because of being uncontradicted (<s>abādhyamānatva</s>)

Thus. If this is said with reference to sensory cognition (<s>indriyabuddhi</s>), then it is unestablished (<s>asiddha</s>), because the indistinct form (<s>ākāra</s>) of blue and the like is not observed in the clear apprehension of blue and the like; and [the clear form too]

body.text:
iti | yato yadīndriyabuddhim abhipretyocyate; tadāsiddham, aspaṣṭasya nīlādy ākārasya spaṣṭanīlādyābhāsāyāṃ tatrānupalakṣaṇāt, spaṣṭasyāpi ca dvitīyasyānuyāyinaḥ | tadbhāve[136]ca vyaktidvayāntarālam apy āpnuvataḥ kathaṃ [T. 226b.] tadanugamaḥ[137]? | vyāptau(vyaktau) copalabhyasya sataḥ tatrānupalakṣaṇaṃ kutaḥ? | na hi tasya vyaktāvyaktarūpasambhavaḥ, ekatvāt | tathā cāha --
  vyaktāv ekatra sā vyaktā 'bhedāt sarvatragā yadi |
  jātidṛśyeta sarvatra [sāpi na vyaktyapekṣiṇī] ||
body.translated_text: is a follower of a second distinct [form]. And if that [universal form] were present, since it would pervade even the interval between two individuals, how [could there be] its positive concomitance (<s>anugama</s>)? And for something that exists and is apprehended in an individual (<s>vyakti</s>), whence [would come] its non-observation there? For it is not possible for it to have both manifest and non-manifest forms, since it is one. And so [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>] states: 'If, being manifest in one individual, the universal — because of non-difference — pervades everywhere, then the universal should be seen everywhere [and it should not be dependent on individuals].' ||

body.text: iti | ekatrāpi ca vyaktāv upalabhyamānāyāṃ sakalatrailokyavyāpi rūpaṃ sakalasvāśrayavyāpi vā dṛśyeta? | na hy ekasyāḥ kiñcid dṛṣṭam adṛṣṭaṃ vā nāma kṣaṇikatādivad | dṛṣṭāyām apy ekatraivāśraye darśanāvasāyo na sarvatreti cet; na, vikalpena taddarśanābhyupagamāt | na hi niścayaviṣayīkṛtaṃ cāniścitaṃ ceti yuktam | tataḥ sarvagatarūpadarśane sarvārthānāṃ darśanaprasaṅgaḥ | na hi [S. 34a.] taddarśane[138]
body.translated_text: Thus. And when it is apprehended even in a single individual, should a form pervading the entire triple world, or pervading all its substrata, be seen? For of a single [entity], nothing is both seen and unseen — unlike momentariness and the like. If [one says] that even when seen in just one substratum, the cognitive determination is only there, not everywhere — no, because the seeing of that [universal] is accepted through conceptual cognition (<s>vikalpa</s>). For it is not tenable that [something is] both made the object of ascertainment and not ascertained. Therefore, in seeing the all-pervading form, the consequence would be seeing all objects. For in the seeing of that,

body.text:
tatsahacāriṇa[139]upalabhyasya tadabhinnasvabhāvasya[140]cānupalambho yuktaḥ | tataḥ katham indriyabuddher dvyātmakatā? |
  athānumānādibuddhim[141]; tasyām api svalakṣaṇāpratibhāsanāt kuto dvyātmakatvam? | na hi nāsu sāmānyagrāhiṇīṣv spaṣṭo vyaktyākāra iva lakṣyamāṇaḥ svalakṣaṇapratibhāsaḥ | tadbhāve 'pi tāsāṃ bhāvāt | ākārāntareṇaḥ ca svajñāne [']pratibhāsanāt anekākārāyogād ekasya, atiprasaṅgāc[142]ca | tasmān neyaṃ bhinnārthagrāhiṇyabhinnā sāmānyabuddhiḥ pratibhāti svalakṣaṇodbhāva satī | kintv anādivitatha[T. 227a.]vikalpābhyāsavāsanājanitā satī tathā 'vabhāsate | dṛḍhatvaṃ ca buddher nāvināśitvam, kṣaṇikatvābhyupagamāt kintv abādhyamānatvam | na cāsyās tat sambhavati, leśato bādhakasyoktatvāt | vistaratas tusyādvādabhaṅgād yathāvasaram ihaiva tatra tatra vidhāsyamānād bādhakam avadhāryam | tasmād yathā vyaktyaḥ sāmānyāntaram antareṇa tad ekam upakurvanti tathā 'bhinnajñānābhidhāne api pravartayiṣyantīti tad eva nīlasvalakṣaṇaṃ sāmānyasādhyatvopagatārthakriyākāri
|[ section: 20. kumāriladattasya doṣasya saugatabuddyabādhakatvadarśanam |]
yas[143]tu -- [S. 34b.]
sāmānyaṃ nānyad iṣṭaṃ cet tasya
body.translated_text: it is not tenable that what is apprehended and is its constant companion, and what is of inseparable nature from it, should be non-apprehended. Therefore, how [could] sensory cognition have a dual nature? If [one says this applies to] inferential cognition and the like — in that too, since the particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>) does not appear, whence dual-naturedness? For in those [cognitions] that apprehend universals, no clear appearance of a particular form is observed, as is observed [in sensory cognition]. [Those cognitions exist] even in the absence of that [particular appearance]. And because an additional form does not appear in its own cognition, [and] because of the impossibility of multiple forms for a single [entity], and because of over-extension. Therefore, this cognition of the universal — which is not different from [cognition] grasping distinct objects — does not appear as having arisen from a particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>). Rather, it so appears being produced by the latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>) of beginninglessly false conceptual habituation. And the 'firmness' (<s>dṛḍhatva</s>) of cognition is not imperishability, since momentariness is accepted, but rather being-uncontradicted (<s>abādhyamānatva</s>). And that [uncontradictedness] is not possible for this [cognition], since a refuter has been stated in brief. The refuter should be ascertained in detail from the refutation of <s>syādvāda</s> (Jaina doctrine of qualified assertion), which will be set forth here and there as occasion arises. Therefore, just as individuals (<s>vyakti</s>) serve that one [universal] without [there being] a separate universal, so too they will prompt undifferentiated cognition and designation — and it is precisely the particular of blue (<s>nīla-svalakṣaṇa</s>) that performs the causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyā</s>) attributed to [it as] the object to be proven as universal.
Section: 20. Showing that the defect adduced by <s>Kumārila</s> does not contradict Buddhist cognition

[Section: 22. Showing the defect in the definition of <s>pramāṇa</s> accepted by the <s>Mīmāṃsakas</s>]

children.text: yata evam anarthakriyāsādhanaviṣayatayā darśanapṛṣṭhabhāvino vikalpasya prāmāṇyam ayuktam, tasmādasmadabhimataṃ pramāṇam avisaṃvādi jñānam iti pramāṇalakṣaṇaṃ vyudasya,
children.translated_text: Therefore — since thus the validity (<s>prāmāṇya</s>) of a concept (<s>vikalpa</s>) that arises after perception is untenable, because its object cannot accomplish causal efficacy — therefore, setting aside our own accepted definition of <s>pramāṇa</s>, namely 'non-deceptive cognition' (<s>avisaṃvādi jñāna</s>),
'a <s>pramāṇa</s> has a previously-unascertained object' —
[i.e.,] a <s>pramāṇa</s> is 'cognition of a novel object' (<s>apūrvārthavijñāna</s>),
even in this [definition] too,
even in this other definition of <s>pramāṇa</s> being formulated with audacity, in order to avoid over-extension,

'Of an unascertained particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>).'

anena hi viśeṣaṇenānumānavikalpasya ca prāmāṇyaṃ sidhyati, ālocanājñāna-
pṛṣṭhabhāvinaś ca vikalpasya prāmāṇyaṃ vyudasyata iti sarvaṃ sustham |
  tad evaṃ vidhivikalpasyānarthakriyāsādhanaviṣayatayā 'nadhigatasāmānyādhigame 'pi prāmāṇyaṃ nirākṛtya [T. 228b.] ca śabdasamuccitaṃ smṛtitvaṃ pratiṣedhavikalpena sādhāraṇam prāmāṇyakāraṇaṃ [S. 36b.] darśayann āha --
children.translated_text: For by this qualification, the validity of inferential concept (<s>anumānavikalpa</s>) is established, while the validity of the concept arising after perceptual cognition (<s>ālocanājñāna</s>) is rejected — thus everything is in order. Therefore, having thus refuted the validity of the positive concept (<s>vidhivikalpa</s>) — [even] in ascertaining a previously-unascertained universal — because its object cannot accomplish causal efficacy, and showing that 'being memory (<s>smṛtitva</s>)' combined with verbal [expression], which is common to both positive and negative concepts, is the cause of [its] validity, he says:
'But when the particular has been ascertained' —
by perceptual cognition (<s>ālocanājñāna</s>),
'born from its power' —
arising by force of the ascertainment of the particular,
'the concept imitates that' —

it imitates nothing.
'It is memory (<s>smṛti</s>) alone.'

children.translated_text: the concept arisen from the force of perception. For thus: even memory, whose object is the aspect of a previously experienced particular, does not have that as its object in ultimate reality — because the particular does not appear in its vivid form in memory as it does in sensory cognition. Rather, [it has that as its object] only functionally, as stated. And that [functional object-hood] is common to the positive concept (<s>vidhivikalpa</s>) as well — so how could it not be memory?
[Section: 23. Establishing the validity of inference through the distinctiveness of inferential concept from positive concept]

Here one might [object]: but an inferential concept (<s>anumānavikalpa</s>), even though of the nature of memory, is accepted as a valid means of knowledge. For thus: precisely that mere real entity (<s>vastumātra</s>), excluded from non-fire, which was previously experienced in a kitchen and the like — that very [entity] is remembered in a particular location from seeing smoke. Similarly, the positive concept too will be a <s>pramāṇa</s>. To this [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>] says:
'Of an unascertained' —
'real entity's' —
'form, because of [its] non-ascertainment' —

children.text: | evam manyate -- yat mahānasādāv anagnivyāvṛttaṃ vastumātraṃ prāganubhūtaṃ na tat taddeśādisambandhitayaivānumānavikalpena [T. 229a.] smaryate kintu yatra pradeśe prāgananubhūtaṃ tatsambandhitayā | tataḥ sādhyadharmidṛṣṭāntadharmigrāhidarśanadvayānadhigatasyānagnivyāvṛttasya vasturūpasyāyogavyavacchedenādhigamād yuktam asya prāmāṇyam | na tu darśanapṛṣṭhabhāvino vikalpasya, tadviparītatvād iti | [S. 37b.]

[<s>Dharmakīrti</s>] considers thus: the mere real entity excluded from non-fire that was previously experienced in a kitchen and the like — that is not remembered by the inferential concept as connected with that very place and so forth; rather, [it is remembered] as connected with a place where it was previously not experienced. Therefore, because of the ascertainment — through exclusion of impossibility (<s>ayogavyavaccheda</s>) — of a real entity form excluded from non-fire that was not ascertained by the pair of perceptions grasping the <s>sādhyadharmin</s> and the example's <s>dharmin</s>, its validity is justified. pramāṇavyāpāraviṣayam[152]abhipretyocyate nālambhanalakṣaṇam[153], anyathā 'numānasya parikalpitasāmānyālambhanatayā vastvadhiṣṭhānatvābhāvād avyāpinī pramāṇavyavasthā syād | yadi vastvadhiṣṭhānā pramāṇavyavasthā kathaṃ {p. 35.1} viprakṛṣṭaviṣayāyā[154]anupalabdheḥ prāmāṇyam iti cet; tatrāpi pradhānādivikalpasyaiva[155]bhāvānupādānatayā sādhyatvāt tasyā api vastvadhiṣṭhānatā 'sty evety adoṣaḥ |

children.translated_text: is said with reference to the domain of the operation of <s>pramāṇa</s>, not in the sense of [mere] apprehension — otherwise, since inference apprehends a constructed universal, due to the absence of real-entity-groundedness, the arrangement of <s>pramāṇas</s> would be non-pervasive [i.e., not hold universally]. If the arrangement of <s>pramāṇas</s> is grounded in real entities, how then [can there be] the validity of non-apprehension (<s>anupalabdhi</s>) whose object is distant? Even there, since the concept of [entities like] <s>pradhāna</s> (primordial matter) and the like is the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) precisely because of non-adoption of [their] existence, that [non-apprehension] too is grounded in a real entity — so there is no fault. But how [do we know] that the arrangement of <s>pramāṇas</s> is indeed grounded in real entities? To this he says:
'In causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyā</s>)' —
characterized by pleasure and pain, that which is

If persons’ engagement is toward what is capable of causal efficacy, even so, how is the system of valid cognition (pramāṇa) grounded in real entities (vastu)? For in that case, it would be grounded in what is capable of causal efficacy — [to this objection] he says:
Causal efficacy (arthakriyā) —
for which something is —

indeed —

| tato 'rthakriyāyogyādhiṣṭhānatvena vastvadhiṣṭhānatvaṃ kathaṃ na syāt iti bhāvaḥ | [T. 229b.]
  idaṃ ca vastvāśrayeṇa pramāṇavyavasthāpratipādanam anadhigate svalakṣaṇa ity ukte kadācit paro brūyāt -- vastumātranibandhanā hi pramāṇavyavasthā na svalakṣaṇāśrayaiva | tato yady apy anadhigataṃ svalakṣaṇaṃ nādhigacchati tathāpy anadhigatavasturūpam adhigacchato vikalpasya prāmāṇyaṃ bhaviṣyatīti tadasiddhatodbhāvanārtham uktam --
children.translated_text:
Therefore, how could [the system] not be grounded in real entities, since it is grounded in what is capable of causal efficacy? — this is the purport.
And this demonstration of the system of valid cognition as dependent on real entities [addresses the following concern:] when it is said 'regarding the unapprehended particular (svalakṣaṇa),' an opponent might say: the system of valid cognition is grounded on the mere real entity, not exclusively on the particular. Therefore, even if the particular that is unapprehended is not apprehended, still, for conceptualization that apprehends the unapprehended nature of a real entity, validity will obtain. To raise the unestablishedness of that [objection], it was stated:
'Regarding the unapprehended nature of a real entity' (<s>anadhigatavasturūpe</s>) —

children.text: ty ādi | [S. 38b.] tadasiddhatodbhāvane cānadhigatavasturūpādhigantur eva prāmāṇyaṃ netarasyeti kutaḥ? iti paryanuyoge
children.translated_text: and so forth. And when that unestablishedness is raised — [the question arises:] why is validity only for that which apprehends the unapprehended nature of a real entity, and not for the other? In response to this inquiry,
'Regarding what is capable of causal efficacy' (<s>arthakriyāyogye</s>) —

children.text:
ty ādi uktam | tathā ca vastuviṣayam api prāmāṇyaṃ bruvatā svalakṣaṇaviṣayam evoktaṃ bhavati, tasyaivārthakriyāsāmarthyalakṣaṇatvāt, sāmānyasya ca tadviparītatvāt iti manyate |
  punar apy anubhavottarakālabhāvino nīlavikalpasya prāmāṇyam apanetum upacayahetum āha --
children.translated_text:
and so forth was stated. And thus, even one who asserts validity with respect to real entities (<s>vastu</s>) has [in fact] stated that it is with respect to the particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>) alone, because only that has the characteristic of being capable of causal efficacy, while the universal (<s>sāmānya</s>) is of the opposite nature — so he thinks.
Furthermore, to remove the validity of the blue-conceptualization that arises after the [perceptual] experience, he states the cumulative reason:
Even from that (<s>tato 'pi</s>) —
from the aforementioned conceptualization, [and] not merely from the experience of the blue particular —
only toward a real entity (<s>vastu</s>) —
only toward the particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>) —
through determinate judgment of that (<s>tadadhyavasāya</s>) —
through determinate judgment of the particular, since engagement toward it would be impossible otherwise —
a person’s engagement [occurs].

children.text: adhigate svalakṣaṇe tatsāmarthyajanmā vikalpo na pramāṇam iti sambandhaḥ | pūrvam anadhigatavasturūpānadhigater aprāmāṇyam uktam | adhunā tv adhigatasyaivādhigamād iti [S. 39a.] {p. 36.1} vidhipratiṣedharūpatayopapattyor[156]bhedaḥ | yad vā
children.translated_text: When the particular has been apprehended, the conceptualization born from its capacity is not a <s>pramāṇa</s> — this is the syntactic connection. Previously, invalidity was stated because [conceptualization] does not apprehend the unapprehended nature of a real entity. Now, however, [invalidity is stated] because [it only] re-apprehends what has already been apprehended — the difference [between the two arguments] lies in their being [respectively] in the form of positive and negative reasoning. Or alternatively,
'because of being the object of that, as an effect' (<s>kāryatas tad viṣayatvāt</s>) —

children.text: iti yad uktaṃ tad evopacayahetuvyājena sphutīkṛtam |

[there is] non-difference in acquisition and preservation (<s>abhinnayogakṣematva</s>).

body.text:
| yogaḥ aprāptasya viṣayasya paricchedalakṣaṇā prāptiḥ, kṣemaḥ tadarthakriyānuṣṭhānalakṣaṇaṃ paripālanam | abhinnau yogakṣemāvastheti sa tathoktaḥ | tatra vikalpasya nirvikalpapratyakṣeṇābhinno yogaḥ svalakṣaṇādhyavasāyataḥ | abhinnaḥ kṣema ālocanāvijñānād iva vikalpād api svalakṣaṇa eva pravṛtteḥ | ayam asyābhiprāyaḥ -- yadi vikalpo nirvikalpacetasaḥ prameyāntaraviṣayas tadā tatraiva puruṣaṃ pravartaya tu tatsādhyām arthakriyām adhigantum | naiva vā pravartayet, tadviṣayatvābhimatasya sāmānyasyābhinnajñānalakṣaṇāyā evārthakriyāyā upagamād [S. 39b.] vikalpodayād eva ca tatsiddheḥ
| na hi nīlānubhavāt prameyāntaraviṣayāḥ pītādipratyayāḥ puruṣaṃ nīlavastuni pravartayanti, sādhitārthakriyā vā kvacid apīti | tasmād ālocanājñānān naivāyaṃ prameyāntaraviṣayaḥ | viśeṣeṇa yair evaṃ vyākhyāyate -
body.translated_text:
‘Acquisition’ (<s>yoga</s>) is the attainment characterized as the ascertainment of a previously unattained object; ‘preservation’ (<s>kṣema</s>) is the maintenance characterized as the performance of causal efficacy with respect to that [object]. [That] whose acquisition and preservation are non-different is so called. Therein, for conceptualization, acquisition is non-different from non-conceptual perception (<s>nirvikalpapratyakṣa</s>) because of the determinate judgment of the particular. Preservation is non-different [because] engagement is toward the particular alone, from conceptualization just as from bare sensory cognition. His intent is this: if conceptualization has as its object something different from the object of non-conceptual cognition, then let it direct the person toward that very [different object] in order to attain the causal efficacy to be accomplished by that. Or else it should not direct [the person] at all, since the universal, which is held to be its object, is accepted as having only causal efficacy identical with cognition, and since that [cognition] is achieved from the very arising of conceptualization.
For the blue-cognitions and others, having as their objects something different from the particular, do not direct a person toward the blue real entity, nor do they have accomplished causal efficacy anywhere at all. Therefore, this [conceptualization] does not have a different object of valid cognition than the bare sensory cognition. Especially [this is so] for those who explain thus:
‘Through non-conceptual cognition, even of a thing having a dual nature —
the grasping [occurs].’

body.text: iti[158]| tato nīladarśanasyaiva nirvikalpasya prāmāṇyaṃ yuktam, na tadabhinnopayogasya [T. 230b.] smṛter iva vikalpasyāpi darśanāt pṛthag[159]eva | anyathā niṣphalāṃ pramāṇāntarakalpanāṃ kurvataḥ smṛtīcchādveṣaprayatnādi pramāṇam anuṣajyata iti pramāṇānām iyattā viśīryeteti |
body.translated_text: Thus. Therefore, validity belongs only to the non-conceptual seeing of blue, not separately to conceptualization, which has the same utility [as perception] — just as [there is no separate validity for] memory, since it is [merely] a seeing. Otherwise, for one who makes the fruitless postulation of an additional <s>pramāṇa</s>, memory, desire, aversion, effort, and so forth would follow as <s>pramāṇas</s>, and thus the fixed number of <s>pramāṇas</s> would be shattered.

body.text:
atra `na' kārasyopari pratāv eva `3' iti likhitaṃ vartate
[158] viśeṣeṇa teṣāṃ mate naivāyaṃ prameyāntaraviṣaya iti saṃbedhaḥ
[159] prāmāṇyaṃ yuktam
body.translated_text:
Here, above the syllable ‘na,’ ‘3’ is written in the manuscript.
[158] Especially, in their view, this [conceptualization] does not have a different object — this is the connection.
[159] validity is proper
[section: 26. Validity and invalidity in streaming cognitions, in relation to the yogin and others.]

body.text: yadaikasminn eva nīlādivastuni [S. 40a.] dhārāvāhīnīndriyajñānāny utpadyante tadā pūrveṇābhinnayogakṣematvād uttareṣām indriyajñānānām aprāmāṇyaprasaṅgaḥ | na caivam, ato 'nekānta iti pramāṇasaṃplavavādī darśayann āha --

children.translated_text: ‘By the moment of the prior perception’ (<s>pūrvapratyakṣakṣaṇena</s>) —
and so forth. He resolves this:
No (<s>na</s>) —
there is no unwanted consequence of validity for the subsequent [cognitions]. Why?
Because of the difference in acquisition and preservation (<s>nānāyogakṣematvāt</s>) —

children.text: | tathā hi -- pratikṣaṇaṃ viṣayaparicchedalakṣaṇo yogaḥ, tadarthakriyānuṣṭhānalakṣaṇaś ca kṣemaḥ paripālanarūpo bhidyate | tato vipakṣe vṛttyabhāvāt na hetur anaikāntikaḥ | kadā nānāyogakṣematvam? |
children.translated_text: For thus: at each moment, the acquisition characterized as the ascertainment of the object, and the preservation characterized as the maintenance consisting in the performance of causal efficacy with respect to that, differ. Therefore, since [the reason] does not occur in the dissimilar instance (<s>vipakṣa</s>), the logical reason is not inconclusive. When is there difference in acquisition and preservation?
When there is the desire for a result to be accomplished by a specific moment (<s>kṣaṇaviśeṣasādhyārthavāñchā</s>) —

children.text:
| yadā kṣaṇaviśeṣasādhye 'rthe hitāhitalakṣaṇe vāñchā prāptiparihārec chā yogināṃ paropakāram uddiśya bhavati kasyacit[161]kathañcit kvacid upayogāt tadā[162]| yathā darśanamārgge[163]duḥkhe[164]dharmajñānakṣāntir damā(r
daśā)nām[165]anuśayānāṃ vāsanāṃ[166]nirodhayati, tadviruddhāśayotpādanāt | duḥkhe dharmajñānaṃ[167]kleṣaviviktatālakṣaṇāṃ nirvāṇaprāptim utpādayati, [S. 40b.] anuśayaviruddhāśayadārḍhyotpādanāt | tata eṣāṃ[168]grāhakāṇi paracittajñānāni[169]pṛthag eva pramāṇāni | [T. 231a.] parahitādhānadīkṣāvatāṃ ca samastavastuvistaravyāpijñānālokāvabhāsitāntarātmanāṃ bhagavatāṃ kaścid evārthakṣaṇaḥ kasyacid eva parārthasyānugrāhako[170]vibandhako veti sarvabhāvān pratikṣaṇaṃ vīkṣamāṇānām adhyakṣa cetasām tadviṣayakṣaṇānāṃ bhinnārthakriyāsūpayogato nānāyogakṣematvāt | tad yadi pratiksaṇaṃ[171]ksaṇavivekadarśino 'dhikṛtyocyate tadā bhinnopayogitayā pṛthak prāmāṇyāt nānekāntaḥ | atha sarvapadārtheṣv ekatvā 'dhyavasāyinaḥ sāṃvyavahārikān puruṣānabhipretyocyate tadā sakalam eva [S. 41a.] {p. 38.1} nīlasantānam ekam arthaṃ sthirarūpaṃ tadsādhyāṃ
cārthakriyām ekātmikām adhyavasyantīti prāmāṇyam apy uttareṣām aniṣṭam eveti kuto 'nekāntaḥ? iti darśayann āha --
children.translated_text: When the desire — the wish for attainment and avoidance — arises for a result, whether beneficial or harmful, to be accomplished by a specific moment, [this applies] to yogins for the sake of benefiting others, since [each moment] has some particular utility for someone in some way. For example, on the path of seeing in [the Buddhist system], the <s>dharmajñānakṣānti</s> (patience of doctrinal knowledge) regarding suffering eliminates the latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>) of the latent afflictions (<s>anuśaya</s>), because it produces a disposition contrary to them. The <s>dharmajñāna</s> (doctrinal knowledge) regarding suffering produces the attainment of <s>nirvāṇa</s> characterized as freedom from afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>), because it produces firmness of the disposition contrary to the latent afflictions. Therefore, the cognitions of others’ minds (<s>paracittajñāna</s>) that apprehend these are each separately valid cognitions. And for the Blessed Ones (<s>Bhagavat</s>), who have undertaken the vow of bestowing benefit on others, whose inner self is illuminated by the light of knowledge pervading all the details of all things — some particular moment of an object is beneficial to some particular other’s purpose, and some is obstructive — thus, for those who observe all entities at each moment, for the directly perceiving minds, because of the utility of the moments pertaining to those objects in distinct causal efficacies, there is difference in acquisition and preservation. Therefore, if it is said with reference to those who see the distinction of moments at each moment, then, because of the separate validity due to distinct utility, the reasoning is not inconclusive. But if it is said with the intention of ordinary persons who determine oneness in all entities, then, since they determine the entire blue-continuum as a single object of stable form and the causal efficacy to be accomplished by it as having a single nature, the invalidity of the subsequent [cognitions] is precisely what is unwanted — so how is there inconclusiveness? — showing this he says:
‘For, regarding the common [effect]’ (<s>sādhāraṇe hi</s>) —

children.text: iti | tatsantānavarttināṃ sarvakṣaṇānām ekatvenādhyavasitānāṃ vyavahartṛbhir yat sādhāraṇaṃ pratikṣaṇam anyānyakāraṇatayā vibhinnam api paramārthato viparyāsād ekatayā 'bhiniviṣṭaṃ rañjanādikaṃ nīlādikakāryaṃ tatra
children.translated_text: thus. The common effect — such as coloring and the like — of all the moments in that continuum, which are determined as one by ordinary users, which is actually distinct at each moment as belonging to different causes but is clung to as one through the error [of misconception] — regarding that,
they do not have —
the subsequent moments of cognition —
[any] difference in capacity —
power to bring about the object —
[difference].

children.text:
| pūrvapratyakṣakṣaṇaviṣaya eva tebhyo 'pi pravṛtter ādyasyaiva tatra[172]prāmāṇyam | tathā hi -- arthakriyārthināṃ tatsādhanaprāpaṇasamarthe jñāne pramāṇavyavahāraṃ [T. 231b.] kurvatām aviklavadhiyām arthakriyāsādhanabhedād eva prāmāṇyabhedavyavahāro jñāneṣu yuktaḥ [S. 41b.] anyathā smṛtyāder api prāmāṇyaprasaṅgaḥ katham apākriyeta?, ādriyeta vā niṣphalā pramāṇavyavasthā prekṣāvatā iti? |
  keṣām iva sādhāreṇe kārye na sāmarthyabhedaḥ?
children.translated_text:
Since engagement from those [subsequent cognitions] too is toward the very object of the first perceptual moment, the validity belongs to the first alone regarding that [common effect]. For thus: for those who desire causal efficacy and who apply the convention of <s>pramāṇa</s> to a cognition capable of delivering the means to that [efficacy], for those of unwavering understanding, the convention of difference in validity among cognitions is proper only because of the difference in the means of causal efficacy — otherwise, how could the unwanted consequence of validity for memory and the like be averted? Or would a discerning person regard a fruitless system of valid cognition?
For whom, regarding the common effect, is there no difference in capacity? —
He says:
‘successive’ (<s>aparāpara</s>) —
‘and those’ —
‘smokes’ (<s>dhūmāḥ</s>) —
‘and by those’ —
‘those that are cognized’ (<s>pramitāḥ</s>) —
‘and those’ —
‘proximate fires’ (<s>sannikṛṣṭāgnayaḥ</s>) —

children.text: ś ca teṣv iva tadviṣayāṇām iva
children.translated_text: ‘as in the case of those’ — i.e., as in the case of those that have those [fires] as their objects —
‘of inferential cognitions’ — regarding a result to be accomplished by fire in general —

children.text: sandhukṣaṇādike vāñchite tadarthakriyāsādhanaprāpaṇavyaktibhedābhāvāt tathā prāmāṇyabhedo na yukto viduṣāṃ tathā 'trāpi | yadā tu pañcatapas taptukāmo bhavati tadā 'parāparadhūmapramitasannikṛṣṭāgniviṣayāṇāṃ apy anumānānāṃ sāmarthyabhedāt prāmāṇyam anivāritam eva |
children.translated_text: since there is no distinction in the manifestation of the capacity to deliver the means of causal efficacy regarding a desired [result] such as kindling and the like, similarly a difference in validity is not proper for the learned, and so too in this case [of successive perceptions]. But when [someone] wishes to perform the five-fire austerity (<s>pañcatapas</s>), then even for the inferences whose objects are the proximate fires cognized through successive smokes, validity is indeed unavoidable because of the difference in capacity.

body.translated_text: When, regarding a single real entity such as blue, streaming sense-cognitions arise, then, because of non-difference in acquisition and preservation from the first [cognition], there would be the unwanted consequence of invalidity for the subsequent sense-cognitions. But this is not so, hence there is inconclusive reasoning (<s>anekānta</s>) — showing [the opponent’s position of] the proponent of the confusion of <s>pramāṇas</s>, he says:

body.text:
yogijñānāni kṣaṇavivartalakṣakāṇīti kṛtvā na ekyogakṣemāṇi, vivakṣitadavadattādeḥ prathamaḥ kṣaṇo dharmāyogyaḥ dvitīyas tu manāgayogyaḥ tṛtīyas tu yogya iti jñāyate yoginā | tataś ca kṣaṇāḥ bhinnāḥ arthakriyā ca bhinnā
[161] jñānakṣaṇasya
[162] yogini
[163] bauddhamate
[164] avajñākāriṇi mlecchādau saṃsāriskandhe
[165] [dharmajñā] nena kṣāntiḥ | samarthena yat sahyata ity arthaḥ
[166] kleśajananaśaktim
[167] vairāgyajñānam
[168] dharmajñānakṣāntyādicittānām
[169] yoginaḥ satkāni
[170] kañcit paracittakṣaṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā bhagavān tasyaivānugrahāya pravartate | kañcit tu dṛṣṭvā audāsīnyam ālambate | kañcit tv avabodhya nigrahāya
[171] pratyakṣaṇām -- T.
[172] kārye
[173] ity āha --
body.translated_text:
Because yogic cognitions have the characteristic of discerning momentary distinctions, they are not of a single acquisition and preservation. The first moment of [the person] such as <s>Devadatta</s> under consideration is ineligible for a [particular] <s>dharma</s>, the second is slightly ineligible, but the third is eligible — thus is known by the yogin. And therefore the moments are distinct and the causal efficacy is distinct.
[161] of a cognition-moment
[162] for the yogin
[163] in the Buddhist system
[164] regarding the suffering that is contemptible, such as barbarians (<s>mleccha</s>) and the like, the aggregate of <s>saṃsāra</s>
[165] [doctrinal] knowledge-patience: that which is endured by one who is capable — this is the meaning
[166] the power to generate afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>)
[167] the knowledge of dispassion
[168] of the minds [such as] <s>dharmajñānakṣānti</s> and others
[169] the real cognitions of the yogin
[170] Having seen a certain moment of another’s mind, the Blessed One acts for the benefit of that very [being]. But having seen another, he adopts indifference. But having understood yet another, [he acts] for [its] restraint.
[171] <s>pratyakṣāṇām</s> — T.
[172] regarding the effect
[173] he says —
‘Successive smokes’ (<s>aparāparadhuma</s>) —
thus.
‘successive’ (<s>aparāpare</s>) —
‘and’ — T.
section: 27. The purport of the refutation of the validity of conceptualization.

body.text: tad evaṃ `yathā nīlaṃ dṛṣṭvā nīlam iti jñāna(m)' ity udāharaṇe nīlavikalpasya prāmāṇyaṃ nirākṛtya prakṛte yojyann āha --

children.translated_text: ‘By this’ (<s>etena</s>) —
by this refutation of the validity of the blue-conceptualization that arises after the experience of the blue particular.
‘Since that [conceptualization] is not accepted, even though it assists the form of the object, being a conceptualization’ —

children.text: iti bruvatākumārilena prade[S. 42a.]śādidarśanottarakālabhāvino {p. 39.1} dharmivikalpasya, tathā sambandhapratipattikāle 'gnisvalakṣaṇadarśanasāmarthyabhāvino 'gnisāmānyaviṣayasya sādhyadharmavikalpasya, dhūmālocanājñānapṛṣṭhabhāvino dhūmasāmānyāvabhāsino liṅgavikalpasya, ādigrahaṇād dharma[T. 232a.]dharmisambandhavikalpasya ca pramāṇapṛṣṭhabhāvino
children.translated_text: thus says <s>Kumārila</s>. [By this is refuted:] the validity of the property-bearer-conceptualization (<s>dharmivikalpa</s>) that arises after seeing the location and so forth; likewise the validity of the provable-property-conceptualization (<s>sādhyadharmavikalpa</s>) having as its object the universal of fire, arising from the power of seeing the fire-particular at the time of apprehending the connection; the validity of the logical-mark-conceptualization (<s>liṅgavikalpa</s>) appearing as the universal of smoke, arising after the bare sensory cognition of smoke; and, by the word ‘and so forth,’ the validity of the property-bearer-property-connection-conceptualization (<s>dharmadharmisambandhavikalpa</s>), [all] arising after the <s>pramāṇa</s> —
preceded by perception called bare sensory cognition (<s>ālocana</s>) having as its object merely the intrinsic nature of the property-bearer and so forth —
‘And of the logical mark that is not conceptualized, the grasping of [its connection with] the property-bearer’ —
‘[does not occur] thus’ —
what was accepted out of fear of this objection —
the validity —
that —
has been refuted.

children.text: pratyākhyātam | pūrvakam eva svalakṣaṇaviṣayaṃ darśanaṃ yat pareṇālocanājñānam iti vyavahṛtaṃ tat pramāṇaṃ na tu tadbalabhāvī vikalpo yathoktena nyāyeneti sthitam etat --
children.translated_text: has been refuted. The prior seeing itself, which has the particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>) as its object — what the opponent calls <s>ālocanajñāna</s> (bare sensory cognition) — that is the <s>pramāṇa</s>, but the conceptualization (<s>vikalpa</s>) that arises from its force is not [a <s>pramāṇa</s>], by the reasoning stated above. Thus it is established:
'the establishment of the property of the thesis-subject in the <s>sādhyadharmin</s>, from perception or from inference' —

children.text:
niścaya iti |
  tad evaṃ pratyakṣataḥ pakṣadharmaniścayaṃ bruvatā prasaṅgena darśanapṛṣṭhabhāvino vikalpasya prāmāṇyanirākaraṇāt |
children.translated_text:
[this is] the ascertainment.
Thus, by the speaker who states the ascertainment of the property of the thesis-subject from perception, incidentally, by refuting the validity of the conceptualization that follows perception —
'Perception is free from conceptual construction' (<s>pratyakṣaṃ kalpanāpoḍham</s>)
— has been established.

body.translated_text: Having thus refuted the validity of blue-conceptualization in the example ‘upon seeing blue, the cognition "it is blue,"’ applying [this result] to the topic at hand, he says:
Section: 28. Declaration of the primacy of inference.

children.translated_text: 'this [treatise] is commenced for the purpose of instruction in inference' —
was it said thus, and not in general terms 'for the purpose of instruction in valid cognition'? The disagreement regarding the number [of <s>pramāṇas</s>]

children.text: ity uktam na sāmānyena `samyagjñānavyutpādanārtham' iti? | saṅkhyādivipratipattir apy atra tadviṣayā nirastaiva | parokṣārthapratipatter anumāna[m evāśra]yaḥ | kasmād? yataḥ pakṣadharma eva tadaṃśena vyāpta eva ca hetuḥ kāraṇaṃ tasyāḥ, nānya ity abhidhānāt parokṣārthaviṣayaṃ sarvaṃ pramaṇam anumāne 'ntarbhāvitam iti saṅksepataḥ saṅkhyāvipratipattiḥ samyagjñānaviṣayā nirastā | tathā, vyāpakāṃśasya[174]gamyatvapratīteḥ tadaṃśavyāptivacanena sāmānyaviṣayam anumānaṃ na svalakṣaṇaviṣayam ity ākhyātam [T. 232b.] tasyāsādhāraṇatvāt, asādhāraṇasya ca vyāpakatvāyogāt, vikalpāviṣayatvāc ca |
children.translated_text: and the like, which concerns this very subject, has already been eliminated. The cognition of imperceptible objects has inference alone as its basis. Why? Because it has been stated that 'a property of the thesis-subject, pervaded by a portion of that alone, is the reason (<s>hetu</s>)' — the cause of that [cognition of imperceptible objects] — and nothing else. [Therefore,] all <s>pramāṇas</s> concerning imperceptible objects are subsumed under inference — thus, in brief, the disagreement regarding the number [of <s>pramāṇas</s>], which concerns valid cognition, has been eliminated. Similarly, since the portion of the pervader (<s>vyāpaka</s>) is understood as that which is to be cognized, by the statement of pervasion by a portion of that, it has been declared that inference has the universal (<s>sāmānya</s>) as its object, not the particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>), because that [particular] is uncommon, and because what is uncommon cannot be a pervader, and because it is not an object of conceptualization.
'That which has an uncommon object is the first of those' (<s>tatra tadādyam asādhāraṇaviṣayam</s>) —

children.text: ity ācakṣāṇena svalakṣaṇaviṣayam eva pratyakṣam uktam | {p. 40.1}
children.translated_text: by him who states this, it has been said that perception alone has the particular as its object.
'Seeing alone is the <s>pramāṇa</s>' —

by this declaration, it is indicated that the <s>pramāṇa</s> itself is the result (<s>phala</s>),
because it has the nature of cognizing the object. Similarly, since it will be stated that 'its application is twofold,' inference-for-others (<s>parārthānumāna</s>) will be discussed, because it has the nature of articulating the triple-characterized mark. And in brief, the instruction of inference is also intended. And that [instruction]

children.text:
ity ākhyānāt pramāṇam eva phalam iti sūcitam,
[S. 43a.] tasyārthapratītirūpatvāt | tathā, tasya dvidhā prayoga iti vakṣyamāṇatvāt parārthānumānaṃ kathayiṣyate, tasya trirūpaliṅgākhyānarūpatvāt | saṅkṣepataś cānumānavyutpādanam apy abhimatam | tac ca sarvatrāsty[175]eveti kasmāt
children.translated_text: exists everywhere — so why was it said,
'for the purpose of instruction in inference'?

children.text:
ity uktam[176]? |
  satyam, prādhānyāt tu tadgrahaṇam | tathā hi -- pradhānapuruṣārthopayoginas tattvasya caturāryasatyalakṣaṇasyānumānata[177]eva niścayāt tasya prādhānyam | tathā pratyakṣe 'pi viṣaye vivādasambhave, nānumānād anyan nirṇayanibandhanam ity ato 'py asya prādhānyam | pravartakatvāc ca prādhānyam asya | tathā hi -- yadanubhūtaphalaṃ sukhaduḥkhasādhanam, anubhūyamānaphalaṃ vā dṛśyamānaṃ na tatpravṛttiviṣayo niṣpannatvāt phalasya | tasmād yadanāgataphalaṃ sukhaduḥkhasādhanaṃ pratyakṣam api tatrāpy anumānam eva pravartakam | na hi tasyānāgate sukhaduḥkhe prati yogyatāṃ pratyakṣaṃ nirddhārayati, phalasya [S.43b.] parokṣatvāt | taduktam --
children.translated_text: True; but the mention of that [inference] is because of its primacy. Namely: because the ascertainment of reality characterized by the four noble truths (<s>caturāryasatya</s>), which is useful for the principal human purpose, is from inference alone — therefore its primacy. Similarly, even in a domain that is [supposedly] perceptible, since when a dispute arises there is no other basis for resolution than inference — for this reason too, its primacy. And because it is what prompts action (<s>pravartakatva</s>), it has primacy. Namely: that which has an already-experienced result, being a means to pleasure or pain, or that which has a result being experienced now, being perceived — that is not the object of [purposive] action, because the result is already accomplished. Therefore, that which has a future result, being a means to pleasure or pain, even if perceptible — even regarding that, inference alone is the prompter of action. For perception does not determine its capacity with respect to future pleasure and pain, since the result is imperceptible. As he has said —
'For when the effect is imperceptible, there is no cognition of the causal relation' —

children.translated_text: it has been said. Since the intrinsic nature of what is a means to pleasure or pain — such as water, fire, and the like — is established from perception, and since the capacity for the future result is from inference, both are prompters of action. Therefore, because of its primacy, inference is singled out — enough with excessive elaboration.

Wherever the proving property exists, there the property to be proved also exists independently of any other cause — the establishment of this meaning is the ascertainment of positive concomitance in the essential-nature reason.
But how does the property to be proved invariably accompany the mere existence of the proving property?
'By virtue of being that very nature' (<s>tadbhāvatayā</s>) —

body.translated_text: Therein, the ascertainment of the property of the thesis-subject for the essential-nature, effect, and non-apprehension [reasons] has been stated without distinction, since they are achieved by the same means. But the indication of the ascertainment of positive and negative concomitance must be made with distinction, since they are achieved by different means. Therefore, showing first that in the essential-nature reason the ascertainment of positive concomitance depends on its own <s>pramāṇa</s>, he says —

the property to be proved
