vyatirekavatā[189]upagatena? | tathā hi -- na sattāmātreṇa kṛtakatvādayo dharmāḥ sādhyadharmapratipattinibandhanam, teṣāṃ sadā sannihitatvenānavarataṃ taddharmapratītiprasaṅgāt, kintu vikalpapratibhāsina eva | sa ca vikalpaḥ svapratibhāsinam[190]evākāraṃ bahīrūpatayā 'dhyavasitam anusaran kṛtakānityādirūpatāṃ vastunaḥ pratipadyate, paramārthato 'saṃsparśe 'pi tadrūpasya[191], paramparayā tadupādānatvāt | vyatiriktās tu dharmās tadutpattinimittamātratayā[192]parikalpyante, tad varaṃ yad[193]eva tatkalpanānibandhanaṃ[194]tad eva tathāvidhavikalpaprasavanimittam astu, tasyāvaśyam[195]abhyupagamanīyatvāt, tadabhyupagame ca caritārthā vyatirekavanto dharmā ity alaṃ tatkalpanayā | avaśyaṃ ca vyatiriktā 'nityatādvāreṇāpi vastuna evānavasthāyinam ātmānaṃ pratipadyate(nte), [S. 46a.] [T. 234b.] tadanurūpārthakṛ(kri)y[h9]ārthitayā[196]pravṛtteḥ, anyathā[197]vyatiriktā 'nityatayā nityatvāt[198]tadavagamārthatvenāyam anityasādhyārthakriyārthī[199]nityaṃ
śabdādikam āśaṅkamānaḥ
children.translated_text:
in the ultimate sense. But at the time of conceiving the <s>sādhya</s> and <s>sādhana</s>, since [they] appear as different in the conceptual cognition (<s>kalpanābuddhi</s>) that is indirectly grounded in the referents defined by mutual exclusion (<s>vyāvṛttapadārtha</s>), the relation of provable and prover is not vitiated. For that [relation] does not depend on a real (<s>pāramārthika</s>) difference between the properties of provable and prover and the property-bearer — such as in produced-ness and the like — since in the absence of a [real] relation, the relation of provable and prover would be impossible.
If [one objects:] the relation of produced-ness, impermanence, and the like is co-inherence (<s>samavāya</s>) in a single locus — no, because even if that [samavāya] is something different from those [properties], since the [problem of] absence of relation remains unchanged — 'what is the co-inherence of these two in this locus?' — and because if one postulates further relations, there would be an infinite regress. And if one postulates existence through co-inherence, then produced-ness and the like would also exist in things held to be permanent, such as the self (<s>ātman</s>) and the like. For the very same co-inherence by whose force produced-ness exists in sound would also [have to exist] in permanent things, since it has been accepted as unitary — so what would prevent produced-ness and the like from existing in the self and so forth? If [one responds:] 'it is determined that produced-ness and the like exist only in that which has the nature of coming into being after not having existed, and of being unstable after having existed' — then let that very nature of coming into being after non-existence and instability after existence be accepted as the ground of the conceptual cognition whose object is the exclusion of the superimposition of the contrary form — why is this not accepted? By that very [nature], the existence of the two properties — which are not ultimately different — in the <s>sādhyadharmin</s> [is established]; what need is there of an intermediary entity like produced-ness and the like that is held to be distinct? For properties that are produced-ness and the like are not the ground for the cognition of the property to be proved merely by their existence, since, as they are always present, there would be the absurd consequence of unceasing cognition of that property. Rather, [they function] only as they appear in conceptualization. And that conceptualization, following the form appearing in it — determined as external — cognizes the entity's nature as produced, impermanent, and so forth, even though that form has no ultimate contact [with reality], because indirectly it is derived from that [reality]. But the distinct properties are merely postulated as the mere cause of its [conceptualization's] arising; it is better that what is the ground of that conceptualization itself be the cause of the arising of such conceptualization, since it must necessarily be accepted; and upon accepting it, the distinct properties have fulfilled their purpose — so enough with postulating them. And necessarily, even through the door of the distinct impermanence, [people] cognize the impermanent nature of the entity itself,
since [their] activity is [motivated] by desire for causal efficacy corresponding to that; otherwise, [if impermanence were truly distinct,] since by the distinct impermanence, because of its permanence — [the argument continues that]

kathaṃ bhedapakṣabhāvināṃ doṣāṇāṃ anavasaraḥ? | yaṃ cātmānaṃ purodhāya `imau dharmāu, ayaṃ dharmī' iti vyavasthāpyate[h10]yadi tena bhedas tadā bheda eveti kuto 'nekāntavādaḥ? | athābhedaḥ; tadā `ayaṃ sādhanadharmaḥ, ayaṃ sādhyadharmaḥ, dharmī cāyam' iti kathaṃ pāramārthikaṃ tṛ(tri)tayaṃ sidhyet? | [S. 47a.] tasmāt tattatpararūpavyāvṛttisamāśrayāyāṃ kalpanābuddhau bhedavatām iva dharmadharmiṇāṃ pratibhāsanāt sādhyasādhanabhāvaḥ | tanmātrānubandhas tu vastutaḥ tattatsvabhāvatayaiva yuktaḥ iti manyamānena
children.translated_text:
Is [this person] devoted to the investigation of impermanence? When impermanence, as something distinct [from the entity], has been cognized, let [one's activity] be directed toward that very [impermanence] — why toward the eternal sound-nature? If [you say]: because cognition [of impermanence] is through the medium of that [sound] — then what is the use of this intermediary? It would be better for there to be direct cognition of [impermanence] itself, since the purpose is served by that alone. But this matter, when debated excessively, becomes extremely dense [and impenetrable], so let it rest for now.
As for those followers of <s>Jaimini</s> who think: 'This defect applies only to the <s>Naiyāyikas</s> and others, whose properties are absolutely distinct [from the substance]; but for us, whose properties are somehow both different and non-different, there is no such defect, since that is their very nature' — for them too, if in reality the nature of the proving property is accepted as [identical with] the provable property, we see no benefit in accepting difference-of-a-sort [S. 46b.], since the relation of provable and prover can be established even through a posited difference. And in [actual] identity, difference of any sort is not tenable, because of [there being but] one nature that is non-different. If [you say]: even in that [one nature], there somehow exist both difference and non-difference — no, because of the absurd consequence of an infinite regress. For the two properties, though possessing one nature, being [also] different — to account for the non-difference by that nature, another non-different nature must be posited; and likewise yet another by that [T. 235a.] — there would be an infinite series of natures both different and non-different. And since in the cognition of the conceptual construction, an infinite series of natures of both forms does not appear — why do you deceive yourselves with such a construction? Moreover, since difference-of-a-sort is accepted,
how is there no occasion for the defects that attend the difference position? And with regard to that self [i.e., that entity] upon whose basis it is established that 'these are the properties, this is the property-bearer' — if there is difference from it, then it is just difference, so whence the doctrine of non-exclusivity (<s>anekāntavāda</s>)? Or if non-difference — then how could the ultimate triad of 'this is the proving property, this is the provable property, and this is the property-bearer' be established? [S. 47a.] Therefore, since in the conceptual cognition — which takes as its basis the exclusion from other respective forms — property and property-bearer appear as if different, the relationship of provable and prover [is established]. But the connection with those [properties] alone is, in reality, tenable only as [their being of] the nature of their respective [entities] — thinking thus,
'in reality, by being of that nature' (<s>vastutas tadbhāvatayā</s>)
— was stated.

children.translated_text: — by the restrictive particle [<s>eva</s>] he states the pervasion (<s>vyāpti</s>). And the form of the invariable concomitance with the mere existence of the proving property is thereby declared, since it is shown that merely by being existent [something] is momentary, without any other ground. And since that [pervasion] is established through identity-in-reality, he shows the means of its establishment — the operation of the invalidating cognition:
'in the case of non-momentariness' (<s>akṣaṇikatve</s>)
— when the opposite of momentariness obtains —
'because of the contradiction with causal efficacy' (<s>arthakriyāvirodhāt</s>)

children.text: arthasya -- kāryasya kriyā -- niṣpattis tasyā virodhāt
children.translated_text: — of the object — i.e., the effect — the performance (<s>kriyā</s>) — i.e., the production — because of the contradiction of that [causal efficacy] —
'that which is characterized by that' (<s>tallakṣaṇam</s>)
— that whose defining characteristic (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>) is causal efficacy —
'of reality' (<s>vastutvasya</s>)

children.text: arthakriyāsāmarthyātmanaḥ, tat tathoktam | arthakriyā hi tatsāmarthyarūpaṃ vastutvaṃ lakṣyate |
children.translated_text: — i.e., of that whose nature is the capacity for causal efficacy; hence it is so stated. For reality is defined as the form of the capacity for causal efficacy.
'that' (<s>tad</s>)
— reality of such a kind —
'is lost' (<s>hīyate</s>)

children.text:
nivartate, tadviparyayarūpasyāsattvasyā ''karṣaṇāt | etac ca bādhakaṃ pramāṇaṃ vyāpakānupalabdhirūpam uttaratrāvasaraprāptaṃ svayam eva vakṣyati | tadanayā bādhakapramāṇavṛttayā sādhyadharmasya [S. 48a.] vastutaḥ sādhanadharmasvabhāvatā sidhyati | tayā ca vastutas tadbhāvatayā
sādhanadharmabhāvamātrānubandha iti |
children.translated_text:
— ceases, because of the attraction [toward it] of its opposite form, namely non-existence. And this invalidating cognition, which has the form of non-apprehension of the pervader (<s>vyāpakānupalabdhi</s>), [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>] himself will state later when the occasion arises. Thus, by this operation of the invalidating cognition, the identity-in-reality of the provable property with the nature of the proving property is established [S. 48a.]. And through that identity-in-reality,
there is invariable concomitance with the mere existence of the proving property.

body.translated_text: What then is that 'being of that nature in reality' (<s>vastutas tadbhāvatā</s>), by which — as the ground [of the inference] — the invariable concomitance of the provable property with the mere existence of the proving property is established? To this he says —

<s>satvā(ttvā)khyahetuviparītāsatva(ttva)-</s>
[206] <s>yena sādhya-</s> — T.
[Section: 32. The determination of positive concomitance (<s>anvayaniścaya</s>) in the case of the effect-reason (<s>kāryahetu</s>).]

body.text: evaṃ svabhāvahetau [T. 236a] viparyaye bādhakapramāṇavṛttyā tādātmyasiddhito 'nvayaniścayaṃ pratipādya kāryahetau pratipādayann āha --

children.translated_text: 'In the case of the effect-reason' (<s>kāryahetau</s>)

children.text: anvayaniścayaḥ iti prakṛtam | kaḥ punar asau kāryakāraṇayor bhāvaḥ? |
children.translated_text: — 'the ascertainment of positive concomitance' is the topic under discussion. What then is the relationship between effect and cause?
'effect-ness' (<s>kāryatvam</s>)
'and cause-ness' (<s>kāraṇatvam</s>)

— and the cognition of that [relation] is the ascertainment of positive concomitance in the case of the effect-reason. And showing how the establishment of the cause-effect relation comes about, he says —
'establishment' (<s>siddhiḥ</s>)

children.text: pratītiḥ sā kāryahetāv anvayaniścayaḥ | yathā ca kāryakāraṇabhāvasiddhir bhavati tathopadarśayann āha --
children.translated_text: — cognition. That [cognition] is the ascertainment of positive concomitance in the case of the effect-reason. And showing how the establishment of the cause-effect relation comes about, he says —
'For instance' (<s>yathā</s>)
and so forth. The word 'for instance' (<s>yathā</s>) is for the purpose of illustration.
'This' (<s>idam</s>)
— smoke and the like —
'of this' (<s>asya</s>)
— of fire —
'when perceived' (<s>upalambhe</s>)
'being' (<s>sati</s>)
'is perceived' (<s>upalabhyate</s>)

children.text: iti sambandhaḥ | anena kāryakāraṇabhāvasiddhau pratyakṣavyāpāram āha | na ca kevalaṃ pratyakṣaṃ kāryakāraṇabhāvam asandigdhaṃ sādhayati, kintu prākpravṛttānupalambhasahāyam iti [S. 48b.] darśāyitum āha --
children.translated_text: — this is the syntactic connection. By this he states the role of perception in establishing the cause-effect relation. And [the point is that] perception alone does not establish the cause-effect relation beyond doubt; rather, it does so with the assistance of prior non-apprehension — [S. 48b.] to show this, he says —
'that which, having fulfilled the conditions for apprehension, is not apprehended' (<s>upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptam anupalabdham</s>)

children.text:
iti | yadi tad dhūmādikam upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptaṃ satsv anyai(nye)ṣūpalambhapratyayeṣu
dṛśyātmakaṃ sat nopalabdhaṃ bhavati agnyādisāmagrīsannidhānāt prāk tādātmyādi(tadagnyādi)sāmagryām upalabhyamānāyām upalabhyamānaṃ tatkāryaṃ sidhyati | na tūpalambhapratyayāntarvaikalyād anupajātopalabdhiyogyarūpaṃ sat, taddeśasannihitam apy anupalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptatayāgnyādisāmagrī sannidhānāt prāganupalabdham iti | upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptasya cānupalambhenāgnyādisāmagrī sannidhānāt prāganyatā āgamanaṃ, taddeśakālasaṃnnihitāt kaṭakuṭyā[T. 236b.]der utpattiḥ, taddeśe cā 'sannidhānam iti, tritayam apākriyate | etāvadbhiś ca prakārair atatkāryatā bhavantī bhavet | tato 'nupalambhenā 'tatkāryatāśaṅkānirāsād tadbhāve bhāvagrāhipratyakṣanibandhanaḥ kāryakāraṇabhāvo 'sandigdhaḥ [S. 49a.] sidhyati |
  na cāgnīndhanādibhāve niyatasannidher adṛśyātmanaḥ kutaścit dhūmasya bhāvaḥ syāt ity āśaṅkanīyam | agnīndhanādibhedānuvidhānād dhūmasya | candanāgurukarpūrakeśorṇādīndhanabhede tadanurūpabhedasyāsya darśanād alpamahadindhanavikārakāriṇaścāgnes tadanurūpasya[208]| na cāgnīndhanādisannidhāv adṛśyātmano niyatasannidhānatā yuktā, {p. 46.1} pratibandhābhāvāt | pratibandhe vā tatkāryatā[209]tatkāraṇatā vā syāt | tatkāryatve, nāgnīndhanasamparkkānantaraṃ dhūmajanma syāt, tadbhāvābhāvānuvidhānād eva cāsyāpi tatkāryatvam | tac ca dhūme 'pi samānam | nāpīndhanādikāraṇatvam adṛśyātmanaḥ, indhanādeḥ svahetor eva vṛkṣāder bhāvadarśanāt | tatrāpi tathābhāvakalpanāyāṃ[210]tad evottaraṃ vācyam | punaś codye sa eva parihāro 'navasthā ca | etenaikasāmagryadhīnatā 'pi pratyuktā | tadanvayavyatirekānuvidhānād eva ca dhūmasya tat[211]kāraṇaṃ kalpeta
| tac cāgnyādāv api tulyam | tad api tatra kāraṇam astu iti cet; na, agnyādibhāve 'vaśyam bhāvino 'nyasyāpi kāraṇatvakalpanāyāṃ nimittābhāvāt, kāryavyatirekanibandhanatvāt [S. 49b.] kāraṇabhāvakalpanāyāḥ | tathā agnīndhanā[T. 237a.]der evānyatarābhāve abhavataḥ[212][h11]| bhavatu vā 'nyasyāpi tadbhāve niyatasannidheḥ kāraṇatā | na tu tāvatāgnyādeḥ kāraṇatvahāniḥ, yato dhūmadarśanāt tanniścayena pravṛttau tadvisaṃvādaḥ syāt | na hi sarvasattvakarmādhipatyajanitatve 'pi jagadvaicitryasya dṛṣṭakāraṇahānitas tatkāryadarśanād vā pravṛttānāṃ atatprāptir ity alam atiprasaṅgena |
  kiṃ rūpaḥ punar asau kāryakāraṇabhāvo 'nupalambhasahāya pratyakṣanibandhana ity āha --
children.translated_text:
— if that smoke and the like, having fulfilled the conditions for apprehension — being of a perceptible nature when the other conditions for apprehension are present — is not apprehended prior to the proximity of the fire-aggregate and the like, then when that fire-aggregate and the like are being perceived, it is perceived [and thereby] established as their effect. But [it is] not [the case that something] whose perceptible form has not yet arisen due to the deficiency of other conditions for apprehension, even though present in that location — [such a thing], having fulfilled the conditions for non-apprehension, is [what we mean by] 'not apprehended prior to the proximity of the fire-aggregate.' And by the non-apprehension of what has fulfilled the conditions for apprehension, three [alternative explanations] are eliminated: [1] its being from elsewhere [i.e., having come from another place] prior to the proximity of the fire-aggregate, [2] [its] arising from a jar, wall, etc. present at that location and time, and [3] its not being present at that location. And by these many modes, whatever would constitute its not being the effect of that [fire] would [in each case] be [an alternative explanation] — [T. 236b.] and since by non-apprehension the suspicion of its not being the effect of that [cause] is removed, the cause-effect relation, grounded in the perception that grasps existence-when-that-exists, is established beyond doubt [S. 49a.].
Nor should it be suspected that, given the existence of fire-fuel and the like, some invisible entity in constant proximity [might be] the [real cause] of smoke. For smoke follows the distinctions of fire-fuel and the like — since in the case of different fuels such as sandalwood, aloe, camphor, animal hair and wool, a correspondingly different [smoke] is observed; and fire, which modifies according to small or large [quantities of] fuel, [produces smoke] correspondingly. And constant proximity of an invisible entity in the presence of fire-fuel and the like is not tenable, because there is no causal constraint (<s>pratibandha</s>). Or if there were constraint, it would either be an effect or a cause of that [fire]. If an effect, then the generation of smoke would not [occur] immediately upon the conjunction of fire and fuel — but since [smoke] follows the presence and absence of that [conjunction], its being an effect of that [fire] is [confirmed]. And the same applies to smoke [being an effect of fire]. Nor is the invisible entity a cause like fuel and the like, since fuel and the like are observed to come into being from their own causes — trees and so forth. And if one were to posit such existence there too, the same reply applies; and upon further objection, the same refutation, and an infinite regress. By this, the [objection of] dependence on a single aggregate is also answered. And since smoke follows the positive and negative concomitance of that [fire-aggregate alone], that is posited as the cause.
And the same holds for fire and the like [i.e., one cannot posit another cause for fire itself]. Let that [invisible entity] too be a cause therein — [one might say;] no, because in the case of the existence of fire and the like, there is no ground for positing the causality of another [entity] whose existence is certain, since the positing of causal status depends on the exclusion of the effect [when the supposed cause is absent] [S. 49b.]. For it is precisely upon the absence of one or another among fire, fuel, etc. [T. 237a.] that [smoke] does not arise. Or even if some other entity in constant proximity were a cause when that [fire] exists — still, the causality of fire and the like is not thereby lost, such that there would be deception for one who, having seen smoke, proceeds with the ascertainment of that [fire]. For even if the diversity of the world is generated by the sovereignty of the karma of all beings, there is no failure to attain [the intended result] for those who proceed on the basis of observed causes or from seeing their effects. Enough of this over-extension.
What then is the nature of this cause-effect relation, [which is] grounded in perception assisted by non-apprehension? He says —
'Existence when that exists, and non-existence when that is absent' (<s>tadbhāve bhāvaḥ tadabhāve 'bhāvaś ca</s>)
— for that which is
regarded as the cause — only when it exists does that which is regarded as the effect exist.
'When that is absent' (<s>tadabhāve</s>)
— when what is regarded as the cause is absent —
'absence' (<s>abhāvaḥ</s>)
'alone' (<s>eva</s>)

children.text:
kāryatvenābhimatasyābhāvaś ca | sa eva kāryakāraṇabhāvo nānyaḥ |
  sa hi tābhyām anyo bhavan svabhāvato 'pratipannakāryakāraṇarūpayor vā bhaved, yadvā svabhāvenaiva kāryakāraṇātmanoḥ | yadyādyaḥ pakṣaḥ tadā sarvatraivākāryaka(kā)raṇabhūte 'pi vastuni [S. 50a.] bhavet tanniyamakāraṇābhāvāt | tataḥ sarvaṃ sarvasya kāryaṃ syāt | {p. 47.1} svabhāvena cātadrūpasyānyayoge 'pi na tadrūpatā | na hi bhāvāḥ pratiniyatarūpatyagenānyayoge 'pi rūpāntaramābhajante, yato nānyayogas teṣāṃ pūrvarūpaṃ nāśayati vināśahetvayogād vakṣyamāṇakāt | nā 'py apūrvam utpādayati tasya tato 'rthāntaratvaprasaṅgāt | na hi teṣu niṣpanneṣv aniṣpanno bhinnahetuko vā tatsvabhāvo yuktaḥ | ayaṃ hi bhedo [T. 237b.] bhedahetur vā viruddhadharmādhyāsaḥ kāraṇa bhedaś ca | tataś cet na bhedaḥ, anyanimittābhāvāt ekaṃ dravyaṃ viśvaṃ syāt ityādi prasajyeta | pratibhāsabhedo 'pi hi itaretarābhāvarūpatayā viruddhadharmādhyāsatāṃ nātikrāmati | tataś ca pūrvake vastunī
[S. 50b.] tadavasthe eveti na tayor anyayoge 'pi kāryakāraṇarūpatāpattiḥ |
  atha dvitīyaḥ pakṣaḥ, tadā svabhāvata eva tayoḥ kāryakāraṇarūpatvād anyas tadbhāvaḥ kathaṃ na vaiyarthyam anubhavet? | kāryakāraṇabuddhī api tadbhāvabhāvitvamātranibandhane nārthāntaranimitte, tasyopapalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptasya[218]kāryakāraṇarūpavivekinā rūpāntareṇāpratibhāsanāt | tathāvidhāsyāpi[219]grahaṇakalpanāyām atiprasaṅgaḥ | anupalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptatāyāṃ[220]kathaṃ kāryakāraṇabhāvabuddhī tannibandhane? | na hi tad arthāntaraṃ svasattāmātreṇa tadbuddhī pravartayati | sadā sannihitatvenāsya tayoḥ sarvadodayaprasaṅgāt | na ca viśeṣaṇam agṛhītaṃ [S. 51a.] viśeṣye svaviśiṣṭapratyayanibandhanam ity ayuktā 'syānupalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptatā | na ca dṛṣṭasyāpy anupalakṣaṇaṃ yuktam, kāryakāraṇabuddhyos tannibandhanatopagamāt | na hi yannimitto yo 'nyatrātadbuddhibhāji tadvyavasāyaḥ sa tadanupalakṣaṇe[221]yuktaḥ | devadatte
children.translated_text:
And the absence of that which is accepted as the effect. That itself is the causal relation (<s>kāryakāraṇabhāva</s>), and no other [entity]. For that [causal relation], if it were other than those two [cause and effect], would either [1] exist in things whose cause-effect nature has not been intrinsically established, or [2] exist in things that are intrinsically of the nature of cause and effect. [S. 50a.] If the first alternative [holds], then it would exist in every entity even where there is no cause-effect [relation], since there would be no reason restricting it. Then everything would be the effect of everything. {p. 47.1} And when what is not of that nature is associated with another, it does not [thereby] acquire that nature due to its essential nature [being fixed]. For entities do not adopt another form through association with another while abandoning their determined form, since association with another does not destroy their prior form — because of the absence of a cause of destruction, as will be explained — nor does it produce a new [form], since that [new form] would be something entirely different from it [the entity]. For when those [entities] have been produced, it is not justified that a form belonging to them [but] not [yet] produced, or having a different cause, [should arise]. For this difference, or the cause of difference, is the superimposition of contradictory properties (<s>viruddhadharmādhyāsa</s>) and the difference of causes. If therefore there is no difference, then because there is no other ground [for difference], the absurd consequence would follow that a single substance is the universe, and so forth. For even the difference of appearances does not transcend the character of superimposition of contradictory properties, since it has the form of mutual non-existence. [S. 50b.] And therefore, the prior two entities remain in the same state — so even through their association with another, the nature of cause and effect does not arise in them.
If the second alternative [holds], then since those two [cause and effect] are of the nature of cause and effect by their very essential nature, how would an additional causal relation (<s>tadbhāva</s>) not be pointless? The cognitions of cause and effect too would be grounded merely in the existence of that [causal] relation [between the two], not caused by something separate — since that [separate relation], which would meet the criterion for being perceived, does not appear with a form distinct from the cause-effect nature. And if one imagines the grasping of something of that kind [i.e., a separate relation] that does not so appear, there is over-extension. And if it meets the criterion for non-apprehension (<s>anupalabdhilakṣaṇaprāpta</s>), [S. 51a.] how can the cognitions of cause and effect be grounded in it? For that separate entity does not, by its mere existence, activate those cognitions — since, being always proximate, there would be the absurd consequence of those [cognitions] always arising. And a qualifier that is not grasped is not the ground for a cognition qualified by it in the qualified thing — therefore, its meeting the criterion for non-apprehension is unjustified. And it is not justified to characterize as non-apprehended what is in fact observed, since the cognitions of cause and effect are accepted as being grounded in it. For that the determination of which is grounded in something, such that in [something] other than that, the cognition of it does not occur — it is not justified to characterize it as non-apprehended in [the case of] <s>Devadatta</s> —

children.text:
daṇḍivyavasāyavad
daṇḍānupalakṣaṇe | na cārthāntarasya kāryakāraṇābhyāṃ sambandho ghaṭate, sambandhāntarakalpanāyām anavasthā[T. 238a.]prasakteḥ | kāryakāraṇabhāvābhyupagame kāryakāraṇābhyām asahabhāvitā sadbhāvasya | tataś ca kāryakāraṇakāle tasyāsannidhānāt kathaṃ {p. 48.1} kāryakāraṇabuddhihetutā? | niruddhayor adhyāhṛtya[222]tatpratyayakalpanāyāṃ[223]ca kalpitaviṣaya eva kāryakāraṇatādhyavasāyaḥ syāt na vastuviṣayaḥ | sa ca viśiṣṭabhāvābhāvanibandhano 'bhyupagata eveti kim arthāntarakalpanayā? | kalpitaviṣayatve tadvyavasāyasya[224], tasyā[225]vaiyarthyāt kāryakāraṇayoś cāyaugapadyāt | na hi [S. 51b.] tābhyām asau janyate, pratyekajanyaś ca kathaṃ kāryakāraṇabhāvaḥ? | yadā ca kāraṇena janyate tadā kiṃ svakāryasahito janyate, atha kevalaḥ? | kevalo 'pi kiṃ svakāryāt prāg, atha paścāt? | yadi svakāryasahitas tadu(do)bhayor anyata eva bhāvāt parasparam asambandha iti kāryasambandhitā 'sya hīyeta | atha
kevalaḥ svakāryāt prāk; tadā kṣaṇikatayā kāraṇasya tam[226]eva janayitvā dhvaṃsāt kathaṃ svakāryakriyā? | tasyāṃ cāsatyāṃ kathaṃ tadapekṣam[227]asya kāraṇatvam? | tasmiṃś cāsati katham akāraṇena kāryakāraṇasambandho janyate? | atha svakāryaṃ kṛtvā paścāj janyeta tadā 'pi svakāryakāle eva vinaṣṭatvād asatastaduttarakālabhāvikāryakāraṇabhāvajananaṃ kutaḥ? | tadbhāvaś[228]ca sambandha ucyate |
[S. 52a.
children.translated_text: like the determination 'bearer of a staff' — in the non-apprehension of the staff. And the relation of a separate entity with cause and effect is not tenable, since in imagining another relation [to connect them], infinite regress would follow. [If one resorts to] accepting causal relation: the non-co-existence of that [separate] entity with the cause and effect [at the same time]. And therefore, since at the time of cause and effect that [separate entity] is not proximate, how can it be the ground of the cognitions of cause and effect? {p. 48.1} And if one imagines the condition of that [entity] by interpolating [it between] the two that have ceased, the determination of causality would pertain only to an imagined object, not to a real object. And that [determination, as grounded in the presence and absence of a specific entity,] has already been accepted — so what is the point of imagining a separate entity? Since the determination [of causality] would have an imagined object — because of the pointlessness of that [imagined entity]; and because cause and effect are non-simultaneous. [S. 51b.] For that [entity] is not produced by those two [together], and if produced by each individually, how can it be the causal relation? And when it is produced by the cause, is it produced together with its own effect, or alone? And if alone, is it before its own effect, or after? If together with its own effect — then since those two [the relation and the effect] are entirely different, they are unrelated to each other, and thus its connection with the effect would be lost. Or if alone, before its own effect — then, since the cause is momentary, having produced that [relation] alone and then perishing, how can it perform its own effect-activity? And in the absence of that [effect-activity], how can its causality, which depends on that [activity], exist? And in its absence, how can the causal relation be produced by what is not a cause? Or if it is produced after having produced its own effect — even then, since [the cause] has perished at the very time of its own effect, how can a non-existent [cause] produce a causal relation belonging to a subsequent time? And that state [of dependence] is called a relation. [S. 52a.
and

S. 52b.] ............ [S. 53a.] Or, if production [is at issue] — if the complete [causes], by their very nature, produce that [effect], what obstruction of power is there among them with respect to the effect? Such that another [causal complex] is imagined. And there too, in requiring yet another causal complex, the absurd consequence of infinite regress [follows]. Therefore, the complete [causes] alone are the producers.
And their causality is inferred from the exclusion of the effect upon the removal of each one — thus he says —
'Even when the other' —
i.e., [the other causes] included within that causal complex;
'causes' —
i.e., producers, {p. 49.1} are present — because each one among them is a revealer;
'in the absence of this one' —
i.e., in the absence of the one intended to be determined as a producer;
'does not exist' —

children.text:
ity anenānupalambhasya viṣaya uktaḥ | pratyakṣavṛttis tu pūrvoktaivā 'nupalambharahitā tadbhāve bhāvagrāhiṇī saṃbandhyate |
 tathā cāyam api tadbhāve bhāvaḥ tadabhāve 'bhāvaś ca kāryakāraṇabhāvaḥ kiṃ sādhanaḥ? ity āha --
children.translated_text:
by this, the object of non-apprehension (<s>anupalambha</s>) has been stated. The operation of direct perception, however, is as previously described — devoid of non-apprehension, apprehending the presence [of the effect] in the presence [of the cause] — is connected [with the foregoing].
Thus, this too — the presence [of the effect] in the presence [of the cause] and the absence [of the effect] in the absence [of the cause] — constituting the causal relation: what establishes it? — he says —
'Established by direct perception and non-apprehension' (<s>pratyakṣānupalambha-sādhana</s>);

'non-apprehension preceded by direct perception' — i.e., having the nature of direct perception that grasps other objects distinguished from that [object], serving as the means of establishing it — thus
the causal relation is established by direct perception and non-apprehension.

children.text: | yas tv anupalambhasāpekṣeṇa [S. 53b.] pratyakṣeṇa sādhyata iti prāguktaḥ so 'nupalambhapūrvakaṃ pratyakṣaṃ sādhanam asyeti anupalambhapratyakṣasādhana iti vaktavyaḥ |
children.translated_text: However, that which is established by direct perception dependent upon non-apprehension — as stated earlier — should be called 'established by non-apprehension-preceded direct perception' (<s>anupalambha-pratyakṣa-sādhana</s>). [S. 53b.]
'Of that' (<s>tasya</s>) —
of the causal relation, which consists of positive and negative concomitance (<s>anvaya-vyatireka</s>);
'establishment' (<s>siddhi</s>) —
ascertainment;
'by the two as described' —

children.text:
pratyakṣānupalambhābhyāṃ kāryahetāv anvayaniścaya iti sambadhyate |
  nanu cānvayaniścayo nāma kāryahetoḥ sarvatra kāryasya bhavataḥ svakāraṇasattayā 'nugamanam
children.translated_text:
by direct perception and non-apprehension — the ascertainment of positive concomitance (<s>anvaya-niścaya</s>) regarding the effect-reason is connected [here].
But the ascertainment of positive concomitance means: the determination that wherever the effect-reason [exists], the effect exists [there too], by following [it] through the existence of its own cause —

children.text: ity evam avasāyaḥ tat[231]kathaṃ kāryakāraṇabhāvasiddhir evā 'sāv[232]ucyate? ity āśaṅkya kārya[T.239b.]kāraṇabhāvasiddhinibandhanatvād anvayaniścayasya kāraṇe kāryopacārād ananyopāyasādhyatāṃ darśayitum, darśanamātranibandhanaṃ ye tam icchanti tanmataniṣedhārtham asāv evam ukta iti darśayann āha --
children.translated_text: — such is the understanding. Then how is that itself called the establishment of the causal relation? — Anticipating this [objection], in order to show that because the ascertainment of positive concomitance is grounded in the establishment of the causal relation, and because the effect is figuratively attributed to the cause, [the causal relation] is not establishable by any other means; and in order to negate the view of those who hold that the ascertainment of positive concomitance is grounded in mere observation — he shows that it is stated thus, and says —
'Only in the causal relation indeed' (<s>kāryakāraṇabhāva eva hi</s>) —
only when the causal relation exists;
'indeed' (<s>hi</s>) —
because;
'of something else' (<s>arthāntarasya</s>) —

children.text: sādhyād vyatiriktasya, yas tv avyatiriktaḥ [S. 54a.] tasya viparyaye bādhakapramāṇavṛttyā tādātmyaniścayād evānvayaniścaya iti pūrvam uktam evety arthāntaragrahaṇam | tasyārthāntarasya
children.translated_text: of what is different from the probandum (<s>sādhya</s>); but for what is not different [from the probandum], the ascertainment of positive concomitance is from the ascertainment of identity (<s>tādātmya</s>) alone, through the operation of a defeating proof in the contrary case — as was stated earlier — [S. 54a.] hence the word 'something else' is used. Of that something else —
'thus it would be' (<s>evaṃ syāt</s>);

children.text:
| katham? | `yatra nāma kvacid dhūmaḥ tatrāvaśyam agniḥ' iti niyamena `agneḥ tatra bhāvaḥ' ity evaṃ rūpo 'nvayaniścayaḥ | yas tv akāryakāraṇabhāve 'pi rasasyārthāntarasya rūpeṇānvayaniścayaḥ
sa ekasāmagryadhīnatayā tasya[233]svakāraṇavyabhicāradvāraka evety adoṣaḥ |
  {p. 50.1} atha yadi nāma kāryam agner dhūmas tathāpi kim iti yatrāsau tatrāvaśyam agnir bhavati yataḥ kāryakāraṇabhāvasiddhinibandhano 'nvayaniścaya ucyata ity āha --
children.translated_text:
How? The ascertainment of positive concomitance of the form: 'wherever there is smoke, there necessarily is fire' — the ascertainment in the form 'fire exists there.' But the ascertainment of positive concomitance of taste (<s>rasa</s>), being a separate thing, with form (<s>rūpa</s>) — even in the absence of the causal relation — is mediated through the non-deviation from its own cause, due to dependence on a single causal complex, and hence is faultless.
{p. 50.1} Now, even if smoke is indeed the effect of fire, still, why does fire necessarily exist wherever smoke exists, such that the ascertainment of positive concomitance is said to be grounded in the establishment of the causal relation? — he says —
'Only in the existence of fire' (<s>agneḥ bhāve eva</s>) —
only in the presence [of fire];
'indeed' (<s>hi</s>) —
because;
'existence' (<s>bhāva</s>) —
the presence of smoke;
[is due to its] being an effect —

children.text: | tasmāt kāryakāraṇabhāve saty eva yathokto 'nvayaniścaya iti | yadi hi yatra dhūmas tatrāvaśyam agnir na syāt tadā 'gnim antareṇāpy asya bhāvād agnibhāva [S. 54b.] eva bhāvalakṣaṇaṃ kāryatvaṃ hīyeta |
children.translated_text: therefore, only when the causal relation exists does the ascertainment of positive concomitance as described [hold]. For if wherever there is smoke, fire were not necessarily present, then, since [smoke] would exist even without fire, the character of being an effect — [defined as] presence only in the presence of fire — [S. 54b.] would be lost.

body.translated_text: Having thus, in the case of the natural reason (<s>svabhāvahetu</s>), demonstrated the ascertainment of positive concomitance through the operation of the invalidating cognition establishing identity — [T. 236a.] [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>], now demonstrating [the same] in the case of the effect-reason (<s>kāryahetu</s>), says —

Section: 33. Statement of the means of positive concomitance ascertainment in non-apprehension.

children.translated_text: 'In non-apprehension too' (<s>anupalabdhāv api</s>) —

not only has the ascertainment of positive concomitance for the essential-nature and effect reasons been stated, but the ascertainment of positive concomitance for non-apprehension too is being stated. Of what form is it? — he says —

children.text: na kevalaṃ svabhāvakāryaheto(tvo)r anvayaniścaya uktaḥ kintv anupalabdhāv apy anvayaniścaya ucyate | kiṃ rūpo 'sau? ity āha --

children.translated_text: 'Of the convention of non-existence' (<s>asad-vyavahārasya</s>) —

children.text: sādhyadharmasya yogyatāyāś ca sādhyatvāt tadyogyatā 'sadvyavahāro 'bhipretaḥ, tasya, upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptasya yā
children.translated_text: [i.e.,] of the property of the probandum (<s>sādhya-dharma</s>); and since what is to be proved is eligibility (<s>yogyatā</s>), the intended [convention of] non-existence means the convention of non-existence of that [eligible entity]; of that which meets the criterion for being perceived (<s>upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāpta</s>), the
'non-apprehension' (<s>anupalabdhi</s>) —
which has the form of apprehension of something other than that;
'in that alone' (<s>tanmātre</s>) —
not requiring any other ground;
'operation' (<s>vṛtti</s>) —
the activity of the convention of non-existence; of that [convention],
'establishment' (<s>sādhana</s>) —

children.text: siddhiḥ anupalabdhāv anvayaniścayaḥ | kutaḥ punar asadvyahārasya tanmātre vṛttir bhavati? ity āha --
children.translated_text: accomplishment — [this is] the ascertainment of positive concomitance in non-apprehension. But why does the convention of non-existence operate in that alone? — he says —
'Because of the demonstration of the absence of any other ground' (<s>nimittāntarābhāvopadarśanāt</s>).

children.text:
iti | yadā hy asadvyavahārasya yathoktānupalabdhivyatiriktaṃ buddhivyapadeśārthakriyāvirahādikaṃ nimittaṃ na bhavatīti [S. 55a.] sādhyate tadā yathoktānupalabdhimātre 'sya vṛttiḥ siddhā bhavati | tathā(tayā)[234]cānupalabdhāv anvayaniścayaḥ | anyathā hi nimittāntarāpekṣāśaṅkāyāṃ
satyām api yathoktānupalabdhau nāvaśyam asadvyavahārasya bhāva iti kuto 'nvayaniścayaḥ syāt? | nimittāntarābhāvas tu vistaratovādanyāya ukta iti tata evāvadhāryaḥ |
 athavā sadvyavahārasya yannimittam upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptasya sattvam tad asadvyavahāranimittād anyatvāt nimittāntaraṃ tatrānupalabdher abhāva upadarśyate yena pramāṇena tad evam uktam, tena, sati vastuni tasyā [T. 240b.] asambhavaniścayād anupalabdhāv anvayaniścayaḥ | tac ca tadvyatirekacintāyāṃ darśayiṣyāmaḥ |
  {p. 51.1} tad evaṃ trayāṇām api hetūnāṃ tathāsvaṃ pramāṇenānvayaviniścaya uktaḥ | svabhāvahetau viparyaye bādhakapramāṇavṛttyā tādātmyasiddhinibandhanatvāt, kāryahetau pratyakṣānupalambhābhyāṃ kāryakāraṇabhāvasiddhinimittatvāt, [S. 55b.] anupalabdhau nimittāntarābhāvaprasādhakamāṇatastadabhāvasiddhihetutvāc ceti |
children.translated_text:
— thus. For when it is established that the convention of non-existence has no cause other than the aforementioned non-apprehension — distinct from cognitive designation, causal efficacy-absence, and the like — then the restriction of its [non-existence convention's] occurrence to the mere aforementioned non-apprehension is established. And thereby, the ascertainment of positive concomitance in non-apprehension [is achieved]. Otherwise, if the suspicion of dependence on another cause persists, then even when the aforementioned non-apprehension is present, the convention of non-existence would not necessarily occur — so how could there be ascertainment of positive concomitance?
But the absence of another cause has been stated in the elaborate discourse (<s>vādanyāya</s>) — so it should be ascertained from that.
Alternatively: the cause of the convention of existence — namely, the being (<s>sattva</s>) of that which has attained the defining characteristics of apprehension — since it is different from the cause of the convention of non-existence, it is shown to be another cause whose non-apprehension in that [context] constitutes absence — by whichever <s>pramāṇa</s> this has been stated. By that, from the ascertainment that [non-apprehension] is impossible when the entity exists, there is ascertainment of positive concomitance in non-apprehension. And this we shall demonstrate in the discussion of the negative concomitance of that.
Thus, the ascertainment of positive concomitance for all three types of reasons, each by its own <s>pramāṇa</s>, has been stated: in the essential-nature reason, because the establishment of identity (<s>tādātmya</s>) is grounded in the operation of a counterbalancing <s>pramāṇa</s> against the contrary; in the effect-reason, because it is grounded in the establishment of the cause-effect relation through perception and non-apprehension; and in non-apprehension, because it is grounded in the establishment of the absence of another cause through the <s>pramāṇa</s> that proves it.

body.translated_text: Now he states the ascertainment of positive concomitance in non-apprehension —
'then' (<s>tadā ca</s>) — T.
Section: 34. Stating the means of ascertaining negative concomitance for the effect and essential-nature reasons.

body.text: samprati trayāṇām api hetūnāṃ svasvapramāṇanibandhanaṃ vyatirekaniścayaṃ pratipādayitukāma āha --

children.translated_text: 'the ascertainment of negative concomitance too' —

children.text: na kevalam anvayaniścayo yathāsvaṃ pramāṇanibandhanas tayor uktaḥ api tu
children.translated_text: not only has the ascertainment of positive concomitance been stated as grounded in its respective <s>pramāṇa</s> for those two, but also —
'the ascertainment of negative concomitance too, for the effect and essential-nature reasons' —

children.text:
r yathāsvaṃ pramāṇanimitta ucyate |
  kaḥ punar asau?
children.translated_text:
is stated as having its respective <s>pramāṇa</s> as its cause.
What then is that [negative concomitance]?
'the establishment of absence in the absence of the <s>sādhya</s>' —

children.text: | yāv atadātmaka[tadātmakau hetū kāraṇavyāpakarūpasādhyasya sādhakau] sādhyābhāve cābhāvasiddhis tayoḥ | kena pramāṇena? |
children.translated_text: for those two reasons that are of such-and-such nature, which prove the <s>sādhya</s> having the form of cause-and-pervader — the establishment of [their] absence in the absence of the <s>sādhya</s>. By what <s>pramāṇa</s>?
'by the non-apprehension of the cause and of the pervader' —

children.text: | kāryahetau kāraṇānupalabdhyā sādhyābhāve 'bhāvaniścayaḥ | svabhāvahetau vyāpakānupalabdhyā | kadā punas te 'nupalabdhī sādhike tasya bhavataḥ? |
children.translated_text: in the effect-reason, by the non-apprehension of the cause, there is ascertainment of absence in the absence of the <s>sādhya</s>. In the essential-nature reason, by the non-apprehension of the pervader. But when do those two non-apprehensions become capable of proving that [absence]?
'when the relations of effect-cause and pervaded-pervader have been established' —

children.text: pratyakṣānupalambhābhyāṃ kāryakāraṇabhāvasiddhau satyāṃ kāraṇānupalabdhiḥ kāryahetau sādhyābhāve 'bhāvasya sādhikā, viparyaye ca bādhakapramāṇavṛttyā tadbhāvatāsiddhito | vyāpyavyāpakabhāvasiddhau satyāṃ [S. 56a.] [T. 241a.] vyāpakānupalabdhiḥ svabhāvahetau sādhyābhāve 'bhāvasya sādhiketi | tad evaṃ bruvatā ubhayatra tādātmyatadutpattilakṣaṇapratibandhaniścayād eva dvayor apy anvayavyatirekayoḥ niścaya iti uktaṃ bhavati | ata evānyatra --
children.translated_text:
when the cause-effect relation has been established through perception and non-apprehension, the non-apprehension of the cause proves the absence [of the effect-reason] in the absence of the <s>sādhya</s>, and [the identity relation is established] through the operation of a counterbalancing <s>pramāṇa</s> against the contrary, from the establishment of identity. When the pervaded-pervader relation has been established, the non-apprehension of the pervader proves the absence [of the essential-nature reason] in the absence of the <s>sādhya</s>.
Thus, by the speaker who states [all this], it is said that in both cases, the ascertainment of both positive and negative concomitance is from the ascertainment of the necessary connection (<s>pratibandha</s>) characterized by identity and causal origination. For this very reason, elsewhere —
'or from the relation of cause and effect' —
and so forth, has been stated. Of what kind [are these non-apprehensions]?
'having a visible object' (<s>dṛśyaviṣaya</s>) —

children.text: dṛśyo viṣayo yayos te tathokte | yadi kāraṇavyāpakāv upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptau bhavatas tadā tadanupalabdhī sādhyābhāve 'bhāvaṃ sādhyata iti yāvat | kadā punas tayoḥ dṛśyaviṣayatāviśeṣaṇam apekṣyate? ity āha --
children.translated_text: those whose object is visible — they are described as such. If the cause and the pervader have attained the defining characteristics of apprehension, then their non-apprehension proves the absence [of the reason] in the absence of the <s>sādhya</s> — this much [is meant]. But when is the qualification of 'having a visible object' required for those two? To this he says —
'of the one whose domain is specified' (<s>uddiṣṭaviṣayasya</s>) —

children.text: uddiṣṭaḥ -- kathito viṣayaḥ -- ādhāro vaidharmyadṛṣṭāntalakṣaṇo yasya sādhyābhāve 'bhāvasya tasyopadarśane kriyamāṇe | {p. 52.1} tatrāpi kasmād dṛśyaviṣayatā 'pekṣyate? iti cet āha --
children.translated_text: that whose domain — i.e., the substratum characterized as the dissimilar example (<s>vaidharmyadṛṣṭānta</s>) — has been specified, i.e., stated — when the demonstration of the absence [of the reason] in the absence of the <s>sādhya</s> for that is being carried out. Even there, why is the qualification of 'having a visible object' required? To this he says —
'non-apprehension' —
and so forth.
'otherwise' (<s>anyathā</s>) —

children.text: yadi dṛśyaviṣayatāviśeṣaṇam anupalabdhyor nāpekṣyate | yadā 'nupalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptaṃ [S. 56b.] viṣayaṃ vaidharmyadṛṣṭāntarūpam upādatte tadā 'nupalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptau tatra kāraṇavyāpakāv api bhavata iti
children.translated_text: if the qualification of 'having a visible object' is not required for the two non-apprehensions — when one takes as the domain in the form of the dissimilar example that which has attained the defining characteristics of apprehension, then even the cause and pervader in that [domain] have attained the defining characteristics of apprehension — and so —
'of that which has attained the defining characteristics of apprehension' (<s>upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptasya</s>) —
of the cause or of the pervader —
'somewhere' (<s>kvacit</s>) —
in a remote domain such as Mount <s>Sumeru</s> and the like —
'because the absence would not be established' —

children.text:
kathamābhyāṃ sādhyābhāve 'bhāvasiddhiḥ syāt, kāraṇavyāpakānupalabdhyor evāsiddhatvāt ity abhiprāyaḥ |
  athānuddiṣṭaviṣayasyāpy abhāvasyopadarśane 'nupalabdhyor daśyaviṣayatāviśeṣaṇaṃ kim iti nāpekṣyate? ity āha --
children.translated_text:
how could there be establishment of the absence [of the reason] in the absence of the <s>sādhya</s> through these two, since the non-apprehension of the cause and the non-apprehension of the pervader themselves would be unestablished? — this is the intent.
But why, when demonstrating the absence even for one whose domain is not specified, is the qualification of 'having a visible object' not required for the two non-apprehensions? To this he says —
'for one whose domain is not specified' (<s>anuddiṣṭaviṣayam</s>) —
that whose domain — in the form of the dissimilar example — is not specified in the declaration of the absence of the reason in the absence of the <s>sādhya</s> — for that,

children.text: anuddiṣṭo viṣayaḥ -- vaidharmyadṛṣṭāntarūpo yasmin sādhyābhāve hetvabhāvakhyāpane tat

children.translated_text: 'when merely the necessary connection (<s>pratibandha</s>) has been established' —
when this is the case, even without the qualification of 'having a visible object,' since —
'it is established' —
therefore —
'not there' —
for one whose domain is not specified —
in establishing negative concomitance —
'for the two non-apprehensions' —
'the qualification of having a visible object is required' —

children.text: aṅgīkriyate | [S. 57a.] tathā hi -- aśeṣapadārthaparigraheṇa sāmānyenāpi bruvato yo yatra pratibaddhasvabhāvaḥ tādātmyatadutpattibhyāṃ sa tadabhāve 'vaśyam eva na bhavatīti niḥsvabhāvatvā 'hetukatvaprasaṅgāt | taduktam -
children.translated_text: [i.e., it is not] accepted. For when speaking generally, encompassing all objects without exception — 'that which has a necessary nature connected to something, through identity or causal origination, necessarily does not exist in the absence of that' — because of the unwanted consequence of essencelessness and causelessness. As he has said —
'Even in the case of the essential nature, the invariable accompaniment follows mere existence;
in its absence, the absence of the self-existent would follow, because of non-difference.' ||
Similarly —
'Smoke is the effect of fire, because it follows the properties of an effect;
being such, even in [fire's] absence, it would violate the condition of having a cause.' ||

children.text:
iti |
tatas tatra dṛśyaviṣayatā'pekṣyamāṇānupakārikaiveti na tayā kiñcid iti bhāvaḥ |
children.translated_text:
— thus.
Therefore, the qualification of 'having a visible object' that is required there would be of no help at all — so nothing [is achieved] by it — this is the purport.
'when merely the necessary connection has been established' —

children.text: ity anena ye pratibandhaṃ hetor na varṇayanti kintv adarśanamātrād eva vyatirekam āhus teṣāṃ tadasambhavaṃ ca darśayati | tathā hi -- asati pratibandhe yadi sarve sādhyavirahiṇo 'rthā dṛśyā bhavanti tadā teṣv anupalabdhasya sādhanasyābhāvaḥ śiṣyet(ta) | tad āhakumārilo 'pi -- {p. 53.1}
children.translated_text: by this, he also shows the impossibility of [the view of] those who do not describe a necessary connection (<s>pratibandha</s>) for the reason but assert negative concomitance merely from non-observation. For if, in the absence of a necessary connection, all objects devoid of the <s>sādhya</s> were visible, then the absence of the <s>sādhana</s>, which has not been apprehended among them, would remain. Indeed, <s>Kumārila</s> too says —

children.text: gatvāgatvātu tān deśān yady artho nopalabhyate |
children.translated_text: 'If, having gone and returned to those places, the object is not apprehended,
then, from the absence of another cause, it is understood to be non-existent.' ||
<s>ŚV</s> <s>arthā</s>- 38

iti |
deśādiviprakarṣitayā[235]tv adṛśyatve saty api tatra[236][S. 57b.] hetāv anupalambhamātrasya sambhavāt sandigdho 'sāv 'śeṣe sādhyābhāve sādhanābhāvalakṣaṇo vyatirekaḥ tathāvidhasyaiva[237]yatra yatra sādhyābhāvaḥ [T. 242a.] tatra tatra sādhanābhāva iti vīpsāpadābhyām abhidhānāt | anvayaniścayo[238]'pi prāk pratibandhanibandhana eva varṇitaḥ tatas tenāpi[239]pareṣāṃ darśananibandhanām[240]anvayasiddhim icchatām abhāvo 'syāpi[241]kathita eva, sarvārthānāṃ hetumatāṃ sādhyadharmavattayā draṣṭum aśakyatvād anumātṛbhiḥ | aśeṣadeśādiviṣayasya ca sādhyānugamasya yatra yatra hetuḥ tatra tatra sādhyam iti vīpsayā pratipādanāt | na ca katipayadeśādau sādhanadharmasya sādhyadharmeṇa sahabhāvasya bhūyo darśane 'pi vyāptiḥ sidhyati, asati pratibandhe kvacid bahulaṃ tathādṛṣṭānām apy anyathā tv asyāpi sambhavāt, tadasambhave[242]bādhakapramāṇābhāvāt |
children.translated_text:
— thus.
But when invisibility obtains due to remoteness of place and so forth, since the mere non-apprehension of the reason is possible even there, that negative concomitance — characterized by the absence of the <s>sādhana</s> in every [instance of] absence of the <s>sādhya</s> — is doubtful, since it is stated by the reduplicative words (<s>vīpsāpada</s>) 'wherever there is absence of the <s>sādhya</s>, there is absence of the <s>sādhana</s>.' The ascertainment of positive concomitance too was previously described as grounded in the necessary connection alone; therefore, by that [argument] too, the absence of the positive concomitance that the opponents wish to ground in observation alone has been stated, since all objects that have causes cannot be observed as possessing the <s>sādhya</s>-property by the inferrer. And since the <s>sādhya</s>'s accompaniment [of the reason] across all places and the like is conveyed by the reduplicative expression 'wherever there is the reason, there is the <s>sādhya</s>.' And even when the co-occurrence of the proving property with the property to be proved is observed frequently in some places and the like, pervasion is not established, since in the absence of a necessary connection it is possible that [things] observed frequently in one way might be otherwise somewhere — and because there is no counterbalancing <s>pramāṇa</s> against such [possibility].

body.translated_text: Now, wishing to explain the ascertainment of negative concomitance for all three types of reasons, grounded in their respective <s>pramāṇas</s>, he says —

body.text:
nanu yo 'pi na dṛśyās teṣv adarśanam asti, ato 'darśanād eva sarvatra vyatirekaniścayaḥ ity āha
[236] sādhye
[237] aśeṣasādhyābhāve sādhanābhāvalakṣaṇasya
[238] dṛśye 'dṛśye ca
[239] pratibandhanibandhanenānvayena
[240] darśanamātrani- -- T.
[241] anvayasya
[242] anyathā tv -
body.translated_text:
[Objection:] Even among those that are not visible, non-observation exists; therefore, negative concomitance is ascertained everywhere merely from non-observation. To this he says:
[236] in the <s>sādhya</s>
[237] characterized by the absence of the <s>sādhana</s> in every absence of the <s>sādhya</s>
[238] whether visible or invisible
[239] by positive concomitance grounded in the necessary connection
[240] <s>darśanamātrani</s>- — T.
[241] of positive concomitance
[242] 'but otherwise' —
Section: 35. Stating the means of ascertaining negative concomitance in non-apprehension.

children.translated_text: 'the ascertainment of negative concomitance in non-apprehension' —

children.text: ucyata iti śeṣaḥ | [S. 58a.] kim ātmako 'sau? ity āha --
children.translated_text: is stated — this is to be supplied. What is its nature? To this he says —
'of that which has attained the defining characteristics of apprehension' (<s>upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptāt</s>) —
from that which has the other conditions of apprehension present —
'and having a visible nature' (<s>dṛśyasvabhāvāt</s>) —
'of an existing [thing]' (<s>sataḥ</s>) —
of an existing [thing] having the form of absence-of-the-<s>sādhya</s> —
'of the non-apprehension' (<s>anupalambhasya</s>) —

children.text: tadviviktopalambhātmano yo 'bhāvaḥ sato yadgrāhakaṃ pratyakṣaṃ tadbhāvalakṣaṇas tasya
children.translated_text: that whose nature is the apprehension of what is distinct from that [entity] — the absence of that existing [thing]; that which grasps it is perception, and having the nature of the existence of that [perception] — of that,
'the showing' (<s>darśanam</s>) —

children.text: darśyate -- pratyāyyate 'neneti darśanam upadarśakaṃ pramāṇaṃ tadātmako 'nupalabdhau vyatirekaniścayaḥ | taddhetutvāc ca tat pramāṇaṃ tathocyate[245]| yadi hi sannihitānyopalambhapratyayo dṛśyasvabhāvo bhāvo vidyamāno 'pi nopalabhyeta katham asau {p. 54.1} [T. 242b.] dṛśyasvabhāvaḥ syāt? | yo hi satsv anyeṣūpalambhapratyayeṣu san pratyakṣa eva bhavati sa eva dṛśyasvabhāva ākhyāyate | tasmāt tathāvidhe sannihite
children.translated_text: that by which it is shown, i.e., demonstrated — that is the demonstrating <s>pramāṇa</s>; the ascertainment of negative concomitance in non-apprehension has this nature. And because that [non-apprehension] is the reason for [the convention of absence], that <s>pramāṇa</s> is so called. For if an entity having a visible nature, existing, with the other conditions of apprehension present, were not apprehended, how could it have a visible nature? For that which, when the other conditions of apprehension are present, is itself directly perceptible — that alone is called 'having a visible nature.' Therefore, when such [conditions] are present,

children.text:
'vaśyaṃ pratyakṣavṛttyā[246]bhavitavyam, anyathā 'sya na kadācid
api pratyakṣatā syāt, viśeṣābhāvād iti | prayogaḥ -- yad yanmātranimittaṃ tat [S. 58b.] tasmin sati niyamena bhavati | tad yathā bījādisāmagrīmātranimitto 'ṅkuraḥ | yathoktopalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptatāmātranimittaṃ ca sati vastuni tathāvidhe pratyakṣam iti svabhāvahetuḥ | [ete]na pramāṇena svabhāvānupalabdhau sādhyābhāve 'bhāvalakṣaṇo vyatireko niścīyate | etac ca pramāṇam anvayaniścayasyāpi nimittam | anenaiva nimittāntare 'nupalabdher abhāvopadarśanāt | kāraṇavyāpakānupalabdhyos tu vakṣyamāṇayoḥ pratibandhadvayasiddhyupāya evānvayavyatirekaniścayanibandhanam | sa ca kāryasvabhāvahetvor upadarśita eveti pṛthag noktaḥ | tathā hi -- kāraṇavyāpakayor abhāvaḥ kāryavyāpyābhāvābhyām avaśyam anvitaḥ kāryavyāpyābhāvavyatireke ca tadbhāvalakṣaṇe 'vaśyaṃ[247]vyatiricyate[248]kāraṇavyāpakayor bhāvāt | anyathā kāryavyāpyayor ahetukatvaniḥsvabhāvatāprasaṅgād iti [S. 59a.] na kiñcit pṛthagabhidhāneneti |
children.translated_text:
there must necessarily be perception [of it], otherwise it would never be perceptible at all, since there would be no distinguishing [condition]. The formal argument: whatever has a certain totality of conditions as its sole cause necessarily occurs when that [totality] is present — for example, a sprout, whose sole cause is the totality of conditions such as seed and the like. And perception, when the entity exists, has the sole cause of the aforementioned attainment of the defining characteristics of apprehension — this is an essential-nature reason (<s>svabhāvahetu</s>). By this <s>pramāṇa</s>, the negative concomitance characterized by the absence [of the entity] in the absence of the <s>sādhya</s> is ascertained in the essential-nature non-apprehension. And this <s>pramāṇa</s> is also the cause of the ascertainment of positive concomitance, since by this very [pramāṇa] the absence [of another cause] is demonstrated in [the context of] non-apprehension of another cause.
As for the non-apprehension of the cause and the non-apprehension of the pervader — which will be discussed — the very means of establishing the twofold necessary connection is the ground of the ascertainment of positive and negative concomitance. And that has already been demonstrated for the effect and essential-nature reasons — so it is not stated separately. For the absence of the cause and the pervader is necessarily accompanied by the absence of the effect and the pervaded; and in the negative case — when the effect or pervaded exists — the cause and pervader necessarily exist [i.e., the negative concomitance holds]. Otherwise, there would be the unwanted consequence of the effect and pervaded being causeless and essenceless. Therefore, nothing [more needs to be] stated separately.

body.translated_text: Now, with reference to non-apprehension, he says —
'The attainment of the defining characteristics of apprehension' means the completeness of the other conditions of apprehension and the specific nature [of the entity].

-- [NB Pari- 2]
[244] anupalabdho (?) sādhyam asattvam
[245] ananyopāyasādhyatāṃ darśayitum
[246] -vaśyaṃ tathāvidhapra- -- T.
[247] sati
[248] kāraṇavyāpakābhāvo nivartate
body.translated_text:
— [<s>NB</s> <s>Pari</s>- 2]
[244] non-apprehended (?); the <s>sādhya</s> is non-existence
[245] to show that it is not achievable by any other means

[247] when [it] is present

Section: 36. The designation by name of the three types of reason.

children.translated_text: 'a property of the thesis-subject, pervaded by a portion of that, is the reason' —
has been explained. Now —
'it is threefold only' (<s>tridhaiva saḥ</s>) —
to explain this, he says —
'having this definition' (<s>etallakṣaṇaḥ</s>) —

children.text: `pakṣadharmaḥ san yas tadaṃśena vyāpto hetuḥ' ity etallakṣaṇaṃ yasya sa etallakṣaṇaḥ |
children.translated_text: that whose definition is this — 'the reason is that which, being a property of the thesis-subject, is pervaded by a portion of that' — [that which] has this definition is [called] 'having this definition.'
'Threefold alone is it' —
the explanation of 'it' (<s>saḥ</s>) is:
'the reason' (<s>hetu</s>) —
thus. The exposition of 'threefold alone' is:
'of exactly three kinds' —

children.text: ti | tān hetūn svena svena nāmnā kīrttayati --
children.translated_text: thus. He names those reasons by their respective names:
'Essential nature (<s>svabhāva</s>), effect (<s>kārya</s>), and non-apprehension (<s>anupalabdhi</s>)' —
thus.
The particle '<s>ca</s>'
serves to aggregate the [three] reason-hoods.
The word '<s>iti</s>'

children.text: śabdaḥ samāptiṃ sūcayann avadhāraṇārtham eva sphuṭayati |
children.translated_text: indicating completion, makes the restrictive sense (<s>avadhāraṇa</s>) explicit.
'For example — when impermanence' —
of some [thing] such as sound and the like,
'is the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum), [the reason] being-existent (<s>sattva</s>)' —
is an illustration of the essential-nature reason.
'At a location possessing fire' —
when [that is] the <s>sādhya</s>,
'smoke' —
is a demonstration of the effect-reason.
'And in [establishing] absence' —
and in the usage of absence,
'the non-apprehension of what fulfills the conditions of apprehension (<s>upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāpta</s>)' —
is the presentation of non-apprehension.

body.translated_text: Thus, by this much text —
Section: 37. Demonstrating by <s>pramāṇa</s> that [things
outside the threefold reason are pseudo-reasons]

body.text: kasmāt punaḥ trividha eva hetuḥ? ity āśaṅkya [S. 59b.] trividhahetuvyatiriktānām arthānāṃ hetvābhāsatayā hetuviruddhayā vyāptes triṣv eva hetutvaṃ niyataṃ bhavatīti hetvābhāsatāṃ pramāṇavatīṃ tadvyatirekiṇāṃ darśayann āha --

children.translated_text: 'In this alone' —
in the threefold reason designated as essential nature, effect, and non-apprehension,
'because of the restriction of invariable concomitance (<s>avinābhāva</s>)' —

children.text: trividhahetuvyatirikteśv artheṣv avinābhāvā 'bhāvād ity arthaḥ | tataś cāvinābhāvavikalatvāt svabhāvakāryānupalabdhivyatirekiṇo 'rthā hetvābhāsāḥ prameyatvādivat ity uktaṃ bhavati | avinābhāvābhāvaś ca trividhahetuvyatiriktatvād eva tādātmyatadutpattyor avinābhāvavyāpikayor abhāvād vyāpakānupalabdhito 'vagataḥ |
children.translated_text: meaning: because of the absence of invariable concomitance in things other than the threefold reason. Therefore, because of being deficient in invariable concomitance, things other than essential nature, effect, and non-apprehension are pseudo-reasons, like <s>prameyatva</s> (knowability) and the like — thus it has been stated. And the absence of invariable concomitance is understood from the non-apprehension of the pervader (<s>vyāpakānupalabdhi</s>) — because of the absence of <s>tādātmya</s> (identity) and <s>tadutpatti</s> (origination from that), which pervade invariable concomitance, precisely because [the pseudo-reasons] are other than the threefold reason.

body.translated_text: Anticipating [the question] 'Why is the reason exactly threefold?', and showing — with rational support — that things other than the threefold reason, being pervaded by the contradictory of reason-hood through their pseudo-reason-hood, have reason-hood restricted to the three alone, he says:
Section: 38. Analysis of invariable concomitance (<s>avinābhāva</s>)

body.text: atha ko 'yam avinābhāvaḥ? kasya cāsau? kathaṃ vā 'traiva niyata ucyate? ity ata āha --
body.translated_text: Now, what is this invariable concomitance? Whose is it? And how is it said to be restricted to this [threefold reason] alone? To this he says:
'The pervasion as stated' — of the pervader (<s>vyāpaka</s>) —

body.text: -- tatkāraṇatayā tadbhāvatayā ca | yatra tadvyāpyaṃ kāryaṃ svabhāvo vā sannihitas tatra bhāva eva |
body.translated_text: by virtue of being its cause or by virtue of being its nature. Wherever the pervaded — an effect or an essential nature — is present, there [the pervader] necessarily exists.
'Or of the pervaded' —

body.text: -- kāryasya svabhāvasya vā | yatra tatkāraṇasvabhāvākhyaṃ vyāpakaṃ sannihitaṃ tatraiva dharmiṇi na tadabhāve 'pi bhāva iti yā vyāpakavyāpyadharmatayā vyāptir uktā sā
body.translated_text: i.e., of an effect or an essential nature. Wherever the pervader — called 'cause' or 'essential nature' — is present, in that very <s>dharmin</s>, [the pervaded] does not exist even in its absence. The pervasion stated thus, by virtue of the pervader-pervaded relation —
'the pervasion as stated is the invariable concomitance.'
Whose? —
'Of the property of the thesis-subject' (<s>pakṣadharma</s>) —
i.e., the property of the <s>sādhyadharmin</s> (property-locus of the probandum).
'That' —
invariable concomitance of such a form,
'from the threefold' —
from the reason as stated,
'elsewhere' —
in things other than it,
'does not exist.'

body.text: | yato 'tra ca tṛ(tri)vidhe 'sti, tādātmyatadutpattyor avinābhāvena vyāptayor bhāvāt, kṛtakatvānityatvavadanayor vyāpyavyāpakabhāvād iti,
body.translated_text: Since it does exist in this threefold [reason] — because <s>tādātmya</s> and <s>tadutpatti</s>, being pervaded by invariable concomitance, are present, [as in] the pervader-pervaded relation between being-produced (<s>kṛtakatva</s>) and impermanence (<s>anityatva</s>) — therefore,
'therefore in this alone' —
in the threefold reason, by way of its absence elsewhere,
'it is restricted' —
it is said. By this,
'pseudo-reasons' —
'are other than that' —
the meaning of this,
'because of the restriction of invariable concomitance' —

body.text:
ity upapattisahitasyārthāḥ
pradarśitaḥ | yathā ca trividhād hetor anyatrāvinābhāvo nāsti tathā prāg evoktam |
  {p. 56.1} yadi v[h12]ā svabhāvād anyo 'rtho 'rthāntaram,
body.translated_text: together with its justification, has been demonstrated. And how invariable concomitance does not exist elsewhere than the threefold reason has already been stated previously. Or alternatively, an entity other than essential nature is something different (<s>arthāntara</s>);

body.text: tac ca[249]kāryād apy anyat -- kāraṇam anubhayaṃ [T. 244a.] vā | anupalabdher apy anyad yathoktāyāḥ -- anupalabdhimātram upalabdhir vā pratiṣedhyasya tadanyasyāpi viruddhasyāviruddhasya vā | tatrārthāntaram yady anantarakāryaṃ[250]tasyārvādgarśibhiḥ itaravivekena lakṣayitum aśakyatvāt aliṅgatvam | kāryadarśanāt [S. 60b.] vivekāvasāye 'pi sādhyasiddhyuttarakālabhāvī pakṣadharmatāvasāyo 'nvayānugamanaṃ ca vyarthaṃ | vyavahitakāryam api kāraṇaṃ na kāryasya liṅgam, antarālapratibandhavaikalyasambhavena vyabhicārāt | taduktam |
body.translated_text: and that [something different] is also other than effect — it is a cause, or something that is neither [cause nor effect]. And what is other than non-apprehension as stated — mere non-apprehension, or apprehension of what is to be negated, or also of what is other than it, whether contradictory or non-contradictory. Therein, if something different [were used as a reason and] its immediate effect, because it cannot be characterized in distinction from the other by those whose vision extends back [only to the proximate], it has the status of non-mark (<s>aliṅga</s>). Even if distinction [from the cause] is determined from seeing the effect, the determination of the property of the thesis-subject and the ascertainment of positive concomitance — being subsequent to the establishment of the <s>sādhya</s> — would be pointless. A cause that has a distant effect is also not a mark of the effect, because of deviation (<s>vyabhicāra</s>) due to the possibility of deficiency in the intervening causal restriction. As stated:
'Because of the possibility of restriction [being broken] in the effect that follows the connection of the aggregate's result and powers,'
there is inconclusiveness (<s>anaikāntika</s>) [in such a reason]. ||
PV 3.7

body.text:
iti | yogyatānumāne tu nārthāntaraṃ liṅgam |
  nāpy anubhayam, apratibandhena gamakatvāyogāt | kathaṃ kṛttikodayavijñānād rohiṇyāsattiklṛptiḥ? iti cet | nanu' sā 'pi naivāsati pratibandhe yuktā viśeṣābhāvena sarvataḥ sarvapratītiprasaṅgāt ity uktatvāt | tasmān nakṣatracakrasya saṅkrāntihetur eva kālavyavadhānena kaścit kalpayitavyaḥ, yathā bhūtasaṃakṣobhaḥ paścātkālabhāvino varṣasyeti hetudharmānumānena kāryaliṅgajaiva kalpayitavyā |
 anupalabdhimātram api sāmśayahetuḥ, [S. 61a.] [T. 244b.] pramāṇanivṛttāv apy arthābhāvāsiddheḥ | upalabdhir api pratiṣedhyasya katham abhāvaṃ sādhayet?, abhrāntopalambhasyābhāvāyogāt | viruddhopalabdhis tu pratiyogyabhāvaṃ sādhayati | kintu sa virodhas tadbhāve saty anyānupalambhād eva siddha iti taddvāreṇānupalabdhir eva prayuktā bhavati | anyathā 'niṣiddhopalabdher abhāvāsiddheḥ | aviruddhopalabdhiḥ punaḥ pratiṣedhe 'naikāntikī, sahabhāvasambhavād aviruddhānām | na cāparaḥ prakāraḥ sambhavatīti nāvinābhāvo 'nyatra vidyata iti |
{p. 57.1}
body.translated_text: Thus. And in capability-inference (<s>yogyatānumāna</s>), something different is not a mark. Nor is something that is neither [cause nor effect a valid mark], because without restriction (<s>pratibandha</s>) it cannot serve as an indicator. 'How then is the cognition of the proximity of <s>Rohiṇī</s> from the knowledge of the rising of <s>Kṛttikā</s>?' — if [one asks] thus: 'That too is not justified without restriction, because in the absence of a distinguishing feature, there would be the consequence of everything being cognized from everything' — since this has been stated. Therefore, some cause of the revolution of the star-circle, with a temporal interval, must be postulated — just as the agitation of the elements is [the cause] of future rain — [and] the inference of the cause-property should be construed as having a mark that is an effect. Mere non-apprehension too is a reason that produces doubt, because even when a means of valid cognition ceases, the absence of the object is not established. And how could apprehension of what is to be negated establish absence? — because the impossibility of non-erroneous apprehension [co-existing with] absence. Apprehension of something contradictory does establish the absence of the counter-positive. However, that contradiction, being established only from the non-apprehension of the other when the former is present, means that non-apprehension itself is what is really employed, through that [contradiction] as a medium. Otherwise, since absence is not established from non-prohibited apprehension. And the apprehension of something non-contradictory is inconclusive with respect to negation, because of the possibility of coexistence of non-contradictory [things]. And no other mode is possible — therefore invariable concomitance does not exist elsewhere.
2. Analysis of the Essential-Nature Reason
Section: 1. Stating the definition of the essential-nature reason

body.text:
kāryahetor api yad anyad abhyupagamyate tad api tac ca ...........'rthāntaram evety arthaḥ
[250] anantaraṃ kāryaṃ yasmāt kāraṇāt
[251] sāmagryāḥ phalaṃ ca tāḥ śaktayaś ca
body.translated_text:
whatever other thing is admitted beyond the effect-reason, that too is ... something different — this is the meaning
[250] the immediate effect from which cause
[251] the result of the aggregate, and its powers

children.translated_text: 'Therein' —

children.text: hetutraye svabhāvahetos tāval lakṣaṇam ucyate | sādhyate yena tat sādhanam | tac cāsau dharmaś ca tasya bhāvas tadbhāvaḥ | sa eva
children.translated_text: in the triad of reasons, the definition of the essential-nature reason is first stated. That by which [something] is proved is the means of proof (<s>sādhana</s>). And that is also a property (<s>dharma</s>); its existence (<s>bhāva</s>) is the 'existence of the proving property' (<s>tadbhāva</s>). That itself is
'the mere existence of the proving property' (<s>sādhanadharmabhāvamātra</s>).
Its
'invariable accompaniment' (<s>anvaya</s>).
That in which this [invariable accompaniment] is present — in the property to be proved (<s>sādhyadharma</s>), by the metaphorical transfer of the aggregate to a part —
'the essential-nature reason' (<s>svabhāvo hetuḥ</s>).

children.text: | sādhyadharmasya śrutatvāt tasyaiva svabhāva iti gamyate | kathaṃ punar asau sādhyadharmasvabhāvo? yāvatā bhedena pratīyata ity ata
children.translated_text: Since the property to be proved has been mentioned, it is understood that [the essential nature is] of that very [property]. But how is it the essential nature of the property to be proved? Since it is cognized as different [from it] — to this,
he says:
'From the other' —
'and from the other' —
from what is non-existent (<s>asat</s>) and from what is non-momentary (<s>akṣaṇika</s>) — that which is
'the exclusion' (<s>vyāvṛtti</s>) —
of that, the
'difference' —
constructed through the difference in delimitations (<s>avadhi</s>), by which — the reason-entity —
of the proving property from the property to be proved,
the
'difference' —
even when that obtains,
even when that exists,
'in reality' —
in the ultimate sense,
