children.text:
iti? | evaṃ manyate -- vyatiriktāv api kṛtakatvānityatvākhyau dharmāv abhyupagacchadbhir avaśyam `abhūtvā bhavanaṃ bhūtvā cābhavanam anavasthāyisvabhāvatvam' abhyupagantavyam, [S. 63a.] anyathā ''tmādiṣv api kṛtakatvānityatve viśeṣābhāvād bhavetām | tato yad eva `abhūtvā bhavanaṃ bhūtvā[ 'bhavanaṃ] cānavasthāyitvam' upādīyate bhāvasya tayor eva taddarśanabalotpannakṛtakatvānityatvabhedāvabhāsikalpanādvāreṇa sādhyasādhanabhāvo 'stu, kiṃ vyatiriktadharmakalpanayā? | [T. 246a.] kalpayitvā 'pi vastv ātmana evārthakriyānibandhanatayā tadarthibhiḥ cintyatvāt | taduktam --
{p. 59.1}
children.translated_text: It is considered thus: even by those who accept the properties called being-produced and impermanence as distinct, it must necessarily be accepted that 'coming into being after not having existed, and ceasing to be after having existed, is the nature of being unstable' — otherwise, being-produced and impermanence would also belong to things held to be permanent, such as the self (<s>ātman</s>) and the like, because of the absence of a distinguishing feature. Therefore, let the very nature of 'coming into being after non-existence and instability after existence,' which is adopted as belonging to the entity, be the basis for the <s>sādhya</s>-<s>sādhana</s> relation through the door of constructing the appearance of the distinction of being-produced and impermanence that is born from seeing that [nature] — what need is there for postulating distinct properties? Even after postulating, since the entity itself is what is considered by those who desire its causal efficacy, because it is the ground of causal efficacy. As stated:
'By those who do not deny word-referents, through the division into existent and non-existent positions,
it is precisely the real entity that is investigated here,
whose arising of result is restricted. ||

body.translated_text: Accordingly,
Of what use to those who desire its [causal efficacy] are the elaborations of something incapable of causal efficacy?
What is the use of examining the beauty or ugliness of a eunuch (<s>ṣaṇḍha</s>) for a woman desiring a lover?' ||

body.text:
iti | tasmād dṛṣṭā api bhāvāḥ kenacid[254]ātmanā tadanyavyāvṛttena kathañcin niścitāḥ tadanyenāpy[255]atadrūpavyāvṛttenātmanā[256]bhrāntikāraṇasadbhāvād[257]aniścīyamānāḥ,[258]niścitāniścitayo[259]rūpayoḥ pramāṇāntarataḥ pratibandhāvasāyapurovarttino[260]'numānato niścīya(yaṃ)ta iti anityatāsvabhāvabhūtasyaiva kṛtakatvasya vināśaṃ prati liṅgatā yuktā | tathā ca vināśasvabhāva eva kṛtakatvākhyo hetuḥ tair athoktanyāyādiṣṭo bhavati | tasyā[261]'tanmātrānvayitve 'rthāntaranimittatayā viśeṣaṇenātatsvabhāvatā [S. 63a.] kathyate |
  syānmatam -- kṛtakatvena sākṣād hetumān vināśo 'numīyate tataḥ prāk pradhvaṃsābhāvaviśeṣaṇā sattā tatsamavāyo vā 'nityatā vyavasthāpyate | ata evātmādiṣv anityatāprasaṅgābhāvaḥ | vināśa iti ca bhāvābhāvaṃ pradhvaṃsalakṣaṇaṃ manyāmahe | kṛtakatvaṃ tu svakāraṇasattāsamavāyam | tasya[262]viśeṣaṇena vināśo 'sva(śāsva)bhāvatākhyāpane[263]na kiñcid aniṣṭam iti |
 tad ayuktam, tathāvidhasya[264]vināśasya hetumattāvirodhāt, svayam eva caitad ācāryo [T. 246b.] vakṣyati | na ca tenānumitena kiñcit, tasyārthakriyāsāmarthyavikalatvāt | sukhaduḥkhasādhane jñātvā yathārhaṃ pratipitsavo hi kiñcit[265]parīkṣante na vyasanitayā | tasmād anenāsthirasvabhāvataiva bhāvasyānumātavyā | saiva ca hetumatī {p. 60.1} kalpanīyā | anyathā bhāvavilakṣaṇasya[266]pradhvaṃsābhāvasya mudgarāder udaye 'pi tasya bhāve 'nupayogāt sa bhavas tadavastha [S. 64a.] eveti kathaṃ tadviśeṣaṇā sattā tatsamavāyo vā anityatā syāt? | avicalitarūpasya ca bhāvasya mudgarādikṛtapradhvaṃsābhāvaviśeṣaṇau sattāsamavāyau yady anityatā, kiṃ nātmāder api? iti prasaṅgaḥ tadavastha eva | svakāraṇasamavāyo 'pi cābhūtvā bhavanam anicchato na sidhyati | abhūtvā bhavata eva ca yā sattā saiva kṛtakatvaṃ varṇyate | na ca sattāsamavāyayor nityatayopagatayor niratiśayatvāt prāk pradhvaṃsābhāvau viśeṣaṇaṃ yujyate | abhūtvā
bhavanopagame ca tad eva kṛtakatvam asthirasvabhāvatā ca vināśo 'stu | kiṃ niṣphalayā apramāṇikayā pramāṇabādhitayā 'rthāntarakalpanayā? | evaṃ kṛtakatvavināśayos tādātmyopagamo 'vaśyam bhāvī pareṣām api | tato vināśasyāsthāyitvalakṣaṇasyārthāntaranimittatopagame kṛtakatvasyātatsvabhāvatā viśeṣaṇena khyāpyate | tanniṣpattāv aniṣpannasya bhinnahetukasya ca tatsvabhāvatvāyogāt |
  tathā, tasmin sādhye [S. 64b.] kṛtakatvasya vyabhicāraḥ | tathā hi -- ye yatra hetva[T. 247a.]ntarāpekṣiṇo na te tatrāvaśyam bhāvinaḥ, yathā vāsasi rāgaḥ | hetvantarāpekṣī ca kṛtakeṣv api bhāveṣu pradhvaṃsābhāva iti viruddhavyāptopalabdhiḥ |
 nanu vāsasi rāgasya parimitahetutvāt tasya ca svakāraṇāyattasannidhānatvāt tadāśrayasya ca vidhurapratyayopanipātenāsthiratayā nāvaśyam bhāvitā yuktaiva | na punar vināśasya, taddhetūnām ānantyād avaśyaṃ kasyacid ghaṭādiṣu sannidheḥ | na ca vināśasyāśrayaṃ prāk taddhetusannidheḥ kecid upaghnanti, yatas tadabhāvād vināśo nārabhyeteti |
body.translated_text:
Therefore, even entities that have been perceived — [though] ascertained in some way by a certain aspect (<s>ātman</s>) that is excluded from what is other than it — being unascertained with respect to yet another aspect excluded from what is not of that form, due to the existence of causes of error — the two aspects, ascertained and unascertained, are ascertained through inference, which is preceded by the determination of the causal constraint (<s>pratibandha</s>) from another <s>pramāṇa</s>. Thus the logical-mark status of produced-ness (<s>kṛtakatva</s>) — which is itself of the nature of impermanence — with respect to destruction is tenable. And accordingly, the reason called 'produced-ness,' which is of the very nature of destruction, is indicated by the <s>Ācārya</s> [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>] through the principles stated above. When it is [objected that the reason] does not have concomitance exclusively with that [destruction], it is stated through a qualifier that it is not of that nature, due to depending on another cause [S. 63a.].
One might think: destruction is directly inferred as having a cause through produced-ness; then impermanence — [defined as] existence qualified by subsequent annihilatory absence (<s>pradhvaṃsābhāva</s>), or the inherence (<s>samavāya</s>) of that [absence] in existence — is established [only] after that. Hence there is no unwanted consequence of impermanence for the <s>ātman</s> and the like. And by 'destruction' we mean the annihilatory absence of an entity, characterized as <s>pradhvaṃsa</s>. And 'produced-ness' [means] the inherence of one's own cause in existence. [So] there is nothing undesirable in declaring, through a qualifier, the non-identity of that [produced-ness] with destruction.
That is incorrect, because destruction of such a nature [i.e., caused destruction] is not incompatible with having a cause — and the <s>Ācārya</s> himself [T. 246b.] will state this. Nor does anything [useful follow] from that [destruction] being inferred [as caused], since it lacks the capacity for causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyāsāmarthya</s>). For people examine something having known [it to be] a means to happiness or suffering, [being] desirous of attaining [the appropriate response] — not out of idle curiosity. Therefore, by this [reason of produced-ness], what should be inferred is the very instability of nature (<s>asthirasvabhāvatā</s>) of the entity. And that alone should be posited as having a cause. Otherwise — since <s>pradhvaṃsābhāva</s>, being entirely unlike the [positive] entity, [means that] even upon the arising of a hammer-blow and the like, that entity [S. 64a.] remains in the same state [prior to the supposed destruction] since [the absence] is of no use to it — how could existence qualified by that, or the inherence in that, be impermanence? And if impermanence consists in the existence and inherence of an entity — [whose] form remains unchanged — being qualified by <s>pradhvaṃsābhāva</s> caused by hammer-blows and the like, then why not also for the <s>ātman</s> and the like? — the unwanted consequence remains exactly the same. Moreover, the inherence of one's own cause is not established for one who does not accept coming-into-being-after-not-having-been (<s>abhūtvā bhavana</s>). And the very existence (<s>sattā</s>) that belongs to what comes-into-being-after-not-having-been is itself described as produced-ness. And since existence and inherence, being accepted as eternal, are without degrees, the qualification by prior and annihilatory absence is not tenable. And if coming-into-being-after-not-having-been is accepted, then let that very produced-ness and the instability of nature be [what is meant by] destruction. What is the use of a fruitless, unwarranted, and pramāṇa-contradicted construction of something different? Thus, even for the opponents, the acceptance of identity between produced-ness and destruction is inevitable. Therefore, when destruction — characterized as non-persistence — is accepted as depending on another cause, the non-identity of produced-ness [with destruction] is declared through a qualifier — because what has not yet come about, and what has a different cause, cannot be of that nature.
Furthermore, there is deviation (<s>vyabhicāra</s>) of produced-ness with respect to that <s>sādhya</s> [S. 64b.]. For those [reasons] which depend on another cause at a certain place do not necessarily occur there — like [T. 247a.] the color in a garment. And <s>pradhvaṃsābhāva</s>, even among produced entities, depends on another cause — thus there is the apprehension of pervasion by the contradictory (<s>viruddhavyāptopalabdhi</s>).
But [one might object:] since the color in a garment has limited causes, and since those [causes] have their proximity dependent on their own causes, and since the substratum of that [color] is unstable due to the occurrence of destructive factors — its not necessarily occurring is indeed reasonable. But not so for destruction, since its causes are infinite, [so] some [cause] is necessarily present in pots and the like. Nor does anyone destroy the substratum [of the entity] prior to the proximity of the cause of destruction, such that destruction would not begin due to its absence.

children.translated_text: 'Just as in pots and the like, causes that effect destruction are observed,

body.translated_text: That is incorrect, because even though there are many causes of destruction, nevertheless, since their proximity depends on their own causes, and since even among those causes that are proximate, there are also infinite obstructing [factors], and since the power [of the destructive cause] is obstructed by those [obstructors] when they exist — causes do not necessarily bear fruit. Thus someone might not be destroyed — and so the deviation is not averted. But [one might ask:] if this color in a garment, even though dependent [on other causes], were observed everywhere — would it not then be necessarily occurring? It would, if it were so observed. But it is also observed otherwise. If so, then one should not trouble one's mind with the suspicion that destruction, which is observed everywhere, might be otherwise. Or is your honor an omniscient light of knowledge pervading the entire extent of all things, that you speak thus? Or if [destruction] is thus [i.e., universal], how would the operation of inference, [even] regarding what is observed, not become futile? [T. 247b.] Moreover, even when one has observed the destruction of some [thing] caused by [a specific] cause, since things born of causes are also observed [to behave] otherwise — the suspicion having arisen, how could one ascertain such a state [of necessary destruction] regarding things remote in place, time, and nature? Furthermore, this entity constantly undergoes destruction characterized by the absence of the entity — for if the destruction of that [destruction] were accepted, the entity would resurface — which is absurd. Nor is any cause of the destruction of that [destruction] observed, unlike [the observable causes of destruction] for pots and the like. As stated —

children.translated_text: not so for destruction itself — that'
'cause of that [destruction]'
'how could it arise?' ||

iti | tataḥ kṛtakatvasya vināśe sādhye tenaiva vyabhicāraḥ kiṃ neṣyate? |
  bhāvānām ayam aikāntika eva dharma iti cet, kutaḥ punar etad vasitam? | teṣām anyathābhāvasyānupalambhād iti [S. 65b.] cet | nanv ayam anupalambho bhavann apy ātmāder anivarttakaḥ sattāyāḥ, katham anyatrānyathābhāvaṃ nivarttayati? |[272]tasyānumānenopalambhād iti yady ucyate tadā tatrāpy[273]anumāne vipakṣe vṛttim anupalambha[274]eva hetoḥ kathaṃ nivarttayati? iti yat kiñcid etat | tasmāt sādhūktam -- `hetumati vināśe kṛtakatvasyāsvabhāvatāṃ vyabhicāraṃ cāha' iti alam atijalpiteneti |
body.translated_text:
Therefore, why is it not accepted that produced-ness itself deviates (<s>vyabhicāra</s>) when destruction is the <s>sādhya</s>?
If [you say:] this is an invariable property of entities — then on what basis is this established? If [you say:] because no alternative state is observed for them [S. 65b.] — but this non-observation, even when it exists, does not remove the existence of the <s>ātman</s> and the like — so how does it remove the alternative state for other things? If it is said: because that [non-existence of the <s>ātman</s>] is observed through inference — then how does non-observation alone remove the occurrence of the reason in the counter-instance, even in that inference [proving the <s>ātman</s>'s non-existence]? All of this amounts to nothing. Therefore it is well said: 'He states the non-identity and the deviation of produced-ness when destruction is [regarded as] having a cause.' Enough of this excessive argumentation.

body.text: idānīṃ yady api svārthānumānaṃ prakṛtaṃ tathāpi kaścit prayogadarśanābhyāsāt prayogabhaṅgyaiva pratipadyata iti svārthānumāne 'pi {p. 62.1} tatsambhavāt[275]prasaṅgena

children.translated_text: in order to teach inference-for-others (<s>parārthānumāna</s>) as well, he says —
'Of that' (<s>tasya</s>)
— of the natural reason (<s>svabhāvahetu</s>) —
'in two ways' (<s>dvidhā</s>)
— the verbal example (<s>vacanodāhāra</s>) [T. 248a.] that demonstrates the triple characterization is
'the formulation' (<s>prayogaḥ</s>).

children.text: | tam eva darśayati -- samāno dharmo yasya tasya bhāvaḥ tena
children.translated_text: He shows that very [twofold formulation]: that which has a similar property — its state [expressed] by that is
'one [formulation] through similarity' (<s>sādharmyeṇa ekaḥ</s>)
— a formulation.
'The other' (<s>aparaḥ</s>)

children.text: visadṛśo dharmo yasya tasya bhāvaḥ tena
children.translated_text: — that which has a dissimilar property — its state [expressed] by that is
'through dissimilarity' (<s>vaidharmyeṇa</s>).
He states an example for each of these in order:
'For instance: whatever exists' (<s>yathā yat sat</s>)
— the word 'whatever' (<s>yat</s>), with the distributive force of repetition (<s>vīpsā</s>), is primary.
'all of that' (<s>tat sarvam</s>)

children.text: iti tacchabdo 'pi vīpsāpradhāna eva | atra sarvagrahaṇena cāśeṣaparigrahād [S. 66a.] bahirvyāpter nirāsaḥ |
children.translated_text: — the word 'that' (<s>tat</s>) too has the distributive force as primary. And here, by the word 'all' (<s>sarva</s>), through the exhaustive inclusion [of all instances], [S. 66a.] the exclusion of external pervasion (<s>bahirvyāpti</s>) is accomplished.
'such as pots and the like' (<s>yathā ghaṭādayaḥ</s>)

children.text: iti | yasya sattvakṣaṇikatvayoḥ pratibandhaprasādhakaṃ pramāṇaṃ ghaṭādau pravṛttaṃ taṃ prati tatra smṛtisamādhānārthaṃ dṛṣṭāntavacanaṃ na sādhyasiddhyartham | dṛṣṭāntamātrataḥ sādhyasiddher abhāvāt | na hy ekasya tathā bhāve sarvas tathā bhavati, atiprasaṅgāt |
children.translated_text: — for one in whom the <s>pramāṇa</s> that establishes the causal constraint between existence and momentariness has operated with respect to pots and the like, the statement of the example is for the purpose of consolidating memory regarding that [constraint], not for establishing the <s>sādhya</s>. Because the <s>sādhya</s> is not established merely from an example. For it is not the case that because one thing is so, everything is so — since that would lead to an absurd over-extension.
'And the word "and"' (<s>saṃś ca śabdaḥ</s>)

— is for the inclusion of the property of the thesis-subject (<s>pakṣadharmopasaṃhāra</s>).
The example of the <s>vaidharmya</s> formulation —
'Likewise' (<s>tathā</s>)

children.text: ityādi | tathāśabdaḥ samuccaye | vaidharmyeṇa ca prayoga udāhriyate | atrāpi sarvagrahaṇaṃ vibhaktivipariṇāmena sambandhanīyam
children.translated_text: and so forth. The word 'likewise' is for conjunction (<s>samuccaya</s>). And a formulation through dissimilarity is being exemplified. Here too, the word 'all' (<s>sarva</s>) should be connected with a change of case-ending:
'in the absence of momentariness' (<s>kṣaṇikatvābhāve</s>)
'in all [cases]' (<s>sarvasmin</s>)
'there is absence of existence' (<s>sattvābhāvaḥ</s>).

children.text:
iti |
  prayogadvaye 'pi sarvagrahaṇasya phalaṃ darśayann āha --
children.translated_text: Showing the result of the word 'all' in both formulations, he says —
'in every [locus] possessing the proving property' (<s>sarvasmin sādhanadharmavati</s>)
— in the property-bearer, not merely in the example-subject (<s>dṛṣṭāntadharmin</s>) —
'of the provable property' (<s>sādhyadharmasya</s>)
'the inclusion' (<s>upasaṃhāraṇam</s>)
— i.e., the bringing together (<s>upasaṃhāra</s>),
the conveying (<s>ḍhaukana</s>). By that, which is
'pervasion' (<s>vyāptiḥ</s>)

children.text: `vyāpakasya tatra bhāva eva' ityādi rūpā tasyāḥ pradarśanaṃ pratipādanaṃ tad eva
children.translated_text: — of the form 'the pervader necessarily exists therein' and so forth — [the word] 'all' [serves for] the demonstration, i.e., the establishing, of that [pervasion]. That itself is
'the defining characteristic' (<s>lakṣaṇam</s>)

children.text:
yayoḥ tau tathoktau | tataś ca ye [T. 248b.] [S. 66b.] sādhyadharmiṇaṃ parihṛtya bahirvyāptiṃ pradarśayanti te -- yady api dṛṣṭāntadharmiṇi sādhyadharmeṇa sādhanadharmo vyāptaḥ tāvatā 'sya sarvatra tathābhāvābhāvāt sādhyasiddhir ayukteti -- nirastā bhavanti | sarvatra vā sādhyadharmeṇa sādhanadharmasya vyāptiḥ tadbhāve, sā tathāvidhaiva kin na pradarśyate yenāsamarthā bahirvyāptir ākhyāyate? | na hi `sa śyāmaḥ, tatputratvāt, paridṛśyamānaputravad' iti tatputratvasya {p. 63.1} śyamatvena sādhyād bahiḥ paridṛśyamānaputre vyāptipradarśane 'pi sādhyasiddhir bhavati
| tasmād yaiva sarvopasaṃhāreṇa vyāptiḥ pramāṇasiddhapratibandhanibandhanā sādhyasiddhau samarthā saiva tatsmṛtaye[278]pradarśanīyā | na ca sarvopasaṃhāreṇa vyāptipradarśane 'pi dharmaviśiṣṭo dharmy api tadaiva pratīyate, yataḥ pakṣadharmopadarśanottarakālabhāvino 'numānasya smṛtitvaṃ [S. 67a.] syāt | tasyāḥ[279]sādhyadharmiṇi sādhyadharmāvinābhūtasādhanadharmapratītinibandhanatvena tadupadarśanāt prāg asambhavāt | tatpūrvikāyāṃ[280]ca vyāptau anantaraṃ[281]viśeṣaviṣayam anumānaṃ kathaṃ smṛtiḥ syāt? iti |
children.translated_text:
of the two [formulations], which are thus designated. And therefore, [T. 248b.] [S. 66b.] those who, setting aside the subject of the proof (<s>sādhyadharmin</s>), demonstrate only external pervasion (<s>bahirvyāpti</s>) — [thinking] 'even if the proving property is pervaded by the provable property in the example-subject, the <s>sādhya</s> is not thereby established, since it is not so everywhere' — are refuted. Or [if asked:] is the pervasion of the proving property by the provable property [something that holds] everywhere when that [provable property] exists? — if it is precisely of that nature, why is it not demonstrated as such, [instead of] declaring the powerless external pervasion? For in [the argument] 'he is dark-complexioned, because of being his son, like [other] observed sons' — even by demonstrating the pervasion of 'being his son' by dark-complexion in the observed son, [which is] external to the <s>sādhya</s>, the <s>sādhya</s> is not established.
Therefore, only that pervasion which is grounded in a causal constraint established by a <s>pramāṇa</s>, [demonstrated] through universal inclusion (<s>sarvopasaṃhāra</s>), is capable of establishing the <s>sādhya</s> — and that alone should be demonstrated, for the purpose of recalling that [constraint]. And even when pervasion is demonstrated through universal inclusion, the property-bearer qualified by the property is not cognized at that very [moment] — because [S. 67a.] the inference, which arises subsequent to the demonstration of the property of the thesis-subject, would [then] be [mere] memory. Since that [inference] is grounded in the cognition of the proving property as inseparable from the provable property in the subject of the proof — and since [this inference] is impossible prior to the demonstration of that [property] — and when the pervasion is prior to that, how could the inference, which has a specific object, be [mere] memory immediately [after]?

body.translated_text: Now, although inference-for-oneself (<s>svārthānumāna</s>) is the topic under discussion, nevertheless, since some [persons] understand [things] precisely through the mode of formal demonstration (<s>prayoga</s>), due to habitual familiarity with demonstrations — and since that [formal demonstration] is possible even in inference-for-oneself — incidentally,

body.text:
nanu ca
sādharmyaprayogasya vyāptipradarśanalakṣaṇatvaṃ yuktam, sādhanadharme sati sādhyadharmasyāvaśyam bhāvitāpradarśanāt; vaidharmyaprayogasya tu katham? | tatra hi kevalaṃ sādhyābhāve hetvabhāvaḥ kathyate, na tu hetau [T. 249a.] sati sādhyasya bhāva eveti | naiṣa doṣaḥ | na hy atra sādhyābhāve hetvabhāvas tuccharūpo darśyate,

children.text: tasya[282]heturūpatāvirodhāt[283]| vastudharmo hi sattvādiko hetuḥ | tasyātmana[284]evābhāvaḥ kathaṃ [hetusva]rūpaṃ bhaviṣyati, yatas trirūpo hetur bhavet | kintu nivṛttau nivṛttidharmakatvaṃ svagato dharma upadarśyate vaidharmyaprayogeṇa, tathāvidhe[285]ca sādhanadharme 'vaśyaṃ tayā sādhyadharmasya bhāvaḥ pratīyata eva, anyathā tannivṛttau nivṛttidharmakatvasyaivāyogād iti na vyāptipradarśanalakṣaṇatvaṃ vaidharmyaprayogasya na yujyate | [S. 67b.]
children.translated_text: since that [absence] does not contradict the form of being a reason. For a real property such as existence (<s>sattvā</s>) and so forth is the reason. How can the absence of its very self be the form of a reason, such that the reason would be three-formed (<s>trirūpa</s>)? Rather, what is demonstrated by the dissimilarity formulation is an intrinsic property of [the reason's] cessation: the character of being that which ceases when [the probandum] ceases. And when the proving property is of such a nature, the existence of the probandum-property is necessarily understood — otherwise, the very character of ceasing when that [probandum] ceases would be unjustified — therefore, it is not the case that the dissimilarity formulation does not have the character of demonstrating pervasion. [S. 67b.]

body.translated_text: Objection: It is justified that the similarity formulation (<s>sādharmya-prayoga</s>) has the character of demonstrating pervasion (<s>vyāpti</s>), since it demonstrates that when the proving property exists, the property to be proved necessarily exists. But how [is this justified] for the dissimilarity formulation (<s>vaidharmya-prayoga</s>)? For therein, merely the absence of the reason in the absence of the probandum (<s>sādhya</s>) is stated, not that when the reason exists, the probandum necessarily exists. — This is not a fault. For the absence of the reason in the absence of the probandum is not demonstrated here in a trivial manner,

'Of the trivial form'
[283] 'Because of its having no connection with the form that is the character of the designation of pervasion with the reason' — T.
[284] 'Of existence-'
[285] 'In [a property] whose essential nature is the character of cessation in the counter-class'
Section: 6. The pointlessness of the thesis-formulation (<s>pratijñā-prayoga</s>).

body.text: nanu dvividhe 'pi prayoge pratijñāprayogo nopadarśitaḥ tat kathaṃ tadarthāvagatiḥ?, tadarthapratyāyanāya ca sādhanaprayogo 'bhimataḥ ity ata āha --

children.translated_text: 'Here' (<s>atra</s>) —
in these two formulations;
'merely through the power of the statement connecting the thesis-subject-property' —
{p. 64.1} for a reason to be stated;
'of the thesis-meaning' (<s>pratijñārthasya</s>) —
of the probandum characterized by the combination of property and property-bearer (<s>dharma-dharmi-samudāya</s>);
'cognition' (<s>pratīti</s>);
of the reason (<s>hetu</s>);
'not' (<s>na</s>);
'the formulation of the thesis has [not] been shown.'
The opponent, not understanding the capacity [of the proof-formulation alone], says —
'Without having been shown' (<s>apradarśite</s>) —
by statement;
'the object to be cognized' (<s>prameya</s>) —
the probandum (<s>sādhya</s>);
'how' (<s>katham</s>) —
in no way;
'cognition of that' (<s>tat-pratīti</s>) —
cognition of the thesis-meaning;
'thus' (<s>iti</s>) —
in this way;
'if' (<s>ced</s>) —
if you think so, then at the time of inference-for-oneself (<s>svārthānumāna</s>);
'by oneself' (<s>svayam</s>) —
without another who demonstrates;
'in the cognition' (<s>pratipattau</s>);
'of the object to be cognized' (<s>prameyasya</s>);
'who is the demonstrator?'

children.text:
? naiva [T. 249b.] kaścit | svayam eva tu sādhyāvinābhūtasādhanadharmadarśanāt prameyaṃ pratipadyate tathā parārthānumāne 'pi tata eva tatpratītir astu kiṃ pratijñāvacanena?
|
 yadi svayaṃ pratipattikāle na kaścit prameyasyopadarśayitā kathaṃ [S. 68a.] tarhi tatpratipattiḥ? ity ata āha --
children.translated_text:
No one at all! But one understands the object to be cognized by oneself, from the observation of the proving property that is invariably concomitant with the probandum. Likewise, in inference-for-others (<s>parārthānumāna</s>) too, let the cognition of that [probandum] be from that very [source] — what need is there for a thesis-statement?
If no one demonstrates the object to be cognized at the time of one's own cognition, [S. 68a.] then how is there cognition of it? — to this, he says —
'Located at the site' (<s>pradeśa-stha</s>) —
located in the thesis-subject (<s>sādhya-dharmin</s>);
'smoke' (<s>dhūma</s>) —
the proving property;
'of one who has perceived' (<s>upalabdhavataḥ</s>) —
of one who has seen by direct perception;
'of that' (<s>tasya</s>) —
of smoke;
'with fire' (<s>agninā</s>) —
by virtue of the strength of the ascertainment of restriction (<s>pratibandha</s>) with the probandum-property, previously established through a valid means of cognition;
'of the pervasion' (<s>vyāpteḥ</s>) —
of the invariable concomitance;
'upon recollection' (<s>smaraṇe</s>);
'when' (<s>sati</s>);
'from the power of that alone' —
from the power of grasping the thesis-subject-property and grasping the pervasion alone, without the thesis-formulation;
'fire is here' —
of this form;
the cognition of the thesis-meaning arises.

children.text:
|
  syānmatam -- tatrāpy asya karṇapiśācikādiḥ prameyaṃ kathayaty evety ata āha --
children.translated_text: One might think: even there, some ear-demon (<s>karṇa-piśācikā</s>) or such [invisible being] tells him the object to be cognized — therefore, he says —
'And not' (<s>na ca</s>) —
not at all;
'there' (<s>tatra</s>) —
at the time of inference-for-oneself;
'anyone' (<s>kaścit</s>) —
any invisible being such as an ear-demon;
'fire is here' —
thus;
'to this one' (<s>asmai</s>) —
the object to be cognized to the cognizer;
'communicates' (<s>nivedayati</s>) —

children.text:
kathayati | yadi bhavān satyavādī naivaṃ vaktum arhati | tathā hi -- vayam api pradeśasthadhūmadarśanāt tasyāgninā vyāptismaraṇasāpekṣād agniṃ [S. 68b.] pratipadyāmahe | na cāsmabhyaṃ kaścit nivedayati `agnir atra' iti, bhavati ca tatpratipattiḥ, tathā tadanyasyāpi sā yuktarūpaiveti |
  yady api na kaścit nivedayati tathāpi svayam eva prameyaṃ vyavasthāpya tatpratipattaye liṅgam anu[T. 250a.]sariṣyatīti cet, āha --
children.translated_text:
tells. If you are truthful, you should not say this. For indeed — we too understand fire from observing smoke at a site, dependent upon the recollection of its pervasion with fire. [S. 68b.] And no one communicates to us 'fire is here,' yet there is cognition of it; likewise, for another person too, such [cognition] is perfectly appropriate.
Even if no one communicates [the probandum], still, [the person] himself, having determined the object to be cognized, will follow the logical mark for the purpose of cognizing it — if [one objects]; he says —
'Nor' (<s>nāpi</s>) —
not only does no one communicate;
'by oneself too, prior' (<s>svayam api prāg eva</s>) —
prior to the operation of the logical mark, [one] does not cognize;
'anything' (<s>kiñcit</s>) —
such as fire and so forth. Why? {p. 65.1} — if [one asks];
'a valid means of cognition' (<s>pramāṇa</s>) —
the reason (<s>hetu</s>);
'without' (<s>antareṇa</s>);
because the cognition 'fire is here' is without;
'due to the absence of a ground' (<s>nimittābhāvāt</s>).

children.text:
| trirūpo hi hetuḥ parokṣārthapratīter nimittam, tadabhāve sā kathaṃ bhavet? | atha liṅgam antareṇāpy evaṃ pratītir bhavatīti brūyāt tadā pratītāviṣyamāṇāyāṃ liṅgasya vaiyarthyam, tasyānumeyapratipattyarthatvāt, tena vinā tatpratipattau katham asya niṣprayojanatā na syāt? |
  atyantamūḍhatāṃ ca parasya darśayann āha --
children.translated_text:
For the three-formed reason is the ground for the cognition of an imperceptible object; in its absence, how would that [cognition] arise? Or if one were to say that even without a logical mark such cognition arises — then, when cognition arises [by itself], the logical mark would be pointless, since it exists for the purpose of cognizing the inferendum; if there is cognition of that without it, how would it not be purposeless?
Showing the extreme confusion of the opponent, he says —
'By oneself' (<s>svayam eva</s>) —

children.text: svatantra eva `agnir atra' -- iti vyavasthāpya | kathaṃ [S. 69a.] svatantro vyavasthapayati ? |
children.translated_text: independently, having determined 'fire is here.' How does one independently determine? [S. 69a.]
'Without cause' (<s>akasmāt</s>) —
because the determination is without a valid means of cognition;
'for the purpose of cognizing that' (<s>tat-pratipattaye</s>) —
for the purpose of cognizing the object to be cognized, which was determined without any ground;
'afterward' (<s>paścāt</s>);
'the logical mark' (<s>liṅga</s>) —
the ground for that [cognition];
'he follows — what is this order of cognition?'

children.text:
paripāṭiḥ? | tathā hi -- prathamaṃ liṅgānusaraṇam, tataḥ sādhyapratipattir iti vipaścitāṃ kramaḥ | ayaṃ tv apūrvo 'numātā yas tadviparyayam āśrayata iti upahasati | yattalloke gīyate -- śiro muṇḍayitvā nakṣatraṃ pṛcchatīti tattulyatvād asya kramasya | tasmāt pakṣadharmagrahaṇavyāptismaraṇasāmarthyād eva svayaṃ pratipadyate | tac ca pratipādakaṃ kathitam eveti na kiñcit prameyanirddeśena |
  yadi nāma svārthānumānakāle svayam eva sādhyaṃ [T. 250 b.] pratipadyate tad yuktam eva, liṅgasyāpi tatra svayam eva pratipatteḥ | parārthānumāne tu parato yathā liṅgaṃ pratyeti tathā prameyam api parata [S. 69b.] eva pratyetavyam | ato yukta eva pratijñāprayoga ity ata āha --
children.translated_text:
What is this sequence? For indeed — first the following of the logical mark, then the cognition of the probandum — this is the order of the wise. But this is a novel inferrer who resorts to the reverse — thus he ridicules [the opponent]. Because this sequence is similar to what is sung in the world: 'Having shaved the head, he asks about the [auspicious] constellation.' Therefore, from the power of grasping the thesis-subject-property and recollecting the pervasion alone, one cognizes by oneself. And that demonstrating [power] has already been described — therefore, nothing [is gained] by indicating the object to be cognized.
Granted that at the time of inference-for-oneself, one cognizes the probandum by oneself — that is perfectly proper, since the logical mark too is cognized by oneself there. But in inference-for-others, just as the logical mark is cognized from another, so too the object to be cognized should be cognized from another alone. Therefore, the thesis-formulation is perfectly proper — to this, he says —
'Even by another' (<s>pareṇāpi</s>) —

children.text: na kevalaṃ svayam eva prāg vyavasthāpyamānaṃ plavate pareṇāpi vādinā
children.translated_text: not only does [the probandum] determined by oneself prior [to the mark] float [i.e., remain groundless]; even when stated by another, the debater —
'that' (<s>tat</s>) —
the object to be cognized;
'being stated, floats indeed' —

children.text: tadvacanasya sandigdhārthābhidhāyakatayā sādhyaniścayānaṅgatvāt prameyagāmbhīryānavagāhinaḥ paramparayā 'py atatsambaddhasya vivakṣāmātranibandhanatayoparyevāvasthāpanāt | kasmāt plavate? iti cet,
children.translated_text: because his statement, expressing a doubtful meaning, is not a factor in the ascertainment of the probandum; since one who does not fathom the depth of the object to be cognized, even indirectly, being unconnected with that [probandum], is situated merely at the level of intention, placed above [without depth]. Why does it float? — if [one asks];
'due to the absence of utility' (<s>upayogābhāvāt</s>) —

children.text:
nāsya sādhyapratītiṃ prati kaścid upayogaḥ, tatpratyāyanasamarthasyānabhidhānād iti yāvat |
  {p. 66.1} paras tūpayogamātraṃ kadācid brūyād ity āśaṅkyāha --
children.translated_text:
it has no utility with respect to the cognition of the probandum, since what is capable of conveying that [probandum] has not been expressed — this is the extent [of the meaning].
{p. 66.1} But the opponent might sometimes claim mere utility — anticipating this, he says —
'The indication of the subject-matter' (<s>viṣayopadarśana</s>) —

children.text: hetor yo viṣayaḥ sādhyaṃ tadupadarśanaṃ pratijñāvacanasyopayogaḥ
children.translated_text: the subject-matter of the reason is the probandum; its indication is the utility of the thesis-statement;
'if this is the view' (<s>cet matam</s>).
To this, he says —
'By that very' (<s>tenaiva</s>) —
by the subject-matter itself;
'first' (<s>tāvat</s>) —

children.text: c chabdaḥ krame | viṣayasyopadarśyamānasyārthavattāyāṃ tadupadarśanaṃ pratijñāvacanasya prayojanaṃ bhavet | viṣayeṇaiva tu darśyamānena
children.translated_text: the word indicates sequence. When the subject-matter being indicated is meaningful, then its indication would be the purpose of the thesis-statement. But when the subject-matter itself is being demonstrated [by the proof-formulation] —
'what is the purpose?' (<s>ko 'rthaḥ</s>) —

children.text:
kiṃ [S. 70a.] prayojanam? |
  nanu sādhyapratītiḥ sādharmyavatprayogādipratītiś ca viṣayopadarśanasyārthaḥ | tatas tadupadarśanaṃ pratijñāvacanasya prayojanam | tathā hi asati sādhyanirdeśe `yat kṛtakaṃ tad anityam' ity ukte `kim ayaṃ sādharmyavān prayogaḥ? [T. 251a.] uta vaidharmyavān?' iti na jñāyeta | ubhayaṃ hy atrāśaṅkhyate -- kṛtakatvenānityatve sādhye sādharmyavān, nityatvenākṛtakatve vā vaidharmyavān iti | `anityaḥ śabdaḥ' `akṛtako vā' iti tu pratijñāvacane saty ubhayam asandigdham avagamyate | hetuviruddhānaikāntikapratītiś ca na syāt | pratijñāpūrvake tu prayoge `anityaḥ śabdaḥ, kṛtakatvāt' iti hetubhāvaḥ pratīyate, `nityaḥ, kṛtakatvāt' iti viruddhatā, `prayatnānantarīyakaḥ kṛtakatvāt' ity anaikāntikatvam | hetoś ca trairūpyaṃ na gamyate, tasya sādhyāpekṣayā vyavasthānāt | sati pratijñāvacane avayave samudāyopacārāt sādhyadharmī pakṣa iti tatra [S. 70b.] vṛttasya kṛtakatvasya pakṣadharmatvaṃ; sādhyadharmasāmānyena
ca samāno 'rthaḥ sapakṣa iti tatra varttamānasya sapakṣe sattvam; na sapakṣo 'sapakṣa iti sādhyadharmavirahiṇy avṛttasyāsapakṣe 'py asattvaṃ pratīyeta ity āśaṅkyāha --
children.translated_text:
what is the utility? [S. 70a.]
Objection: The cognition of the probandum and the cognition of the similarity-formulation and such are the purpose of indicating the subject-matter. Therefore, its indication is the purpose of the thesis-statement. For in the absence of indicating the probandum, when one says 'whatever is produced is impermanent,' it is not known 'Is this a similarity formulation? Or a dissimilarity one?' For both are possible here: with producedness proving impermanence, it is a similarity [formulation]; or with permanence proving non-producedness, it is a dissimilarity one. But when the thesis-statement 'sound is impermanent' or 'non-produced' is present, both are understood without doubt. And the cognition of [the reason as] contradictory (<s>viruddha</s>) or inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>) would not arise [without it]. But when the formulation is preceded by the thesis — 'sound is impermanent, because of being produced' — the reason-nature is understood; 'permanent, because of being produced' — the contradictory nature; 'caused by effort, because of being produced' — the inconclusive nature. And the three-formed nature of the reason is not understood [without it], since it is established relative to the probandum. When the thesis-statement is present, by figurative attribution from the component to the composite, the thesis-subject is 'the <s>pakṣa</s>' — and the producedness present therein [S. 70b.] has the status of thesis-subject-property; and what has a similar meaning with the probandum-property in general is the 'similar instance' (<s>sapakṣa</s>), and the presence [of the reason] in the similar instance where it occurs; and 'not the similar instance is the dissimilar instance,' and the non-existence in the dissimilar instance, which lacks the probandum-property, of what does not occur [there] — would be understood. — Anticipating this, he says —
'If the cognition' —

children.text: sādhyasya niścayalakṣaṇā sādharmyavat prayogādeś ca svarūpāvadhāraṇātmikā |
children.translated_text: of the probandum, having the character of ascertainment, and of the similarity-formulation and such, having the nature of determining their own form;
'otherwise' (<s>anyathā</s>) —
without the thesis-statement;
'would not be [possible], then' —

children.text: yaduktaṃ sādhyasiddhyarthaṃ sādharmyavat prayogādijñānārthaṃ ca viṣayopadarśanam iti tat
children.translated_text: what was said — that the indication of the subject-matter is for the purpose of establishing the probandum and for the purpose of knowing the similarity-formulation and such — that
'would all be splendid' (<s>sarvaṃ śobheta</s>);

children.text: yāvatā svārthānumānakāle pratijñāvacanam antareṇāpi pakṣadharmagrahaṇa[T. 251b.]sambandhasmaraṇataḥ sādhyasiddhilakṣaṇā bhavaty eva pratītiḥ ity ākhyātam eva | tadvat parārthe 'py anumāne {p. 67.1} bhaviṣyati | yata evaṃ
children.translated_text: but since it has already been explained that even without the thesis-statement, at the time of inference-for-oneself, from the grasping of the thesis-subject-property and the recollection of the connection, the cognition characterized as the establishment of the probandum does indeed arise — so too it will be in inference-for-others. Since this is so,
'therefore' (<s>tasmāt</s>);
'this one' (<s>eṣa</s>) —

children.text: pratijñāprayogavādī yadā svayaṃ sādhyaṃ pratyeti tadā svayaṃ sādhyasya [S. 71a.]
children.translated_text: this advocate of the thesis-formulation — when he himself cognizes the probandum, then in his own [S. 71a.]
'cognition' (<s>pratītau</s>) —
in which the subject-matter is presented through the thesis-statement, by a person;
'by some [person]' (<s>kenacit</s>);
'without that' (<s>tena</s>);
'even without' (<s>vināpi</s>);
'cognizing' (<s>pratiyan</s>) —

children.text: sādhyaṃ niścinvan liṅgasāmarthyād eva | yadā 'smābhiḥ pratipādyate tadā
children.translated_text: ascertaining the probandum, from the power of the logical mark alone. When it is demonstrated by us, then —
'seeing us as clients, [he] seeks an unmanifest' —
characterized as the thesis-formulation —
'price' (<s>mūlya</s>).
Like whom?
'Like a festival-Brahmin' (<s>parva-brāhmaṇa iva</s>).

children.text:
| yathā dakṣiṇām antareṇāpy anyadā aurdvarathiko brāhmaṇo bhuñjāno 'nyadā śrāddhādiparvaṇy arthinaṃ śraddhāluṃ bravīti -- yadi me ghṛtapūraṃ ghṛtapūraṃ prati rūpakaṃ dadāsi tato 'haṃ bhuñje nānyatheti | tena tulyo bhavān apīti |
  kiñca, yad api bravīṣi -- parārthānumānakāle yathā liṅgaṃ pareṇānabhidhīyamānaṃ na pratyeti pratipādyas tathā sādhyam apīti | tadaitad yujyate yady asau vādivacanamātreṇa liṅgam api niścitya tadanusāreṇa sādhyam avagacchet, parapratītyarthinaś ca tadā vayam api pratijñāṃ kin na prayuñjmahe liṅgavacanarahitām? | [S. 71b.] asmadvacanasyaiva taṃ prati pramāṇatayā, tata evānumeyapratīteḥ, tadvacanasya[287]caritārthatvāt | na caitad asti, yataḥ
children.translated_text:
Just as a Brahmin who performs the <s>aurdhvarathika</s> (post-funeral rites), who at other times eats without payment, on occasions such as <s>śrāddha</s> festivals says to the petitioner who has faith: 'If you give me a ghee-cake [and] a coin per ghee-cake, then I will eat — not otherwise.' You are like that one.
Moreover, as for what you say — 'At the time of inference-for-others, just as the logical mark, when not stated by another, is not cognized by the person to be convinced, so too the probandum' — this would be justified if that person, merely from the debater's statement alone, having ascertained the logical mark too, would understand the probandum in accordance with it. And in that case, when we desire the other's cognition, why would we not formulate the thesis alone, without the statement of the logical mark? [S. 71b.] Since our statement alone would have the status of valid cognition for him, since the cognition of the inferendum would be from that alone, and since his [the debater's] statement would have served its purpose. But this is not the case, since —
'Even from our statement' (<s>asmadvacanād api</s>) —

children.text: na kevalaṃ svārthānumānakāle 'smadvacanam antareṇa ity api śabdaḥ | kintu [T. 252a.] yadāpy asmadvacanaṃ pravṛttaṃ tadāpi
children.translated_text: Not only at the time of inference-for-oneself is [the mark cognized] without our statement — the word 'also' (<s>api</s>) [indicates:] but even when our statement has been made,
'not at all' —
from our statement —
'does [the other person] cognize even the logical mark' —

children.text: , kuta eva sādhyasiddhaye 'nusariṣyati? | api tu svayam asya yadi talliṅgaṃ kutaścit pramāṇataḥ siddhaṃ bhavati
children.translated_text: much less will [the mark] be followed for the establishment of the <s>sādhya</s>. Rather, if on his own that logical mark has been established for him from some <s>pramāṇa</s>,
'by our statement, however' —
merely with respect to that,
'only a reminder and focusing of attention is produced' —

children.text:
| tadā svayaṃ siddham eva liṅgam anusṛtya sādhyaṃ pratyeti | nāsmadvacanāt
pānīyam api pibatīti |
children.translated_text: then, following the mark that has been established on its own, he cognizes the <s>sādhya</s>. One does not drink even water merely because of our statement.
'Therefore' —
'what difference is there between these two' —
states, namely that characterized by the statement of the thesis and that characterized by the non-statement [of the thesis] —

children.text:
?, ubhayatra svayaṃsiddhaliṅgasāmarthyād eva sādhyapratīter na kaścit | tataḥ svaparārthānumānayoḥ svayaṃsiddhaliṅgānusaraṇam, tataḥ sādhyapratītiṃ ca prati viśeṣābhāvāt pratijñopanyāsaḥ parārthānumāne 'pi vyartha [S. 72a.] eva | liṅgam api hi tāvad atra nābhidhīyate yadi tat {p. 68.1} pūrvaprasiddhaṃ svayam anusmaret kim aṅgaḥ sandigdhārthābhidhāyakaṃ pratijñāvacanam upādīyate? |
  syānmatam -- yadi nāma sādhyasiddhau pratijñāvacanasya nopayogas tadartho 'sya prayogo mā bhūt, sādharmyavat prayogādijñānārthaṃ tu tadupādānam avasthitam eva, tasyānyathā pratīty abhāvāt ity ata āha --
children.translated_text:
since in both cases the cognition of the <s>sādhya</s> arises solely from the power of the mark established on its own, there is none. Therefore, since in both inference-for-oneself and inference-for-others there is the following of the independently established mark, and since there is no difference with respect to the cognition of the <s>sādhya</s>, the presentation of the thesis (<s>pratijñā</s>) is entirely superfluous even in inference-for-others. For even the logical mark is not articulated here [in inference-for-oneself] — if one would oneself remember it as previously known, why should the thesis-statement, which expresses a matter of doubt, be adopted?
One might think: even if the thesis-statement has no use in establishing the <s>sādhya</s>, let it not be employed for that purpose; but its adoption remains established for the purpose of knowledge of the mode of formulation (<s>prayoga</s>) — whether by similarity or by dissimilarity — since that [knowledge] cannot be obtained otherwise. To this he says —
'And the cognition of the mode of formulation — whether by similarity and so forth — is observed even without the thesis-statement' —

children.text:
, tatas tadartho 'pi pratijñopanyāso na śobhate |
  kutaḥ punaḥ sādharmyavat prayogāder asati sādhyanirdeśe pratītiḥ? [T. 252b.] ity āha --
children.translated_text:
therefore, the presentation of the thesis is not fitting even for that purpose.
But how is there cognition of the mode of formulation by similarity and so forth in the absence of the statement of the <s>sādhya</s>? To this he says —
'merely from the statement of the property-of-the-thesis-subject and the [pervasion] relation' —

children.text:
| evaṃ manyate -- naiva hi kaścit `yat kṛtakaṃ tad anityam' etāvan mātram abhidhāyā ''ste, sādhananyūnatayaivāsya parājayāt, kintv avaśyaṃ hetor ddharmiṇy upasaṃhāraṃ karotīti | tatra yadi `kṛtakaś ca śabdaḥ' iti brūyāt tadā [S. 72b.] sādhy(dha)rmyavat prayogapratītiḥ, atha `nityaś ca' ity abhidadhyāt tadā vaidharmyavata iti sambandhavacanapūrvakāt pakṣadharmavacanāt prayogadvayāvagatiḥ |
  hetuviruddhānaikāntikā api pakṣadharmavacanamātreṇa na pratīyante | yadā tu sambandhavacanam api kriyate tadā katham apratītiḥ? | tathā hi `yat kṛtakaṃ tad anityam' iti pakṣadharmavacane saty ukte hetur avagamyate, vidhīyamānenānūdyamānasya vyāptaḥ | `yat kṛtakaṃ tan nityam' ity abhidhāne viruddhaḥ, viparyayavyāpteḥ | `yat kṛtakaṃ tat prayatnānantarīyakam' iti pradarśane vyabhicārād anaikāntikādhyavasāyaḥ |
  trairūpyam api hetor gamyata eva, yato vyāptipradarśanakāle vyāpako dharmaḥ sādhyatayā 'vagamyate | yatra ca vyāpyo dharmo dharmiṇy upasaṃhriyate sa vyāpakadharmaviśiṣṭatayā 'vagamyamānaḥ sādhyasamudāyaikadeśatayā pakṣa ity upasaṃhṛtasya vyāpyadharmasya pakṣadharmatvāvagatiḥ, [S. 73a.] sā ca vyāptir yatra dharmiṇy upadarśyate sa sādhyadharmasāmānyena samāno 'rthaḥ sapakṣaḥ pratīyata iti sapakṣe {p. 69.1} sattvam avagamyate, sāmarthyāc ca [T. 253a.] vyāpakanivṛttau vyāpyanivṛttir yatrāvasīyate so 'sapakṣa ity asapakṣe 'py asatva(ttva)m api niścīyata iti, yadi pakṣādibhir api jñātaiḥ kiñcit prayojanaṃ | na tu vyavahartaṇāṃ pakṣādisaṅketāpekṣā parokṣārthagatir bhavati | tathā hi -- yat kvacit dṛṣṭaṃ tasya yatra pratibandhaḥ tadvidas tasya tad gamakaṃ tatra iti hi loke vastugatir bhavati, na pakṣādisaṅketagrahaṇāpekṣā | tatra yatheṣṭaṃśāstrakārāgamakarūpapratipattaye svasaṅketenānyathā
vā lakṣaṇaṃ praṇayantu | na tu vyavahārakāle tadanusaraṇaṃ kvacid upayujyate | tatsaṅketapratipāditam eva tu yathoktaṃ gamakaṃ rūpam upayogi vyavahartṛṛṇām | tac cet pratipannaṃ tāvataiva sādhyasiddhiḥ sañjātā iti pakṣasapakṣādisaṅketāparijñāne 'pi [S. 73b.] na kiñcit plūyate | ata evācāryapādair `nnāntarīyakāryadarśanaṃ tadvido 'numānam' iti gamakarūpamātram eva pakṣādisaṅketānapekṣaṃ pratipāditam | svaprajñāparādhāstu(ttu) tatrāpi kaiścid asanta eva doṣāḥ prakīrtyanta iti kim atra brūmaḥ? |
children.translated_text:
thus. He thinks as follows: no one merely states 'whatever is produced is impermanent' and stops, since his defeat [would result] from the deficiency of the proof-statement. Rather, he necessarily makes the subsumption (<s>upasaṃhāra</s>) of the reason in the property-bearer. Therein, if he says 'and sound is produced,' then the cognition of the formulation by similarity [is achieved]; if he says 'and [sound is] permanent,' then [the cognition is] of [the formulation] by dissimilarity. Thus, from the statement of the property-of-the-thesis-subject preceded by the statement of the relation, both modes of formulation are understood.
Even [pseudo-]reasons that are contradictory (<s>viruddha</s>) or inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>) are not cognized merely from the statement of the property-of-the-thesis-subject. But when the statement of the relation is also made, how could there be non-cognition? For when, with the statement of the property of the thesis-subject, 'whatever is produced is impermanent' is stated, the reason is understood — the stated [property] is pervaded by what is being affirmed. When 'whatever is produced is permanent' is stated, [the reason is] contradictory, because of pervasion by the contrary. When 'whatever is produced is caused by effort' is presented, there is the determination of inconclusiveness due to deviation.
The triple characterization of the reason is also understood, since at the time of showing the pervasion, the pervading property is understood as the <s>sādhya</s>. And when the pervaded property is subsumed in the property-bearer, being understood as qualified by the pervading property, [the property-bearer] is understood as the thesis (<s>pakṣa</s>) — being one part of the aggregate of the <s>sādhya</s> — thus, the understanding of the subsumed pervaded property as a property-of-the-thesis-subject [is achieved]. And the pervasion being demonstrated in whichever property-bearer — that which shares in the generality of the <s>sādhya</s>-property is understood as the similar instance (<s>sapakṣa</s>) — thus, presence in the similar instance is understood. And by implication, where the cessation of the pervaded is ascertained upon the cessation of the pervader — that is the dissimilar instance (<s>asapakṣa</s>) — thus, absence in the dissimilar instance too is ascertained. [This is] if even the knowledge of thesis, similar instance, and so forth has any purpose. But the cognition of imperceptible objects by those who reason does not depend on the conventions of thesis and so forth. For in the world, the cognition of reality proceeds thus: 'that which has been observed somewhere, wherever there is a necessary connection of it, for one who knows that [connection], that is indicative of that [object] there' — it does not depend on grasping the conventions of thesis and so forth. With respect to that, let the treatise-authors frame their definitions by their own conventions or otherwise, for the understanding of the form of what has come down in tradition. But the following of that [convention] is never useful at the time of actual reasoning. Rather, only the indicative form as described — established by those conventions — is useful for reasoners. And if that has been understood, the establishment of the <s>sādhya</s> has been achieved by that much alone — so even when the conventions of thesis, similar instance, and so forth are not fully known, nothing is lost. For this very reason, the Master [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>] has taught only the indicative form — 'the seeing of a necessary effect by one who knows that [connection] is inference' — independent of the conventions of thesis and so forth. But those who, through the fault of their own intellect, proclaim non-existent defects even in that — what shall we say about them?
'Therefore' —

children.text: sādharmyavat prayogādijñānārtham api pratijñāvacanaṃ pakṣadharmasambandhavacanamātra [T. 253b.] eva yathoktena prakāreṇa pratīter ayuktam iti
children.translated_text: even for the purpose of knowledge of the mode of formulation by similarity and so forth, the thesis-statement is inappropriate, since cognition [arises] merely from the statement of the property-of-the-thesis-subject and the relation, in the manner stated. Thus —
'what' —
of the thesis-statement —
'use is there?' —

children.text:
naiva kaścit |
  svayaṃ cāyaṃ vādī yena krameṇānumeyaṃ pratipannavāms tamullaṅghya parapratipattaye kramāntaram āśrayan paravañcakatayā dhūrtta eva pratīyate, na saddhṛtta ity upadarśayann āha --
children.translated_text:
none at all.
And this debater himself, transgressing the order by which he himself has understood the object to be inferred, and resorting to a different order for the other's understanding — is perceived as a cheat through his deception of the other, not as one of good conduct. Showing this, he says —
'just as [one has attained] one's own ascertainment' (<s>svaniścayavat</s>) —
and so forth. Just as the production of one's own ascertainment was accomplished, so too —
'for producing the ascertainment of others as well' —
by those devoted to the welfare of others —
'the means of proof is stated' —
'therein' —

children.text: etasmiṃ(smin) nyāye sati svayam ayaṃ vādī
children.translated_text: when this principle holds, this debater himself —
'without the indication of the provable' —
without the indicative statement —
'even' —
at the time of inference-for-oneself —
'having understood' —
the provable [proposition] —
'the other' —
the one in doubt and so forth —
'instructing' —
making [the other] understand the provable as he himself has understood it —
'a novel' —
[novel] compared to what was experienced previously as the —
'order' —
the means in the cognition of the provable — different from that —
'resorts to — what here' —
'by resorting to a different order' —
'is the reason?' —

children.text:
? naiva kiñcit paravyāmohanaṃ muktvā | tathā hi -- yadi svapratipattikramaḥ {p. 70} pratītinibandhanaṃ
kiṃ tatparityāgena kramāntarāśrayaṇam?, kathaṃ tena svayaṃ pratipannavānasīti? | yata evaṃ
children.translated_text: None at all, other than the deception of the other. For if one's own order of understanding is the ground of cognition, what [purpose is served] by abandoning that and resorting to a different order? How then has one understood [the matter] oneself? Since this is so —
'therefore, of the provable' —
of the <s>sādhya</s> —
'by the statement' —
called the thesis —
'there is no purpose whatsoever' —
why? Because 'even otherwise' — even without that —
'of cognition' —
of the cognition of the <s>sādhya</s> —
'there is arising' —
this is the conclusion.

body.translated_text: Objection: In neither of the two formulations has the thesis-formulation been shown. Then how is the understanding of its meaning [achieved]? And the proof-formulation (<s>sādhana-prayoga</s>) is intended for conveying that meaning — therefore, he says —

<s>vyavasthāpayiṣyati</s> — T.
[287] <s>liṅga</s>-
Section: 7. The non-essentiality of the subsumption, conclusion, and so forth to the proof-statement.

body.text: evaṃ pratijñāṃ sādhanavākyād apanīyāparam apy upanayanigamanādikaṃ paraparikalpitaṃ sādhanavākyād apanetum uktam eva nyāyam atidiśann āha --
body.translated_text: Having thus removed the thesis from the proof-statement, extending the very principle already stated to remove also the subsumption (<s>upanaya</s>), conclusion (<s>nigamana</s>), and the like — as postulated by the opponent — from the proof-statement, he says —
'by this' —
by the principle that 'cognition arises even otherwise' —
'the subsumption, conclusion, and the like' —
by the word 'and the like,' doubt (<s>saṃśaya</s>), desire to know (<s>jijñāsā</s>), and so forth —
'are answered' —
refuted. Therein —
'The subsumption depending on the example is the connection [of the example to the thesis-subject], saying "thus" or "not thus"' —
'The re-statement of the thesis is the conclusion' —
this is the definition of these two.
'The statement of the <s>sādhya</s> is the thesis' —

body.text: iti tu pratijñāyāḥ | etenety etad eva darśayati --
body.translated_text: — this is [the definition] of the thesis. 'By this' shows the following —
'by this much alone' —
by the mere statement of the property-of-the-thesis-subject and the relation alone, without subsumption and the like —
'because of the existence of the cognition of the <s>sādhya</s>' —

body.text:
utpatter iti |
  atrodyo(ddyo)takaraḥprāha -- pratijñā tāvad viṣayanirddeśārtham avaśyakarttavyā, yato lokaḥ prathamaṃ karma cchedyādikaṃ nirūpayati | tataḥ kuṭhārādikaṃ sādhanaṃ vyāpārayati | upanayenāpi yāvad dṛṣṭānte dṛṣṭasāmarthyo hetur ddharmiṇi nopasaṃhriyate tāvat kutaḥ sādhyapratītiḥ? | svārthānumānadṛṣṭaś ca pratyavamarśapratyayārtho 'nena darśyate | tathā hi -- svārthānumāne prathamaṃ pradeśe dhūmaṃ paśyati, tato `yatra yatrāhaṃ dhūmamadrākṣaṃ tatra tatrāgnim api' iti vyāptiṃ [T. 254b.] smarati | tato `dhūmaś cātra' iti punaḥ pratyavamṛśati, sa pratyavamarśārthaḥ parārthānumāne upanayenocyate | [S. 75a.] nigamanam apy avaśyābhidhānīyam, yato yady api pūrvaṃ anityaḥ śabda ity uktam, na tu tāvatā 'sya niścayo jātaḥ | samprati tu pramāṇabalāyāto 'rthaḥ tatsampratyayārtham anena nigamyate | aśeṣapramāṇavyāpāraś cānenopasaṃhriyate | tathā hi āgamaḥ pratijñā,
hetur anumānaṃ, {p. 71.1} dṛṣṭāntaḥ pratyakṣam upamānam upanayaḥ | tadetasya pramāṇacatuṣṭayasyāpi vyāpāro nigamanenopasaṃhriyate -- iti katham asya na sāphalyam? ity etad āśaṅkyāha --
body.translated_text:
[i.e.,] because of [its] arising.
Here <s>Uddyotakara</s> says: the thesis must necessarily be made, for the purpose of indicating the subject-matter, since ordinary people first determine the work to be done — such as cutting and the like — and then employ the instrument such as an axe and the like. And even by the subsumption, so long as the reason, whose power has been observed in the example, is not subsumed in the property-bearer — how can there be cognition of the <s>sādhya</s>? And the reflective cognition (<s>pratyavamarśa</s>) observed in inference-for-oneself is shown by this [subsumption]. For in inference-for-oneself, one first sees smoke in a location; then one remembers the pervasion: 'wherever I saw smoke, there [I saw] fire too'; then one reflects again: 'and there is smoke here' — that reflective [cognition] is expressed by the subsumption in inference-for-others. The conclusion too must necessarily be stated, since even though 'sound is impermanent' was stated earlier, the ascertainment did not arise from that much alone. But now, the meaning having acquired strength from the <s>pramāṇa</s>, it is concluded by this [conclusion] for the purpose of conveying that ascertainment. And the operation of all <s>pramāṇas</s> is brought together by this [conclusion]. For tradition (<s>āgama</s>) is the thesis, the reason is inference, the example is perception [and] comparison (<s>upamāna</s>), the subsumption [also represents comparison]. Thus the operation of this quartet of <s>pramāṇas</s> is brought together by the conclusion — so how can it be purposeless?
Anticipating this [objection], he says —
'abandoning the obstinacy of the <s>Ḍiṇḍikas</s>' —

body.text: ḍiṇḍikāḥ --nagnācāryāḥte niṣphalam upary upari nāmalekhane prasaktāḥ tatas teṣām iva `pareṇokte tasyopari mayā 'vaśyam ayuktatayā niṣphalam apy abhidhānīyam' ity asthānābhiniveśaṃ tyaktvā
body.translated_text: the <s>Ḍiṇḍikas</s> — the naked preceptors (<s>Jain ascetics</s>) — they are engaged in pointlessly inscribing names one on top of another; just as they [act], [so too] abandoning the misplaced attachment [of thinking] 'whatever the opponent has said, I must necessarily say something on top of that, even if pointless and inappropriate' —
'closing one's eyes' —
withdrawing the outward distraction —
'just reflect for a moment' —
'whether by this much' —
by a statement consisting of merely the property-of-the-thesis-subject and the relation — of the <s>sādhya</s>,
'will there be cognition or not?' —

body.text: ? iti | yāvatā yāvān eva [S. 75b.] parārthānumāne 'rtho 'bhidhānīya ity asmābhir anujñāyate tāvān evānyūnānatiriktaḥ svārthānumāne 'pi pratītihetur dṛṣṭaḥ, tasya ka iha śakter vyāghāt? yenāsau parārthānumāne 'pi pratītiṃ na kuryāt |
body.translated_text: Since exactly as much content as we acknowledge should be stated in inference-for-others — that much alone, neither less nor more, is observed as the cause of cognition even in inference-for-oneself — what here could obstruct its power? So that it would not produce cognition even in inference-for-others.
'since [cognition] exists' —
of cognition —
'what use is a garland of elaborations?'

body.text:
pratijñopanayanigamanalakṣaṇayā [T. 255a.], bālapratārakatadupayogopavarṇalakṣaṇayā[288]vā? | tathā hi ḥ pratijñopanayanigamanaprayoge 'pi yadi pramāṇaniścitā svasādhyavyāptiḥ sādhanadharmasya na syāt, sādhyadharmiṇi vā sadbhāvas tadā 'sya[289]naiva pratītihetutā | tatsambhave[290]tu pratijñādyabhāve 'pi svārthānumāna iva gamakarūpāvaikalyāt sā[291]na nivāryata iti kim asthānanirbandhena iti? | na hi sādhyadharmākṣepaṇasāmarthyavirahe sādhanadharmasya vādivacanamātrāt sādhyaniścayo yuktaḥ, hetūpanyāsavaiyarthyaprasaṅgāt, tasya tadākṣepasāmarthye vā pratijñāvacanasyeti[292]|
  yat tūktam `viṣayapradarśanāya pratijñā' ity atraśāstrakṛtaiva dattam utta-ram | yaś ca sādhanaṃ prayuṃkte tena `aham anena [S. 76a.] sādhanenāmuṣmiṃ(ṣmin) sādhye pratītiṃ sādhayiṣyāmi' iti karma nirūpyaiva tat[293]prayuktam iti na laukikanyāyātikramaḥ, anyathā yadi sādhanād yasya sādhyapratītir upajāyate tenaiva karma nirūpaṇīyam kathaṃ tadabhāve svārthānumāne [T. 255b.] sādhyasiddhiḥ {p. 72.1} sādhananibandhanā syāt? | yaś cāgnidhūmayoḥ sambandhaṃ cetasi vyavasthāpya `kvāgniḥ kvāgniḥ?' ity agniṃ
body.translated_text:
characterized as thesis, subsumption, and conclusion, or as the teaching that serves to deceive the naive? For thus: even in a syllogism with thesis, subsumption, and conclusion, if the pervasion of the proving property with what is to be proved, ascertained by a <s>pramāṇa</s>, were not [present], or if the existence [of the proving property] in the thesis-subject’s property-bearer [were not present], then this [syllogism] would have no capacity to generate cognition. But when those [conditions] are present, even without the thesis and so forth, just as in inference for oneself (<s>svārthānumāna</s>), since the indicative form is complete, that [capacity] is not prevented — so what is the point of insisting on what is out of place? For without the capacity to entail the provable property, a mere statement by the proponent of the proving property does not properly produce certainty of the provable, since there would be the unwanted consequence of the pointlessness of adducing the reason; or if [the proving property] has that capacity to entail [the provable], then of the statement of the thesis.
As for what was said — ‘the thesis is for showing the subject-matter’ — the author of the treatise himself has given the reply to this. And the one who employs a proof has employed that [proof] only after determining the task [thinking:] ‘I shall establish cognition of this provable through this proof’ — hence there is no violation of common-sense procedure. Otherwise, if the one for whom cognition of the provable arises from the proof must himself determine the task, how could the establishment of the provable, grounded in the proof, occur in inference for oneself, where that [determination] is absent? And one who, having established the connection of fire and smoke in the mind, searches for fire [thinking] ‘Where is fire? Where is fire?’ —

body.text: paryeṣate sa pradeśe dhūmadarśanamātrād[294]evāgniṃ pratipadyata iti kathaṃ svārthānumāne pratyavamarśapratyayaḥ syāt? | atha kadācid asau dṛṣṭas tatreti[295]parārthe 'py asyopādānaṃ tadā dadhyādikam api bhuktvā kadācid dhūmād agniṃ pratipannavān iti kin na dadhibhojanāder api kādācit kasyopādānam? |
body.translated_text: that person, merely from seeing smoke in a location, cognizes fire — so how could the reflective judgment (<s>pratyavamarśa</s>) arise in inference for oneself? If [one argues:] because he was once seen there, [smoke] is adopted in inference for others too — then, since one who has eaten curds and the like has also once cognized fire from smoke, why should not eating curds and the like also be occasionally adopted [as evidence]?

body.text: yat punaruktam `āgamaḥ pratijñā' iti, tatra yadi vādivacanam evāgamas tadā tata eva sādhyasiddher hetvādyupādānam anarthakam | atha pratijñārthasyāgame pāṭhād āgamaḥ pratijñā, tadā na kvacid āgame paṭhyate atra pradeśe 'gnir iti [S. 76b.] katham āgamatvaṃ pratijñāyāḥ? |
body.translated_text: As for what was further said — ‘scripture (<s>āgama</s>) is the thesis’ — there: if the proponent’s statement itself is scripture, then since the provable would be established from that alone, the adoption of the reason and so forth would be pointless. If the thesis is scripture because the thesis-meaning is read in scripture, then since nowhere in scripture is it read ‘there is fire in this location,’ how could the thesis have the nature of scripture?

body.text: `hetur anumānam' ity apy ayuktam, na hi pakṣadharmatvamātraṃ hetuḥ, tasya trirūpatvāt | dṛṣṭānto 'pi na sarvaḥ pratyakṣa iti kathaṃ `dṛṣṭāntaḥ pratyakṣam' bhavet? | upamānaṃ tu pramāṇam eva na bhavati, kathaṃ tadvyāpāra upasaṃhriyeta nigamanena? | yadi cāvaśyaṃ dṛṣṭānte dṛṣṭasāmarthyo hetur ddharmiṇy upaneyaḥ tadopanaya evāstu kiṃ `kṛtakatvāṭ' iti pakṣadharmanirddeśena?, sa eva dṛṣṭasāmarthyaṃ hetum upasaṃhariṣyati pakṣadharmatāṃ ca darśayiṣyatīti na kiñcit tena | tato yatra ca pratijñāyāḥ prathamata eva prayogo neṣyate tatra tasyāḥ punarvacanaṃ kuto nigamanaṃ bhaviṣyati? | ity āha --
body.translated_text: ‘The reason is inference’ is also improper, for the mere property of belonging to the thesis-subject (<s>pakṣadharmatva</s>) is not the reason, since that has three characteristics (<s>trirūpatva</s>). Nor is every example perceptual, so how could ‘the example is perception’ hold? And analogy (<s>upamāna</s>) is not a <s>pramāṇa</s> at all — how could its function be subsumed by the conclusion? If the reason must necessarily be applied to the thesis-subject after its capacity has been demonstrated in the example, then let the subsumption (<s>upanaya</s>) alone exist — what need for the statement of the thesis-property through ‘because of being produced’? That [subsumption] itself will subsume the reason whose capacity has been demonstrated and will show the thesis-property — so nothing [is gained] by that. And where the employment of the thesis at the very beginning is not accepted, how could its restatement be a conclusion? Hence he says:
Therefore (<s>iti</s>) —
hence (<s>tasmāt</s>) —
just this much —
consisting merely in the statement of the connection of the thesis-property, in the proof-statement —
is the preferable employment —
not one consisting of five members — this is established.

body.text:
pratijñādi-
[289] hetoḥ
[290] vyāptyādisambhave
[291] [pratī] tihetutā
[292] upanyāsavaiyarthyaprasaṅgāt
[293] sādhanam
[294] -ṣate sadhūmapradeśadarśana- -- T.
[295] svārthānumāne
body.translated_text:
thesis and so forth-
[289] of the reason
[290] when pervasion and so forth are present
[291] [capacity to generate] cognition
[292] because of the unwanted consequence of pointlessness of adducing
[293] the proof
[294] -searches; from seeing a location with smoke- — T.
[295] in inference for oneself
section: 8. There is no fixed order for the statements of reason and example in the logical sentence.

body.text: atra sādhanavākye na kevalaṃ pratijñādiprayogo na yuktaḥ paropagataḥ [S. 77a.] `pūrvaṃ hetuḥ prayoktavyaḥ paścād dṛṣṭāntaḥ' iti kramaniyamo 'pi na kaścit | kutaḥ? sarvathā yadi pūrvaṃ hetuḥ paścād vyāptiḥ atha pūrvaṃ vyāptiḥ paścāt pakṣadharmaḥ prayujyate, tathāpi gamakatvāt |
body.translated_text: Here, in the proof-statement, not only is the employment of the thesis and so forth improper, [but] the fixed order accepted [by the opponent] — ‘first the reason should be employed, then the example’ — is also not [necessary]. Why? Because in either case — whether first the reason and then the pervasion, or first the pervasion and then the thesis-property — even so, there is indicative power.
[section: 9. Refutation of the threefold employment of the reason.]

body.text: nanu tasya dvidhā prayoga ity ayuktam uktam | yatas trividho hetuḥ -- anvayī vyatirekī anvayavyatirekī cetinaiyāyikāḥ, tatas tasya tridhā prayogaḥ -- sādharmyeṇa vaidharmyeṇa sādharmyavaidharmyābhyāṃ ceti vaktavyam ity ata āha --

children.translated_text: ‘Even in the statement of the connection’ (<s>sambandhavacane ’pi</s>) —

children.text: na kevalaṃ kramaniyamo na yuktaḥ kintu
children.translated_text: not only is the fixed order not proper, but also —
‘there is no difference in meaning at all’ —

children.text: ubhayatrāpi trirūpasadbhāvāt | tataḥ sarva eva hetur anvayavyatirekī, na tv anvayī vyatirekī vā kaścid dhetur astīti bhāvaḥ | tat kutas traividhyaṃ prayogasya syāt? iti manyate | kutaḥ punararthabhedo nāstīti? cet, āha --
children.translated_text: because the three characteristics (<s>trairūpya</s>) are present in both [cases]. Therefore, every reason is indeed positive-and-negative (<s>anvayavyatirekin</s>); there is no reason that is merely positive-only or negative-only — this is the purport. So how could there be a threefold employment? — so he thinks. But why is there no difference in meaning? — if asked, he says:
‘In both ways’ (<s>ubhayathā</s>) —

children.text: sādharmyeṇa vaidharmyeṇa ca prayoge yady api vidhipratiṣedharūpatayā dharmabhedaḥ [T. 256b.] pratīyate tathāpi
children.translated_text: in employment through similarity and through dissimilarity, although a difference in the properties is perceived in the form of positive and negative [statements], nevertheless,
‘of precisely that nature’ (<s>tadbhāvasyaiva</s>) —
of precisely the essential-nature-hood (<s>svabhāvatā</s>) of the proving property in the provable — through the employment by similarity and dissimilarity —
‘the declaration’ (<s>khyāpanāt</s>) [is made].

children.text:
|
  nanu sādharmyaprayoge hetubhāve [S. 77b.] sādhyasya bhāvaḥ, vaidharmye ca sādhyābhāve hetvabhāvaḥ śabdād avagamyate, na tādātmyam | tat kim ucyate `tadbhāvasyaiva khyāpanāt'? ity ata āha --
children.translated_text: But in the employment through similarity, the existence of the provable when the reason is present, and in [the employment through] dissimilarity, the absence of the reason when the provable is absent, is understood from the words — not identity (<s>tādātmya</s>). So why is it said ‘because of the declaration of precisely that nature’? To this he says:
‘For it is not [the case]’ (<s>na hi</s>) —

children.text: ityādi | yadi sādharmyaprayoge tadbhāvo nākṣipyeta tadā sādhanasya
children.translated_text: and so forth. If the identity were not entailed in the employment through similarity, then, of the proof —
‘when that which is not of its nature exists’ (<s>atatsvabhāvasya bhāve</s>) —
why —
invariably —
necessarily —
‘would the provable exist’?

children.text:
? | kādācit kas tu bhavatu nāma? | `yat kṛtakaṃ tad anityam' ity ekāntabhāvaś ca hetau sati sādhyasya vyāptyā sādharmyaprayoge 'bhidhīyate | sa[296]ca tādātmyam antareṇānarthāntarasya na sambhavatīti sāmarthyāt tadākṣipati |
  katham ivātatsvabhāvasya bhāve na ekāntenānyabhāva iti āha --
children.translated_text:
Let it exist only occasionally! And the invariable existence of the provable when the reason is present is stated in the employment through similarity by means of pervasion (<s>vyāpti</s>). And that [invariable existence] is not possible without identity (<s>tādātmya</s>), since otherwise it would be an irrelevant thing (<s>anārthāntara</s>) — therefore by implication it entails that.
How is it that when what is not of its nature exists, the other does not invariably exist? He says:
‘When being-produced (<s>kṛtakatve</s>) [is present]’ —

children.text:
ty ādi | yadi prayatnānantarīyakatvām antareṇāpi kṛtakatvasya bhāvād atatsvabhāvatvam anityatve[297]'py ayam eva vṛttāntaḥ | tataś ca tādātmyavirahāt prayatnānantarīyakatvasyānityatvenānvayo na syāt, tannivṛttau[298]vā nivṛttir[299]iti kathaṃ tatas[300]tat[301][S. 78a.] {p. 74.1} pratīyate? | naiṣa doṣaḥ, prayatnānantarīyakapadārthasvabhāvasyaivānityatvasya[302]tena[303]sādhanāt, tatra ca tādātmyasadbhāvād anvayavyatirekāv anivāritau anityatvakṛtakatvamātrāpekṣayā[304][T. 257a.] tu tādātmyaviraho 'syābhihita[305]iti |
 nanv agninivṛttāv atatsvabhāvasyāpi dhūmasya nivṛttir dṛṣṭā 'nvayaś cety āha --
children.translated_text:
and so forth. If being-produced is not of the same nature as impermanence, because being-produced exists even without being-a-product-of-effort (<s>prayatnānantariyakatva</s>), the same situation [applies] to impermanence as well. And therefore, due to the absence of identity, there would be no positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>) of being-a-product-of-effort with impermanence, nor negative concomitance — the cessation [of impermanence] upon the cessation of that — so how could that [impermanence] be cognized from that [being-a-product-of-effort]? This is not a fault, because what is proved [as impermanent] is precisely the entity whose own nature is being-a-product-of-effort; and since identity is present there, positive and negative concomitance are unavoidable. But with reference merely to impermanence and being-produced [in general], the absence of identity has been stated.
But [the objection:] upon the cessation of fire, the cessation of smoke, which is not of its essential nature, is also observed, as well as positive concomitance — he says:
‘Of the effect’ (<s>kāryasya</s>) —

children.text: iti | anvayavyatirekayor hi pratibandho nibandhanam, tena tayoḥ vyāpteḥ, tadabhāve tayor apy abhāvāt | tatrārthāntarasya dhūmasyāgnau
children.translated_text: thus. For of positive and negative concomitance, the necessary connection (<s>pratibandha</s>) is the ground; through that, there is pervasion of the two; in its absence, there would be absence of both. Therein, of smoke, which is a different entity from fire —
‘the necessary connection characterized as origination from that is the basis of positive and negative concomitance’ —

children.text: astīti bhavetāṃ tau[306]| yatra tv anarthāntarasya tāv ucyete tatrāvaśyaṃ tādātmyena bhavitavyam ity abhiprāyaḥ | atrodāharaṇam
children.translated_text: thus those two would obtain. But where positive and negative concomitance are stated of what is not a different entity, there must necessarily be identity — this is the intent. Here the illustration:

children.text: yathā-- anayor eva kṛtakatvaprayatnānantarīyakatvayor viparyayeṇa naikanivṛttāv
children.translated_text: ‘For example — of these very two, being-produced and being-a-product-of-effort, conversely, upon the cessation of one —
the cessation of the other’ —

children.text: -- `yat prayatnānantarīyakaṃ na bhavati [S. 78b.] tat kṛtakam api na bhavati' ity evaṃrūpā | yata evaṃ tasmād anvayavyatirekayor yathālakṣaṇaṃ hetubhāve sādhyasyāvaśyaṃ bhāvaḥ, sādhyābhāve ca hetor avaśyam abhāvaḥ ity eko 'pi sādharmyamukheṇa vaidharmyamukheṇa vā prayukto dvitīyam ākṣipati, svavyāpakapratibandhākṣepāt[309], tasyāpi[310]cetareṇa[311]vyāpteḥ | tasmād ubhayatra trairūpyapratīter
children.translated_text: — [takes the form:] ‘what is not a product of effort is also not produced’ — of such a form. Since this is so, therefore, as the definition states, when the reason is present, the provable must necessarily be present, and when the provable is absent, the reason must necessarily be absent. Thus, even one [mode] employed through the door of similarity or through the door of dissimilarity entails the other, because of the entailment of the necessary connection with its own pervader, and because that [pervader] too is pervaded by the other [mode]. Therefore, from the cognition of the three characteristics in both [modes] —

children.text: ekasya śabde(bda)to 'parasyārthata iti sambandhavacane 'pi prayoga eva vidhimukhena pratiṣedhamukhena vā bhidyate nārtha iti siddhiṃ tatas tasya dvidhā prayogaḥ sādharmyeṇa vaidharmyeṇa ca | na tu sādharmyavaidharmyābhyām api, tadarthasyānyatareṇaiva [T. 257b.] prakāśanāt |
children.translated_text: ‘one [is established] verbally, the other by implication’ — thus even in the statement of the connection, only the employment differs — through the door of positive [statement] or through the door of negative [statement] — not the meaning. Therefore it is established: there is a twofold employment — through similarity and through dissimilarity. But not through both similarity and dissimilarity, since the meaning of that [combined mode] is made manifest by either one alone.

children.text: sarvo hetur anvayavyatireky eva vastuto na kaścid anvayī vyatirekī vā nāmety etad upasaṃharann āha --
children.translated_text: Concluding that every reason is in reality positive-and-negative (<s>anvayavyatirekin</s>), and none is merely positive-only or negative-only, he says:
‘Therefore, in one [mode]’ (<s>iti naikatrā</s>) —
through the door of positive concomitance or through the door of negative concomitance, in the proof-statement —
‘of the two’ (<s>dvayoḥ</s>) —
of positive and negative concomitance —
‘the employment’ —
direct verbal statement — is accepted,
‘because of pointlessness’ (<s>vaiyarthyāt</s>) —

children.text:
pratītapratyāyane prayojanābhāvāt |
  {p. 75.1} tām evārthato 'parasya pratītiṃ sphuṭayann āha --
children.translated_text:
because of the absence of purpose in making known what is [already] cognized.
Making explicit the cognition of the other [mode] by implication, he says:
‘By being of that nature’ (<s>tatsvabhāvatayā</s>) —

children.text: ityādi | yadi tatsvabhāvatayā sādhyena hetor anvayaḥ sidhyati tata eva
children.translated_text: and so forth. If the positive concomitance of the reason with the provable is established by being of the same nature, then from that very [fact] —
‘the absence [of the reason] in the absence of that [provable] is also established’ —
because what is of the same nature as that cannot possibly exist when that is absent, due to its having no self-nature [independent of that].
‘Likewise’ (<s>tathā</s>) —
when the absence of the proof upon the absence of the provable, by being of that nature —
is established —
and —
when that is the case, from that very [fact], of the reason with the provable —
‘the positive concomitance is also established.’
