body.text: section: 24. kāraṇānekatve 'pi kāryasyaikatvaṃ sāmagrībhede ca kāryabhedaḥ |
body.translated_text: Section: 24. The unity of the effect despite multiplicity of causes, and the difference of effects from difference of assemblages

children.translated_text: there is difference of the effect,

children.text:
anekatvaṃ tadā pratibandhābhāvād anekāntaḥ | na ca tadabhyupagamyata iti na kācit kṣatiḥ |
  atha sāmagrīlakṣaṇasya kāraṇasya bhedaḥ sāmagryantarād vailakṣaṇyaṃ kāryasyāpi bhedo 'tatkāraṇebhyo bhinnasvabhāvatocyate | tadā[402]tasyeha[403]bhāvāt kathaṃ na kāraṇabhedāt kāryabhedaḥ syāt? iti abhiprāyavatā `na'[404]kāraṇabhedāt kāryabhedo na syāt | kutaḥ? |
children.translated_text: i.e., multiplicity — then, because of the absence of invariable concomitance (<s>pratibandha</s>), this is <s>anekānta</s>. But since that is not what we accept, there is no harm. | Now, if the difference of the cause characterized as an assemblage — its dissimilarity from another assemblage — and the difference of the effect too, i.e., its having a distinct essential nature from the effects of other causes, is asserted — then, since that [difference] is present here, how could there not be a difference of effects from a difference of causes? With this intention, [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>] has stated 'No' — there is no [case where] from the difference of causes there is no difference of effects. Why?
'Each according to its own nature' —

children.text:
ity ādy abhihitam |
  ubhayaṃ[405]caitat kāryeṣu pramāṇaparidṛṣṭam iti darśayann āha --
children.translated_text: and so forth has been stated. | And showing that both [principles] are observed through <s>pramāṇa</s> in effects, he says:
'Just as' —

children.text: ityādi | mṛtpiṇḍādibhyo hi bhavato ghaṭasya na kāraṇānekatve 'py anekarūpatā | nā'pi sāmagryantarajanyād abhinnasvabhāvatety udāharaṇārthaḥ | tatra [T. 272b.] sāmagryantarajanyāt tāvad bhedaṃ darśayati --
children.translated_text: and so forth. For from the clay-lump and the like, for [your] pot — despite the multiplicity of causes — there is no manifold nature. Nor is there an identical essential nature with what is produced by another assemblage — this is the purpose of the example. There, he first shows the difference from what is produced by another assemblage:
'From a clay-lump' —

children.text:
ityādi | iha mṛtpiṇḍakulālasūtrāṇi {p. 96.1} vyagrasvabhāvāni kāraṇāntarasahitāni iṣṭakādilakṣaṇāni tadanyajanyebhyo bhinnasvabhāvāni [S. 98b.] yāni kāryāṇi sādhayanti tebhyo vilakṣaṇam eva samagrāṇi ghaṭātmakaṃ kāryaṃ janayanti | tathā hi -- kulālādinirapekṣo mṛtpiṇḍaḥ tadanyajanyād vṛkṣāder vilakṣaṇam evopādānabhāvena mṛdātmakaṃ kāryaṃ janayan dṛṣṭaḥ | kulālādisahito 'pi tadātmakam eva ghaṭam | tatkāraṇāhitaviśeṣaś ca kevalamṛtpiṇḍād bhinnasvabhāvatayā tatkāryād apīṣṭakāder vilakṣaṇam eva karoti | evaṃ kulālādikam
api tadanyopādānasahitaṃ sahakāribhāvena yatkāryam karoti tadvilakṣaṇam eva mṛtpiṇḍasahitaṃ tatkāranāhitaviśeṣaṃ ghaṭātmakaṃ kāryaṃ janayatīti samudāyārthaḥ | tatra mṛtpiṇḍād bhinnaḥ svabhāvo ghaṭasya ye tadanyopādānakāraṇatayā mṛtsvabhāvā na bhavanti vṛkṣādayas tebhyo bhavati |
children.translated_text: and so forth. Here, the clay-lump, potter, and thread — having distinct essential natures — together with other causes produce effects characterized as bricks and the like, having distinct essential natures from those produced by other [assemblages]. Different from those, [the same causes] in their complete state produce the pot-natured effect. {p. 96.1} For thus: the clay-lump, independent of the potter and the like, is seen as producing — in the capacity of material cause — an earth-natured effect different from trees and the like produced by other [causes]. And even when conjoined with the potter and the like, [it produces] a pot of that very [earth] nature. And the distinguishing feature imparted by those causes makes [the effect] of a different essential nature from the mere clay-lump, and hence different from [the effects of the clay-lump alone] such as bricks and the like. Similarly, the potter and the like, conjoined with other material causes, in the capacity of cooperative cause — whatever effect they produce — different from that, when conjoined with the clay-lump, they produce a pot-natured effect with the distinguishing feature imparted by those causes. This is the purport. There, the distinct essential nature of the pot from the clay-lump arises from those [causes] that, not being material causes of other [things], do not have earth-nature — such as trees and the like.
'From the potter' —

children.translated_text: Therefore, a pot produced from the triad of causes that have entered [into its production] is born with a nature that is indeed different from each individual effect and from each pair of effects produced by something other than that [complete aggregate]. Thus, due to the difference in the aggregate (<s>sāmagrī</s>), the effects are indeed mutually distinct, having non-intermixed natures — and so the non-confusion of the specific effects with the operations [of their causes] is established. And because of its non-production in parts, [the effect] conforming to the presence and absence of each individual cause in its particular state — even when produced by each individual [cause], it is actually examined by those who contemplate reality (<s>tattvacintaka</s>) as 'this is produced by that,' since a particular [feature] not seen in the proximity of a homogeneous alternative cause of that individual [cause] is seen in the proximity of the other. Because those who desire a specific effect undertake the employment of multiple causes for the purpose of assembling the aggregate of causes capable of producing the desired effect through the series of effects in which they mutually contribute assistance. Since thus, due to the difference in the aggregate, the effects characterized as bricks-wheel-undivided-pot and divided-pot are indeed different,

parasparātmatāviraheṇa kāraṇena saṃsthānaviśeṣeṇa mṛt na pratibhāseta, na mṛtsvabhāvena ca saṃsthānaviśeṣaḥ, yathā tadanyarūpeṇa | na[413]hi yo yasya svabhāvo na bhavati sa tenātmanā svagrāhiṇi jñāne pratibhāsate, rūparasavat; jñānaṃ vā tadrūpavikalārthasāmarthyenotpadyamānaṃ tadrūpam anukartuṃ yuktam, {p. 98.1} bhrāntatāprasaṅgena tadvaśād arthavyavasthānābhāvaprasakteḥ | tasmāt mṛtsaṃsthānayor ekātmataiveti [T. 274a.] na kāraṇānekatvāt kāryasyānekātmakatā aikāntikī, yato bhinnasvabhāvebhyaś cakṣurādibhyaḥ sahakāribhyaḥ ekakāryotpattivirodhād
ekarūpatayā teṣāṃ sādhāraṇaikakāryakriyā, bhinnarūpatayā vā sādhāraṇakāryakaraṇam iyeta | [S. 100b.] etac caikasāmagryapekṣayaikakāryakartṛtvam ucyate | paramārthatas tu tatsāmagryantarggatānāṃ sajātīyasyā 'pi kṣaṇāntarasyārambhāt sāmagryantarāvayavatvena ca kāryāntarasyāpi yathā ekapratyayajanitaṃ kiñcid ekaṃ nāsti tathā 'nekapratyayajanitam apīti kāraṇānekatvāt kāryānekatvopagame 'pi na kācit kṣatiḥ | tata ekakāryāpekṣayā 'nekatvaprasañjane sandigdhavyatirekatā, sāmānyena sādhane siddhasādhyateti ca |
children.translated_text: by the absence of mutual identity — because of the reason [that] configuration-specific [and] clay would not appear [together], nor would the configuration-specific [appear] as having clay-nature, just as [it does not appear] in a form belonging to something else. For that which is not the essential nature of something does not appear with that nature in a cognition that apprehends it, like color and taste [which are distinct]. Or a cognition arising from the capacity of an object deficient in that form would [not] be fit to replicate that form, because of the absurd consequence of being erroneous, and because of the consequence of there being no determination of objects based on that [cognition]. Therefore, clay and configuration have a single identity — and so from the multiplicity of causes, the multiple-selfhood of the effect is not invariable (<s>aikāntikī</s>). Because from the auxiliary causes — eye and the like — which have different natures, there would be a contradiction in the production of a single effect, [so] either their common single-effect production operates through their having a single form, or their common-effect production through having different forms should be accepted. And this unity of effect-production is stated with respect to a single aggregate. But in ultimate reality, since even a homogeneous [cause] of a subsequent moment, being within that aggregate, initiates [an effect], and since as a component of another aggregate it also [initiates] another effect — just as there is nothing singular produced by a single condition, so too nothing [is produced] by multiple conditions — therefore, even if multiplicity of effect is accepted due to multiplicity of cause, there is no harm. Hence, in positing multiplicity with respect to a single effect, there is uncertain exclusion (<s>sandigdhavyatirekatā</s>), and in proving through the universal, the fallacy of proving what is already established.

And this unchanging permanence (<s>kūṭasthanityatā</s>) is not possible in substance either, or this transformation-permanence (<s>pariṇāmanityatā</s>) — because substance apart from modes is unestablished, since it, though meeting the conditions of apprehensibility, is not apprehended as distinct from them. The notion of 'substance' among those modes that produce similar effects is [merely] the conceit of the dull-witted. But it is not apprehended as different from them.
Difference of effect, however, is unestablished for us, because it is precisely certain among the colors and the like that are the agents of those effects. Nevertheless, accepting [the opponent's view] for the sake of argument, we say: effect is of two kinds — occurring at different times and occurring at the same time. Of these, the first could be a basis for difference if it were possible here. But it is not possible, because property and property-bearer are simultaneous. And same-time [effect-difference] is inconclusive for [establishing] difference in the effect, because it is possible in cloths and the like which undergo differentiated modifications. For cloths and the like, undergoing differentiated modifications, are observed to produce multiple effects. And they do not differ in their property-bearer form, because there is no contradiction in a single [entity] performing multiple actions. For here the cause itself does not assume the nature of the effect, such that by accepting the single cause-nature's having the form of one effect, it would not assume the nature of another effect due to the absence of that other form. Rather, something unprecedented, previously non-existent, coming into being in the presence of something, is its effect. There, when object, sense-faculty, and mental attention — which have distinct forms contributed by mutual material causation — are in proximity, and in the existence of a distinguished and non-distinguished moment, the acceptance of multiple actions is not contradicted, since for each [cause] the conformity to the presence and absence of that [particular state] [is observed]. For even in a single action, the basis for it is precisely its being conditioned by the presence of that [state]. And that [condition] is the same even in multiple actions.
But [the opponent objects]: since in the proximity of those [causes], the effect characterized as cognition is possible, their nature as producers of that is ascertained, because the cause's nature as producer is determined relative to the nature of the effect. Therefore, from those whose essential nature is to produce cognition, how is it possible for each individually to produce another effect? Or, if that is [their nature], they would have the nature of producing something other [than cognition]. And consequently they would not produce cognition at all, since they would have the nature of producing something else.
This is not a fault, because they have the nature of producing multiple effects. Thus: in that state, each of them has the nature of producing distinguished homogeneous and other moments, since we observe the existence of those [moments] immediately following the existence of those [causes]. There, the statement 'they have the nature of producing cognition alone' excludes the nature of not producing that, since that alone is the counter-correlate — not the nature of producing something else. And from this there would not be multiple-selfhood of those [causes], because a single excellence of self is the cause of multiple effects. For a thing designated by the word 'many' based on exclusion from the opposite relative to something else does not actually become manifold in form, since a single self, distinguished with respect to each [exclusion], is so designated. Just as: 'form is visible and tangible.' For here the word-meanings are not based on difference of essential nature, since the absurd consequence of absence of co-referentiality [would follow]. If [one argues]: 'there is no fault, because the grounds for those [designations] are present in a single [entity]' — no, because those [grounds], not depending on the assistance of that single [entity], are not suited to that [co-location]. Or, if there is [such] dependence, how could a single [entity] not produce multiple effects? If [one argues]: 'because it contributes through multiple selves' — no,
because of the absurd consequence that the fault of absence of co-referentiality would remain the same. And we do not perceive through direct perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) any difference of self in blue and the like. Nor is there an inference of difference of self merely from difference of effect, because of the absence of a necessary connection (<s>pratibandha</s>), because of the absence of a means of valid cognition (<s>pramāṇa</s>) to ascertain that. Because even entities that produce multiple effects, like lamps and the like, are apprehended through direct perception as having a single self. Nor [is it established] through inference, because there too, there is no invalidating cognition against the contrary [view]. And if one does not accept that a single [entity] performs multiple actions, then the observed invariable co-occurrence of specific qualities of color, taste, smell, and touch — which is ascertained by <s>pramāṇa</s> — would not obtain. Because invariable co-occurrence of things having different causes is impossible. [If one argues:] 'even of the grounds for those [qualities], which have births not dependent on that single cause, invariable co-existence is impossible' — [then the reply is:] 'the invariable co-occurrence in a single [locus] is due to their having the nature of a single property-bearer' — no, because it is precisely the multiple-naturedness of a single [entity] that is in question. And for one who experiences single-naturedness through the manifold, the impossibility of avoiding multiplicity [in the same way] as with that [manifold] — otherwise, how would the difference between property and property-bearer not be invariable? Thus: with respect to that self which is put forward [as the basis] and [on the basis of which] it is determined 'this is the property-bearer and these are the modes' — if there is difference of that [self], then there is simply difference.
Nor would there be single-effect production from multiple [causes]. For object, sense-faculty, and mental attention, not depending on the mutual material-cause assistance, are not reasonably capable of jointly initiating a single effect. And no single [cause] ever produces something entirely on its own. Consequently, the causal relation everywhere would collapse, since neither a multiple [cause] nor a single [cause] has single or multiple action, and there is no other alternative.
Nor is the universe without a cause, because of the regularity of place, time, and nature. Therefore, the invariable co-occurrence of entities is due to their births being dependent on a single aggregate, or [there is] the regularity of single-effect production. And therefore, when a moment of one's own continuum and the material cause from another simultaneously contribute, how could a single [entity] not produce multiple effects? Hence, how could difference be supposed from difference of effect? And one who, while asserting the single-naturedness of substance and modes, rejects the multiple-effect production of a single [entity] — how is he not insane? — since essential nature itself is reality, and otherwise the absurd consequence of it being without essential nature [would follow]. And since substance and modes have a single essential nature, the difference of their effects is based on a single reality — so one who asserts difference from difference of effect is clearly shameless (<s>ahrīka</s>) indeed and deserves to be disregarded.

body.translated_text: But if there is single-naturedness of clay and configuration-specific, the <s>Ahrīka</s> and others accept difference due to difference of number and the like — then how could this serve as an example for the unity of what is produced from multiple conditions? For everywhere, of substance (<s>dravya</s>) and mode (<s>paryāya</s>), difference is accepted due to difference of number, name, defining characteristic, and effect; and non-difference due to non-difference of place, time, and essential nature — as with a pot and its color and the like. Thus: one pot, many colors and the like — this is difference of number. 'Pot,' 'colors and the like' — this is difference of name. The substance-like is characterized by continuity (<s>anuvṛtti</s>) and is permanent, while the distinguishing [modes] are characterized by exclusion (<s>vyāvṛtti</s>) and are momentary; but for the <s>Jaiminīya</s>, some persist for a period of time — this is difference of defining characteristic. Water is carried by means of a pot, while attachment to objects [arises] through colors and the like — this is difference of effect. Thus everywhere, of substance and mode, there is difference through number and the like, but non-difference through place and the like — so how, given the partial difference of clay and configuration, could there not be multiplicity of the effect produced by clay and potter? Just as there is unity, so too by those two, [the effect] is produced with non-different nature — [so one might argue:] that which has multiple causes is indeed multiple, while that which is one is produced by auxiliary causes having non-different form and thus has a single cause — so there is no deviation [from the rule]. This is not correct. When difference in essential nature is not accepted, difference [established] otherwise is unproven, and the refutation of single-effect production from multiple [causes] is not overcome. Or if difference in essential nature is accepted, the non-appearance of clay and configuration through mutual non-identity — [i.e.,] through configuration-specific and clay-nature-specific [not appearing together] — is unavoidable. For if there is no difference in essential nature between property and property-bearer, then even from difference of number and the like there is no difference at all. For numbers and the like, which are of another's form, even when differentiating, are not capable of overriding the non-difference that is of [the thing's] own nature. First, difference of number is incapable, since even in a single substance, usage with plurality is observed — as in '<s>gurava</s>' (heavy ones, teachers). And since the plural is not invariably absent [for a single substance], colors and the like are not the ground here, for if colors and the like were the ground, then '<s>guruḥ</s>' (one heavy/teacher) would never occur in the singular. If [one argues]: 'possibly the mere property-bearer-form is intended as the referent' — no, because in intending it as one, there would be the absurd consequence of non-cognition of entirety and heaviness. And since in the class-word '<s>vrīhayaḥ</s>' (rice grains), neither the property-bearer nor its colors and the like are denoted, there is no response. And since a thing possessing both forms is the referent of the word '<s>guru</s>,' how could there be an intention of the property-bearer-form alone as one? Therefore, since '<s>eko guruḥ</s>' (one teacher/heavy one) is observed as co-referential, the modes too are objects of the singular number. And they differ in their mode-form. So how could difference be established from difference of number? Name too is dependent on convention (<s>saṅketa</s>). And that [convention] operates dependent on will — so how could there be real difference from that? Since difference of names is observed even in a single [entity], how could it be a ground for difference? As in: <s>Indra</s>, <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Purandara</s>. If [one argues:] 'from burning, from being able, and from destroying, a difference of powers is understood' — no, because the whole [entity] is the agent of the effect. For it is not the power alone that burns, is able, and destroys. What then? The property-bearer-form too [does so], because of the acceptance of their having a single essential nature, and because co-referentiality of the words denoting those [powers] with '<s>śaknotyādi</s>' (is able, etc.) is not observed. And because [those usages] are objects of unfailing cognitive apprehension, the supposition of figurative usage (<s>upacāra</s>) is not appropriate. And for those modes that have no correspondence with reality whatsoever — what is there to say? Difference of defining characteristic too is not a valid ground, because it is unestablished. For no single entity is ever established as continuing [unchanged] anywhere. Thus: the permanent substance is not accepted by <s>Ahrīka</s> and others as eternal in the sense of being unchangingly permanent (<s>kūṭasthanityatā</s>), because of the acceptance of transformation-permanence (<s>pariṇāmanityatā</s>). And that [permanence] is through the continuity of the series of prior and subsequent moments. For there is no annihilation of it in that form, as there is of modes — the modes alone are destroyed in their mode-form, not the substance — thus it is accepted as permanent. Not

body.translated_text: The <s>Vaiśeṣika</s> too, who asserts that a single substance is the inherent cause (<s>samavāyikāraṇa</s>) of substance, quality, and action, and that a single action is the efficient cause of conjunction, disjunction, and <s>saṃskāra</s> — [yet] rejects the multiple-effect production of a single [entity] — is refuted by the very revolt of his own doctrine. And here, difference of power is not the basis, for how could these powers, which are independent of assistance from that single [entity], be the substrata of determinate objects? Or [how could they] not extend to individuals without parts? Therefore, from whatever excellence of self of this [entity] there is the contribution of multiple powers, from that very [excellence] there is also multiple-effect production — and enough with this overly extensive discussion.

children.translated_text: And variegatedness is having manifold essential natures. And whence is there unity when there is manifold essential nature? It is merely that, even in [what is actually] multiplicity, because of observing a single effect among many, this is a delusion of those with dull minds — like [the usage of] 'army' and the like — caused by observing a single designation.

children.text: tad evaṃ tāvat pratyekam ahetutvaṃ deśakālasvabhāvānām ekatvaprasādhane | samuditānām api vyabhicāritvaṃ paryāyaiḥ | tathā hi -- paryāyā abhinnadeśakālasvabhāvāś ca paryāyarūpeṇa ca bhidyante pūrvoktāc ca dharmadharmiṇor niṣedhān[452]nobhayavādasambhava iti |
children.translated_text: Thus, so far, the incapacity of place, time, and essential nature individually to establish unity [has been shown]. And the deviation [from the rule] even of [these three] collectively [has been shown] through the modes. For thus: the modes, though non-different in place, time, and essential nature, differ in their mode-form; and because of the previously stated negation of property and property-bearer, the both-fold doctrine (<s>ubhayavāda</s>) is untenable.

body.translated_text: And the non-difference that is accepted on the basis of non-difference of place, time, and essential nature is also untenable. For thus: even when place and time are non-different, color, taste, smell, and touch differ in their mode-form — so how is non-difference established from that? And if the essential nature is the dual form of continuity (<s>anuvṛtti</s>) and exclusion (<s>vyāvṛtti</s>) for both substance and mode individually, then there would be two entities like a pot and a cloth, not a single thing with two forms — so how from that could non-difference be established? And it is not correct that continuity and exclusion constitute the essential nature, because those two depend on that which continues and that which is excluded. Therefore, another essential nature of that which continues and that which is excluded must be stated, but it is not that their very continuity and exclusion is their essential nature, because an entity-qua-entity depends on that which possesses it. For memory is not the essential nature of the rememberer. And if continuity and exclusion are the essential nature, then a difference of essential nature from the defining characteristic must be stated. If [one says:] 'the essential nature is earth-nature and the like' — even here, if non-difference means similarity, then precisely difference obtains, because similarity subsists in similar [but distinct] things. And so there would be just two entities, not a single thing with two forms. But if unity — absence of a second form — is what is accepted as non-difference, then how is there dual-formedness? For by the word 'form' (<s>rūpa</s>) here, essential nature is denoted. And if that is one, how is there dual-formedness? For these are contradictory — single-naturedness and dual-formedness. But again, if unity in essential nature is not accepted, how then is that called 'one' while being many? Not because of being produced from a single cause, since everywhere the difference of causes is established through the distinction of material and efficient causes. Nor because of being the agent of a single effect, since even for a single [entity], the acceptance of a difference of effects — those with distinct transformation and those without distinct transformation — [is made]. Nor is there unity merely because of being the referent of a single designation, since even for a single [entity], multiple synonyms are possible. And since all things — whether conventionally designated or not — are fit [to be so designated], and since the fitness for being the referent of a single designation is sometimes impossible [for some things], and since difference of powers implies difference of objects — this has been addressed when refuting [the argument] that difference [arises] from difference of designation. Nor is it one because of being the object of a single cognition, since even from a single [thing] multiple cognitions arise. For thus: many observe the rising of the moon [T. 278a.] — {p. 104.1} how is its unity accepted? And since many things can be the object of a single cognition, there would be the absurd consequence that blue, yellow, and the like are one. In every way, this does not hold — namely, the dual-formedness of what is one. Cognition, however, arising as a reflection of blue, is made known as specifically delimited by the exclusion of the appearance of yellow and the like — but it does not in reality have two forms. | Now, if because substance and mode are fused together like <s>Narasiṃha</s> (the man-lion), it is called one due to having a variegated form (<s>śabalarūpa</s>) — that is untenable, because the variegated form of <s>Narasiṃha</s> is not established. For he is of the form of an aggregate of many atoms, and those atoms individually do not have the form of <s>Narasiṃha</s>; the upper part has the lion-form and the lower part has the man-form; and he would be a different species entirely from man and lion, not one of variegated form. For a multi-colored form is what is called 'variegated.'

'When non-difference is not abandoned' —
'the difference would be merely the product of conceptual construction (<s>kalpanā</s>).' |
'Of that [construction]' —
'if it is false, then there would be falsity in [the claim of] non-difference too.' || 20 ||

body.translated_text: 'Of things whose nature is mutual absence, the cause of the absence of one is the other.' |

body.text: ekabhāvo yatas tasmān naikasya syād dvirūpatā|| 21 ||
body.translated_text: 'Since their being one is due to that [mutual absence], for what is one there cannot be dual-formedness.' || 21 ||

children.text: tasya bhedo 'pi tābhyāṃced yadi yenātmanāca te |
children.translated_text: 'If its difference too is from those two — by which nature they [are],' |

body.translated_text: 'the property-bearer, the property, and something other than those — if the difference is of that nature,' || 43 ||
'then in that case too, yet another difference is imagined beyond those.' |
'For the purpose of establishing their non-difference, the absurd consequence would arise as before.' || 44 ||
'And property-bearer-hood of that would thus obtain, because of the other two being dependent on that.'

children.translated_text: 'Something else entirely' —
and so forth.
For configuration (<s>saṃsthāna</s>)

children.text: hy avayavasanniveśa ucyate | sa ca saṃyogalakṣaṇatvād guṇarūpaḥ |
children.translated_text: is said to be the arrangement of parts. And that, being characterized as conjunction (<s>saṃyoga</s>), is of the nature of a quality (<s>guṇa</s>).
'Therefore' —
its otherness from the earth-substance

children.text: dravyaguṇayor asaṃkīrṇasvabhāvatvāt[473]| tena yadi mṛtpiṇḍasya mṛdātmatāyāṃ vyāpāraḥ kulālasya tatsaṃsthānaviśeṣe kathyate, tadā tayor atyantabhedāt kāraṇānekatvāt kāryānekatvaṃ prāptam iti | siddhāntavādy āha --
children.translated_text: because of the unmixed essential nature of substance and quality. Therefore, if the operation of the clay-lump is said to be in its earth-nature, and of the potter in the specific configuration of that — then, because of the absolute difference of those two, from the multiplicity of causes, multiplicity of the effect would follow. The <s>Siddhāntavādin</s> says:
'It has been stated regarding this' —

children.text: iti | mṛtsaṃsthānayoḥ svabhāvabhede dūṣaṇam uktam {p. 108.1} mṛtsaṃsthānayor aparasparātmatayā ityādikam iti na saṃsthānasya mṛddravyād anyatvam | tato mṛtpiṇḍopādānāhitātiśayena tatkāryakṣaṇasahakāriṇā kulālena tadupādānopakṛtātmanā tatkāryakṣaṇasahakāriṇā mṛtpiṇḍena ca pratyekaṃ sakalam eva mṛtsaṃsthānātmakaṃ kāryaṃ kriyata iti na kāraṇānekatve 'py anekatvam asya | atraivopacayahetum āha --
children.translated_text: thus. The refutation of the difference in essential nature between earth and configuration has been stated — {p. 108.1} 'by the mutual non-identity of earth and configuration' and so forth — therefore configuration is not other than the earth-substance. Hence, by the potter as cooperative cause of that effect-moment, who is assisted by the additional feature imparted by the clay-lump as material cause, and by the clay-lump assisted by that material-cause contribution as cooperative cause of that effect-moment — by each individually, the entire effect having the nature of earth-configuration is produced. Thus, even with the multiplicity of causes, there is no multiplicity of this [effect]. Here he states the reason for the accumulation [of the argument]:
'Moreover' —
and so forth. That configuration which belongs to the pot —
'if from that' —
'of earth' —
'were different' —

children.text: tadā kulālaḥ pṛthag eva kim iti na karoti? | na hi bhinnānām āvaśyakam apṛthakkaraṇam, kulālaś cānvayavyatirekābhyāṃ tasya saṃsthānasya guṇātmanaḥ kāraṇatayā gamyata iti
children.translated_text: then why does the potter not produce [it] separately? For there is no necessity that distinct [things] be produced non-separately. And the potter is understood through co-presence and co-absence as the cause of that configuration, which is of the nature of a quality — therefore,
'he separately too' —
'that' —
'from the effect.' |
The opponent says:
'A quality' — and so forth.
'A substance possessing qualities; [a quality] is not a cause in conjunctions and disjunctions, [being] non-independent' —
VaiSū 1.1.16

children.text: iti guṇalakṣaṇāt sarvadā [S. 108b.] guṇo dravyapratantraḥ, sa kathaṃ kadācit pṛthak kriyeta? |vaiśeṣika evabauddhīyaṃcodyam āśaṅkyāha --
children.translated_text: — because of this definition of quality, a quality is always dependent on substance. How then could it ever be produced separately? | The <s>Vaiśeṣika</s> himself, anticipating this Buddhist objection, says:
'The configuration of that' —

children.text: ityādi | yadi svabhāvenaiva tasya guṇātmanaḥ saṃsthānasya
children.translated_text: and so forth. If that configuration, which is of the nature of a quality, by its very essential nature —
'possessed of action, possessed of quality' —
VaiSū 1.1.15

children.text:
ityādivacanād ādhārasvabhāvaṃ tat mṛddravyaṃ, saṃsthānaṃ vā tathāvidhaṃ kapālādheyātmakaṃ tadā kim iti kulālavyāpāram apekṣate? | svata eva kiṃ na bhavati? iti codakābhiprayaḥ |
  evaṃ codyam āśaṅkyavaiśeṣikaḥparihāram āha --
children.translated_text: — because of such statements, that earth-substance is the substratum by nature, or the configuration is of such a kind, having the nature of being superimposed on the potsherd — then why does it require the operation of the potter? Why does it not arise of its own accord? — this is the intent of the objection. | Anticipating such an objection, the <s>Vaiśeṣika</s> states the resolution:
'No, from that' —

children.text: ityādi | yat tat mṛddravyaṃ pṛthuvudhnodarādyākāraṃ ca saṃsthānaṃ tayor yaḥ sambandha ādhārādheyalakṣaṇaḥ tatra yā
children.translated_text: and so forth. That earth-substance and the configuration having the form of broad base, belly, and the like — their relation characterized as substratum and superstratum — therein, the
'fitness' (<s>yogyatā</s>) —
'that' —
'both of these, from the potter' —
'because they obtain [it] from him, therefore' —
'[they] require the potter.'
He states the fault of not requiring the potter:
'Otherwise' —

children.text: yadi tayoḥ parasparasambandhayogyatāyāṃ kulālāpekṣā na syāt tadā svabhāvata eva mṛtpiṇḍasya [T. 281a.] tathāvidhasaṃsthānasambandhayogyatvaṃ bhavet | tasmiṃś ca sati vastuna eva tatsaṃsthānasambandhayogyatālakṣaṇā dharmatā 'stīti kulālasannidheḥ prāg api saṃsthānaviśeṣeṇa sambandhaḥ syād itivaiśeṣikīyaścodyaparihāraḥ |
children.translated_text: if there were no requirement of the potter for the fitness of the mutual relation of those two, then the clay-lump would by its very nature have fitness for the relation with such a configuration. And that being so, since the property-nature of the thing itself — the fitness for the relation with that configuration — exists, even before the proximity of the potter, there would be a relation with the specific configuration — this is the <s>Vaiśeṣika</s>'s resolution of the objection.

body.translated_text: Here, anticipating the <s>Vaiśeṣika</s> position, [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>] says:
because substance and configuration have the nature of being such-and-such an effect — T.
{p. 109.1} [Section: 31. Establishing the non-difference of substance and quality]

children.translated_text: 'Thus' —

children.text: ityādi | yadi [S. 109a.] parasparasambandhayogyatāyāṃ kulālam apekṣate evaṃ
children.translated_text: and so forth. If [the <s>Vaiśeṣika</s>] requires the potter for the fitness of the mutual relation, then
'that fitness of the earth-substance comes from the potter' — this
is entailed. And not —
'of these two' —
of the earth-substance and fitness, of the essential nature —
'difference' —

children.text: nānātvam | yadi hi syāt tadā yogyatāyāḥ dravyāt pṛthakkaraṇaṃ
children.translated_text: i.e., distinctness. For if there were [difference], then the separate production of fitness from substance
'would follow as before.'

children.text: | atha yogyatāyā api yogyapāratantryād apṛthaksiddhiṃ brūyāt tadā tasyā api vastudharmatayaiva prāg api samāveśo mā bhūd iti dravyeṇa saha sambandhayogyatāyā anyā yogyatā kulālād bhavatīty eṣṭavyā | sā 'pi pṛthakkaraṇaprasaṅgā[t] dravyād bhinnasvabhāvā nopagantavyā | pṛthakkaraṇaprasaṅge vā punaḥ sa eva parihāraḥ tadīyaḥ, punas tad evottaram, ity anavasthāprasaṅgād avaśyam abhinnasvabhāvatā kapālātmamamṛddravyayogyatayor abhyupagantavyā | kim evaṃ sati siddhaṃ bhavati? ity ata āha --
children.translated_text: | But if one were to assert the non-separate establishment of fitness too, because of a quality's dependence on that which is qualified — then, lest that [fitness] too, being a property of the real thing, be inherent even before [the potter] — it must be maintained that yet another fitness for the relation of fitness with the substance comes from the potter. And since that [further fitness] too would entail the absurd consequence of separate production, it should not be regarded as having a different essential nature from the substance. Or, in the case of the absurd consequence of separate production, again the same resolution of his [applies], and again the same reply — and because of the absurd consequence of infinite regress (<s>anavasthā</s>), the non-different essential nature of the earth-substance in the form of potsherds and the fitness must necessarily be accepted. What is established when this is so? — to this he says:
'There is, to begin with' —

children.text:
ityādi | mṛtpiṇḍakulālābhyāṃ
kapāladravyasya [S. 109b.] saṃyogaviśeṣasambandhayogyasyārambhāt yadaikasvabhāvatve 'py ekasyānekapratyayopādheyaviśeṣatā tadā siddhaḥ āsmākīnaḥ pakṣaḥ | tataś ca kim asmākaṃ mṛtsaṃsthānayor ekasvabhāvatvasādhanāya atinirbbandhanena? | [T. 281b.] yadi yogyatām apy āśrityānekapratyayajanyatve 'py ekatvāt nānātvaprasaṅgābhāvaḥ sidhyati kāryasya, na kiñcid dravyaguṇavādanirākaraṇeneha prayojanam, anyatraiva tannirākaraṇasya kṛtatvād ity abhiprāyaḥ | nirbandhagrahaṇena ca mṛtsaṃsthānayor aparasparātmatayā saṃsthānamṛtsvabhāvaviśeṣābhyāṃ tayor apratibhāsanaprasaṅgāt ity anayopapattyā sādhitam evānayor ekatvam, yuktyantarāṇāṃ sambhave 'pi tadabhidhānalakṣaṇo nirbbandho na kriyate, prakṛtasiddher anyathā 'pi bhāvād ity ācaṣṭe |
children.translated_text: and so forth. Since from the clay lump and potter, the material substance of the potsherd — which is fit for the connection with a specific conjunction — is produced, when even in a single essential nature, a single [entity] acquires specific features imparted by multiple conditions, then our position is established. And therefore, what need is there for us to insist excessively on proving the single essential nature of clay and configuration? | If, relying on fitness, even when [the effect] is produced by multiple conditions, the absence of the consequence of multiplicity is established due to [its] unity, then there is no purpose here in refuting the substance-and-quality doctrine, since that refutation has been accomplished elsewhere — this is the purport. And by the word 'insistence' [Dharmakīrti indicates that] since by the mutual non-identity of clay and configuration, the consequence that the two would not appear through the configuration-specific and the clay-nature-specific [separately] — by this reasoning, the unity of these two has already been established; even though other arguments are possible, the insistence characterized by stating them is not undertaken, since the matter at hand is established by other means as well — [Arcaṭa] explains. |

body.translated_text: The <s>Siddhāntavādin</s> says:
'thus it is established' — T.

body.text: section: 32. sāmagrībhede kāryabhedasya kāraṇabhede 'pi ca kāryasyaikyasyopasaṃhāraḥ |
body.translated_text: Section: 32. Conclusion regarding the difference of effect from difference of aggregate and the unity of the effect despite difference of cause.

body.text: tad evaṃ sāmagrībhedāt [S. 110a.] sāmagryantarajanyebhyo bhedaḥ sahakāriṇām anekatve 'pi ca kāryasyaikatvam aviruddham iti pratipādya {p. 110.1} upasaṃharann āha --

children.translated_text: 'Therefore the auxiliary causes' (<s>tena sahakāriṇaḥ</s>)

children.text: ityādi | yena -- pratyayāntarapracaye tadvikalasāmagryāḥ sāmagryantaraṃ sampadyate, tac ca pūrvasāmagrījanyād bhinnaṃ kāryāntaram eva janayati; ekasāmagrīvyapadeśaviṣayāṇāṃ ca saha-kāriṇām anekatve 'py anekasyaikakriyāvirodhābhāvāt tadanvayavyatirekānuvidhāyinaś ca kāryasyaikasya darśanāt svabhāvata ekatvaṃ sādhitam -- tena kāraṇena sahakaraṇaśīlā ekasāmagryantarggatāḥ pratyayāḥ sāmagry-antaraiḥ saha
children.translated_text: and so forth. By which [reason] — that upon the accumulation of another condition, an aggregate lacking it becomes another aggregate, and that [other aggregate] produces only a different effect from that produced by the prior aggregate; and that despite the multiplicity of auxiliary causes that are the objects of the designation of a single aggregate, because there is no contradiction of multiple [causes] having a single activity, and because a single effect is seen to follow the presence and absence of those [causes], [their] unity is established by [their] essential nature — by that reason, the conditions that enter into a single aggregate, having the character of co-operating, are with other aggregates
not objects of a single utility (<s>naikopayogaviṣayāḥ</s>)

children.text:
eka upayogasya viṣayo yeṣāṃ te na bhavanti, sāmagryantarair eva saha bhinnopayogāviṣayatvasya nyāyabalāt pratīteḥ | anena yat prāg vikalpitaṃ `yadi kāraṇaśabdena sāmagrī bhaṇyate tadā tadbhedād asty evātatsāmagrījanyebhyaḥ kāryasya bheda iti kim ucyate
-- na kāraṇabhedād bhedaḥ [T. 282a.] syāt' iti etad
children.translated_text: — those whose utility is not one and the same do not exist [as such], since it is understood by the force of reasoning that they are objects of different utility precisely with other aggregates. By this, what was previously conjectured — 'if by the word cause the aggregate is meant, then due to its difference there is indeed difference of the effect from those produced by a non-identical aggregate, so why is it said there is no difference from difference of cause?' — this

children.text:
udāharaṇopadarśitaṃ nigamitam[475]| atha kāraṇaśabdena sāmagrīvyapadeśaviṣayāḥ sahakāriṇa ucyante tadā tadbhedād anekatvalakṣaṇāt kāryasyānekatvalakṣaṇo bhedo neṣyata eva, anekasyaikakriyāvirodhābhāvāt, ekasyānekata utpattidarśanāc ceti mṛtsaṃsthānayor ekātmakatopadarśitaṃ [S. 110b.] nigamayati -- `kāryasvabhāvasya' mṛtsaṃthānātmana `ekatve 'pi' nānātvābhāve 'pi `vastutaḥ' paramārthataḥ kalpanābuddhau mṛtsaṃsthānayor bhinnayor iva pratibhāsane 'pīti |
 evam udāharaṇe sāmagrībhedāt kāryāṇāṃ bhedo naikasāmagrīviṣayapratyayabhedād anekatvaṃ kāryasyeti pratipādya prakṛte cakṣurādau yojayann āha --
children.translated_text:
has been concluded as demonstrated by the example. Now, if by the word 'cause' the auxiliary causes that are the objects of the designation of an aggregate are meant, then from their difference — characterized as multiplicity — the difference of the effect characterized as multiplicity is simply not accepted, because of the non-contradiction of multiple [causes] having a single activity, and because one [effect] is seen to arise from multiple [causes] — [thus <s>Dharmakīrti</s>] concludes what was shown through the single-nature-hood of clay and configuration — 'even when there is unity' — [i.e.,] even when there is no multiplicity — 'of the essential nature of the effect' — whose nature is clay-and-configuration — 'in reality' — in ultimate terms, even though in conceptual cognition clay and configuration appear as if different. |
  Having thus demonstrated with the example that there is difference of effects from difference of aggregate but no multiplicity of the effect from difference of conditions within a single aggregate, [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>] applies [this] to the case at hand — the eye and the like — saying —
'Just as here' (<s>yathā iha</s>)
'in the example' (<s>udāharaṇe</s>)
'difference of cause' (<s>kāraṇabhedaḥ</s>)

— difference of aggregate, characterized as the triad of aggregates: clay-lump without potter, clay-lump with potter, and the additional aggregate with thread — 'among different' — among those of different essential natures — 'specific [effects]' — characterized as brick-wheel-undivided-pot, and divided-pot — [has] utility
that is not of a single effect (<s>naikakāryaḥ</s>)
but rather is of different effects only,
likewise (<s>tathā</s>)

children.text:
tenaiva prakāreṇa cakṣurādibhyo vijñānasyotpattau sāmagryantarāt sāmagrīlakṣaṇakāraṇabhedo 'nekakārya ity unneyaḥ |
  {p.111.1} etad eva vibhajann āha --
children.translated_text:
in the same manner, in the production of consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>) from the eye and the like, the difference of cause characterized as an aggregate — [being productive of] a different aggregate — is to be inferred as having multiple effects. |
  Analyzing this very [point], [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>] says —
'For thus' (<s>tathā hi</s>)

children.text: ityādi | yā cakṣūr uparahitā samanantarapratyayākhyavijñānalakṣaṇā pratyayāntarasāpekṣā sāmagrī, tato vijñānasya [T. 282b.] vikalpakasyetarasya vā tadupādeyatvena yā bodharūpatopalabdhā sā cakṣurvijñānasyāpi bhavati |
children.translated_text: and so forth. Whatever aggregate, accompanied by the eye, having the nature of the consciousness called the immediately preceding condition (<s>samanantarapratyaya</s>), dependent on other conditions — from that, whatever cognitive nature (<s>bodharūpatā</s>) of consciousness, whether conceptual or otherwise, is apprehended as appropriated by it — that belongs also to visual consciousness (<s>cakṣurvijñāna</s>). |
'Of that very' (<s>tasyaiva</s>)
— of visual consciousness. Of what kind?
'Existing as having the nature of apprehension' (<s>upalambhātmanaḥ sato bhavataḥ</s>)

children.text: jāyamānasya tadaiva tadekakāryapratiniyatasya cakṣurindriyasya sannidhānāt [S. 111a.] samanantarapratyayopādānopakṛtāt tato
children.translated_text: — being born, determined at that very [moment] to a single effect of the visual sense-faculty, due to the proximity of the eye-faculty; being assisted by the material cause [which is] the immediately preceding condition — from that,
'the determination to the apprehension of form' (<s>rūpagrahaṇapratiniyamaḥ</s>)

— the determination to having the aspect of form (<s>rūpākāratā</s>), possessing discrimination from the aspects of sound and the like — such is the effect, because the aggregate consisting of the immediately preceding condition accompanied by the eye is productive [of it]. |
'From the object' (<s>viṣayād</s>)
— from the immediately preceding condition which has the additional [factor of the] object, and from the sense-faculty —
'by that' (<s>tena</s>)
— by the object —
'similarity of form' (<s>tulyarūpatā</s>)

children.text:
na kevalaiva rūpapratibhāsitā bhrāntavijñānasyeveti viṣayendriyamanaskāralakṣaṇasāmagrīkāryam evaṃ pradarśitam | tad anyad ekadvayajanyaṃ tu kāryaṃ
svayam abhyūhyam | atrābhinnatve 'pi vastutaḥ
children.translated_text: — not merely the appearance of form as in an erroneous cognition — thus the effect of the aggregate characterized by object, sense-faculty, and mental attention (<s>manaskāra</s>) has been demonstrated. The other effects produced by one or two [of these] are to be inferred by oneself. Here, despite the non-difference in reality
'of the effect' (<s>kāryasya</s>)
— characterized as visual consciousness —
'of the causes' (<s>kāraṇānām</s>)

children.text: viṣayendriyamanaskārāṇāṃ bhinnebhyaḥ svabhāvebhyaḥ kevalānām eṣāṃ yaḥ svabhāvas tato bhinnā evātajjanyebhyo[479]vidhiśe(-nyebhyo 'pi viśe)ṣā bodharūpatādilakṣanā
children.translated_text: — of object, sense-faculty, and mental attention — from [their] different essential natures, [i.e.,] from the essential natures of each of these individually, the specific features characterized by cognitive nature and the like are indeed different from those not produced by that [aggregate], being not produced by it.
'they arise' (<s>bhavanti</s>)

children.text: | atajjanyāpekṣayā[480]caikātmakā api bahutvena nirdiṣṭāḥ | yata evam
children.translated_text: | And in relation to those not produced by it, even those having a single nature are spoken of as multiple. Because thus
'therefore' (<s>iti</s>)

children.text: tasmāt na kāraṇabhede 'pi | [S. 111b.] yathaikasāmagryantarggatapratyayabhede 'py abhedo naivaṃ sāmagrīlakṣaṇakāraṇabhede 'py abhedaḥ sāmagryantarasjanyebhyaḥ
children.translated_text: — therefore, not even from difference of cause. Just as from difference of conditions within a single aggregate there is no difference [of effect], so too from difference of cause characterized as aggregate there is no non-difference [of effect] from those produced by another aggregate —
'of the specific effect' (<s>kāryaviśeṣasya</s>)

children.text:
viśiṣṭasya kāryasyeti |
  tena yaducyate -- [T. 283a.] `yadi sahakāriṇāṃ bhede 'py abhinnaṃ kāryaṃ bhavati sāmagrībhede 'py abhinnam astu, atha sāmagrībhedād bhinnaṃ bhavati sahakāribhedād api kim iti bhinnaṃ na bhavati viśeṣābhāvāt?' iti tadapāstaṃ bhavati | tathā hi parasparopasarppaṇādyāśrayāt pratyayaviśeṣād ekakāryoddeśenetaretarasantānopakārāc ca sahakāriṇāṃ pratiniyataśaktīnām udayād ekaṃ
children.translated_text:
— of the distinguished effect. |
  Therefore, what was said — 'if the effect is non-different even when there is difference of auxiliary causes, let it be non-different even when there is difference of aggregate; but if it is different from difference of aggregate, why is it not also different from difference of auxiliary causes, since there is no distinguishing feature?' — that is dispelled. For thus, from a particular condition based on mutual approximation and the like, for the purpose of a single effect, through the mutual assistance of each other's continua, since the auxiliary causes with determined capacities arise, one

children.text: kāryaṃ samājāyate[481]| {p. 112.1} sāmagryantarasya tu kāryāntaraprabhavaśaktinibandhanebhyo hetvantarebhyaḥ svabhāvabhedavato bhāvād bhinnakāryaprasūtir iti kuto viśeṣābhāvaḥ? |
children.translated_text: effect is produced. But since the other aggregate, being of different essential nature from the causes that ground the power to produce another effect, brings forth a different effect — so how could there be no distinguishing feature? |

body.translated_text: Thus, having demonstrated that there is difference from those produced by another aggregate due to difference of aggregate, and that the unity of the effect is not contradicted even when the auxiliary causes are multiple, [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>] concludes saying —

body.text:
-ṇopadarśanāt niga- -- T.
[476] viṣayeṣu -- T.
[477] eva -- T.
[478] -dhikārāt -- T.
[479] eva tajja- -- T.
[480] ato janakāpekṣayā -- T.
[481] kāryaṃ na jāyate -- T.
body.translated_text:
'-ṇopadarśanāt niga-' — T.
[476] 'viṣayeṣu' — T.
[477] 'eva' — T.
[478] '-dhikārāt' — T.
[479] 'eva tajja-' — T.
[480] 'ato janakāpekṣayā' — T.
[481] 'kāryaṃ na jāyate' — T.

body.text: section: 33. janakatvam evādhāratvaṃ na tu sthāpakatvam |
body.translated_text: Section: 33. Productive capacity (<s>janakatva</s>) is supportive, not maintaining (<s>sthāpakatva</s>).

body.text: nanu ca sarvaṃ kāryaṃ sādhāraṃ[482]yathā upādāyarūpam | tad dhi bhūtebhyo

children.text: jāyamānaṃ tāny evāśrayata[483]iti bhavadbhir iṣyate | tathā 'nyad api vijñānādikaṃ kāryam | ato 'nenāpi kiñcit kāraṇam āśrayaṇīyam | tasya ca kāraṇasya pūrvaṃ janakatvaṃ paścāt [S. 112a.] kāryaṃ pratyādhārabhāva eva, na jananam, tatas tatsvabhāvasya jananād ity anekāntaḥ tadavastha evety ata āha --
children.translated_text: rests upon those very [elements] — so you accept. Likewise other effects too, such as consciousness and the like. Therefore, some cause must be the support (<s>āśraya</s>) of this [effect] too. And of that cause, previously [there is] productive capacity, afterwards, with respect to the effect, there is the status of support (<s>ādhārabhāva</s>) only, not production. Therefore, 'because of the production of that which has that essential nature' — the inconclusiveness remains in the same condition — thus [the opponent argues]. To this [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>] says —
'These very same' (<s>ta evaite</s>)
— those just mentioned —
'differences in the powers of causes' (<s>kāraṇaśaktibhedāḥ</s>)
— the specific powers of causes. Of what kind?
'Each in its own way' (<s>yathāsvaṃ</s>)

children.text: yeṣāṃ kāraṇaśaktibhedānāṃ sahakārilakṣaṇānāṃ yadātmīyaṃ sāmagryantarajanyāt prativiśiṣṭaṃ kāryaṃ tasya janane 'vyavadheyā vyavadhātuṃ [T. 283b.] pratibandhum aśakyā śaktir yeṣāṃ tadbhāvas[484]tayā
children.translated_text: — of those differences in causal power characterized as auxiliary causes, whose own specific effect — distinguished from that produced by another aggregate — in the production of that, whose power is unobstructable (<s>avyavadheyā</s>), incapable of being blocked, [existing] in that state —
'by virtue of unobstructable power' (<s>avyavadheyaśaktitayā</s>)
— by virtue of necessarily effect-producing power —
'[they] stand ready' (<s>pratyupasthitāḥ</s>)
— being engaged —
'of the effect of the aggregate' (<s>sāmagrīkāryasya</s>)
— of [the effect] produced by a single condition —

children.text:
kasyacid
abhāvāt[485]sarvaṃ sāmagryā eva kāryam iti kṛtvā sāmagrīkāryasya svabhāvasthityāśraya ity ucyante | kasmāt punar avyavadheyaśaktitā?
children.translated_text: since there is nowhere an absence [of any component], all [effects] are effects of the aggregate only — hence they are called the support of the essential nature and existence of the aggregate's effect. And why is the power unobstructable?
'Because of momentariness' (<s>kṣaṇikatvāt</s>)

children.text: | na hi kṣaṇikasya śaktiḥ pratibandhuṃ śakyate,
children.translated_text: | For the power of what is momentary cannot be obstructed,

children.text:
svabhāvāntarotpādane yāvat[486]pratibandhako vyāpriyate tāvat kṣaṇikasya svakāryaṃ kṛtvaiva nirodhāt |
  kathaṃ punar asamānakālaṃ kāraṇam ādhāro yujyate?, ity ata āha --
children.translated_text:
because, while the obstructor is occupied in producing an alternative essential nature, what is momentary ceases, having already accomplished its own effect. |
  But how could a cause that is not simultaneous with [its effect] be reasonably [called] a support? — to this [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>] says —
'For thus' (<s>tathā hi</s>)
and so forth. Since
'that' (<s>tat</s>)
— the effect characterized as consciousness —
'from those' (<s>tebhyaḥ</s>)
— from the eye and the like —
'from all together' (<s>samastebhyaḥ</s>)
— as having cognitive nature, different from what is other than and not produced by that —
'having a distinctly specific essential nature, one' (<s>prativiśiṣṭasvabhāvam ekaṃ</s>)

children.text: khaṇḍaśaḥ kāryasyānutpādād ekaikasmāt sakalasyaiva bhāvād ekaṃ jātam, tasmāt te ādhārā ucyante | na hi janakād anya evopakārakaḥ | na cānupakāraka {p. 113.1} ādhāraḥ, atiprasaṅgāt | tato bhinnakālasyādhārabhāvo na virudhyate | yad api bhūtānām upādāyarūpaṃ pratyāśrayatvam[487]ucyate tad api svadeśasyāsya janakatvam eveti na kiñcit prāg janakaṃ bhūtvā paścāt
children.translated_text: — since the effect is not produced in parts, since it exists from [all causes taken] together, [it is] born as one. Therefore they are called supports. For there is no benefactor other than the producer. Nor is a non-benefactor a support, because of over-extension. Therefore, the support-status of that which is of different time is not contradicted. And even the support-status of the elements with respect to derived form (<s>upādāyarūpa</s>) — that too is simply the productive capacity of its own location — so nothing, having first been a producer, afterwards
assumes the status of a maintainer (<s>sthāpakatā</s>), from which inconclusiveness would arise. |

body.translated_text: But is not every effect supported (<s>sādhāra</s>), like derived form (<s>upādāyarūpa</s>)? For that, being born from the elements (<s>bhūta</s>),
