body.text: section: 34. atiśayotpādanaṃ na sahakāritvaṃ kintu ekārthakāritvam |
body.translated_text: Section: 34. The production of an increment (<s>atiśaya</s>) is not auxiliary-causality (<s>sahakāritva</s>) but rather single-purpose-efficacy (<s>ekārthakāritva</s>).

body.text: punar anyathā tatsvabhāvasya jananād ity anekāntodbhāvanaṃ parasyāśaṅkyāha --

children.translated_text: 'In those whose power has no obstruction' (<s>apratirodhaśaktikeṣu</s>)

children.text: avidyamānaḥ pratirodhaḥ -- pratibandho yasyāḥ śakteḥ sā yeṣām [T. 284a.] apratirodhaśaktikatvaṃ cānantarakāryatvāt | ye hy utpannāḥ kālakṣepeṇa kāryaṃ kurvanti teṣāṃ syād api śaktipratibandho, na tu ya udayānantaram eva kāryaṃ kurvanti | anena kṣaṇakṣayiṇām upaghātakābhāvam āha | anugrāhakaviraham apy āha --
children.translated_text: — those whose power has no obstruction, i.e., no blocking, and their having unobstructable power is because of producing an effect immediately. For those who, having arisen, produce their effect after a delay — for them there might be obstruction of power; but not for those who produce their effect immediately upon arising. By this, [<s>Arcaṭa</s>] states the absence of destroyers for momentary entities. He also states the absence of enhancers —
'In those upon whom no specific feature can be imposed' (<s>anādheyaviśeṣeṣu</s>)
| And this character of having no imposable specific feature —
'in momentary [entities]' (<s>kṣaṇikeṣu</s>)

children.text: ity anenāha | na hi kṣaṇikānāṃ viśeṣa ādhātuṃ śakyate, viśeṣādhāyakena tatsahabhāvinā tadanantaraṃ tadutpādanāt | tadā [S. 113a.] ca tasya nirodhāt | teṣv evaṃvidheṣu
children.translated_text: — he states by this. For a specific feature cannot be imposed upon momentary [entities], because it is produced in the immediately subsequent [moment] by [a cause] coexisting with that [specific feature]. And at that time, that [momentary entity] has ceased. In those of such character,
among conditions, what is the purpose of mutual auxiliary causation (<s>sahakāra</s>)?

children.text:
yena sahakāriṇa ucyante? | nanv anādheyaviśeṣatvenaiva sahakāritvābhāvaḥ pratipādita iti kim artham idam apratirodhaśaktikeṣv iti? | na hi śaktipratirodhakaḥ
sahakārī bhaṇyate | satyam | sarvathā tu tatrākiñcitkaratvajñāpanārtham etad uktam | śaktipratibandhakāpanayanena copakāritvakalpanāṃ sahakāriṇāṃ nirasyati | tasmād atiśayādhāyinaḥ sahakāriṇo 'sambhavāt kṣaṇikānāṃ svahetumātrapratibaddham eva janakatvam | tac caivaṃ vidhaṃ sarvadā 'sti | na ca kevalā janayantīti tatsvabhāvasya jananād ity anekānta eveti manyate |
 etat pariharati --
children.translated_text:
by which they are called auxiliary causes? But has not the absence of auxiliary-cause-hood been demonstrated precisely by [their] not being able to confer any distinguishing feature — so what is the purpose of [the phrase] 'in those whose power is unobstructed'? For an auxiliary cause is not said to be one that obstructs [another's] power. True. But this is stated in order to make known [their] complete inefficacy there in every respect. And by [the argument of] removing the obstruction of power, he rejects the supposition that auxiliary causes contribute through [such removal]. Therefore, since auxiliary causes that confer a distinguishing feature are impossible for momentary entities, their productive capacity is bound solely to their own causes. And that [capacity] of this kind always exists. But they do not produce [an effect] in isolation — [so the opponent] thinks: 'since that of its own nature produces, this is an inconclusive [reason].'
He resolves this:
'Indeed not' —

children.text: naiva atiśayotpādanaṃ[489]sahakriyā yatas tadabhāvāt sahakāriṇo na syuḥ | kva punar atiśayotpādanaṃ
children.translated_text: the production of a distinguishing feature is indeed not the cooperative action (<s>sahakriyā</s>), since from the absence of that, there would be no auxiliary causes. But where is the production of a distinguishing feature
— the cooperative action of conditions — not present?
'Everywhere' —

children.text: | na hi kvacid api sahabhāvinām atiśayotpādanalakṣaṇā[490][T. 284b.] sahakriyā {p. 114.1} sambhavati | kā tarhi sahakriyā? ity āha --
children.translated_text: for nowhere at all is the cooperative action characterized as the production of a distinguishing feature possible among co-existing [causes]. What then is the cooperative action? To this he says:
'The accomplishment of a single purpose' —
the completion of a single effect, which [is performed]
'by many' —
'even' —

children.text: sambhāvanāyām | [S. 113b.] nyāyabalād evaṃvidhām eva sarvatra sahakriyāṃ sambhāvayāmaḥ, nānyām iti | atrodāharaṇam --
children.translated_text: [used] in the sense of possibility. By the force of reasoning, we conceive cooperative action to be of this very kind everywhere, and of no other kind. Here is an example:
'Just as of the final' —
of the immediately subsequent effect such as a sprout and the like,
'of the causal aggregate' —
of the aggregate of conditions (<s>pratyayasāmagrī</s>).

body.translated_text: Again, anticipating the opponent's raising of inconclusiveness in another way regarding 'because of the production of that which has that essential nature,' [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>] says —

-production- — T.
[490] -production- — T.

body.text: section: 35. ekakāryakāritvam eva mukhyaṃ sahakāritvam itarat tu gauṇam |
body.translated_text: Section: 35. The production of a single effect alone is the primary cooperative causation; the other is secondary

body.text: syād etat -- aupacārikam etat sahakāritvam, atiśayotpādanam eva tu mukhyam ity ata āha --

children.translated_text: 'That very' —
characterized as the causation of a single effect —
'is the primary cooperative causation' —

children.text: nātiśayotpādanalakṣaṇam, tasyaiva gauṇatvāt | etac cottaratra vakṣyate | kuta etat? ity āha --
children.translated_text: not that characterized as the production of a distinguishing feature, since that itself is secondary. And this will be stated later. How is this [known]? He says:
'Because of that very other [cause]' —
with respect to the intended effect —
'being a cause' —

children.text:
| kāraṇasya ca sahakārivyapadeśaḥ nākāraṇasya | yataḥ saha -- yugapat sarvantaḥ sahakāriṇa ucyante, antyaś ca kāraṇakalāpa evaṃvidha iti | yathā cāntyasyaikārthakāraṇaṃ sahakāritvam evaṃ pūrvasyāpi kāraṇakalāpasyottarottaraviśiṣṭakṣaṇāntarārambhiṇa ity avaseyam, antyasyodāharaṇatayā nirddeśāt | tasmāt sarvaṃ kāryam aṅkurādikaṃ viśeṣalakṣaṇaṃ vā 'nekapratyayajanyam iti | sarvatraikārthakriyaiva copacīyamānāpacīyamānakāryakāriṇaḥ kāraṇakalāpasya sahakāritvam, na viśeṣotpādanam iti |
  syād etat -- ekārthakaraṇam api tatra [S. 114a.] sahakāritvam astu atiśayotpādanalakṣaṇam apīty ata āha --
children.translated_text:
and the designation 'auxiliary cause' belongs to a cause, not to a non-cause. Because those that [exist] simultaneously — all together — are called auxiliary causes, and the final causal aggregate is of this very kind. And just as the cooperative causation of the final [aggregate] is the production of a single effect, so too of the prior causal aggregate, which initiates successively distinguished subsequent moments, this should be understood — since the final [aggregate] is indicated as an example. Therefore, every effect — sprouts and the like, or of a specific character — is produced from multiple conditions. And everywhere, the cooperative causation of the causal aggregate, which produces effects that are augmented and diminished, consists solely in the production of a single effect, not in the production of a distinguishing feature.
One might think: let there be cooperative causation characterized as the production of a single effect there, but also that characterized as the production of a distinguishing feature — therefore he says:
'And there' —
'in the final moment' —
'because of the impossibility of producing a distinguishing feature' —

children.text: nātiśayotpādanam api sahakāritvam | kuto viśeṣasya [T. 285a.] karttum aśakyatvam? ity ata āha --
children.translated_text: the production of a distinguishing feature too is not cooperative causation. Why is it impossible to produce a distinguishing feature? To this he says:
'Of the single [entity]' —
'which is without parts' —
'because of the non-distinction of essential nature' —

children.text: | na hi tatra `ayam anāhitātiśayo bhāgaḥ svahetubhyo jātaḥ, ayaṃ tu sahakāribhir āhitātiśayaḥ' iti viveko 'sti | yadi nāmāvivekaḥ, viśeṣas tu kim iti na kriyate? ity ata āha --
children.translated_text: for there is no distinction there such as 'this part has arisen from its own causes without a conferred distinguishing feature, while this [part] has a distinguishing feature conferred by the auxiliary causes.' Even if there is non-distinction, why is a distinguishing feature not produced? To this he says:
'Because the production of a distinguishing feature is characterized by the arising of another essential nature' —

children.text:
, nirbhāge ca kutaḥ svabhāvāntarasya vyavasthā? |
  syānmatam -- bhinnasvabhāva evāntyasya viśeṣo 'stu ity ata āha --
children.translated_text:
and in what is without parts, how could there be the determination of another essential nature?
One might think: let the distinguishing feature of the final [moment] be of a different essential nature — therefore he says:
'An alternative entity' —

children.text: ityādi | yadi bhāvāntaralakṣaṇo viśeṣo {p. 115.1} bhavet tadā tasyāntyatvam eva hīyeta | hīyenāṃ(hīyatāṃ) ko doṣaḥ? iti cet;
children.translated_text: and so forth. If the distinguishing feature were characterized as an alternative entity, then its being the final [moment] itself would be lost. 'Let it be lost — what is the fault?' If so:
'And then' —
'because of not being the final [moment]' —
'it would not be a direct cause' —
since this is so,
'therefore, of the [primary] cause' —
'of the primary [cause]' —
'from the auxiliary causes' —
from [their] proximity —
'there is no production of a distinguishing feature' —

children.text:
ity ekārthakriyaiva sahakāritvam iti |
  nanv asatyāṃ sahakāribhyo viśeṣotpattau kāryajanane sāmarthyam eṣāṃ na yujyata ity ata [S. 114b.] āha --
children.translated_text:
thus, the production of a single effect alone is cooperative causation.
But [the opponent objects]: if there is no production of a distinguishing feature from auxiliary causes, the capacity of these [causes] for producing an effect is not reasonable — therefore he says:
'They are capable' —

children.text: ityādi | yadi hi te svabhāvenāsamarthā utpadyeran tadaiṣāṃ sahakāribhyaḥ sāmarthyotpattir abhyupagamyeta | yāvatā
children.translated_text: and so forth. For if they were produced as incapable by their own nature, then the arising of capacity from auxiliary causes would be conceded. But since
'those final conditions are born already capable by their very own nature, together' —
'delayed only by a moment' —
'of which' —
because of being fixed to a single moment, therefore

children.text: prāk paścāt pṛthak tv abhāvo nāsti | yebhyaścānantaram eva kāryam utpadyate
children.translated_text: there is no prior, subsequent, or separate existence. And from which the effect arises immediately,
'not after an interval of time' —
'there' —
'in those of such a nature' —
'the production of a single effect alone is cooperative causation' —

children.text:
nātiśayotpādanalakṣaṇam |
  svabhāvataḥ sāmarthyasya [T. 285b.] bhāvavirodhāt, parasparataś cānabhyupagamāt samarthasya janmaivāyuktam iti manvānaḥ paraḥ āha --
children.translated_text:
not that characterized by the production of a distinguishing feature.
Since the existence of capacity by nature is contradictory to [the nature of] entities, and since [capacity] from one another is not accepted — the opponent, thinking that the very birth of a capable [entity] is unreasonable, says:
'Whence is [it] capable?' —
and so forth. The proponent (<s>siddhāntavādin</s>) says:
'From their own causes' —

children.text: iti | paramatāpekṣayā tu svabhāvata ity uktam | paro
children.translated_text: thus. But with respect to the opponent's position, it is said 'by nature.' For the opponent

children.text: hy atyantasya (hy utpannasya)[493]kāraṇasya sahakāribhyaḥ sāmarthyam icchatīti tanniṣedhaparaṃ[494]svabhāvata iti vacanam | na tu svabhāvataḥ kiñcij jāyate, tasyāhetukatvaprasaṅgāt |
children.translated_text: wants capacity of the ultimate (or: of the produced) cause from auxiliary causes — so the statement 'by nature' is directed at negating that. But nothing arises from its own nature [alone], because of the absurd consequence of being without a cause.

body.translated_text: One might think: this cooperative causation is figurative (<s>aupacārika</s>), while the production of a distinguishing feature is the primary [meaning] — therefore he says:

body.text:
sākṣād -- T.
[492] -lambino janmanas teṣāṃ -- T.
[493] hy utpāda[ka]sya -- T.
[494] tanniṣedhāya paraṃ -- T.
body.translated_text:
directly — T.
[492] -delayed birth of those- — T.
[493] 'of the producing [cause]' — T.
[494] 'for the purpose of negating that' — T.
Section: 36. Establishing the regularity of single-effect production in momentary entities

body.text: ekārthakriyāniyama eva kṣaṇikānām ayuktaḥ, kevalānām apy aṃtyakṣaṇasarūpāṇāṃ darśanāt | tathā hi -- `idam evaṃrūpaṃ naivaṃ ca' iti darśanādarśanābhyāṃ [S. 115a.] vibhajyate | tatra yādṛśāḥ kṣityādayas tadanyapratyayasannidhāv upalabhyante tādṛśā eva kevalā api | tatas tadanyasahitā iva kevalā api samartham aṅkurajanane svaṃ svaṃ kṣaṇāntaram ārabheran | tataḥ kevalasyāpy aṅkurādijananasvābhāvyād ajananāc ca `tatsvabhāvasya jananāt' ity anekānta eveti manyamānaḥ para {p. 116.1} āha --

children.translated_text: 'Those' —
their own causes — earth, seeds, and the like —
'this' —
'capable [entity]' —
'of another' —
'of another condition' —
'only in the proximity' —
'why?' —
'do they produce?' —

children.text: ? na kevalāni?, sahitānām eva sarvadā sambhavāt iti cet āha --
children.translated_text: Why not when alone? If [you say]: because those that are together always exist [together] — he says:
'Sometimes' —
'at some time' —
'otherwise too' —
'even when alone' —
'they would be' —

children.text:
bhaveyuḥ | tathā hi -- dṛśyanta evādhyātikabāhyāḥ kvacit kārye yādṛśā yatsahitāḥ tādṛśā eva tadrahitā
apīti | [T. 286a.] janayan tu kevalā api sambhavantaḥ samartham, ko doṣaḥ? iti ced āha --
children.translated_text: they would exist. Thus: internal and external [causes] are indeed observed — just as they are when accompanied by something in some effect, so too they are exactly the same even when without that [accompaniment]. But if even those that are alone and capable do produce [the effect], what is the fault? He says:
'And then' —
since even those that are alone would be capable producers,
'even a single one' —
not merely many,
'somewhere' —

children.text: d deśādau [S. 115b.] samarthaḥ utpannaḥ kṣitibījādir aṅkurādikāryaṃ
children.translated_text: in some place and the like, a single earth-seed and the like, having arisen as capable, would produce an effect such as a sprout and the like —
'would produce' —

children.text:
yadi tatsvabhāvasyāvaśyaṃ janakatvam | na ca kevalo janayati tatsvabhāvasambhave 'pi tato 'nekānta iti paraḥ |
  etat pariharann āha --
children.translated_text:
if the productive capacity of its own nature were invariable. But a single [cause] does not produce [an effect] even when its own nature is present — therefore [this is] inconclusive, says the opponent.
Resolving this, he says:
'Successive and further' —
and so forth. By successive and further [conditions] — granary, the effort of the person who removes from it, throwing into a basket, conveying to the field, scattering, and the like —
'by conditions' —
by which
'conjunction' [occurs] —
by that reason,
'having different powers at each moment' —
never having a single power across prior and subsequent times,

children.text: aparāparapratyayayogalakṣaṇahetubhede 'py abhinnaśaktitāyām[495]ahetukatvaprasaṅgāt | anyatrāpi ca śāliyavabījādau śaktibhedasya hetubhedanibandhanatvāt |
children.translated_text: because if there were undifferentiated power despite the difference of cause characterized by the conjunction with successive and further conditions, the absurd consequence of being without a cause [would follow]. And because in other cases too — rice, barley, seeds, and the like — the difference of power is based on the difference of cause.
'The dispositions (<s>saṃskāra</s>)' —
produced by meeting and combining with conditions,
'continuing' —
existing as a continuum,
'although from some similarity' —

children.text: varṇena saṃsthānena anyena vā kenacitprakāreṇa sādṛśyād ekākāraparāmarśapratyayajananalakṣaṇāt samānaṃ rūpam eṣām iti
children.translated_text: from similarity in color, configuration, or some other aspect — due to the characteristic of producing a cognition that apprehends [them under] a single form — 'these have the same form,' thus
'having the same form' —
'similar' —
'they are cognized' —
'they are recognized' —
'nevertheless' —
just as with artificial and natural gems, pearls, and the like, due to the difference of the aggregate characterized by the conjunction with successive and further conditions,
'indeed different' —

children.text: visadṛśa eva na pratyabhijñānavaśād abhinnaḥ tulyarūpa
children.translated_text: indeed dissimilar — not identical through the force of recognition, not of the same form —
'of these' —
'of seeds and the like' —
'is the essential nature.'
Since this is so,
therefore,
because of the established fact that the moments have different essential natures and different powers, being produced by successive and further aggregates,
'only something specific' —
earth, seed, and the like —
'of some' —
specific effect — sprout and the like — or that which is capable of producing it —
'is the cause' —

children.text:
| na sarvaṃ sarvasya | tathā ca vyagrāṇāṃ kṣitibījādinām aṅkurajananasvabhāvatā
samarthakṣaṇajananasvabhāvatā vā nāsty eveti tatsvabhāvasya jananād ajanakasya cātatsvabhāvatvād ity atra nānekāntaḥ yato yo yatsvabhāvaḥ sa svahetor evotpadyamānaḥ tādṛśo bhavati na punas tadbhave hetvantaram apekṣata ity atrānekāntaḥ syād iti | pratyabhijñānasya ca sarūpatāviṣayasya sāmagrībhedād anumitabhinnaśaktisvabhāvatvena bādhyamānatayā prāmāṇyābhāvāt na tataḥ sarūpatāsiddhiḥ kṣaṇakṣayiṇām iti |
  pūrvaṃ ca `ata evāna(eva ta)yor avasthayor vastubhedo niśceyaḥ' ity[496]ādinā [S. 116b.] ekatvāviṣayaṃ pratyabhijñānaṃ nirastam | adhunā tu tulyasvabhāvatāviṣayam iti bhedaḥ | etad api tatra `aparāparotpatteḥ' ity[497]anenoktam eva | vipañcanārthaṃ[498]tu punaḥ iha upanyastam |
children.translated_text:
not everything of everything. And thus, earth, seeds, and the like that are [still] engaged [in processing] do not have the nature of producing sprouts, or the nature of producing a capable moment. Therefore in [the argument] 'since that of its own nature produces, and since what does not produce is not of that nature' — here there is no inconclusiveness. Because whatever has a particular nature, being produced from its own cause alone, becomes of that nature, and does not require another cause for being of that nature — the inconclusiveness would be in this [latter claim]. And since recognition (<s>pratyabhijñāna</s>), whose object is similarity of form, is contradicted by the inference of different-power-nature based on the difference of aggregate, and thus lacks <s>pramāṇa</s>-validity, there is no establishment of similarity of form for things that perish each moment.
And previously, with [the passage] 'therefore the real difference between those two states must be ascertained' and so forth, recognition as not having unity as its object was rejected. But now [recognition] as not having similarity of nature as its object [is rejected] — this is the distinction. This too was already stated there with 'because of successive and further production' — but it is presented here again for the purpose of elaboration.

body.translated_text: The very regularity of single-effect production in momentary entities is unreasonable, since even those that are alone are observed to have the same form as the final moment. Thus: [things] are distinguished by observation and non-observation as 'this is of such a form and not otherwise.' There, things like earth and the like, as they are observed in the proximity of another condition, are exactly the same even when alone. Therefore, just like those accompanied by another [condition], even those that are alone should initiate their own respective subsequent moments, being capable of producing sprouts. Therefore, since even alone [they have] the natural capacity to produce sprouts and the like, and since [alone they do] not produce — the opponent, thinking 'since that of its own nature produces, [this is] an inconclusive [reason],' says:
-even when different despite difference- — T.
for the purpose of communicating the subject matter — T.
Section: 37. Explanation of the determination of cause-effect relation in momentary entities

body.text: kiñcid eva kasyacit kāraṇam ity uktam tatra kiṃ kasya kāraṇam iti śakyaparicchedam apy ādhyātmikeṣu tāvad darśayann āha --

children.translated_text: 'There' —
and so forth.
'There' —

children.text: teṣu pratikṣaṇaṃ śaktisvabhāveṣu kṣaṇikeṣu bhāveṣu | vyavadhānaṃ -- vyavadhīyate yena, tadādir yeṣāṃ atidūrātyāsannatvādīnāṃ te 'vidyamānā[499]yasmin deśe so 'vyavadhānādiḥ deśo yasya so 'vyavadhānādideśaḥ, [T. 287a.] rūpam indriyaṃ cādī yasya manaskārādeḥ
children.translated_text: among those momentary entities whose essential nature is power at each moment. Obstruction (<s>vyavadhāna</s>) — that by which [perception] is obstructed; those whose beginning is that — such as being too far or too near and the like — when those are absent in a place, that is a place without obstruction and the like; form, sense-faculty, and the like are the beginning of which — of mental attention and the like —

children.text: sa rūpendriyādiḥ[500]sa cāsau kāraṇakalāpaś ca sāmagrīlakṣaṇas tathoktaḥ, avyavadhānādideśaś cāsau rūpendriyādikāraṇakalāpaś ca sa
children.translated_text: that which has form, sense-faculty, and the like as its beginning — and that is also a causal aggregate characterized as an aggregate (<s>sāmagrī</s>), thus designated; and that which is a place without obstruction and the like and is a causal aggregate having form, sense-faculty, and the like —
'is the capable cause for the production of cognition' —

children.text: nānyaḥ, tadbhāva eva tasya bhāvāt, anyabhāve 'pi cābhāvāt, etanmātranibandhanatvāc ca samarthāsamarthavyavasthāyāḥ |
children.translated_text: and not another, because its existence [occurs] only when that [aggregate] exists, and because of its absence even when other [things] exist, and because the determination of capable and incapable is based solely on this [aggregate].
'Of those' —
of the sense-faculties and the like,
'the mutual approaching' —
the mutual drawing together.
and so forth

because of grasping, removal of obstruction ............
...... because of the impossibility [of causal efficacy] due to dependence on the aggregate. This faultless principle of the determination of cause-effect relation, having been demonstrated in the inner [domain], extending it to other [domains] as well, [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>] says —
'By this method' —

children.text: ityādi | yo 'yam anantaraṃ hetuphalabhāvapratiniyame nyāya uktaḥ so 'anyatrā 'pi
children.translated_text: and so forth. The method that has been stated just now regarding the determination of cause-effect relation — that is 'elsewhere too,'
'everywhere,'

children.text: draṣṭavyaḥ | sarvatreti vacanāt akṣaṇikeṣv api pratītir mmā bhūt ity āha --
children.translated_text: to be observed. Lest from the word 'everywhere' there be an understanding [that this applies] even to non-momentary entities, he says —
'At each moment' —

children.text: ityādi | yāḥ kṣaṇe kṣaṇe 'nyāś cānyāś ca svabhāvabhedānvayinyaḥ śaktayo bhavanti tatrāyam ekārthakriyāpratiniyamaḥ sahakāriṇāṃ draṣṭavyaḥ | na tu ye sthiraikasvabhāvā bhāvāḥ paraiḥ kalpyante teṣv api | sthairyaṃ santānāśrayeṇāpi vyapadiśyetety ekagrahaṇam | kṣaṇe 'py ekatvam astīti sthiragrahaṇam |
children.translated_text: and so forth. The powers that at each and every moment are different, being accompanied by differences of essential nature — with respect to those, this determination of single-effect production of auxiliary causes is to be observed. But not with respect to those entities that are imagined by opponents as having a stable, single essential nature. The word 'single' [is used] because permanence could be designated even on the basis of a continuum. The word 'stable' [is used] because even in a single moment there is unity.

body.translated_text: It was said that 'only something specific is the cause of something specific' — there, showing that what is the cause of what is ascertainable, at least in internal [phenomena], he says:

avyavadhīyamānā — T.
[500] satpe- — T.
Section: 38. The absence of single-effect-producing capacity in non-momentary entities.

body.text: kasmāt punaḥ sthiraikasvabhāveṣu neṣyate? ity āha --

children.translated_text: 'Essential nature' —

children.text:
- ityādi | kāmaṃ bhāvaḥ svayaṃ na bhavet | na tu svata eva svabhāvasyānyathātvaṃ sambhavati | tataś ca sthiraḥ padārtho yadi kāryotpādanasamarthasvabhāvaḥ tato 'syākriyā nopapadyata iti sarvadaiva kuryāt | athāsamarthasvabhāvaḥ, tadāpi kriyā 'nupapannā, sarvadaiva na kuryād iti bhāvaḥ | yat tu kadācit karoti kadācin na [S. 118b.] ity etan na labhyate | tataś cākṣaṇikānāṃ tatkāryakriyāsamarthasvabhāvatve sahitāsahitāvasthayor ekarūpatvāt kevalānām api tatkāryakriyāprasaṅgena kuta ekārthakriyāpratiniyamalakṣaṇaṃ [T. 288b.] sahakāritvaṃ sambhavet? |
  atra para āha --
children.translated_text: and so forth. Granted, an entity may not [produce] of its own accord. But it is impossible for the essential nature to become otherwise by itself. And therefore, if a stable entity has an essential nature capable of producing effects, then its non-activity is untenable — so it should always produce. If, on the other hand, it has an essential nature that is incapable, then too activity is untenable — it should never produce. The meaning is: that it sometimes produces and sometimes does not is not obtainable. And therefore, if non-momentary entities have the essential nature capable of producing that effect, then since they have a single form in both the accompanied and unaccompanied states, from the absurd consequence that even alone they would produce that effect — how could the auxiliary-causation characterized as single-effect-production determination be possible? Here the opponent says —
'Accompanied by another' —

children.text:
ityādi | yady api kevalasyāpy akṣaṇikasya samarthaḥ svabhāvaḥ tathāpi anyasahitaḥ karoti na kevalaḥ | ayam api hy asya svabhāvaḥ yad -- `anyasahitena svakāryaṃ karttavyam na samarthasvabhāvenāpi satā kevalena' iti |
  siddhāntavādy āha --
children.translated_text: and so forth. Even though the essential nature of a non-momentary entity is capable even when alone, nevertheless it produces [only] when accompanied by another, not when alone. For this too is its essential nature — that 'the effect is to be produced when accompanied by another, not when alone, even though having a capable essential nature.' The proponent (<s>siddhāntavādin</s>) says —
'What of the one alone?' —

children.text: ityādi | anyasahitenaiva svakāryaṃ karttavyaṃ na kevalena ity etat kevalasyāsamarthasvabhāvatve yujyate nānyatheti manyamānasya praśnaḥ | paras tv anavagatābhiprāya āha --
children.translated_text: and so forth. This is the question of one who thinks: 'That the effect is to be produced only when accompanied by another and not when alone — this is coherent only if the essential nature of the one alone is incapable, not otherwise.' But the opponent, not having grasped the intention, says —
'Capable' —

children.text: iti | kevalasyāpy akṣaṇikasya samartha eva {p. 119.1} svabhāvaḥ anyathā 'syākṣaṇikataiva hīyeteti | siddhāntavādy āha --
children.translated_text: thus. The essential nature of the non-momentary entity, even when alone, is indeed capable — otherwise its very non-momentariness would be lost. The proponent says —
'Why does it not produce?' —

children.text:
iti | na hi samarthasyākriyā, sahitasyāvasthāyām iva yujyata iti sahitasyaiva kriyām icchatā kevalasyāsamarthasvabhāvataivopagantavyā |
 atha matam -- kevalasya yadi śiraś chidyate tathāpi na karotīty ata āha --
children.translated_text: thus. For the non-activity of something that is capable is not reasonable, just as in the accompanied state — so one who wishes [to maintain] activity only of the accompanied [entity] must accept that the essential nature of the one alone is incapable. Now if [one] thinks: 'Even if the head of the one alone is cut off, still it does not produce' — therefore he says —
'Not producing' —

children.text: ityādi | kāryānumeyaṃ hi sāmarthyaṃ na ca kevalasya kadācid api kāryakriyā 'stīti kathaṃ sāmarthyaṃ kalpyate? | nāyaṃ niyamaḥ yat samarthasvabhāvenāvaśyam eva kāryaṃ karttavyam, anyathā 'pi darśanāt iti manyamāna [S. 119a.] āha paraḥ --
children.translated_text: and so forth. For capacity is to be inferred from the effect, and since the one alone never has the activity of producing an effect, how can capacity be supposed? Thinking 'There is no such rule that something with a capable essential nature must necessarily produce an effect, since it is observed otherwise too,' the opponent says —
'Weavers and the like' —
and so forth. The proponent, refuting [this], says —
'One of a playful disposition' —

children.text: ityādi | devānāṃpriyaḥ ṛjuḥ mūrkho vā [T. 289a.] sukhasaṃvardhitatvāt ramaṇasvabhāvaḥ, krīḍanaṃ bāladharmaḥ, tatsādharmyeṇa prajñāvaikalyaṃ darśayati, sukhaidhitatvena śāstreṣv anabhiyogam | yo hy anabhiyukto durvuddhiś ca sa
children.translated_text: and so forth. A '<s>devānāṃpriya</s>' (literally 'dear to the gods,' i.e., a simpleton) — simple or foolish, having been nurtured in comfort, of a pleasure-loving nature; 'playfulness' is the characteristic of children — by analogy with that he shows the deficiency of wisdom; by being nurtured in comfort, the lack of application to the treatises. For one who is unapplied and of poor understanding,
'even what has been done' —
a matter, due to being of a forgetful nature, again and again
'causes to be done' —

children.text: punaḥ pratividhāpayati | kva punar etat prativihitam? ity āha --
children.translated_text: causes to be carried out again. Where then has this been carried out? To that he says —
'For thus' —

children.text:
-- ityādi | `bījādivad anekāntaḥ' ity[501]anena prastāvena nirlloṭhitam evaitat |
  tad evam akṣaṇikasya samarthasvabhāvatve
children.translated_text: and so forth. This has already been thoroughly examined in the occasion [of the verse] 'Like seeds and the like, [the reason is] inconclusive.' Thus, if the essential nature of a non-momentary entity is capable,

since the essential nature of producing the effect belonging only to the accompanied [state] would be contradicted, the non-activity of the one alone is untenable — thus concluding the demonstration, he says —
'Therefore, of that essential nature' —
of that which is capable of producing the effect,
'because of the impossibility of becoming otherwise' —
because of the absence of incapacity at any time,
'of that which has that property' —
of that which has the property of causal efficacy, the being-so is the causal activity,
'as in the final state' —
just as in the accompanied state,
'is unavoidable.'

body.translated_text: Why is it not accepted with respect to those having a stable, single essential nature? To this he says —

body.text:
p. 83, 15
[502] -syaivaikakārya- -- T.
[503] -sya kriyā- -- T.
[504] -cid apy asam- -- T.
body.translated_text:
p. 83, 15
[502] -syaivaikakārya- — T.
[503] -sya kriyā- — T.
[504] -cid apy asam- — T.
Section: 39. Refutation of the capacity in the form of the entity's own essential nature, as accepted by the <s>Mīmāṃsaka</s>.

body.text: syānmatam -- kevalo 'yam akṣaṇiko 'samartha eva | tataḥ kevalo na [S. 119b.] karoti, sahitāvasthāyāṃ tv asya sāmarthyaṃ sahakāribhyo jāyate | tataḥ sahita eva karotīty ata āha --

children.translated_text: 'When capacity arises in the final state' —
'of what kind?' —
of that which was previously incapable,
'existing' —
of that capacity,
'of which that arises' —
'when its being of that essential nature' —
is accepted by the <s>Mīmāṃsaka</s> and others. For

children.text: teṣāṃ samarthyasya sāmarthyasya[505]ca svabhāvabhedo 'bhimataḥ | kathañcit tadbhede 'pi tatsvabhāvatayaiva pratīyamānatvād iti te manyante |
children.translated_text: a difference of essential nature between capacity and the possessor of capacity is not accepted by them. Even if there is some difference, they think it is understood as having that very essential nature.
'That is simply the arising of something unprecedented' —
that arising is of an unprecedented entity itself — which is [the arising]

children.text:
apūrvasyaiva vastunaḥ sā utpattir yā tatsvabhāvasya sāmarthyasya | na hy ekasvabhāvatve sāmarthyam evāpūrvam upajātaṃ na samarthaḥ iti yuktam, tayoḥ svabhāvabhedaprasaṅgāt, viruddhadharmādhyāsasya bhedalakṣaṇatvāt |
  nanu pratīyamāne eva sāmarthyatadvator utpattyanupattī ekasvabhāvatā ca kathaṃ nihnotuṃ śakyate? iti cet | na | apramāṇena pratīteḥ, anyathā pratītyanusāriṇā bhavatā dvicandrādayo 'pi na nihnotavyāḥ | bādhakapramāṇasambhavāt te 'pahnūyanta iti cet | ihāpi vastuna ekasvabhāvasyotpattyanupattī parasparaviruddhe bādhike kiṃ neṣyete? | vyavasthitasyaiva vajropalāder ddharmiṇaḥ [S. 120a.] tatsvabhāvaṃ sāmarthyam utpannam iti ca pūrvāparakālayor apratibhāsamānavivekaḥ kathaṃ pratīyāt? |
  vijñānādikāryasyānutpattiyaugapadyodayaprasaṅgāt cakṣurādisānnidhye prāg asat tat sāmarthyam utpannaṃ kramavac ceti niścaya iti cet | yady evam ekākāratayā pūrvāparakālayor adhi(vi)kṛtaṃ pratyabhijñānam upajāyamānam apūrvasāmarthyapratibhāsaviviktopalādigrāhy[506]apy anumānād arthāpattito vā bādhām anubhavan na pramāṇam ity upagataṃ syāt | tathā, utpattyanutpattyor ekasvabhāvatāyāṃ virodhāt samarthasyaivāpūrvasyotpattiḥ[507]sadṛśāpabhāvagrahakṛtaś cārvāgdarśanānām ekatvavibhramo lūnapunarjjāteṣv iva keśanakhādiṣv iti kiṃ neṣyate? |
children.translated_text: of capacity, which is of that essential nature. For when they have a single essential nature, it is not reasonable [to say] 'only the capacity has arisen as unprecedented, not the one that is capable' — because of the absurd consequence of difference of essential nature between those two, since superimposition of contradictory properties is the defining mark of difference. But if the arising and non-arising [of capacity], and the single-naturedness of capacity and its possessor, are indeed perceived, how can they be denied? No — because the perception is by a non-<s>pramāṇa</s>; otherwise, you who follow perception should not deny even double-moons and the like. If [one says:] 'Those are denied because of the possibility of an invalidating <s>pramāṇa</s>' — here too, are not the arising and non-arising, which are mutually contradictory and invalidating, of an entity with a single essential nature [to be] accepted? And how could [the entity] — the property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>) such as a diamond and the like, which is established [as unchanging] — when its capacity of that essential nature has arisen, be perceived as not manifesting a distinction between the earlier and later times? If [one says:] 'From the non-arising, simultaneity, and sequential arising of the effect such as cognition and the like, in the proximity of the eye and the like, [we ascertain that] that capacity, previously non-existent, has arisen sequentially' — if so, then the recognition that arises apprehending [the entity] as having a single form at the earlier and later times, even though grasping the stone and the like as devoid of the manifestation of unprecedented capacity, experiencing invalidation from inference or from <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption), is accepted as not being a <s>pramāṇa</s>. Indeed, since arising and non-arising are contradictory in having a single essential nature, there is the arising of a capable [entity] that is itself unprecedented, and the confusion of unity on the part of ordinary people is caused by the apprehension of a similar successor — just as with hair, nails, and the like that are cut and regrown — why is this not accepted?

body.translated_text: One might think: this non-momentary entity, when alone, is simply incapable. Therefore, it does not produce when alone; but in the accompanied state, its capacity arises from the auxiliaries. Therefore, it produces only when accompanied — to this he says —

teṣāṃ sāmarthyasyāsāma- — T.
[506] -rahita-
[507] -syaivānanubhūtapūrva- — T.
Section: 40. Refutation of the capacity in the form of a non-essential-nature of the entity, as accepted by the <s>Naiyāyika</s>.

body.text: atha sāmarthyaṃ sahakāripratyayasānnidhyalakṣaṇam evety atatsvabhāvam iti nāpūrvotpattiprasaṅga [T. 290a.] itinaiyāyikādayo manyeran atrāha --
body.translated_text: If the <s>Naiyāyika</s> and others think: the capacity is precisely characterized as the proximity of auxiliary conditions, and thus is not of that [entity's own] essential nature, so there is no absurd consequence of unprecedented arising — to this he says —
'When not being of that essential nature' —
of the capacity, when accepted,
'that' —
the entity such as a seed and the like,
'as before' —
because of not relinquishing that form,
'even afterwards, is simply a non-producer.'

body.text:
| {p. 121.1} kutaḥ? | sāmarthyam ity ākhyā yasya padārthāntarasya sahakāripratyayasānnidhyalakṣaṇasya sa evātiśaya[śabda]vācya itinaiyāyikair abhyupagamāt | tata eva tadbhāvabhāvitvena kāryotpatteḥ | te 'pi sahakāriṇaḥ pratyayāḥ yady akṣaṇikāḥ teṣv apy evaṃ [S. 120b.] prasaṅgo 'nivārita eveti kṣaṇikataivaikārtha[kriyā]pratiniyamalakṣaṇaṃ sahakāritvam icchato 'bhyupeyā |
  punar apy akṣaṇikānām ekārthakriyāpratiniyamaṃ nirākartum upacayahetum āha --
body.translated_text: Why? Because it is accepted by the <s>Naiyāyika</s> that the excellence designated by the name 'capacity' — which is characterized as the proximity of auxiliary conditions — that same thing is what is denoted by the word 'excellence.' And precisely from that [proximity] alone, through being conditioned by its presence, the effect arises. If those auxiliary conditions too are non-momentary, then the same absurd consequence with respect to them too is unavoidable — and so one who accepts the auxiliary-causation characterized as single-effect-production determination must accept momentariness. And again, to refute the single-effect-production determination of non-momentary entities, he states an additional reason —
'Moreover' —

body.text: ityādi | yo 'sāv akṣaṇiko bhāvaḥ sakaleṣu sahakāriṣu svakāryaṃ karotītīṣyate, sa tadaiva tāvat kasmāt karoti? | yena hi kāraṇena tatkāryakriyāsvabhāvatvena tadā karoti tene(nai)va sthirasvabhāvatvāt prāg api kuryāt, tataḥ kuto 'syaikārthakriyāpratiniyamaḥ? iti bhāvaḥ |
body.translated_text: and so forth. That non-momentary entity which is accepted as producing its own effect when all the auxiliaries are present — why does it produce precisely then? For by whatever reason it produces then, due to having the essential nature of producing that effect, by that very same [reason], since its essential nature is stable, it should produce even before — so whence its single-effect-production determination? This is the meaning.
'Some other reasoning is sought, such that it would appear thus' —

body.text: iti sarvatreyam apratihatā yuktir iti manyamānaḥkumārilaḥprāha --
body.translated_text: thinking that this reasoning is undefeated everywhere, <s>Kumārila</s> says —
'Seen producing' —
and so forth. Since
I have seen it producing the effect precisely at that time,
'by the force of that observation we say it produces' —

body.text: kim atrānyayopapattyā [T. 290b.] 'bhihitayā[510]?, prāk tat kurvan na dṛṣṭaḥ tena na karotīty ekārtha[kriyā]pratiniyamaḥ sidhyati akṣaṇikānām apīti | bhāvo hi kāryaṃ karoti tajjananasvabhāvatayā na darśanabalenādṛṣṭasyāpi svakāryakaraṇāt ato nedam uttaraṃ sambadhyata ity upahasann āha --
body.translated_text: what need is there for another reasoning as stated? Previously it was not seen producing that, therefore it does not produce — thus the single-effect-production determination is established even for non-momentary entities. For an entity produces an effect due to having the essential nature of generating it, not by the force of observation — since even what is unseen produces its own effect. Therefore this reply is incoherent — thus mocking [<s>Kumārila</s>], he says —
'Oh, what great power!' —

body.text: ityādi | mahāprabhāvasya bhavato mahāsāmarthyaṃ darśanam, yasmād etad bhāvān kāryakaraṇasvabhāvavikalān api -- yadi kāryakaraṇasvabhāvatvād bhāvāḥ kāryaṃ kuryuḥ tadaitad evottaraṃ kiṃ noktam?, yataḥ [S. 121a.] kāryakaraṇe darśanam uttarīkṛtam iti kṛtvā --
body.translated_text: and so forth. Great is the power of your observation, O one of great efficacy, since this [observation] — entities that are deficient in the essential nature of producing effects — if entities were to produce effects due to having the essential nature of producing effects, then why was this very reply not stated? Because the observation was given as the reply regarding effect-production, [therefore] —
'by mere essential nature' —
by the mere existence of the self,
'it engages in various kinds of activities' —

body.text: tat kathaṃ mahāsāmarthyaṃ na syāt? | na cātra me kācid akṣamā[511]kintu
body.translated_text: then how could it not be a great power? And here I have no objection; but
'if perchance something' —
'a cause' —
'somehow' —
of one who is inattentive or distracted,
'of his honor' —
this is a term of respect,
'were to exceed the range of observation' —
'then' —
'alas!' —

body.text: iti dainyodbhāvanam etat, aprasavo dharmo 'sya tad idam --
body.translated_text: this is an expression of distress; whose property is non-production, that is —
'having the property of non-production' —
having its lineage departed,
'it would be' —

body.text:
ti iyam asmākaṃ cintā cittaṃ dunoti |
  para āha --
body.translated_text: this is our worry that torments [our] mind. The opponent says —
'Indeed, we do not' —
and so forth. We indeed do not assert that the causal activity of entities that are devoid of the essential nature of producing effects [occurs] by the force of our observation; rather,
of entities — by the force of our observation, we say their causal efficacy; rather,

body.text: svabhāvenaiva te bhāvāḥ tatkāryakaraṇasvabhāvāḥ, tataḥ svakāryaṃ kurvanti |
body.translated_text: Those entities are, by their very essential nature, of the nature of producing that effect; therefore they produce their own effect.
'Observing them' —
'we merely know' —

body.text:
ta[512]ete kārakasvabhāvā iti | darśanasya hi yathāvasthitavastuvijñāne vyāpāraḥ, nāvidyā(dya)mānasvabhāvakriyāyām iti|
  siddhāntavādy āha --
body.translated_text: that these have the nature of being agents. For the operation of perception is in cognizing things as they are, not in creating a non-existent essential nature. | The <s>Siddhāntavādin</s> says:
'True, there is this too' —

body.text: | kiṃ vayaṃ nyāyānurāgitayā nyāyyaṃ [T. 291a.] vacanam upalakṣayāmaḥ, uta bhavān eva sarvadā nyāyyavacanarahito 'pi kathañcin nyāyyam uktavān iti sañjātaparitoṣaḥ pṛcchati -- kiṃ tad? ity āha --
body.translated_text: | 'Do we, out of love for logic, note a logical statement, or is it that you — always devoid of logical statements — have somehow for once said something logical, and so, having become satisfied, ask: what is it?' — he says:
'The essential nature of those' —
of entities —
'has the property of effect-production' —
has the property of producing effects —
'by that' —
by that reason —
'all together' —

body.text: samagrāḥ pratyayāḥ sahakāriṇo yeṣāṃ teṣām akṛtvā kāryaṃ
body.translated_text: those for whom the conditions — the cooperative causes — are complete, without having produced the effect —
'there is no arriving at indifference' —

body.text: naudāsīny apratipattiḥ iti satyam -- idam apy asti bhavato nyāyyaṃ vacanam iti, kintu idam asi praṣṭavyaḥ -- [S. 121b.]
body.translated_text: there is no arriving at disregard or non-engagement. True — this too is a logical statement of yours. But this must be asked:
'That essential nature having the property of immediate causal activity (<s>akṣepakriyā</s>) — is it of those [entities] only at the final state' —
at the state of completeness, at the moment just prior to the arising of the effect —
'arisen?' —
'Or was it present even before' —
even in the state of mutual separation —
'[as well]?' —

body.text:
? |
  tatra tadaivotpanne tatsvabhāvatve 'pūrvotpattir eva, atatsvabhāvatve so 'kāraka eveti prāguktadoṣabhayāt para āha --
body.translated_text: | Therein, if [it] arises only then: if it has that essential nature, then it is simply a new arising [of that nature]; if it does not have that essential nature, then it is simply a non-agent. Out of fear of the previously stated fault, the opponent says:
'It was [present]' —

body.text: | kutaḥ? pracyutaś ca utpannaś ca pracyutotpannaḥ[513], tasya pratiṣedhaḥ
body.translated_text: | Why? 'Fallen away and arisen' — that which has fallen away and arisen (<s>pracyutotpanna</s>) — the negation of that is:
'unfallen and unarisen' —

body.text: sthira ekaḥ svabhāvo yeṣāṃ bhāvānāṃ teṣāṃ kasmiṃścit kāle
body.translated_text: of those entities whose essential nature is stable and single — at any time,
'of any' —
essential nature observed therein —
'because of the impossibility of absence.' —

body.text:
| kṣaṇikeṣv eva hy ekadā dṛṣṭaḥ svabhāvo 'nyadā na bhavet tadā tasyānyatvāt | nāpracyutānutpannapūrvāpararūpeṣu sthireṣu bhāveṣv iti |
  {p. 123.1} atrāha --
body.translated_text: | For only in momentary [entities] could an essential nature seen at one time not exist at another time, since it would then be something different. But not in stable entities whose prior and subsequent forms are unfallen and unarisen. | {p. 123.1} Here [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>] says:
'Then what now?' —

body.text: ityādi | syānmatam -- naivedam anena vākyena sadṛśam asmad vākyam ity āha --
body.translated_text: and so forth. One might think: 'This statement of ours is not at all similar to that statement [of <s>Dharmakīrti</s>].' So he says:
'Or what of this?' —

body.text: ityādi | yady etad anena tulyaṃ [T. 291b.] na bhavati tadā sakalasahakāryavasthāyāḥ[514]
body.translated_text: and so forth. If this is not equivalent to that, then even before the state [of completeness with] all cooperative causes,
'even before' —
'this' —
'having the essential nature of immediate causal activity' —
having the essential nature of unhesitating effect-production —
'and yet does not produce the effect' —

body.text:
ty asya bhāṣitasyārtho vaktavya iti |
  naiyāyikās tu manyante -- bhāvānāṃ sahakārisannidhānāsannidhānāpekṣayā kārakākārakasvabhāvavyavasthā, na svabhāvataḥ, tenāyam apracyutotpannasthiraikasvabhāvatve 'pi [S. 122a.] na prāg api svakāryajananasvabhāvaḥ, kintu sannihitasakalasahakāripratyaya eveti | tanmatam āśaṅkamāna āha --
body.translated_text: — the meaning of this statement must be explained. | But the <s>Naiyāyikas</s> think: the determination of entities as having agent or non-agent nature is relative to the proximity or non-proximity of cooperative [causes], not intrinsically. Therefore, even though this [entity] has a stable, single, unfallen-and-unarisen essential nature, it does not have the nature of producing its own effect even before [completeness]; rather, only when all cooperative conditions are proximate. Anticipating their view, [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>] says:
'[When] conjoined' —
and so forth. | He refutes this:
'Then it is different' —

body.text: ityādi | yadi nāma sahitasya svakāryajananasvabhāvatā, kevalasya ca tadviparītarūpatā, anyatvaṃ tu kasmād bhavati? ity ata āha --
body.translated_text: and so forth. Even if the conjoined [entity] has the nature of producing its own effect, and the isolated [entity] has the opposite nature — why would there be otherness? To this he says:
'Difference of essential nature' —
and so forth.
'For difference of essential nature is indeed the defining characteristic of difference of entities.' —

body.text:
| sa cet tatkāryajanakājanakarūpatayā bhidyate, śāliyavabījādīnām iva kathaṃ iva bhāvabhedo na syāt? | na hi svabhāvād anyo bhāvaḥ yatas tadbhede 'pi na bhidyeta, niḥsvabhāvatāprasaṅgāt |
  nanu coktaṃ svato janakājanakasvabhāvatāvirahāt pratyayāntarabhāvādyapekṣatvāt janakājanakarūpatāyās tadbhede 'pi kuto bhāvabhedaprasaṅgaḥ?,[515]tasyāparāpekṣasvabhāvabhedalakṣaṇatvāt[516]ity ata āha --
body.translated_text: | And if that [entity] differs by having the form of being a producer and non-producer of that effect — like rice, barley, and seed — how could there not be a difference of entities? For there is no entity apart from essential nature, such that even with a difference of that [essential nature], it would not differ — because of the absurd consequence of being without essential nature. | But it was said: because of the absence of intrinsic producer/non-producer nature, and because the producer/non-producer nature depends on other conditions, even with a difference of that [nature], whence the absurd consequence of entity-difference? — because [entity-difference] is defined by a difference of essential nature not dependent on anything else. To this he says:
'For it, even in conjunction' —

body.text:
ityādi | tadaitad uttaraṃ bhāvatkaṃ sambadhyeta[517]yadi bhāvo yo 'sau paraḥ sahakāritvābhimataḥ [T. 292a.] sannidhīyate tadrūpeṇa karttā syāt na svarūpeṇa | na caitad asti, tathābhāve hi paramārthataḥ sa eva paraḥ[518]karttā syāt | tatra tu kartṛtvavyapadeśaḥ [S. 122b.] kalpanānirmita eva bhavet | na ca kalpanānuvidhāyin yo 'rthakriyāḥ | na hi māṇavako dahanopacārād ādhīyate pāke | tataś ca nāsyānupakāriṇo bhāvam apekṣeta kāryam iti tadrahitebhya eva {p. 124.1} sahakāribhyo bhavet | yad vā tebhyo 'pi na bhavet | teṣām api pararūpeṇa kartṛtve svayam akārakatvāt | tataḥ sarveṣām evaṃ svayam akārakatve pararūpeṇāpy akārakatvāt sarvathā kārakocheda eveti na kiñcit
kutaścit jāyeta | tasmāt svarūpeṇaiva bhāvaḥ svakāryasya karttā na pararūpeṇeti nāsyottarasyāvakāśaḥ | tato 'nyaḥ sahito 'nyaś ca kevalaḥ ity etad avicalam eveti |
  atha yena svarūpeṇāyaṃ janakas tad asya sahitāsahitāvasthayoḥ sarvadā 'sti tadā svarūpaṃ ca svakāryajanakam asya sthirasvabhāvasya prāg api sahitāvasthāyās tad eva yatsahitāvasthāyām akṣepakriyāsvabhāvam iti tasmāt na kathaṃcit kāryakriyāvirāmaḥ | athavā kadācit paro brūyāt svahetubhir evāyaṃ pratyayāntarāpekṣaḥ [T. 292b.] svakāryajananasvabhāvo janita iti kevalo na karoti | na cāsya sahitāsahitāvasthayoḥ svabhāvabhedaḥ, pratyayāntarāpekṣasvakāryajananasvabhāvatāyāḥ [S. 123a.] sarvadā bhāvāt ity ata āha --
body.translated_text: and so forth. This reply would be substantive only if the entity that is the other — regarded as a cooperative cause — when it becomes proximate, were the agent in its own form, not in the [principal entity's] own form. But this is not the case, for if it were so, then in ultimate reality that other alone would be the agent. And in that case, the designation of agency [to the principal entity] would be merely a product of conceptual construction. But causal efficacies do not follow conceptual construction. For a boy is not employed in cooking merely because of the figurative attribution of burning [to him]. Therefore, the effect would not depend on the existence of that which does not contribute — and so the effect would arise from the cooperative causes alone, devoid of it. Or it would not arise even from those [cooperative causes], since for them too, if agency is in the form of another, they themselves would be non-agents. Therefore, when all are thus non-agents in their own form, and also non-agents in another's form, there would be a complete severance of agency in every way — and nothing would arise from anything. Therefore, an entity is the agent of its own effect in its own form only, not in another's form — so there is no room for this reply. Hence, 'the conjoined is different and the isolated is different' — this remains firmly established. | Now, if that very own form by which this is a producer is always present in both its conjoined and isolated states, and if its own form is the producer of its own effect, and [that form] of this entity with stable essential nature exists even before the state of conjunction — it is the very same as that which in the state of conjunction has the nature of immediate causal activity — therefore, there is in no way a cessation of causal activity. Or, someone might at some point say: 'This [entity] was produced by its own causes as having the essential nature of producing its own effect dependent on other conditions — therefore when isolated it does not produce. And there is no difference of essential nature between its conjoined and isolated states, because the essential nature of producing its own effect dependent on other conditions is always present.' To this he says:
'For it, even in conjunction' —

body.text:
ityādi | svarūpeṇaivāsya kartṛtvāt tasya ca prāg api bhāvāt pratyayāntarāpekṣāyāś ca tato labhyasyātmātiśayasyābhāvenāyogāt upakāralakṣaṇatvād asya, anyathā 'tiprasaṅgāt, kevalasya kāryakaraṇam anivāryam iti akurvataḥ kathaṃ sahitāvasthāyā na bhedaḥ syāt? iti bhāvaḥ | pratyayāntarāpekṣasvakāryakaraṇasvabhāva ity api pararūpeṇākārasya
pratyayāntarasannidhānopalakṣitakāle kārakatvaṃ na prāg ity ayam arthaḥ | tataś ca kadācit kāryakriyāsvabhāvo na sarvadā iti bruvatā kathaṃ sarvadā kāryajananasvabhāvatā 'syoktā bhavati? | nanv evaṃ svabhāvabheda evāsya tadatatkālayoḥ samarthitaḥ syāt | tasmān nākṣaṇikānām ekārthakriyāpratiniyamalakṣaṇaṃ sahakāritvam iti sthitam |
  paraḥ
body.translated_text: and so forth. Because its agency is in its own form only, and because that [own form] is present even before [conjunction], and because the requirement of other conditions is untenable due to the absence of any additional feature of the self obtainable from that [condition] — since [cooperative causation] is defined as conferring assistance, and because otherwise there would be over-extension — the production of the effect by the isolated [entity] is unavoidable. So if it does not produce [when isolated], how could there not be a difference from the conjoined state? — this is the purport. Even with [the claim that] 'it has the essential nature of producing its own effect dependent on other conditions,' the meaning is: agency characterized by another's form obtains at the time marked by the proximity of another condition, but not before. And therefore, when one says 'it sometimes has the nature of causal activity, not always,' how can its always having the nature of producing effects have been asserted? But thus a difference of essential nature between those two times [conjoined and isolated] would indeed have been established. Therefore, it is established that for non-momentary [entities], cooperative causation defined as the restriction of a single causal efficacy is untenable. | The opponent,
demonstrating that the same fault applies [to the Buddhist], says:
'Even for one who [accepts]' —

body.text: ityādi subodham | yadi nāma kṣaṇikas tathāpi kinna bhavati? ity āha --
body.translated_text: and so forth — this is easily understood. Even if [the entity] is momentary, why does [the objection] not apply? He says:
'It has been stated — of what kind' —
'whose activity is not separate from the cooperative [causes]' —
'is the activity.' —

body.text: | `te[520]{p. 125.1} samarthā [S. 123b.] eva svabhāvato 'ntyāḥ pratyayāḥ saha jāyante kṣaṇikā yeṣāṃ [T. 293a.] prākpaścātpṛthagbhāvo nāsti' ity atra |
body.translated_text: | 'They themselves are capable by their very nature — the final conditions arise together — they are momentary, and their prior, subsequent, or separate existence does not obtain' — regarding this:
'How could that which exists in a single moment' —
that which has the disposition of existing in only the one final moment —
'be otherwise' —

body.text: antyakṣaṇāt prāk paścāt pṛthag vā bhavet?
body.translated_text: exist before or after or separately from the final moment?
'And that which' —
'otherwise' —
'exists, that' —
'very one existing in the final moment' —
whose essential nature is assisted by the continuum of cooperative [causes], having the property of immediate causal activity —
'is not' — therefore this —
'raised in the non-momentary thesis' —
'absurd consequence' —
does not obtain
in the momentary thesis. Why?
'Of the agent and non-agent' —

body.text: ityādi | kārako 'ntyaḥ akārakas tadanyaḥ tayor yaḥ
body.translated_text: and so forth. The agent is the final [moment]; the non-agent is what is other than that. Of those two, the
'essential nature' —

body.text:
sa bhinno 'pi bhedāvivakṣayaikatvenoktaḥ | tathā kārakasya
yo hetur upāntyaḥ, akārakasyāpi yo hetus tadanyaḥ sa bhinno 'py abhedavivakṣayaivaikatvenoktaḥ | tena kārakākārakayor yau svabhāvau tayor ekatra dharmiṇi virodhāt | tathā tayoḥ svabhāvayor janakau yau hetū -- ekaḥ kārakasvabhāvajanako 'nyaś cākārakasvabhāvajanakaḥ -- tayor apy ekatra dharmiṇi virodhāt, anyatve sati | akārakasvabhāvajanakahetor utpannasyākārakasya svabhāvasyānyatvāt
body.translated_text: that, though distinct, is called one with the intention of not expressing the difference. Similarly, the cause of the agent — the penultimate [moment] — and the cause of the non-agent — the other [moment] — that, though distinct, is called one with the very intention of expressing non-difference. Therefore, because the two essential natures of agent and non-agent are contradictory in a single property-bearer, and because the two causes — one producing the agent-nature and the other producing the non-agent-nature — are also contradictory in a single property-bearer, given their being different, and because the essential nature of the non-agent produced from the cause of the non-agent-nature is different —

body.text: yaśca bhavati sa eva na bhavatīti nāyaṃprasaṅga
body.translated_text: 'that which exists is the very one that does not exist' — this absurd consequence [does not arise].
Thus. |

body.text: aparas tv anyathā sthirarūpeṣv ekārthākriyāpratiniyamaṃ [S. 124a.] kalpitavān tam upanyasyati

children.translated_text: 'One who also thinks' —
and so forth. Of an entity,

children.text:
hy akṣepakriyādharmaiva[523]sarvadā svabhāvaḥ[524], na tu [T. 293b.] yathā kecid brū(bru)vate -- sahakārisannidhānāpekṣā vastūnāṃ kārakasvabhāvavyavasthā, na svata iti | svato 'kārakātve pararūpeṇa kārakatvāyogāt kārakavyavasthocchedaprasaṅgāt | sa evaṃvidhasvabhāvo na kadācit sāhityaṃ svakāryakaraṇe 'pekṣate yato 'nyaḥ sahito 'nyaś ca kevalaḥ kārakākārakasvabhāvabhedāt syāt | sa tarhi sarvadā tatsvabhāvaḥ kāryaṃ kinna karoti? iti cet | kāryasya pratyayāntarāpekṣasvabhāvatayā tasmiṃ(smin) sarvadā janakatvenāvasthite 'pi kevalād abhāvāt, tenātra kāryam evāparādhyati, yat tasmiṃ(smin) kevale janakatayā 'vasthite 'pi pratyayāntarāṇy apekṣata iti | tataḥ {p. 126.1} tadātmanaḥ kāryasya sahitebhya eva bhāvād ekārthakriyālakṣaṇaṃ sahakāritvam akṣaṇikānām
apy upapadyata iti | siddhāntavādī pūrvadoṣānatikramam asya darśayann āha --
children.translated_text: the essential nature is always precisely the property of immediate causal activity (<s>akṣepakriyādharma</s>), and not, as some say — 'the determination of entities as having agent-nature depends on the proximity of cooperative causes, not intrinsically.' Because if [an entity is] intrinsically a non-agent, agency in another's form is untenable, and because there would be the absurd consequence of the complete severance of the determination of agency. That entity of such essential nature never requires conjunction for producing its own effect, such that 'the conjoined is different and the isolated is different' due to difference of agent/non-agent essential nature. 'Then, if it always has that essential nature, why does it not [always] produce the effect?' — if so: because the effect has the essential nature of depending on other conditions, even though [the cause] is always established as having the nature of a producer — [the effect does not arise] from the isolated [cause] because of its absence [as an effect of that type]. Therefore, here it is the effect alone that is at fault — which, even though [the cause] is established in its capacity as producer when isolated, requires other conditions. Therefore, {p. 126.1} because the effect of that nature arises only from [causes] in conjunction, cooperative causation defined as restriction of a single causal efficacy is tenable even for non-momentary [entities]. The <s>Siddhāntavādin</s>, showing that this [view] does not escape the previously stated faults, says:
'Of that [person] too' —
of one who speaks thus —
'how does that' —
the entity regarded as permanent —
'when isolated, produce indeed' —

children.text: `akṣepakriyādharmaiva sa tasya svabhāvaḥ' iti [S.124b.] vacanāt | kāryaṃ ca sahitebhya eva bhavati, `sāmagrījanyasvabhāvatvāt tasya' iti vacanāt | tasmāt kevalān na bhavatīti
children.translated_text: because of the statement 'the property of immediate causal activity is its very essential nature.' And the effect arises only from [causes] in conjunction, because of the statement 'because it has the nature of being produced by the assemblage.' Therefore, it does not arise from [the cause when] isolated — thus
'the contradiction is of the same nature' —

children.text:
yaḥ pūrvam uktaḥ. tathā hi -- yady akṣepakriyādharmā tadā 'vaśyam anena kāryaṃ kartavyam na ced avaśyaṃ karoti katham akṣepakriyāsvabhāvaḥ |
 akṣepeṇa kāryadarśanād akṣepakriyāsvabhāvatā 'vagamyate [T. 294a.] nānyathā iti parābhiprāyāśaṅkayā ''ha --
children.translated_text: as that which was stated previously. For thus: if [it has] the property of immediate causal activity, then it must necessarily produce the effect; and if it does not necessarily produce, how is it of the nature of immediate causal activity? | Anticipating the opponent's intent that 'the essential nature of immediate causal activity is understood from observing the effect through [immediate] instigation, not otherwise,' [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>] says:

{p. 128.1} and so forth. Cooperative causation characterized by a single purposive activity alone [obtains] everywhere — nowhere does the production of an additional feature occur. But where entities, by assisting the continuum through the generation of each successively more distinguished subsequent moment from the preceding conditions, attain the status of being causes of the intended effect — just as fire, water, and the like [assist] in the production of cooked rice and the like from raw rice and the like, and earth and the like [assist] in the production of sprouts and the like from seeds and the like — there, the cooperative activity of the conditions in producing the additional feature is spoken of in the world. [This is] based on the continuum: relying on the effect called 'continuum,' characterized by the second and subsequent distinguished moments [arising] from the preceding moments, and through the determination of the identity of the earlier and later moments — 'this additional feature belongs to that very [thing]' — not based on a [permanent] substance. It is merely conventional and not ultimate.
| But from each preceding moment, which has the nature of maturation of its own causes and proximity conditions, in the production of each subsequent additional feature, the cooperative causation of the preceding causal aggregate is precisely characterized as a single purposive activity — that is the ultimate [truth] even there. So there is no difficulty. | Why is the production of an additional feature based on a [permanent] substance not accepted? | Because in a momentary substantial entity, an additional feature does not arise [in it], since that [feature] has the nature of the immediately subsequent moment.
  But if an additional feature does not arise in a momentary substance like raw rice and the like, let it also not arise in the immediately subsequent [moment]. Then, just as momentary entities, though not acquiring any additional feature from each other, produce only when combined and not alone — so too non-momentary entities [could do the same]. And thus their cooperative causation would be characterized as a single purposive activity. And it cannot be said: 'that nature of something which was previously non-productive would also be so later.' and so forth. If no additional feature is produced, since proximity would be equal to non-proximity, even in the presence of fire and the like, there would be no production of cooked rice from raw rice and the like. Likewise, for one who has entered a dark chamber from a bright [area], if the sense faculty does not gradually acquire an additional feature from its assistants, then, as before, even later it would not produce object-cognition at all. {p. 129.1} Therefore, whatever effect that was [previously] impossible where it is [now] observed — that [cause producing it] must be different from [its former state], just as a <s>kodrava</s> (millet) seed is different from a rice seed. Thus, that which produces that effect through having an additional feature is different from that which has no additional feature. In this way, where the effect arises gradually from cooperative causes, there the cooperative causation characterized by the production of an additional feature is conventional, while the primary [cooperative causation] even there is characterized as a single purposive activity — this has been established.
