aṅkurādeḥ syāt, viśeṣābhāvād ity abhiprāyaḥ | tataś ca parasparato viśeṣotpādānapekṣiṇa eva sahakāriṇaḥ [S. 129a.] kāryaṃ kurvīran |
  kim evaṃ sati siddhaṃ bhavati? iti cet, āha --
body.translated_text:
of the sprout and the like, [the consequence] would follow — the purport is: because of the absence of a distinguishing feature. And consequently, the auxiliary causes, which require the production of a distinguishing feature from one another, would [each on their own] produce the effect.
If [one asks:] 'what is established when this is so?' — he says:
'Therefore' —

body.text: yena kṣaṇikā api parasparato viśeṣotpādā 'napekṣā eva svakāryaṃ kurvanti ekakāryapratiniyamalakṣaṇaṃ ca sahakāritvaṃ pratipadyante tena kāraṇena
body.translated_text: by that reason — that momentary entities too, without depending on the production of a distinguishing feature from one another, produce their own effect, and [that they] have cooperative causation characterized as the regularity of single-effect production —

body.text: akṣaṇikānām api kāraṇatāsyāt, apekṣaṇīyebhyaḥsvabhāvātiśayotpattiśca na syāt
body.translated_text: 'even of non-momentary entities there would be causation, and the arising of an excellence of essential nature from those upon which one depends would not obtain' —

body.text: ity akṣaṇikavādī kṣaṇikapakṣeṇa[531]svapakṣasya sāmyamāpādayati | yad āha -
body.translated_text: thus the proponent of non-momentariness seeks to establish the equivalence of his own position with the momentary position. As he says:

body.text:
p. 113.27
[529] pūrvapūrvakṣa- -- T.
[530] midyate -- T.
[531] kṣaṇikāpekṣaṇāt -- T.
body.translated_text:
p. 113.27
[529] prior-prior-moment- — T.
[530] is refuted — T.
[531] from the standpoint of the momentary — T.

children.translated_text: 'Who would look good arguing thus, if it were not for shamelessness?

body.translated_text: Or ignorance — since all of this is equally [applicable] to momentary entities too.' ||
'The conditions that are causes of the distinguishing feature of those [entities] are in no way
tenable for momentary entities, just as for permanent ones, because of the non-distinction of moments.' ||

body.text: iti | tatraitat syāt prathamakṣaṇe 'pi kṣitibījādayaḥ parasparataḥ samutpannaviśeṣā eva sannidhīyante --

children.translated_text: 'That with which something has a connection — even when far away, it has that [connection].'

children.text: iti nyāyād dhi dūradeśavarttinām api hetuphalabhāvāt ity āśaṅkyāha --
children.translated_text: For by this principle, even things situated in distant places have a cause-effect relation — anticipating this [objection], he says:
'But by the auxiliary cause' —

children.text:
ityādi | sahakāriṇaḥ [T. 298a.] parasparasamparkkavikalā api vastudharmatayaivānyonyam upakurvantīti sahakāriṇā kāryotpādānuguṇaviśeṣajananāya kṛtaviśeṣa eva samparkkakāla upatiṣṭheta, evaṃ [S. 129b.] saty anavasthā syāt | tathā hi -- tadviśeṣotpattāv apy aparaḥ sahakārikṛto viśeṣo 'bhyupagantavyaḥ, tathā tadutpattāv apy anya iti |
  atha naivaṃ sahakāriṇaḥ parasparasya kāryotpādānuguṇaviśeṣanimittam aparaṃ viśeṣaṃ kurvanti, svabhāvata eva tatra teṣāṃ yogyatvāt ity ata āha --
children.translated_text:
and so forth. Even though auxiliary causes lack mutual contact, they assist one another through the very nature of reality (<s>vastudharmatā</s>) — [so if] one that has been given a distinguishing feature by an auxiliary cause were to present itself at the time of contact, for the purpose of producing a distinguishing feature conducive to effect-production, then in that case there would be an infinite regress (<s>anavasthā</s>). Thus: for the production of that distinguishing feature too, another distinguishing feature produced by the auxiliary cause would have to be accepted, and similarly for its production yet another, and so on.
But [if one argues:] it is not so — auxiliary causes do not produce another distinguishing feature as the ground of a distinguishing feature conducive to each other's effect-production, because they are naturally capable of that — to this he says:
'And not' —

children.text: ityādi | naiva hi sahakāriṇaḥ kṣitibījādayaḥ parasparasya kāryotpādānuguṇo yo viśeṣaḥ tadutpādane
children.translated_text: and so forth. For the auxiliary causes — earth, seeds, and the like — [in regard to] the production of each other's distinguishing feature that is conducive to effect-production,
'always' —
at all times, a state of capability —
'by which' —
by which state of capability,
'always connected' —
always bound —
'of these' —

children.text:
kṣitibījādīnāṃ {p. 132.1} kāryotpādānuguṇaviśeṣajanako viśeṣaḥ syāt yataḥ `aviśiṣtād viśeṣotpattau kāryasyāpi syāt' ity etad api parihriyeta |
  kuta etad? ity āha --
children.translated_text:
of earth, seeds, and the like — there would be a distinguishing feature that produces the distinguishing feature conducive to effect-production, by which [the objection] 'if there is production of a distinguishing feature from the undistinguished, the effect too would [follow]' — even this would be resolved.
How is this [known]? He says:
'[From observing] the means for that' —

children.text: ityādi | teṣāṃ kṣitibījādīnām upāye -- yogyadeśopanipāte kāryavyaktidarśanāt[532]apāye ca -- parasparasamparkkavirāme kāryānutpattidarśanāt | yadi hi kāryotpādānuguṇaviśeṣotpādane sarvadā yogyāvasthāḥ syuḥ tadā so 'pi viśeṣaḥ sarvadā [T. 298b.] syāt | tatas tatparamparābhāvi kāryam iti tadupāyāpāyayoḥ kāryasyotpattyanutpattī na syātām | [S. 130a.] tasmān na sahakāriṇaḥ kāryotpādānuguṇaviśeṣotpādane yogyāvasthāḥ sarvadeti | yataḥ sahakāriṇā pṛthagavasthitenānavasthābhayāt kṛtaviśeṣo nopatiṣṭhate parasparataś ca prathamasamparkkakṣaṇabhāvināṃ nopeyate[533]yujyate vā | tena kāraṇenādyo viśeṣaḥ kāryotpādānuguṇaḥ sahakāribhyaḥ samānakālatayā nirupakārasya kṣitibījādeḥ
children.translated_text: and so forth. Of those — earth, seeds, and the like — when the means [is present] — from observing the manifestation of the effect upon arrival at a suitable place; and when [the means] is absent — from observing the non-production of the effect upon the cessation of mutual contact. For if they were always in a state of capability for producing the distinguishing feature conducive to effect-production, then that distinguishing feature too would always exist. And consequently, the effect that follows from the series of that [distinguishing feature] — its production and non-production would not [vary] with the presence and absence of those means. Therefore, the auxiliary causes are not always in a state of capability for producing the distinguishing feature conducive to effect-production. Since, due to the fear of infinite regress, one that has been given a distinguishing feature by an auxiliary cause existing separately does not present itself; and since [a distinguishing feature] existing in moments at the first contact is not accepted or is not tenable — for that reason, the initial distinguishing feature conducive to effect-production, [arising] from auxiliary causes that are simultaneous and thus unhelpful to the earth-seed and the like,
'does not arise' —
yet it is accepted that it does arise. Therefore, since all moments in the non-aggregate state are without distinction from those in the aggregate state,

children.text: , utpadyate cāsau itīṣyate | tena samagrāvasthāvat sarveṣāṃ vyagrāvasthābhāvinām api kṣaṇānām aviśeṣāt

tajjananasvabhāvatve 'py ajananāt samagrāvasthāyām eva jananād | yathā kṣaṇikānām ekārthakriyāpratiniyamalakṣaṇaṃ sahakāritvaṃ tathā sthirasvabhāvānām api bhaviṣyatīti kṣīṇasarvopāyo 'kṣaṇikavādī sāmyam evātura iva bahumanyamānas tatraiva bharaṃ[535]kṛtavān |
children.translated_text: even though they have the nature of producing that [effect], they do not produce [it when not aggregated], and they produce only in the aggregate state. Just as cooperative causation characterized by the regularity of single-effect production [applies] for momentary entities, so too it will [apply] for entities of stable nature — thus the proponent of non-momentariness, having exhausted all his resources, places his burden right there upon the equivalence [argument], as if valuing it like a sick man [values his cure].
The proponent (<s>siddhāntavādin</s>), indirectly mocking the opponent, says:
'For us, [stating it] again and again' —

children.text: ityādi | yadi punaḥ punar vacane 'pi lokasya nyāyapratītir bhavati śataśo 'pi brūmaḥ | kim aṅga punar dvau trīn vā vārān? | na hi parārthapravṛttānām asmākaṃ punaḥ punar abhidhāne kaścid udvego bhavati | evaṃ vādinaś ca śāstrakṛtaḥ kvacit prakārāntareṇa[536]tam evārthaṃ [T. 299a.] sphuṭīkurvato ye punaruktāparihārāya yat ante sa teṣām asthānapariśrama eva | yadi nodvego hanta tarhy ucyatām ity ata āha --
children.translated_text: and so forth. If even by stating [it] again and again, people gain understanding of the reasoning, we will say it even a hundred times. What to speak of two or three times? For there is no weariness for us who are engaged for the benefit of others, in stating [it] repeatedly. And for those who, in order to avoid the charge of repetition against the author of the treatise (<s>śāstrakṛt</s>) who sometimes elucidates the very same point in a different manner — their effort is simply misdirected. 'If there is no weariness, then let it be stated!' — to this he says:
'Not from the production of a distinguishing feature alone' —

and so forth. The cooperative causation of auxiliary causes through the production of a distinguishing feature is nowhere possible in ultimate reality, because for seeds and the like existing at the first moment, due to the absence of that [distinguishing feature], there would be an absence of cooperative causation with respect to producing the distinguishing feature conducive to effect-production. Rather, the production of a single effect alone is conceived, by the reasons stated above, as the ultimate cooperative causation of auxiliary causes. And that [single-effect production] exists even for those that partake of the first contact — so why would they not be auxiliary causes?
The opponent says: that single-effect production too would not be possible for those lacking a distinguishing feature from one another. But if the single-effect production of those lacking a distinguishing feature from one another is accepted, then, since the capacity to produce that [effect] in that state is accepted for each individually, that [production] would occur even separately, just as in that [aggregate] state. Thus: in that state too, they produce without any distinguishing feature from one another. How would their production of that specific effect not follow even when separate? For there is no distinction at all between their aggregate and non-aggregate states. 'Let it be so — what is the fault?' If so:
'And thus' —
when the consequence of producing the distinguishing feature conducive to effect-production separately [obtains],
'that which has the character of arising from that distinguishing feature' —
a sprout and the like —
'the effect too' —

children.text:
viśeṣavat kevalāt sahakāriṇaḥ syāt iti cen manyase, atrāpi sarvam uktam uttaram | tathā hi -- saṃhatāsaṃhatāvasthayor nirviśeṣā eva kṣaṇakṣayiṇo bhāvā iti taducyate tat kiṃ tāvad viśeṣamātrāpekṣayā? āhosvit [T. 299b.] kāryotpādānuguṇaviśeṣajanakaviśeṣāpekṣayā?
| yadi prācyo vikalpaḥ tad ayuktam | na hi kācid viśeṣamātrarahitā 'vasthā [S. 131a.] sambhavati, sarvadā 'parāparapratyayayoganibandhanasyāparāparaviśeṣasya bhāvāt | na hi kadācit kiṃcid ekam eva, ādhāracchāyātapavātaśītāder yathāsambhavaṃ bhāvāt | na ca tabhāve 'pi tat tādṛśam eva, kāraṇabhedāt | etāvat tu syāt -- kaścid viśeṣaḥ kvacit kārye 'nuguṇo na sarvaḥ sarvatreti | etac ca prāg evoktam iti darśayann āha --
children.translated_text:
if you think: 'would arise from even a single auxiliary cause, just as from the distinguishing feature' — here too, all the response has been stated. Thus: entities that perish each moment are indeed without distinction between their aggregate and non-aggregate states — that is being said. But with respect to what? Is it with respect to mere distinguishing feature? Or with respect to the distinguishing feature that produces the distinguishing feature conducive to effect-production?
If the former alternative, then that is wrong. For no state devoid of any distinguishing feature whatsoever is possible, since a distinguishing feature grounded in the conjunction with successive and further conditions always exists. For nothing ever exists as a single [entity] alone, because of the existence — as the case may be — of a support, shade, sunlight, wind, cold, and the like. And even in their presence, it is not of the same nature, because of the difference of cause. But this much may be [said]: some distinguishing feature is conducive to some effect, but not all [features] to all [effects]. And this has already been stated previously — showing this, he says:
'By successive and further conditions at each moment' —

children.text:
iti | `aparāparapratyayayogena pratikṣaṇaṃ bhinnaśaktayaḥ saṃskārāḥ santanvanto yady api kutaścit sāmyāt sarūpāḥ pratīyante, tathāpi bhinna evaiṣāṃ svabhāvaḥ, tena kiñcid eva kasyacit kāraṇam'[537]iti, `kṣaṇikeṣu {p.134.1} bhāveṣv aparāparotpatter aikyābhāvāt'[538]iti cātra saṃkṣiptataram uktam | evaṃ ca `nāsmākaṃ punaḥ punar vacana' ity atra dviḥ punargrahaṇaṃ yujyate | yathā yena prakāreṇa bhāvasantāne viśeṣasyotpattiḥ [ta]d apy uktam
-- `tatra svarasataḥ pūrvakṣaṇanirodhe tebhya eva viśiṣṭakṣaṇotpādād viśeṣotpattiḥ'[539]iti | atha kāryotpādānuguṇaviśeṣajanakaviśeṣāpekṣayā prāgvat prathamasamparkkabhājaḥ parasparato nirviśeṣā ity abhimataṃ tad apy ayuktam | yataḥ kāryotpādānuguṇasya viśeṣasya janakāḥ [S. 131b.] kṣitibījādayaḥ kīdṛśāḥ ye [T. 300a.] vyavadhānādirahitatvenopanipātinaḥ | tadbhāva eva tasya bhāvāt etāvanmātranibandhanatvāc ca
children.translated_text: thus. 'By the conjunction with successive and further conditions, having different powers at each moment, the dispositions, continuing, though cognized as having the same form due to some similarity, nevertheless have a nature that is indeed different; therefore only something specific is the cause of something specific' — and 'because of successive and further production in momentary entities, there is absence of unity' — this has been stated here more concisely. And thus the double use of 'again' in 'for us, [stating it] again and again' is appropriate. The manner in which the distinguishing feature arises in the continuum of entities has also been stated — 'there, upon the natural cessation of the prior moment, from those very [causes] the production of a distinguished moment [follows], hence the production of a distinguishing feature.' Now, if [the objection is] with respect to the distinguishing feature that produces the distinguishing feature conducive to effect-production — [that] those partaking of the first contact are without distinction from one another, as before — that too is wrong. Because the producers of the distinguishing feature conducive to effect-production — earth, seeds, and the like — what are they like? They are those that impinge by being free from obstruction and the like. Because the existence of that [distinguishing feature occurs] only when those [conditions] exist, and because the determination of

children.text: janakaṃ vya(-kavya)vasthāyāḥ[540]| te ca tathāvidhāḥ sarvadā na bhavantī kathaṃ pṛthag api kāryotpādānuguṇaviśeṣārambha eṣāṃ syāt?, yataḥ kevalānām api kāryakriyā prasajyeta tad darśayati -- yogyo deśo yeṣāṃ te yogyadeśāḥ, tadbhāvo yogyadeśatā, sā ādir yeṣāṃ avyavahitadeśatvādīnām avasthābhedānāṃ te tathoktāḥ, te ca te avasthābhedāś ca tathoktāḥ |
children.translated_text: the producer [depends on] that alone. And those of such a nature do not always exist — how then could even separately there be the initiation of a distinguishing feature conducive to effect-production by these [causes]? — since the consequence would be that even those alone [could produce] the effect. He shows this: those whose places are suitable are called 'having suitable places'; the state of that is 'having suitable-place-ness'; those conditions whose initial [characteristic] is that — such as being in an unobstructed place and the like — are so called; and those are both those [conditions] and those state-differences, and are so called.
'Having suitable-place-ness, being in an unobstructed place, and the like' —
'which' —
'are the state-distinctions'

children.text:
kṣitibījādīnām upajāyante te kāryotpādānuguṇaviśeṣalakṣaṇakāryakaraṇaśīlāḥ, naivaṃvidhāḥ sarvadā bījādaya iti katham eṣāṃ pṛthag api tathāvidhaviśeṣārambhaḥ syāt? | etad api prāg evoktam `tatra yo 'vyavadhānādideśo rūpendriyādikalāpaḥ sa vijñānajanane samartho hetuḥ'[541]iti vacanāt | tasya codāharaṇamātratvāt | ihāpi tatra yo 'vyavadhānādideśaḥ kṣitibījādikalāpaḥ sa kāryotpādānuguṇaviśeṣajanane samartho hetur iti pratīyata eva | sa ca [S. 132a.] tathāvidho viśeṣaḥ sarvadā na bhavati, tajjanakasya hetor abhāvāt | parasparopasarppaṇādyāśrayasyaiva [T. 300b.] pratyayaviśeṣasya taddhetutvāt | etad api pūrvam evoktam ity āha -- teṣāṃ ca kāryotpādānuguṇaviśeṣa[janane] viśeṣavatāṃ yata utpattis tad apy uktam asakṛd eva `yas teṣāṃ parasparopasarppaṇādyāśrayaḥ pratyayaviśeṣaḥ sa taddhetujanane samartho hetuḥ'[542]iti | tathā `yathāsvaṃ pratyayaiḥ parasparopasarppaṇāśrayair
ye {p. 135.1} yogyadeśādyavasthā jātās te saha svabhāvaniṣpattyā jñānahetutāṃ pratipadyanta'[543]ity anena, ihāpi gamyamānatvāt | tato yady apy eṣāṃ parasparato 'nupapatter[544]viśeṣo na bhavati, svahetukṛtas tu kena vāryate? | na ca svahetuta eva sañjātaviśeṣāṇāṃ bhāve parasparatas tadāśaṃsā, yataḥ parasparato viśeṣāyogaḥ[545]pratipādyamānaḥ śobheta | teṣāṃ ca kāryotpādānuguṇaviśeṣajanakānāṃ pratyayānāṃ pratyekaṃ sāmarthye 'pi khaṇḍaśaḥ kāryotpādāyogāt sakalasyaiva pratyekaṃ karaṇāt | yathā kevalānām akriyā kartṛviśeṣasyāvyavadhānādideśakṣitibījādikalāpasya pṛthag ekaikasya samarthasya bhāvasyābhāvād ity etad apy asakṛd evoktam `teṣāṃ ca na pūrvaṃ na paścāt na pṛthagbhāva iti samarthānāpi [S. 132b.] pūrvāparapṛthagbhāvabhāvino doṣā nopalīyante' ityādivacanāt | tatas tathāvidhaviśeṣasya svopādānamātranibandhanasyānabhyupagamena [T. 301a.] kevalānām
aprasaṅgāt kutaḥ kāryotpādānuguṇaviśeṣārambhadvārakaṃ kāryam api syād iti? |
 kutaḥ punar ayaṃ kāmacāro labhyate yadaṅkurādikāryaṃ sahakāriṇaḥ parasparasya kāryotpādānuguṇāṃ viśeṣaparamparāṃ janayantaḥ kurvanti, kāryotpādānuguṇaṃ tu viśeṣaṃ vyavadhānādirahitadeśopanipātamātreṇety[546]ata āha --
children.translated_text: Of the earth-seed and the like, those that arise are characterized by the specific feature conducive to effect-production and have the disposition of producing effects — seeds and the like are not always of such a kind, so how could each of them individually undertake the production of such a specific feature? This too has been stated before, from the statement 'There, the aggregate of form, sense-faculty and the like that is in the position of non-obstruction and the like is the capable cause for generating cognition.' And since that [statement] is merely an example, here too it is understood: 'There, the aggregate of earth, seed and the like that is in the position of non-obstruction and the like is the capable cause for generating the specific feature conducive to effect-production.' And that kind of specific feature does not always exist, because of the absence of the cause that generates it — because only the particular condition that is based on mutual approach and the like is the cause of that. This too has been stated before — therefore he says: And the source of the arising of those possessing specific features, conducive to effect-production — that too has been stated more than once: 'The particular condition based on mutual approach and the like is the capable cause for generating the cause of that.' And also through [the statement]: 'Those that have come into the state of suitable location and the like through their respective conditions based on mutual approach, they, along with the completion of their essential nature, attain the status of being causes of cognition' — because the same is understood here too. Therefore, even though their specific feature does not arise from each other — because of impossibility — still, the one produced by their own cause, by what is it prevented? And when those possessing specific features have arisen from their own causes, there is no expectation from each other of that [feature], such that the demonstration of the impossibility of specific features from each other would be attractive. And even though each of the conditions that generate the specific feature conducive to effect-production has capacity individually, because the effect cannot be produced piecemeal, since the whole alone produces [the effect] individually. Just as the non-activity of the isolated ones [obtains] because there is no existence of each individual entity — the aggregate of earth, seed and the like in the position of non-obstruction and the like — being separately capable as an agent-specific [cause] — this too has been stated more than once, from the statement: 'And of those, there is no prior, subsequent, or separate existence — so the faults that pertain to those having prior, subsequent, and separate existence do not attach even to the capable [momentary entities].' Therefore, by not accepting that such a specific feature is grounded merely in its own material cause, since there is no consequence of the isolated ones [producing alone] — how could there be even an effect through the doorway of undertaking the specific feature conducive to effect-production? But whence is this license obtained that the cooperative causes produce the effect such as sprouts and the like by generating for each other a series of specific features conducive to effect-production, while [they produce] the specific feature conducive to effect-production merely by the encounter of a position without obstruction and the like? — to this he says —
'And because of the twofold nature of effects, it is thus distinguished' —

children.text: | kathaṃ dvaividhyaṃ kāryāṇām iti? ata āha -- sahakāribhir avyavadhānādideśair anantaraṃ sañjanitāḥ parasparasya prāgavasthāpekṣaviśiṣṭakṣaṇabhāvalakṣaṇā ye viśeṣās tatparamparayā uttarottaraviśiṣṭaviśiṣṭatarādikṣaṇabhāvarūpayā utpattir ddharmo yasya tadātmakam ekaṃ kāryam | anyac ca tadviparītaṃ yat sahakārisannidhimātreṇa bhavati na parasparakṛtāṃ viśeṣaparamparām apekṣate | atrodāharaṇam --
children.translated_text: How is there a twofold nature of effects? To this he says: The specific features characterized by the existence of distinguished moments relative to the prior states of each other, generated immediately by the cooperative causes in the position of non-obstruction and the like — through the series of those, the arising characterized by the existence of progressively more distinguished moments — that constitutes one kind of effect. And another, opposite to that, which comes about merely by the proximity of the cooperative causes and does not require a series of specific features produced by each other. Here the example is —
'like sprouts and the like' —
by the word 'and the like,'

children.text:
odanādivat | tathā 'kṣepeṇa[547]karaṇaśīlaṃ yadindriyaṃ [S. 133a.] tadvijñānādivac ca | prabhāsvarād apavarakapraviṣṭendriyanirāsārthaṃ
caitad viśeṣaṇam | kuta etad? iti cet {p. 136.1} kāryakāraṇayoḥ svabhāvabhedāt | kiṃcid dhi kāryaṃ kāraṇasāmagrīsannidhimātrajanyasvabhāvam, tad anyat tu tatpariṇāmāpekṣam iti | kāraṇam api kiñcit [T. 301b.] svasannidhimātreṇa kāryajananasvabhāvaṃ svakāraṇebhya eva bhavati, yena parasparakṛtāṃ viśeṣaparamparāṃ svakāryakaraṇe nāpekṣate | anyat tu tadviparītasvabhāvam | yathā kiñcid eva śālyaṅkurajananasvabhāvam, tadviparītaṃ cāparam | śālyaṅkuraś ca tadbījajanyasvabhāvo na yavādibījajanyasvabhāva iti na bhāvānāṃ svahetubalāyātāḥ pramāṇādhigatāḥ svābhāvāḥ paryanuyojyāḥ | ye tu yajjananasvabhāvāḥ pramāṇato 'dhigatāḥ te kiṃ sarvadaiva tatsvabhāvāḥ? āhosvit tadaiva? ity atra cintā pravarttate | tatra sarvadā tatsvabhāvatve paścād iva prāg api tatkāryakriyāprasaṅgena pararūpeṇākārakasya [S. 133b.] bhinnasvabhāvatā kārakākārakāvasthāyoḥ śāliyavabījādīnām iva tattvacintakair
ucyate | sadṛśāparabhāvanibandhanaṃ caikatayā pratyabhijñānaṃ lūnapunarjāteṣv iva keśanakhādiṣu
children.translated_text: like cooked rice and the like. And also like cognition and the like of a sense-faculty that has the disposition of immediate apprehension. And this qualification is for the purpose of excluding a sense-faculty that has entered an enclosure [away] from light. Whence is this [known]? Because of the difference of essential nature between effects and causes. For some effects have the essential nature of being produced merely by the proximity of the aggregate of causes, while the other requires the transformation of those [causes]. And some causes too arise from their own causes with the essential nature of producing effects merely by their own proximity, whereby they do not require a series of specific features produced by each other for producing their own effect. And another has the opposite essential nature. Just as only certain [seeds] have the essential nature of producing rice-sprouts, and another is the opposite of that. And a rice-sprout has the essential nature of being produced from that [rice] seed, not the essential nature of being produced from a barley-seed and the like — so the essential natures of entities, arrived at through the force of their own causes and ascertained by <s>pramāṇa</s>, are not to be questioned. But those that are ascertained by <s>pramāṇa</s> as having the essential nature of producing something — are they always of that essential nature? Or only at that [particular] time? — here the inquiry proceeds. There, if they are always of that essential nature, then by the absurd consequence of producing that effect even before as in the later [state], the one that is a non-producer in another's form has a different essential nature in the producer and non-producer states — just as rice and barley seeds and the like — so say those who contemplate reality. And the recognition [of identity] as one, grounded in the succession of similar [but different] entities, is like [the confusion about] hair, nails and the like that are cut and regrown —

children.text: ity atra[548]virodhābhāvād iti | yadā ca tatkāryakāraṇasvabhāvabhedāt kāryadvaividhyam,
children.translated_text: because there is no contradiction in this. And when, due to the difference of essential nature of the causes and effects of that [entity], there is a twofold nature of effects,
'therein' —
when that obtains,
'from the cooperative causes' —

children.text: kṣitibījādibhyas teṣāṃ parasparasantānopakāram apekṣate yat kāraṇam antyavasthāprāptaṃ tasya yat kāryam aṅkurādikaṃ tajjanmanimittaṃ
children.translated_text: from the earth, seed, and the like — the cause that requires the mutual assistance of their continua and has reached the final state — its effect, the sprout and the like — the ground of that birth is —
'of the cooperative causes' —
the specific feature conducive to effect-production, characterized by the existence of the distinguished second moment immediately after the first moment,
'the first' —
'is' —
'that of those' —

children.text: sahakāriṇāṃ prathamasamparkkabhājāṃ parasparakṛto yo viśeṣas tajjanmā na bhavati parasparopasarppaṇādyāśrayād eva pratyayaviśeṣāt tasya bhāvāt | tataḥ kāryotpādānuguṇād ādyād viśeṣāt prathamakṣaṇopanipātibhiḥ sahakāribhir anyataḥ [S. 134a.] samāsāditaviśeṣaiḥ janitāt tatprabhṛti
children.translated_text: the specific feature produced by each other among the cooperative causes that share the first contact — that is not its birth; because it arises from the particular condition based on mutual approach and the like alone. Therefore, from the first specific feature conducive to effect-production — generated by the cooperative causes that have arrived at the first moment and have obtained specific features from elsewhere —
'the specific features that' —
arise, characterized by the existence of progressively intensified subsequent moments,
'those are of that birth' —
having their birth from the specific features produced by the cooperative causes. Why?
'Because of having that as their source' —

children.text: tasyādyasya viśeṣasya parasparopasarppaṇādyāśrayāt pratyayaviśeṣād āsāditatadanukūlaviśeṣaiḥ sahakāribhiḥ parasparopakāranirapekṣair janyasvabhāvatvāt, taduttareṣāṃ ca viśeṣāṇāṃ {137.1} sahakārikṛtakāryotpādānuguṇaviśeṣajanyasvabhāvatvāt | yata evam
children.translated_text: because the first specific feature has the essential nature of being produced by the cooperative causes — which do not require mutual assistance and have obtained specific features favorable to that — from the particular condition based on mutual approach and the like; and because the subsequent specific features have the essential nature of being produced by the specific feature conducive to effect-production that was produced by the cooperative causes. Since it is thus,
'thus' —
'therefore' —
'there is no infinite regress' —

children.text:
prāg[549]uktā | atha sahakāriṇā kṣityādinā kuśūlādyavastho 'pi bījādiḥ tenāpi kṣityādiḥ kṛtaviśeṣa evopatiṣthetānavasthaivaṃ syāt iti | tasya prakārasyānabhyupabgamāt puruṣaprayatnāder eva [T. 301b.] kṣetraprakiraṇahetor avyavahitasnigdhapṛthivībījasamparkkalakṣaṇasya kāryopādānuguṇaviśeṣajanakasya viśeṣe 'syopagamāt | tatra yad uktaṃ pareṇa `yathā prathamasamparttabhājaḥ kṣitibījādayaḥ parasparasya viśeṣamanād
adhānāh kāryotpādānuguṇaṃ viśeṣaṃ janayanti, tathā [S. 134b.] sthirarūpā api bhāvāḥ tadekakāryapratiniyatāḥ parasparakṛtaviśeṣanirapekṣā eva bhāviṣyanti' iti, tadabhyupagacchann āha --
children.translated_text: as previously stated. But if a seed and the like, even in the state of being in a granary and the like, is [already affected] by the cooperative cause earth and the like, and that earth and the like too possesses a specific feature produced [by the seed] — then there would indeed be an infinite regress. [The answer is:] because that mode [of interaction] is not accepted — since it is accepted that the specific feature is produced by the cause of scattering in the field, namely human effort and the like, characterized by the contact of moist earth and seed without obstruction, which is the generator of the specific feature conducive to effect-production. Regarding what was stated by the opponent: 'Just as earth, seed, and the like, sharing the first contact, generate for each other the specific feature conducive to effect-production without generating specific features, so too entities of stable form, determined to a single effect, will be independent of specific features produced by each other' — accepting this, he says —
'Similarly, even if a non-momentary [entity]' —

children.text: ityādi | kṣaṇikavad akṣaṇiko 'pi yadi kāryaṃ karoti karotu nāma | na kaścid vārayati | kintu yena svabhāvena kāryaṃ karoti sa yadi
children.translated_text: and so forth. If a non-momentary entity too, like a momentary one, produces effects — let it produce; no one prevents it. But the essential nature by which it produces the effect — if that
'has the property of immediate causal activity' —

children.text: apekṣeṇa karotīty evaṃśīlo dharmo yasya sa tathoktaḥ, tadā
children.translated_text: has the disposition of producing dependent [on conditions] — the property whose nature is such is so called — then
'because of the possibility of separate existence, even alone' —
not only when conjoined,
'it would be so' —
it would be a producer of that effect — this has been stated many times.
'But one not of that essential nature' —
but one deficient in the essential nature of immediate causal activity —
'even then' —
even in the accompanied state, as before,
'is simply a non-producer' —

children.text:
pararūpeṇa kartṛtvasya pūrvam eva niṣedhāt |
  tad evam ekārthakriyayā viśeṣotpādanena cākṣaṇikānāṃ sahakāritvaṃ niṣidhyopasaṃharann āha --
children.translated_text: because agency in another's form has been negated previously. Thus, having refuted the cooperative causation of non-momentary entities through both single causal efficacy and the production of specific features, concluding, he says —
'Therefore' —

children.text: ityādi | dvividhasyāpi sahakāritvasyāyogān naivākṣaṇikasya kaścit [T. 303a.] sahakārīti kevalo 'pi svakāryaṃ kuryād iti sahakāripratyayāpekṣasyākṣaṇikasya hetutāṃ bruvāṇasya kiṃ yuktam iti [S. 135a.] darśayann āha --
children.translated_text: and so forth. Because both kinds of cooperative causation are untenable, a non-momentary entity has no cooperative cause at all — so even alone it should produce its own effect. Thus, showing what is reasonable for one who asserts the causality of a non-momentary entity requiring the dependence on cooperative conditions, he says —
'For the most part' —

children.text: ityādi | yo hi sthirahetuvādī tasya yadi sa hetuḥ pratyayāntarāṇy apekṣya kāryaṃ karoti tadā
children.translated_text: and so forth. For one who asserts stable causes, if that cause produces the effect dependent on other conditions, then
'clearly' —

children.text: avaśyaṃ tasya sthirasya hetoḥ pratyayāntarāpekṣakārakasya svabhāvāntarasyotpattir iti |
children.translated_text: necessarily, of that stable cause which produces dependent on other conditions, there is the arising of another essential nature.
'Not of a non-producer' —

children.text: kāryatām ananubhavato 'pekṣety ucyate | yataḥ sahakāriṇāṃ yaḥ
children.translated_text: one that does not experience the status of being a producer is said to require [other conditions]. Because, of the cooperative causes, the
'assemblage' —
coming together,
'abiding in that' —
the continuum of the entity existing therein,
'for the most part' —
predominantly,
'possessing specific features generated by the cooperative conditions' —
'being' —
'is seen producing its own effect' —
'like seeds and the like' —

children.text:
tasmād evaṃ vibhajyate | prāyograhaṇaṃ
cākṣepakārīndriyādisaṅghātavyavacchedārtham | tatsambhavino nyāyasyākṣaṇikeṣu pṛthagbhāvasambhavena kathañcid api kalpayitum aśakyatvāt | prāgakārakasya paścāt kārakasvabhāvāntarotpattis tu na virudhyate | tasyaiva hy akārakasya tadātmā kārakaḥ svabhāvo na yujyate na tv atadātmā | ata eva svabhāvāntaragrahaṇam | tatra kevalam akārakasvabhāvasya svarasanirodhitāmātram upeyam | [T. 303b.] tataḥ sarvaṃ sustham iti |
  atha matam -- kārakasvabhāvāntarotpattir iṣyate yadi sthirasya hetoḥ prāg api kārakasvabhāvo [S. 135b.] na syāt | tasya tu prāg api bhāvāt pratyayāntarāpekṣā tadutpattir apy ukteti ata āha --
children.translated_text: therefore it is thus distinguished. And the word 'for the most part' is for the purpose of excluding the assemblage of sense-faculties and the like that have the nature of immediate apprehension. Because the principle applicable to those cannot be even somehow fabricated with respect to non-momentary entities, due to the possibility of separate existence. But the arising of another essential nature of a producer for one who was previously a non-producer is not contradicted. For of that very non-producer, the producer essential nature that is of the same self is not tenable — but one that is not of the same self [is tenable]. Therefore the term 'another essential nature.' There, one need only accept the mere cessation by its own nature of the non-producer essential nature. Then everything is in order. Now if [one] thinks: 'If the arising of another producer-essential nature is accepted, the stable cause would not have the producer essential nature even before. But since it exists even before, the dependence on other conditions and that arising [of a new nature] have [already] been stated' — to this he says —
'Of the producer' —

children.text: ityādi | yadi hi samagrāvasthāyāḥ prāg api kārakasvabhāvo bhavet tadā 'syākriyā na yujyate, saṃhatāvasthāyām api tatsvabhāvatayaiva karaṇāt, pararūpeṇa kartṛtvasya prāg eva niṣiddhatvāt | na ca karoti | tasmāt so 'sya svabhāvaḥ prāṅ naivāsīt | yadi ca pratyayāntarair apy asau na kriyeta tat
children.translated_text: and so forth. For if the producer essential nature existed even before the state of the aggregate, then its non-activity would be untenable, since even in the conjoined state it produces by that very essential nature, and since agency in another's form has been negated previously. But it does not produce [before]. Therefore that essential nature of its did not exist before. And if it is not produced even by other conditions, then
why does it pointlessly depend on them?

body.translated_text: Thus. There, the following might be [objected]: even at the first moment, earth, seeds, and the like are present with a distinguishing feature already arisen from one another —

Section: 43. Conclusion of the discussion on causeless destruction.

body.text: tad evaṃ `tatsvabhāvasya jananāt'[551]ity asya `yo yatsvabhāvaḥ sa svahetor evotpadyamānaḥ tādṛśo bhavati na punas tadbhāve hetvantaram apekṣate'[552]ity asyānekāntaparihārāyoktasya prakārāntareṇānekānte udbhāvite tatparijihīrṣayā

children.translated_text: 'through the conjunction of successive conditions' —
and so forth was stated. Therein, having concluded the incidental [discussion]

children.text: ity ādy abhihitam | tatra yena nyāyena kṣaṇikānāṃ hetuphalasvabhāvaḥ tasyākṣaṇikeṣv asambhavaṃ pratipādayituṃ prāsaṅgikaṃ yad upakrāntaṃ tat parisamāpayya prakṛtam anubadhnann āha --
children.translated_text: undertaken to demonstrate the impossibility, in the case of non-momentary [entities], of the cause-effect nature that obtains for momentary [entities] by a certain logical procedure — resuming the main topic, [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>] says:
'Therefore, whatever has whatever nature' —

children.text: ityādi | yadi svabhāvenāsthitidharmaṇo bhāvasya [S. 136a.] na nāśakāraṇaiḥ prayojanaṃ svabhāvena sthitidharmaṇo bhaviṣyatīty ata āha --
children.translated_text: and so forth. If for an entity whose nature is one of non-persistence (<s>asthitidharman</s>), there is no purpose served by causes of destruction — [the opponent thinks:] then for one whose nature is one of persistence (<s>sthitidharman</s>), there will be [such a purpose]. To this he says:
'Even for one whose nature is persistence' —

children.text:
ityādi | sthitidharmaṇo 'pi hi naiva nāśakāraṇaiḥ kiñcit prayojanam | tasya svahetubhyaḥ samupajāto yaḥ sthiraḥ svabhāvaḥ {p. 139.1} tadanyathātvasyāsthirātmatāpatteḥ kenacit karttum aśakyatvāt | kāmaṃ hi bhāvāḥ svayaṃ na bhaveyuḥ | na
tu santa eva svaṃ svabhāvaṃ parityajanti | atha sthitidharmaṇo 'py anyathātvapratipattir iṣyate tadā 'nyathātvapratipattau vā
children.translated_text: and so forth. For even for one whose nature is persistence, causes of destruction serve no purpose whatsoever. Because the stable essential nature that has arisen from its own causes — {p. 139.1} the otherwise-becoming of that, i.e., the arising of an unstable nature, cannot be effected by anything. For entities may well not come into being on their own; but once existent, they do not abandon their own essential nature. Now, if the otherwise-becoming of even one whose nature is persistence is accepted, then either upon the realization of otherwise-becoming,
'that very essential nature' —
that very nature of persistence —
'would not be' —

children.text: , ātmabhūtasyāsthitidharmaṇaḥ svabhāvasya paścāt sambhave prāg apy abhāvaāyogāt | na hi tadātamanas tasmiṃ(smin) sannihite kadācidabhāvo yuktaḥ, atatsvabhāvatāprasaṅgāt `viruddhadharmādhyāsasya bhedalakṣaṇatvāt' ity uktam | tathā ca sati
children.translated_text: because, if the essential nature that is the nature of non-persistence were to exist subsequently, it would be untenable for it to be absent earlier. For it is not reasonable that what is of that nature should ever be absent when that [entity] is present — because of the absurd consequence of its not having that nature — as was stated: 'because the superimposition of contradictory properties is the defining characteristic of difference.' And that being so,
'the earlier' —
'only' —
'alternative [obtains]' —
namely, that the entity is by nature of the character of non-persistence.
'And in that case' —

children.text:
pūrvavikalpe prāg evoktaṃ dūṣaṇaṃ vināśahetor vaiyarthyam iti |
  athāsau sthirasvabhāva eva, kevalam asyāsthirasvabhāvatā prāg asati vināśahetor upajāyate, anyathā nivṛttyayogād ity ata āha --
children.translated_text: in the earlier alternative, the previously stated objection — the purposelessness of the cause of destruction — has already been stated. | But if it is of a stable essential nature, and its unstable essential nature arises only when the cause of destruction, previously absent, comes into being — because otherwise cessation would be impossible — to this he says:
'And that which, from another' —
from the cause of destruction, when [the entity] with the nature of persistence exists —
'the otherwise-becoming' —

children.text: asthitidharmatālakṣaṇo bhavati, sa pūrvakāt sthitidharmaṇaḥ svahetusamudbhūtāt svabhāvāt
children.translated_text: characterized as the nature of non-persistence — that, from the earlier essential nature, which arose from its own cause, having the nature of persistence —
'is another' —
i.e., a different —
essential nature. When that [other nature] has been produced,
because of being produced subsequently and because of having a different cause,
'how could it be of that [entity]' —
'the essential nature?' —

children.text: ? | tadātmatayā pratibhāsanād iti cet | sārūpyād alakṣitavivekasya tathā pratibhāsanaṃ syāt yady asau [T. 304b.] pūrvasvabhāve saty evānyato bhavet | anyathā virodhaḥ kathaṃ parihriyeta? | bhavatv aparaḥ svabhāva iti cet | yaś cāparaḥ svabhāvaḥ sa kathaṃ tasya? | na hy anyo 'nyasya svabhāvo yuktaḥ, atiprasaṅgāt | yo 'paraḥ svabhāvaḥ sa kim iti tasya na bhavati? ity ata āha --
children.translated_text: | If [one says:] 'because of appearing as having that identity' — the appearing so may be due to similarity, when the distinction is not noticed, if that [other nature] were to arise from another while the prior essential nature still exists. Otherwise, how would the contradiction be resolved? | If [one says:] 'let it be another essential nature' — that which is another essential nature, how is it of that [entity]? For it is not reasonable that one thing is the essential nature of another — because of over-extension. 'Why does that other essential nature not belong to that [entity]?' — to this he says:
'Difference of essential nature' —

children.text:
ityādi | bhavatu vastvantaram eva tadaparasvabhāvatayā ko doṣaḥ?
ity ata āha --
children.translated_text: and so forth. 'Let it indeed be a different entity; what fault is there in its being another essential nature?' — to this he says:
'And thus' —

children.text: vastvantaratve sati vināśahetor upajāyamānasya svabhāvasya pūrvako bhāvaḥ svahetubhyo yaḥ sthitidharmā [S. 137a.] jātaḥ so 'cyutidharme sthito nivṛttibhāṅ na bhavati, vināśahetor vastvantarotpattau vyāpṛtatvād iti na
children.translated_text: when it is a different entity: the prior entity that was born from its own causes with the nature of persistence — the essential nature that arises from the cause of destruction — that [prior entity], established in the nature of non-cessation (<s>acyutidharma</s>), does not undergo cessation, since the cause of destruction is engaged in the production of a different entity. Therefore, there is no
'of that' —
of the one with the nature of persistence —
'otherwise-becoming' —

children.text:
nivṛttiḥ | na hi mudgarāder vastvantarasya bhāve 'parasya nivṛttir yuktā, atiprasaṅgāt | tadupamarddena tadutpattau ca prāg eva proktam |
  {p. 140.1} nanu ca dṛśyata eva kaṭhinādirūpasya tāmrāder agnyāder vināśahetor dravādisvabhāvāntarotpattiḥ | na ca pūrvakasya pracyutidharmatā ity ata āha --
children.translated_text: i.e., cessation. For it is not reasonable that the existence of a different entity such as a hammer should cause the cessation of another — because of over-extension. [The refutation] through the destruction by that and the production of that has been stated earlier. | {p. 140.1} But it is indeed observed that from fire and the like, which is the cause of destruction, there arises, for copper and the like, which has a hard form, another essential nature such as the molten state. And there is no cessation-nature of the prior [entity]. To this he says:
'By this' —
by what was stated just now —
'of hard things and the like' —
by the word 'and the like' —
the arising of another essential nature such as molten-state, hard-state, and the like, from fire, cold wind, and the like, in copper, gold, and the like — which has a fixed form —
'is refuted' —

children.text:
pratyākhyātā, tulyadūṣaṇatvāt |
  kathaṃ tarhi svabhāvāntarotpattiḥ pūrvasya cāpracyutidharme sthitasyābhāvo [T. 305a.] yuktaḥ? ity āha --
children.translated_text: i.e., rejected, because of having the same fault. | How then is the arising of another essential nature and the absence of the prior [entity], which remains established in the nature of non-cessation, tenable? He says:
'Even there' —
in copper and the like, which has the form of hard and the like —
'of the prior' —
of what has the form of hard, molten, and the like —
'because of being self-cessating' (<s>svarasanirodhitva</s>) —
without the agency of a cause of destruction.
'Upon destruction' —
when that obtains —
'from fire and the like' —

by the word 'and the like,' from the pouring of water, cold wind, and the like; as cooperative causes, through the additional feature arising from the particular condition based on mutual proximity and the like —
'and from the material cause' —

children.text: yat tat kaṭhinādirūpaṃ tāmrādi svarasato virudhyate | tata eva upādānakāraṇād agnyādisahakārikāraṇopādānapratyayopajātaviśeṣād
children.translated_text: that copper and the like which has the form of hard and the like is opposed by its very nature. From that very material cause, with the additional feature arising from the auxiliary-cause condition of fire and the like —
'entirely another' —
an entirely different essential nature of molten, hard, and the like — the mention of 'molten' being illustrative —
'has arisen.' —

children.text:
na tu pūrvakam eva kaṭhinadravādirūpaṃ tāmrādi vyavasthitātmakaṃ dravakaṭhinādisvabhāvena pariṇatam iti |
  atra para āha --
children.translated_text: But the prior copper and the like, which has a fixed essential nature and the form of hard, molten, and the like, has not transformed into the essential nature of molten, hard, and the like. | Here the opponent says:
'Who has said' —
that 'from the cause of destruction, when [the entity] with the nature of persistence exists,

children.text: vināśahetor asthitisvabhāvotpattis[555]tato vināśaḥ' iti, yena `yaś ca parasmād anyathābhāvaḥ so 'paraḥ svabhāvaḥ' ityādy ucyate | kintu sa svayaṃ sthitidharmaiva svahetubhir janito nāsyāsthirasvabhāvatā vināśahetor upajāyate | kathaṃ jñāyate yathā `svahetubhiḥ [T. 305b.] svabhāvena sthitidharmaiva janitaḥ' iti? | vināśahetor agnyāder asambhave avasthānāt | yadi svabhāvenāsthitidharmā svahetor jātaḥ syāt tadā tadasambhave 'pi nāvatiṣṭheta | tasya svabhāvena sthitidharmaṇaḥ svahetubhir evāyam aparaḥ svabhāvo niyamito yaduta
children.translated_text: the essential nature of non-persistence arises, and thence destruction' — such that [you] say 'that otherwise-becoming which is from another is another essential nature' and so forth? Rather, it itself, having the nature of persistence, is produced by its own causes — no essential nature of instability arises in it from the cause of destruction. How is it known that 'it is produced by its own causes as having precisely the nature of persistence by its essential nature'? Because it persists when the cause of destruction — fire and the like — is not present. If it were born from its own cause as having, by its essential nature, the character of non-persistence, then even in the absence of that [cause of destruction] it would not persist. For this [entity] with the nature of persistence, this further essential nature is determined by its own causes — namely,
'from the opposing [entity]' —
from fire and the like, which is antagonistic —
'destruction occurs of its own accord.' —

children.text: | parasmād iti karmaṇi lyaplope pañcamī paramapekṣya ity arthaḥ | svahetubhir evāyaṃ {141.1} niyamitasvabhāvo jāto yathā tvayā virodhinam apekṣya svayaṃ nirva(va)rttitavyam iti | tad uktam -
children.translated_text: | 'From the opposing' — the ablative with the elision of the absolutive (<s>lyap</s>) indicates: 'having awaited the opposing [entity].' It is born with an essential nature determined by its own causes, such that: 'You must cease of your own accord, having awaited the antagonist.' As has been stated:
'That essential nature of it too, by which, having awaited [the antagonist], it ceases —' |
'is like the flow of others [that ceases] with respect to a hammer and the like.' ||

children.text:
iti |
 nanu yady asya vināśo virodhisannidhāne svayam eva bhavaty ahetukaḥ prāpnoti, ahetoś ca deśakālasvabhāvaniyamo na yukta ity ata āha --
children.translated_text: Thus. | But if its destruction occurs of its own accord when the antagonist is proximate, then [destruction] would be uncaused (<s>ahetuka</s>); and for what is uncaused, the restriction to [particular] place, time, and essential nature is not tenable. To this he says:
'And not' —

children.text: naiva vināśo nāma vinaṃṣṭur aparaḥ svabhāvaḥ, yato 'yaṃ doṣaḥ syāt, kintu
children.translated_text: destruction is not at all another essential nature of that which is destroyed — so this fault would [apply only if it were]. Rather,
'the mere falling away from existence (<s>bhāvacyuti</s>) is destruction.' —

children.text:
| [S. 138a.] tasyāś ca niḥsvabhāvatvād dhetumattā naiva yujyate | na hi sā tasya bhavati | kevalam asau svayam eva na bhavati | tato bhavitur abhāvāt kasya hetumattopagamyate ? |
  siddhāntavādy āha --
children.translated_text: | And since that [falling away] is without essential nature, it is not at all tenable that it has a cause. For it does not [positively] belong to that [entity]. It simply ceases to exist of its own accord. Therefore, since there is the absence of any [positive] thing-to-come-into-being, whose having-a-cause is to be accepted? | The <s>Siddhāntavādin</s> says:
'This does not transcend the twofold alternative stated just before' —

children.text:
| kīdṛśaṃ vikalpadvayam? | `kiṃ nityo bhāvaḥ?' ityādi | [T. 306a.] nanu ca kālāntarasthitidharmatām upagacchato naiva nityavikalpasyāvakāśaḥ | na | tadupagame 'pi nityataivopagatā bhavati | tathā hi -- yady ayaṃ saṃvatsarasthitidharmā svahetubhir janitas tadā saṃvatsaraparisamāptau yo 'syādāv udayakāle saṃvatsarasthitidharmā svabhāvo yato 'yaṃ saṃvatsaraṃ sthitaḥ sa eva tadante 'pi | tato 'paraṃ saṃvatsaram avatiṣṭheta | tadante 'pi prathamotpannasaṃvatsarasthitidharmasvabhāvāparityāgād aparāparasaṃvatsarasthitiprasaṅgāt kālāntarasthitidharmatopagame 'pi nityataivopagatā bhavatīti nityavikalpo durnnivāraḥ | vināśahetusannidhau svayaṃ nivarttata iti copagamād anityavikalpo naśvarātmatāvikalpaḥ | tathā hi -- vināśahetvabhimatasannidhau svayaṃ vinaśyato yo 'sya svabhāva sa eva bhāvasyaikarūpatvād utpannamātrasyeti tadaiva vināśaprasaṅgāt katham asya
kālāntarasthitidharmatā sambhavati? | evaṃ vikalpe kṛte pāścātyavikalpopagame kālāntarasthitir evāsya truṭyatīti nityavikalpa evānenopagantavyaḥ | tatra [S. 138b.] vināśahetusannidhau svayaṃ nāśopagame prāṅ nityo bhūtvā paścād anityo [T. 306b.] vinaśvarasvabhāvo bhavatīti brūte |
children.translated_text: | What is that twofold alternative? 'Is the entity permanent?' — and so forth. But [the opponent objects:] 'For one who accepts the nature of persisting for a limited time, there is no room for the alternative of permanence at all.' No. Even upon accepting that, permanence alone is entailed. For thus: if this [entity] is produced by its own causes as having the nature of persisting for a year, then at the completion of the year, the essential nature of persisting for a year that was present at the initial moment of arising — by which it persisted for a year — is the very same even at the end of that [year]. Therefore it would persist for another year. And at the end of that too, because there is no abandonment of the essential nature of year-long persistence that was produced initially, there would be the absurd consequence of persisting for successive years — thus even upon accepting the nature of persisting for a limited time, permanence alone is entailed, and the alternative of permanence is inescapable. And because it is accepted that [the entity] ceases of its own accord when the cause of destruction is proximate, the alternative of impermanence — i.e., the alternative of having a perishable nature — [also applies]. For thus: the essential nature of this [entity] that perishes of its own accord when what is regarded as the cause of destruction is proximate — that very [essential nature] is present from the very moment of arising, since the entity is of a single form. Therefore, because of the absurd consequence of perishing at that very [moment of arising], how is the nature of persisting for a limited time possible for it? When the alternatives are thus formulated, if the latter alternative is accepted, the very persistence for a limited time is shattered — so [the opponent] must accept the former alternative of permanence. In that case, [the opponent] says: upon accepting that it ceases of its own accord when the cause of destruction is proximate — having been permanent before, it afterward becomes impermanent, of a perishable essential nature.
'And in saying so, he also asserts a duality of entities' —

children.text:
| vakṣyamāṇāpekṣaś cakāraḥ | {p. 142.1} kīdṛśaṃ bhāvadvayam? | nityānityau svabhāvau bhedau yasya tathā | yo 'sau nityaḥ svabhāvaḥ prāktanaḥ tasya nityābhimatasya svayaṃ paścān nāśaṃ bruvāṇaḥ sarvadā pratikṣaṇam eva nāśaṃ prāha | anyathā pūrvoktena nyāyena paścād api nāśāsambhavāt | atha pratikṣaṇam asya nāśo na bhavati tadā paścād api tadayogāt sarvadaivānāśaṃ prāheti kṛtvā pūrvasminn ity ābhimate svabhāve vināśahetur asamartho 'kiñcitkara eva |
  nanu ca vināśahetor naiva sāmarthyam upagataṃ pareṇa virodhisannidhim apekṣya svayaṃ nāśopagamāt | na | ata eva tannibandhanatvaprasaṅgāt nāśasya | anyathā hy akiñcitkaraḥ kim ity asāv apekṣyate?, hetubhāvasyāpekṣālakṣaṇatvāt | svahetava evātrāparādhyanti yadakiñcitkare 'pi tatrāpekṣāyāṃ niyuñjata iti cet | kaḥ punar ayam asthānābhiniveśaḥ teṣāṃ yat tatra tathā niyuñjate | [S. 139a.] tasmād upakāryapekṣāyām
children.translated_text: | The word 'also' is with reference to what will be stated [later]. {p. 142.1} What kind of duality of entities? That which has two divisions — a permanent and an impermanent essential nature. That which is the prior permanent essential nature — he who asserts its subsequent destruction of its own accord while it is regarded as permanent — asserts destruction at every single moment. Otherwise, by the reasoning stated earlier, destruction would be impossible even later. But if its destruction does not occur at every moment, then by the same reasoning, it would be impossible even later — so he would in effect be asserting eternal non-destruction. Having concluded this regarding the first posited essential nature, the cause of destruction is utterly incapable, effecting nothing whatsoever. | But the opponent has not at all accepted the capacity of the cause of destruction — because he accepts that [the entity] ceases of its own accord, having awaited the proximity of the antagonist. No. For precisely this reason, there would be the absurd consequence of destruction being contingent on that [antagonist]. For otherwise, why is that inefficacious [factor] awaited, if it does nothing at all? — because the state of being a cause is defined by being awaited. 'It is its own causes that are at fault here, in that they enjoin the requirement of even that which does nothing' — if so, what is this absurd fixation of theirs, that they enjoin [such requirement] in such a way? Therefore, when there is the requirement by that which is to be assisted,

children.text:
eva hetavo[556]niyuñjānāḥ śobhante | anyathā te 'pi kāryātmāno[557]naiva tanniyogamādriyeran[558]| kathaṃ cākiñcitkaro virodhī nāma? | na hy asyāvirodhitvābhimatād[559]viśeṣaḥ kaścid iti yatkiñcid etat |
  yad apy uktaṃ `yathā 'nyeṣāṃ kṣaṇikavādinām akiñcitkaram api mudgarādikam apekṣya [S. 307a.] ghaṭādipravāho nivarttate tathā 'smākam api kālāntarasthāyī bhāvaḥ' iti tad api parasamayānabhijñatayocyate | yato nāsmākaṃ pravāho nāma kṣaṇavyatirikto 'sti yo 'kiñcitkaramudgarādisannidhau nivartteta | kṣaṇā eva hi kevalaṃ santi | te ca svanivṛttau na mudgarādikam apekṣante, svarasata eva nirodhāt | yā tu teṣāṃ kapālādivṛttilakṣaṇā paryudāsavṛttyā nivṛttiḥ yasyāṃ satyām ekatvābhiniveśino lokasya sadṛśāparabhāvarūpasya vibhramanimittasyāpagamāt `nivṛttā ghatādayaḥ' iti vyavahāraḥ, tatrākiñcitkaratvaṃ mudgarādīnāṃ naivāsti, tadbhāva eva teṣāṃ bhāvāt | vegavan mudgarādisahakāriṇo ghaṭakṣaṇāt parasparopasarppaṇādyāśrayāt {p. 143.1} pratyayaviśeṣāt [S. 139b.] sañjātātiśayāt kapālāder bhavanadharmatvāt tasya tajjananasvabhāvād iti |
  svabhāvadvayopagamaprasaṅgād iti parijihīrṣayā para āha --
children.translated_text:
indeed the causes, when engaged [in their operation], shine forth. Otherwise, they too, being of the nature of effects, would not heed that engagement. And how is something that is inefficacious [to be called] an opponent? For there is no distinction of it from what is accepted as non-opposing — so this [objection] is baseless. |
  As for what was also said: 'Just as for the other momentary-ists, the continuum of pots and the like ceases in dependence on the hammer and the like even though [the hammer] is inefficacious [with respect to cessation], so too for us the entity persisting for another time' — that too is said out of unfamiliarity with the other's system. For according to us, there is no 'continuum' apart from moments that would cease in the presence of the inefficacious hammer and the like. For there are simply moments alone. And they do not depend on the hammer and the like for their own cessation, since they cease of their own accord. But as for that cessation of theirs characterized by the occurrence of potsherd and the like — which is a cessation through exclusionary function (<s>paryudāsavṛtti</s>) — when that obtains, because of the disappearance of the similar-subsequent-existence-form that is the cause of the delusion of those attached to unity, the conventional usage 'the pots and the like have ceased' [occurs]; there, the hammer and the like are not at all inefficacious, since their existence is precisely [the condition for] the existence of those [potsherds]. Because from the moment of the pot, due to the particular condition based on the mutual approximation and the like of the cooperative causes such as the hammer and the like which possess velocity, an increment having arisen, the potsherd and the like have the property of coming-into-being; and that [moment] has the essential nature of producing that [potsherd]. |
  With the intent of avoiding the consequence of accepting two essential natures, the opponent says —
'Not previously' (<s>na prāg</s>)
and so forth. Whence is this? |
'Because of having a single essential nature' (<s>ekasvabhāvatvāt</s>)

children.text:
| sarvadaikasvabhāvasya sarvadā nityataiva na paścād anityasvabhāvatāsambhava iti |
  siddhāntavādy āha --
children.translated_text:
| Since what always has a single essential nature is always eternal only, the essential nature of impermanence is not possible afterwards. |
  The <s>Siddhāntavādin</s> (proponent) says —
'That entity then' (<s>sa tarhi bhāvaḥ</s>)
always having an eternal essential nature, by its own nature,
'not entering destruction' (<s>nāśam anāviśan</s>)
— not undergoing [destruction] —

children.text: kathaṃ naiva naṣṭo (kathaṃ naṣṭo) nāma[560]? | kutaḥ?
children.translated_text: how is it ever destroyed? Why?
'Of that essential nature and destruction' (<s>tatsvabhāvavināśayoḥ</s>)
— of the eternal essential nature, and of destruction which is of an impermanent nature —
'because of having mutually exclusive forms' (<s>aparaspararūpatvāt</s>)
— because of having the form of mutual exclusion. Concluding, [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>] says —
'Since thus' (<s>yata evaṃ</s>)

children.text: sthitidharmaṇāṃ vināśo naiva yujyate tasmāt sati asya vināśe yady avaśyambhāvī kṛtakarūpasya sato vināśa iṣyate parais tadā
children.translated_text: destruction is simply not tenable for what has the property of persistence — therefore, if its destruction obtains, and if the opponents accept that destruction is necessarily inevitable for what exists as having the character of being produced (<s>kṛtaka</s>), then
'by [having] the essential nature of destruction' (<s>vināśasvabhāvena</s>)

children.text: vinaśyati nāvatiṣṭhata iti vināśaḥ | karttari bahulavacanād ghañ | sa svabhāvo yasya tena vināśasvabhāvenāsthitidharmaṇā |
children.translated_text: — it perishes, does not persist — thus 'destruction' (<s>vināśa</s>). The <s>ghañ</s> suffix [is used] in the agent sense according to the <s>bahulavacana</s> rule. That whose essential nature is that — by having the essential nature of destruction, [it is] of the nature of non-persistence.
'Therefore' (<s>tena</s>)
— by the real entity existing as having the character of being produced, from its own causes —
'it must exist' (<s>bhavitavyam</s>)

children.text:
anyathā 'vaśyambhāvitayopagatasya kṛtakātmanāṃ satāṃ vināśasyaivāyogāt |
  bhavatv evam iti cet | āha --
children.translated_text:
— otherwise, since destruction, which is accepted as necessarily inevitable, is simply untenable for existing things that are not of the nature of being produced (<s>akṛtaka</s>). |
  If [the opponent says:] 'let it be so' — [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>] says —
'Even so' (<s>tathāpi</s>)

children.text: svayaṃ vināśasvabhāvatve 'pi [S. 140a.] na kevalam avinaśvarasvabhāvatve svabhāvānyathātvāsambhavād vyartho vināśahetur iti prathamavikalpopanyāsa evoktam na punar ucyate | yata evaṃ
children.translated_text: — even when having the essential nature of destruction by itself, because of the impossibility of alteration of essential nature when simply having a non-perishable essential nature, the cause of destruction is purposeless — this is precisely the presentation of the first alternative, it need not be restated. Since thus,
'therefore' (<s>tena</s>)

children.text:
ityādi sugamam |
  tad evaṃ vināśaṃ pratyanapekṣām asāmarthya-vaiyarthyābhyāṃ taddhetvayogena kṛtakalakṣaṇasya sattvasyapūrvācāryadarśatāṃ pratipādya yathā 'sau viparyaye bādhakapramāṇatām anubhavati tad darśayann āha --
children.translated_text:
and so forth — this is easily understood. |
  Thus, having demonstrated the position shown by the previous masters (<s>pūrvācārya</s>) that the existence (<s>sattva</s>) characterized as being produced (<s>kṛtaka</s>) does not depend on anything for destruction, through incapacity and purposelessness, and through the impossibility of a cause for it, [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>] now shows how that [position] functions as a contradicting valid cognition (<s>bādhakapramāṇa</s>) in the contrary case, saying —
'Therefore, destruction' (<s>tasmād vināśa</s>)

children.text: ityādi | prayogas tv evam -- ye yadbhāvaṃ pratyanapekṣās te tadbhāvaniyatāḥ | [T. 308a.] tad yathā -- antyā kāraṇasāmagrī svakāryotpādane | anapekṣaś ca kṛtakarūpaḥ san bhāvo vināśe {p. 144.1} 'vaśyambhāvivināśatayogataḥ parair iti svabhāvahetuprasaṅgaprayogo viparyaye bādhakaṃ pramāṇaṃpūrvācāryapradarśitam |
children.translated_text: and so forth. The formal argument is thus: those which do not depend on anything for their being [in a certain state] are determined to that state of being. For example — the final causal aggregate in the production of its own effect. And the entity existing as having the character of being produced does not depend on [anything for] destruction — because of the acceptance by opponents that its destruction is necessarily inevitable — thus the argument through the reason of essential nature (<s>svabhāvahetu</s>), [which serves as] a contradicting valid cognition in the contrary case, was shown by the previous masters.
'From that' (<s>tataḥ</s>)
— given its determination to that state of being, since destruction is not occasional, destruction [occurs] immediately upon arising — thus
'that which exists' (<s>yat san</s>)
— the entity characterized as produced —
'that is perishable' (<s>sa vināśī</s>)

children.text:
vinaśvarasvabhāvo naśvaratāyāḥ sādhyadharmasya nivṛttau ca kṛtakalakṣaṇasattvanivṛttir iti kṛtvā kṛtakalakṣaṇasya sattvasya kṣaṇikatāyām anvayavyatirekasiddhiḥ sampadyate
'napekṣayā 'nyakrāntasattvakṣaṇikatvayos tādātmyasiddheḥ tannibandhanayor anvayavyatirekayor api niścayāt |
  tad evaṃpūrvācāryān prati akṛtakasya sato 'bhāvāt
children.translated_text:
— having a perishable essential nature. And upon the cessation of the property to be proved (<s>sādhyadharma</s>), i.e., perishability, there is cessation of existence characterized as being produced — thus, the establishment through <s>anvaya</s> (positive concomitance) and <s>vyatireka</s> (negative concomitance) of the momentariness of existence characterized as being produced is accomplished,
because through non-dependence [on any cause for destruction], the identity (<s>tādātmya</s>) of existence and momentariness is established, and therefore the <s>anvaya</s> and <s>vyatireka</s> grounded in that [identity] are also ascertained. |
  Thus, since for the previous masters, uncreated (<s>akṛtaka</s>) existence does not exist,
'What exists without a cause is eternal' (<s>sad akāraṇavan nityam</s>)

children.text: iti nityalakṣaṇavirahād eva na tannityatvam | yat tu [S. 140b.] sad utpattimat tad uktena nyāyenāvaśyaṃ nāśitayopagataṃ paraiḥ kālāntarasthāyi na bhavatīti prati pāditam |
children.translated_text: — because of the very absence of the definition of eternality [applying to produced things], they are not eternal. But what exists and has origination — that, by the reasoning stated, having been accepted as necessarily destined for destruction by the opponents, does not persist for another time — this has been demonstrated. |

body.translated_text: Thus, of the statement 'because of the production of that which has that nature' — i.e., 'whatever has whatever essential nature, that, being produced from its own cause alone, becomes such, and does not require another cause for being of that nature' — which was stated for the purpose of resolving the <s>anekānta</s>, when the <s>anekānta</s> was raised in another manner, with the intention of resolving that,

yadā tu yat sat tat kṣaṇikam eveti sāmānyenocyate kṛtakākṛtakalakṣaṇaṃ sato bhedam anapekṣya prauḍhavāditayā kṛtakasyāpi cāvaśyambhāvī vināśa iti paropagamo [T. 308b.] nāpekṣyate, tadā vināśaṃ pratyanapekṣatvam eva sarvasya na sidhyati | yeṣāṃ hi vināśo bhavaṃ(van) dṛṣṭo ghaṭādīnāṃ teṣām eva taddhetvayogāt tatrānapekṣā yujyate |
ye tu deśādivyavahitāḥ parvatādayo vā vināśam āviśanto na dṛṣṭāḥ teṣām avaśyaṃ vināśitvopagamanibandhanābhāvād antye 'py ayaṃ vināśaṃ pratyanapekṣa eva vinaśyann 'viśeṣād ādāv api tadbhāvaniyata iti vaktum aśakyatvāt tatsvabhāvasāpekṣatvāt[561]| vināśaṃ pratyanapekṣatvāsiddher akṛtakānāṃ cākāśādīnāṃ vināśisvabhāvasāpekṣāṇām ity anapekṣayā sato naśvarasvabhāvatā 'siddheḥ anvayavyatirekayos tannibandhanayor ayogam utpaśyann arthakriyāvirodhalakṣaṇam eva tadā bādhakaṃ pramāṇaṃ tādātmyaprasādhakam abhidhānīyam iti manyamānaḥ pūrvapakṣam utthāpayann āha --

children.translated_text: 'By essential nature' (<s>svabhāvataḥ</s>)
— even when having a perishable nature, by the reasoning stated, of pots and the like whose destruction is observed —
'someone' (<s>kaścid</s>)

children.text: deśādivyavahitaḥ[562]parvatādir vā 'nupalabdhavināśaḥ kṛtako 'pi sadrūpa ākāśādir vā 'kṛtakaḥ [S. 141a.] san na
children.translated_text: — separated by place and the like, or a mountain and the like whose destruction is not apprehended, or even a produced entity having the form of an existent, or space (<s>ākāśa</s>) and the like being unproduced —
'even though not of that essential nature' (<s>atatsvabhāvo 'pi</s>)

children.text:
avināśisvabhāvo 'pi syāt | apiśabdaḥ
sambhāvanāyām | tasya[563]vināśisvabhāvasaṃsādhakapramāṇābhāvād āśaṅkyata etat | tataś ca vināśisvabhāvasāpekṣatvāt tadanapekṣatvam asiddham iti tadvaśāt[564]sādhyasya [T 309a.] kṣaṇikatvasya sattvasvabhāvatvāsiddheḥ tannibandhanā nānvayavyatirekasiddhir iti | kiṃ punar atrāśaṅkānimittaṃ yena kaścid atatsvabhāvo 'py āśaṅkyata ity āha --
children.translated_text: — even though having a non-perishable essential nature — might be. The word 'even' (<s>api</s>) is in the sense of possibility. This is apprehended because of the absence of a valid means of cognition that would establish its perishable essential nature. And therefore, because of the dependence on [having] a perishable essential nature, the non-dependence is unestablished — and because of that, since the identity of the property to be proved — momentariness — with the nature of existence is unestablished, there is no establishment through <s>anvaya</s> and <s>vyatireka</s> grounded in that. But what then is the basis for this apprehension, by which someone might be apprehended as not having that essential nature? — [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>] says —
'For not everything is the essential nature of everything' (<s>na hi sarvaḥ sarvasya svabhāvaḥ</s>)

children.text:
iti | vicitrasvabhāvā hi bhāvā dṛśyante -- kecit[565]sapratighāḥ kecid[566]apratighāḥ, tathā nīlānīlādisvabhāvāḥ, tathā kecid vināśinaḥ anye tv avināśisvabhāvāḥ śaṅkyanta iti pūrvapakṣāśaṅkā |
  na -- `kaścid atatsvabhāvo 'pi syāt' -- iti āśaṅkanīyam, tathābhāve hy akṣaṇikatvaṃ tasya syāt | tasmiṃś ca saty avastutvaprasaṅgāt kuto 'tatsvabhāvatāśaṅkā? | kathaṃ punar akṣaṇikatve 'vastutvaprasaṅgaḥ? | yataḥ[567]sattvasya kṣaṇikatvasvabhāvatayā 'nvayavyatirekasiddhir ity ata āha --
children.translated_text:
| For entities are seen to have diverse essential natures — some have resistance (<s>sapratigha</s>), some are without resistance (<s>apratigha</s>); likewise, [some are] of blue, non-blue, and other essential natures; likewise, some are perishable, while others may be apprehended as having a non-perishable essential nature — thus is the apprehension of the objection. |
  [<s>Dharmakīrti responds:</s>] No — 'even though not of that essential nature, it might be' — this should not be apprehended. For if such were the case, it would be non-momentary. And if it were [non-momentary], because of the consequence of being a non-real-entity (<s>avastu</s>), whence the apprehension of its not having that essential nature? But how does the consequence of being a non-real-entity [follow] from non-momentariness? Because the establishment through <s>anvaya</s> and <s>vyatireka</s> of existence having momentariness as its essential nature — thus [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>] says —
'For capacity' (<s>śaktir hi</s>)
and so forth. |

body.translated_text:
But when it is stated in general that 'whatever exists is momentary alone,' without regard to the distinction of the existent as produced (<s>kṛtaka</s>) and unproduced (<s>akṛtaka</s>), with bold assertion, and when the opponent's concession that 'even of the produced, destruction is necessarily inevitable' is not relied upon — then the non-dependence [on anything] for destruction is not established for everything. For only of those — pots and the like — whose destruction is observed, the non-dependence with respect to that [destruction] is tenable, because of the impossibility of a cause for it. |
But those — mountains and the like — which are separated by place and the like, or which are not observed entering destruction — for them, because of the absence of the basis for accepting necessary perishability, it cannot be said that 'this [entity], even in its final [moment], being non-dependent on anything for destruction, perishes without distinction even at the beginning, and is therefore determined to that state' — because of the dependence on the essential nature of that [entity]. Since the non-dependence on [anything for] destruction is unestablished, and since uncreated [entities] like space (<s>ākāśa</s>) and the like are dependent on [having] a perishable essential nature — since the perishable essential nature of the existent is unestablished through non-dependence [alone] — seeing the impossibility of <s>anvaya</s> and <s>vyatireka</s> grounded in that, [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>], thinking that the contradicting valid cognition characterized precisely as the contradiction with causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyāvirodha</s>) must be stated as establishing the identity [of existence and momentariness], raises the objection (<s>pūrvapakṣa</s>) saying —
