body.text: section: 45. arthakriyākāritvam eva sattvaṃ, tac ca kṣaṇikānām eveti |
body.translated_text: Section: 45. Causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyākāritva</s>) alone is existence (<s>sattva</s>), and that belongs only to momentary entities.

body.text: evaṃ manyate -- iha tāvad idam eva vicāraṇīyam [S. 141b.] kiṃ lakṣaṇam etad bhāvānāṃ sattvaṃ yuktam iti | tatra na sattāyogalakṣaṇam avyāpteḥ, sāmānyādiṣv abhāvāt | vandhyāsutādiṣv api bhāvād ativyāpter vā | vandhyāsutādīnām asattvāt kathaṃ sattāyogaḥ? iti cet | na | itaretarāśrayāt | yatas teṣām asattvaṃ sattāyogavirahād eva [T. 309b.] tadvirahaś cāsattvād iti | yadi ca satām eva sattāyogaḥ evaṃ tarhy anyat sattvalakṣaṇam abhidhānīyam sattāyogasya ca vaiyarthyam, tata eva vastunaḥ sattvāt | sarvārthakriyāsāmarthyavirahāt {p. 146.1} sattāyogābhāvas teṣām iti cet | evaṃ sati yad evārthakriyāsāmarthyayuktaṃ tasyaiva sattāyoga ity arthakriyāsāmarthyam eva bhāvalakṣaṇamāyātam ity apārthakaḥ sattāyogaḥ |

children.translated_text: 'And thus' (<s>itthaṃ ca</s>)

children.text: evam | anyathā sāmānyādīnāṃ kathaṃ svarūpaṃ sattvaṃ syāt? | arthakriyāsāmarthyaṃ tu sarveṣām astīti tad eva bhāvalakṣaṇam |
children.translated_text: — thus. Otherwise, how could universals and the like have existence as their own form? But causal efficacy belongs to all — so that alone is the definition of entities. |
'What is endowed with origination, decay, and permanence is existent' (<s>utpādavyayadhrauvyayuktaṃ sat</s>)
<s>Tattvārthasūtra</s> 5.29

children.text:
ity etad apy ayuktam, dhrauvyeṇotpādavyayayor virodhāt ekasmiṃ(smin) dharmiṇy ayogāt | kathañcidutpādavyayau kathañcit dhrauvyam iti cet | yathotpādavyayau na tathā dhrauvyam, yathā ca dhrauvyaṃ na tathotpādavyayāv iti naikaṃ vastu yathoktalakṣaṇaṃ [S. 142a.] syāt | tato 'nyasya bhāvalakṣaṇasyāyogāt śakteś cāntaśaḥ svajñānajanane 'py upagamāt paraiḥ, anyathā ṣaṭpadārthādivyavasthānāyogāt saiva bhāvalakṣaṇam, sarvaśaktivirahaḥ punarbhāvalakṣaṇam |
  sarvagrahaṇaṃ ca sarvasya vastuno vastvantaraśaktiviraharūpatvād abhāvatānirāsārtham | yasya tu na kvacicchaktiḥ sa evaikāntenābhāva ucyate |
  śaktilakṣaṇam eva sattvam akṣaṇike syāt tataḥ kṣaṇikātmatā [T. 310a.] sattvasya na sidhyatīti kuto 'nvayavyatirekau? iti cet, āha --
children.translated_text:
— this too is untenable, because of the contradiction of origination and decay with permanence, [since] they are not tenable in a single property-bearer. If [one says:] 'in some respect there is origination and decay, in some respect permanence' — then as there is origination and decay, so there is no permanence; and as there is permanence, so there is no origination and decay — thus no single entity would have the stated definition. Therefore, since no other definition of entities is tenable, and since even the opponents accept capacity at least in producing one's own cognition — otherwise the establishment of the six categories (<s>ṣaṭpadārtha</s>) and the like would be untenable — that [capacity] alone is the definition of entities, while the complete absence of all capacity is the definition of entities [being non-existent]. |
  And the word 'all' (<s>sarva</s>) is for the purpose of excluding non-existence — since every real entity has the form of the absence of the capacity for every other real entity. But that which has no capacity whatsoever for anything is called a non-entity (<s>abhāva</s>) without qualification. |
  'The capacity-characterized existence could belong even to a non-momentary [entity] — therefore the identity of existence with momentariness is not established, so whence <s>anvaya</s> and <s>vyatireka</s>?' — if so, [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>] says —
'And indeed, of a non-momentary [entity]' (<s>na caivākṣaṇikasya</s>)

children.text:
kvacit kārye 'ntaśo jñānalakṣaṇe 'pi śaktir asti tat kutas tasya tallakṣaṇaṃ sattvam atītāder iva bhaviṣyati?, yataḥ sattvasya kṣaṇikātmatā na sidhyet |
  nanu ca śakter atīndriyatvāt kāraṇānāṃ kāryārambhaniyamābhāvāc ca kathaṃ tadviraho 'kṣaṇikasya bhavet yato 'sya sarvaśaktivirahalakṣaṇenāsattvena virodhinā nirākriyamāṇaṃ sattvaṃ kṣaṇikātmatām evānubhavet yato 'nvayavyatirekau syātām ity ata āha --
children.translated_text:
there is no capacity anywhere for any effect, even one characterized as cognition — so how could existence characterized by that [capacity] belong to it, as if to past entities and the like? — since the identity of existence with momentariness would not be established. |
  But since capacity is supersensible (<s>atīndriya</s>), and since there is no invariable rule that causes must initiate effects, how could the absence of that [capacity] obtain for the non-momentary, such that its existence — being negated by non-existence characterized as the complete absence of all capacity, which is contradictory [to it] — would undergo the identity of momentariness alone, so that <s>anvaya</s> and <s>vyatireka</s> would follow? — to this [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>] says —
'Through succession and simultaneity' (<s>kramayaugapadyābhyām</s>)

children.text:
ityādi | naiva pratyakṣataḥ [S. 142b.] kāryavirahād vā sarvaśaktiviraho 'kṣaṇikatve ucyate, kintu tadvyāpakavirahāt | tathā hi -- kramayaugapadyābhyāṃ kāryakriyā vyāptā prakārāntarābhāvāt | tataḥ kāryakriyāśaktivyāpakayos tayor akṣaṇikatve {p. 147.} virodhāt nivṛttes tadvyāptāyāḥ kāryakriyāśakter api nivṛttir iti sarvaśaktivirahalakṣaṇam asattvam akṣaṇikatve vyāpakānupalabdhir ākarṣati, viruddhayor ekatrāyogāt | tato nivṛttaṃ sattvaṃ kṣaṇikeṣv evāvatiṣṭhamānaṃ tadātmatām anubhavatīti -- `yat sat tat kṣaṇikam eva' ity anvayavyatirekarūpāyā vyāpteḥ siddhir niścayo bhavati |
  nanu ca prakārāntarābhāvāt kāryam aṅkurādikaṃ bījādinā kramayaugapadyābhyām eva kriyata ity ucyate sa eva tu prakārāntaravirahaḥ [T. 310b.] kāryātmanaḥ kutaḥ siddhaḥ? | prakārāntarasyopalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptatve katham atyantāsambhavaḥ? | kevalaṃ deśādiniṣedhamātram eva syāt |
children.translated_text:
and so forth. It is not said that, in the case of non-momentariness, the absence of all capacity [follows] from direct perception or from the absence of the effect; rather, [it follows] from the absence of what pervades it. For thus: causal efficacy (<s>kāryakriyā</s>) is pervaded by [either] succession or simultaneity, because there is no third alternative. Hence, since succession and simultaneity are contradicted in the case of non-momentariness, from the cessation [of those two], which pervade it, the cessation of causal efficacy-capacity also [follows]. Thus, the absence of all capacity — which constitutes non-existence (<s>asattva</s>) — is drawn [as a conclusion] in the case of non-momentariness through the non-apprehension of what pervades [causal efficacy], because contradictory [properties] cannot co-exist in one [entity]. Therefore, existence (<s>sattva</s>), being excluded [from the non-momentary], abides only in momentary entities and experiences identity with them — thus the establishment, i.e., ascertainment, of the pervasion having the form of positive and negative concomitance (<s>anvayavyatireka</s>) — 'whatever is real is momentary alone' — obtains.
  But [the opponent says:] it is said that an effect such as a sprout and the like is produced by a seed and the like through succession and simultaneity alone, because there is no third alternative. But how is that very absence of a third alternative established with regard to the effect? If the third alternative fulfills the conditions for apprehension (<s>upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptatva</s>), how can it be absolutely impossible? It would merely be a negation with respect to [specific] place and the like.

children.text:
anupalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptatve nā 'sattāniścayo viprakarṣiṇām[568]iti kutas tadabhāvasiddhiḥ? | tataḥ prakārāntareṇārthakriyāsambhavāt kramayaugapadyanivṛttāv api nārthakriyāsāmartthyanivṛttir iti kuto 'kṣaṇikatve sati sarvasāmarthyavirahalakṣaṇam asattvam?, yataḥ sattvasya kṣaṇikātmatayā 'nvayavyatirekau syātām? | na | ubhayathā 'py adoṣāt | [S. 143a.] tathā hi -- kramo nāma paripāṭiḥ kāryāntarāsāhityaṃ kaivalyam aṅkurādeḥ, yaugapadyam api tasyāparair bbījādikāryaiḥ sāhityaṃ | prakārāntaraṃ cāṅkurādeḥ tadubhayāvasthāvirahe 'py anyathābhavanam | tasya cāṅkurādisvabhāvasyānyasahitasya
kevalasya vā 'bhāve pratyakṣabodhagamyamāne saty upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāpta eva svabhāvaḥ kramayaugapadyabhāvabahirbhūto nopalabhyate | vastunaḥ upalabhyasyānyasāhitye kaivalye cāpanīte tadviviktadeśādipratibhāsinaḥ[569]pratyakṣasyodayāt svabhāvānupalambhata evābhāvaniścayādilakṣaṇavyavahāravṛtteḥ | tasya cāṅkurādibhāvasyāvasthādvayabahirbhāvaniṣedhe kayościddeśakālayoḥ deśāntarādau krameṇāṅkurādibhāvavatītarasmin vā bhāve 'pi na kācit kṣatiḥ | tataḥ pratyakṣata eva [T. 311a.] prakārāntarābhāvasiddheḥ kathaṃ kramayaugapadyābhyām arthakriyāśaktir avyāptā syāt? |śāstrakāras tu yathā pratyakṣatā eva prakārāntarābhāvasiddhiḥ tathā svayam
children.translated_text:
Even if [the third alternative] fulfills the conditions for apprehension, there is no ascertainment of non-existence for things that are remote — so how is its absence established? Therefore, since causal efficacy is possible through a third alternative, even when succession and simultaneity are excluded, there is no exclusion of causal-efficacy-capacity — so how, when non-momentariness obtains, does non-existence characterized by the absence of all capacity [follow], such that existence would have positive and negative concomitance with momentariness? No — because there is no fault in either case. For thus: 'succession' means serial order, non-simultaneity, the singularity of the sprout and the like; and 'simultaneity' too is its companionship with other effects of the seed and the like. And a 'third alternative' for the sprout and the like would be its being otherwise even in the absence of both those states. And since the non-existence of that [third-alternative] nature of the sprout and the like — whether accompanied by others or alone — is understood through direct perceptual cognition, when it fulfills the conditions for apprehension, that very nature, lying outside the states of succession and simultaneity, is not apprehended. Because, when the companionship and singularity of the apprehended real entity are removed, from the arising of direct perception that presents [the entity] in a location and the like distinct from those, the determination of absence and the like proceeds from the very non-apprehension of the essential nature. And the exclusion of that nature of the sprout and the like from lying outside the two states — [this] does no harm even if that sprout-nature exists in some other place and time, or by succession in a place other [than the observed one], or even in another entity.
Therefore, since the absence of a third alternative is established from direct perception itself, how could the capacity for causal efficacy be unpervaded by succession and simultaneity? The author of the treatise, showing how the absence of a third alternative is established from direct perception itself, will state, indicating [by analogy]:
'By this, succession and non-succession and the like too' —

children.text:
ti atidiśan vakṣyati |
  {p. 148.1} anupalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptatve 'pi prakārāntarasya kramayaugapadyayor anyo 'nyavya[S.143b.]vacchedarūpatvād evāśrayasi(-d evābhāvasi)ddhiḥ tathā hi -- anyonyavyavacchedarūpāṇām ekaniṣedhenāparavidhānāt tasyā[570]'pratiṣedhe vidhipratiṣedhayor virodhād ubhayapratiṣedhātmanaḥ prakārāntarasya kutaḥ sambhavaḥ? | atra prayogaḥ -- yatra yatprakāravyavacchedena yaditaraprakāravyavasthānaṃ na tatra prakārāntarasambhavaḥ, tad yathā -- nīlaprakāravyavacchedenānīlaprakārāntaravyavasthāyāṃ pīte | asti ca kramayaugapadyayor anyataraprakāravyavacchedena taditaraprakāravyavasthānam vyavacchidyamānaprakārāviṣayīkṛte sarvatra kāryakāraṇarūpe[571]vastunīti viruddhopalabdhiḥ vyavacchidyamānaprakāretaravyavasthānaṃ ca, prakārāntarasambhavaś[572], [573] ca tato bahirbhāvalakṣaṇa ity anayos tattvā 'nyatvarūpayor anyonyaparihārasthitalakṣaṇatvāt | na cātrāpi bādhakāntarāśaṅkayā 'navasthānam
āśaṅkanīyam, pūrvaprasiddhasya [T. 311b.] [S. 144a.] virodhasya smaraṇamātratvāt | viruddhopalabdhiṣu bahirddharmiṇi hetoḥ sadbhāvam upadarśya virodhasādhanam eva bādhakam, tac cehāsti | tato viruddhayor ekatrāsambhavāt pratiyogyabhāvaniścayaḥ śītoṣṇasparśayor iva bhāvābhāvayor iva veti kuto 'navasthā? |
  tatra na krameṇākṣaṇikaḥ kāryāṇi karoty aviśeṣād akārakāvasthāyām iva | sahakāryapekṣā ca dvividhasyāpi sahakāritvasyāyogād anupanyasanīyā | sarveṣāṃ caikakriyākāla eva kriyāprasakteḥ, tatkārakasya svabhāvasya tadaiva bhāvāt | nāpi yugapat, pratyakṣādivirodhāt[574]punas tatkriyāprasaṅgāc ca | kṛtatvān neti cet, na, sāmarthyānapāyāt | anyathā prāg apy akārakarūpāviśeṣād kriyā syāt | kṛtasya karttum aśakyatvād iti cet | śaktāśaktatayā tarhy ekatraiva kārye bhedaprasaṅgaḥ śālikodravabījāder iva | nityaś ca yadā yugapat karoti tataḥ prāg api bhāvāt tadaiva tatkriyāprasaṅgaḥ punas tato 'pi pūrvataram ity evaṃ [S. 144b.] na kadācid yugapat kriyā syāt | pūrvottarakālayoś caikadā yugapat kāriṇo 'nyadā {p. 149.1} sarvārthakriyāsāmarthyavirahalakṣaṇam asattvaṃ syād iti kathaṃ na kṣaṇikatā? | kriyopagame vā kramapakṣa eva | tatra cokto doṣaḥ | evam akṣaṇikatve [T. 312a.] sati cakṣurādyāya-
tanānāmasattvaprasaṅgāt[575]kṣaṇikatāyām eva sattvam iti yat sat tat kṣaṇikam eveti sato naśvarātmatāsiddheḥ anvayavyatirekarūpavyāptisiddhir iti ||[576]
{p. 150.1} [ 3. kāryahetunirūpaṇam |]
children.translated_text:
thus he will say.
  {p. 148.1} Even if the third alternative fulfills the conditions for apprehension, the establishment of [its] absence is grounded in the very fact that succession and simultaneity have the form of mutual exclusion. For thus: since among [properties] having the form of mutual exclusion, the negation of one entails the affirmation of the other, and since the negation of that [affirmation] would contradict the [previous] negation, how is the existence of a third alternative — having the nature of the negation of both — possible? Here the formal argument (<s>prayoga</s>) [is]: wherever the exclusion of one mode [entails] the establishment of the other mode, there a third alternative is not possible — as, for example, in yellow, where the exclusion of the blue mode [entails] the establishment of a non-blue alternative mode. And there is, regarding succession and simultaneity, the establishment of the alternative mode through the exclusion of one mode — with respect to every real entity in the form of cause and effect that is not the domain of the mode being excluded — thus [this is] an apprehension of what is contradictory (<s>viruddhopalabdhi</s>). And the establishment of the alternative to the mode being excluded, and the occurrence of a third alternative outside that — of these two, having the nature of identity and otherness, [they are contradictory] because they are characterized by mutual exclusion.
And here too, the apprehension of infinite regress through suspicion of another defeater should not be suspected, because it is merely the recollection of a previously established contradiction. In apprehensions of contradiction, the very establishment of the contradiction — by showing the existence of the reason in a subject external [to the probandum] — is the defeater, and that exists here. Therefore, from the impossibility of contradictory [properties] in one [entity], there is the ascertainment of the absence of the counter-correlate — like hot and cold touches, or like existence and non-existence. So how could there be an infinite regress?
  Therein, a non-momentary entity does not produce effects successively, because of the absence of any distinguishing feature — just as in the state of non-production. And the dependence on cooperative causes is not to be adduced, because of the impossibility of both types of cooperative causation. And since the activity of all [entities] would extend to the very time of [their] activity, because the nature that is their producer exists at that very time. Nor [does it produce] simultaneously, because of contradiction with direct perception and the like, and because of the absurd consequence of repeated production. [If one says:] 'Not so, because [the effect] has [already] been produced' — no, because the capacity has not departed. Otherwise, since there is no distinguishing feature from the non-producing state even before, production would [have to] occur [then too]. [If one says:] 'Because what has been produced cannot be produced [again]' — then the absurd consequence of division with respect to one and the same effect, through capable and incapable [states], [would follow] — like rice and millet seeds and the like. And when a permanent [entity] produces simultaneously — since it exists even before, the absurd consequence of producing that [effect] at that very [earlier] time, and then even earlier than that — thus simultaneous production would never occur. And for one that produces simultaneously at earlier and later times, at one time, and at another time possesses non-existence characterized by the absence of all causal-efficacy-capacity — how is it not momentary? Or if production is accepted, it is only the succession thesis. And there the fault has been stated. Thus, in the case of non-momentariness, since the absurd consequence of non-existence of the sense faculties and the like [would follow], existence belongs to momentariness alone. Hence, 'whatever is real is momentary alone' — since the perishable nature of the real is established, the establishment of the pervasion in the form of positive and negative concomitance [is achieved]. ||
{p. 150.1} [3. Examination of the effect-as-reason (<s>kāryahetu</s>)]

body.translated_text: The reasoning is thus: Here, first this alone is to be examined — what definition of this existence (<s>sattva</s>) of entities is correct? In that regard, it is not characterized as connection with the universal 'being' (<s>sattāyoga</s>), because of non-pervasion, since it is absent in universals (<s>sāmānya</s>) and the like. Or because of over-extension, since it would be present even in the son of a barren woman and the like. 'Since the son of a barren woman and the like are non-existent, how could there be connection with being?' — if so: No, because of mutual dependence (<s>itaretarāśraya</s>). Since their non-existence is precisely because of the absence of connection with being, and the absence of that [connection] is because of non-existence. And if connection with being belongs only to existents, then another definition of existence must be stated, and the connection with being is purposeless, since the entity's existence [is already established] from that very [entity]. 'The absence of connection with being for those [barren woman's son etc.] is because of the absence of all causal efficacy (<s>sarvārthakriyāsāmarthya</s>)' — if so, then that which alone is endowed with causal efficacy has connection with being — so causal efficacy alone has become the definition of entities, and thus connection with being is pointless. |

body.text: tad evaṃ svabhāvahetau tādātmyasiddhinibandhanam anvayavyatirekaniścayaṃ pratipādya kāryahetau kāryakāraṇabhāvasiddhinimittatvāt tayos tasyāś ca pratyakṣānupalambhanibandhanāyāḥ prāg eva darśitatvāt tadgatam aparam api pareṣāṃ bhrāntikāraṇam apanetuṃ tadviṣayaṃ darśayann āha --

children.translated_text: 'In something different' —
in a real entity to be inferred that is distinct from the reason,
'the effect is the reason.'

children.text: | anarthāntare tu svabhāvo hetur ity uktam | kasmāt [S. 145a.] punar arthāntare kāryam eva hetur ity āha --
children.translated_text: | But when [the entity to be inferred] is not something different, the essential-nature reason has been stated. Why, moreover, is it specifically the effect that is the reason with respect to something different? — he says:
'Because of non-deviation' —

children.text: iti kāryam eva hy arthāntaraṃ na vyabhicarati nānyat yathoktaṃ prāk tataḥ kāryam evārthāntare gamye hetur ucyate saṃyogavaśād gamakatve |
children.translated_text: thus: it is the effect alone that does not deviate from something different, and nothing else — as was stated before. Therefore, only the effect is called the reason when something different is to be inferred, insofar as it indicates by virtue of connection.
'And not by anything' —
thus,

children.text: ādinā yaḥ[578]sarvathā gamyagamakabhāvaprasaṅgaācāryeṇoktaḥ parasya, tam ihāpi kāryahetau paraḥ kadācit prasañjayed ity āśaṅkamāna āha --
children.translated_text: by this beginning — the [objection of] universal inferability between what-is-to-be-inferred and what-indicates, which was stated by the master (<s>ācārya</s>) against the opponent — [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>], apprehending that the opponent might raise [this objection] here too regarding the effect-reason, says:
'Cause-and-effect' —

children.text: ityādi [T. 312b.] yadi hi kāryaṃ hetur ucyate tadā kāryakāraṇabhāvena kāraṇenāsya gamakatvam | tathā ca sati sarvathā gamyagamakabhāvaḥ prāpnoti | agneḥ sāmānyadharmavad viśeṣadharmā api tārṇapārṇādayo gamyāḥ syuḥ | dhūmasyāpi viśeṣadharmavad dravyatvapārthivatvādayo 'pi sāmānyadharmā gamakā bhaveyuḥ | kutaḥ?
children.translated_text: and so forth. If the effect is said to be the reason, then its indicative capacity is by virtue of the cause-effect relation. And that being so, universal inferability would obtain. The specific properties of fire — such as being made of grass, leaves, and the like — would also be inferable, just as its general properties. And the general properties of smoke — such as substance-hood, earthen-ness, and the like — would also be indicators, just as its specific properties. Why?
'Because [they are] produced-and-producer in every respect' —

children.text:
| janyajanakabhāvo hi kāryakāraṇabhāva ucyate | sa ca nāgnidhūmayor aṃśena api tu sarveṇa prakāreṇa | tathā hi -- yathā agnir agnitvadravyatvasatvādibhiḥ sāmānyadharmair janakaḥ tathā tārṇapārṇatvādibhir viśeṣadharmair api, yathā ca dhūmo dhūmatvapāṇḍutvādibhiḥ svaniyatair viśeṣadharmair janyaḥ tathā [S. 145b.]
sāmānyadharmair api sattvadravyatvādibhiḥ | tataś ca yathā tayoḥ kāryakāraṇabhāvaḥ tathaiva gamyagamakabhāvaḥ prāpnoti, tasyaiva tannibandhanatvād iti pūrvapakṣāśaṅkā | atrāha --
children.translated_text: | For the produced-and-producer relation is called the cause-effect relation. And that [relation] between fire and smoke is not partial but rather in every respect. For thus: just as fire is a producer through its general properties such as fire-ness, substance-hood, existence, and the like, so too through its specific properties such as being made of grass and leaves and the like; and just as smoke is produced through its own specific properties such as smoke-ness, pale color, and the like, so too through its general properties such as existence, substance-hood, and the like. And therefore, just as the cause-effect relation [obtains] between those two, so too would the inferability relation obtain, since that [inferability] is precisely grounded in that [cause-effect relation] — this is the apprehension of the prima facie objection (<s>pūrvapakṣa</s>). To this [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>] says:
'[They are] not produced-and-producer in every respect' —

children.text: tataś ca kutas tathā gamyagamakabhāvaḥ syāt? | kasmāt? iti cet, {p. 151.1}
children.translated_text: and therefore, how could inferability in that manner obtain? Why? — if asked, {p. 151.1}
'in the absence of those' —
of those specific properties such as being made of grass and leaves and the like, in their absence —
'of [something that] exists' —

children.text: dhūmamātrasya tebhya eva viśeṣadharmebhyo bhavatīti evam ātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: of smoke alone, [which] exists from those very specific properties — thus, of its own
'because of the absence of the restriction of arising from those.'
| Likewise,
'in the absence of that' —

children.text: agnyabhāve bhavato dravyatvādeḥ [T. 313a.] sāmānyadharmasyāgner evāyaṃ bhavatīty evaṃrūpasya tadutpattiniyamasyābhāvāt kutaḥ sarvathā janyajanakabhāvaḥ?, yataḥ sarvathā gamyagamakabhāvaḥ syāt | na hy asati tadutpattiniyame janyajanakabhāvo vyavasthāpayituṃ yuktaḥ[579]| yata evaṃ
children.translated_text: in the absence of fire — of the general property such as substance-hood that exists [independently of fire] — because of the absence of the restriction of the form 'this arises from fire alone' — how can there be the produced-and-producer relation in every respect, such that there would be inferability in every respect? For without the restriction of arising from that, it is not proper to establish a produced-and-producer relation. Since it is thus,
'therefore the effect' —
smoke and the like —
'with however many essential natures' —

children.text:
r dhūmatvādibhiḥ svagataiḥ | itthambhūtalakṣaṇā
ca tṛtīyā |
children.translated_text: such as smoke-ness and the like, belonging to itself. And the third [case ending] has the sense of 'characterized by.'
'is inseparable' —

children.text: vinā na bhavati | kair vinā na bhavati? | `kāraṇe yāvadbhiḥ svabhāvaiḥ' ity atrāpi sambadhyate | kāraṇāśritair yāvadbhiḥ [S. 146a.] svabhāvair vinā te kāryagatāḥ svabhāvā na bhavanti hetuḥ tais teṣām iti gamyate | kva avinābhāvi? |
children.translated_text: [i.e.,] does not exist without. Without what does it not exist? This connects with 'with however many essential natures of the cause' as well. Those essential natures belonging to the effect do not exist without however many essential natures residing in the cause — thus it is understood that [they] are the reason for those. Where is it inseparable?
'In the cause' —
with respect to the cause — [this is] another meaning.
'In the cause' —

children.text: ādhārasaptamī | idānīṃ kāraṇasthaiḥ svabhāvair yāvadbhir agnitvadravyatvādibhir avinābhāvi teṣāṃ kāraṇagatānāṃ sāmānyadharmāṇāṃ hetuḥ kāryaṃ gamakam | kasmāt? ity āha --
children.translated_text: [this is] the locative of the locus. Now: the effect, being inseparable from however many essential natures abiding in the cause — such as fire-ness, substance-hood, and the like — is the indicator of those general properties belonging to the cause. Why? — he says:
'Because of the restriction of being an effect of those' —

children.text:
teṣām eva kāraṇagatānāṃ sāmānyadharmāṇāṃ tat kāryam ity evaṃrūpasya niyamasya sadbhāvāt | na hi tān sāmānyadharmān kadācid api kāryaṃ vyabhicarati |
 evaṃkāraṇagatam aṃśaṃ pāścātyenārthena[580]nirūpya prāktanenārthena
children.translated_text:
because of the existence of the restriction of the form 'that is the effect of precisely those general properties belonging to the cause.' For the effect never deviates from those general properties.
 Thus, having examined the aspect belonging to the cause by means of the latter meaning, [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>] now examines the aspect belonging to the effect by means of the former meaning, and says:
examining the aspect belonging to the effect, [he] says:
'And by those very' —

children.text:
ityādi | kāryam api tair eva dharmaiḥ [T. 313b.] svagataiḥ kāraṇagatānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ gamakam yathā 'ntarā sambhavino dhūmatvapāṇḍupārṇatvādayo[581]viśeṣarūpāstaiḥ kāraṇagataiḥ sāmānyadharmair vinā na bhavanti | atrāpi `tatkāryatvaniyamāt' ity apekṣyate | teṣām eva kāryagatānāṃ viśeṣadharmāṇāṃ kāraṇagatasāmānyadharmāpekṣayā kāryatvaniyamāt | na hi te viśeṣadharmāḥ kāryagatāḥ [S. 146b.] kāraṇasthasāmānyadharmair vinā kadācid api bhavanti | tatas teṣām eva kāryatvaniyamaḥ, nānyeṣāṃ {p. 152.1} dravyatvādīnāṃ kāraṇasthasāmānyadharmair vinā bhavatām | tad evaṃ kāraṇasya sāmānyadharmā eva gamyā na viśeṣadharmāḥ, kāryasyāpi viśeṣadharmā eva gamakā na sāmānyadharmāḥ, tatkāryatvaniyamāt | ye tu kāraṇasya
viśeṣadharmā yais tatkāryatvaniyamaḥ kāryamātrasya nāstīti na te gamyāḥ | ye ca kāryasya sāmānyadharmā dravyatvādayas teṣām api tatkāryatvaniyamābhāvād eva gamakatvaṃ nāstīti kāryakāraṇabhāvena gamakatve kutaḥ sarvathā gamyagamakabhāvaḥ pareṣām iva prasajyeta? |
children.translated_text: and so forth. The effect too, by those very properties that are its own — the specific forms such as smoke-ness, tawny-leaf-ness, and the like, which arise intermediately — is the indicator (<s>gamaka</s>) of the properties belonging to the cause; [those specific forms] do not exist without the universal properties belonging to the cause. Here too, 'because of the regularity of being an effect of that' should be supplied. Because those very specific properties belonging to the effect have a regularity of being effects relative to the universal properties belonging to the cause. For those specific properties belonging to the effect never exist without the universal properties belonging to the cause. Therefore, the regularity of being effects pertains to those alone, not to others such as substance-ness and the like, which exist even without the universal properties belonging to the cause. Thus, of the cause, only the universal properties are what is indicated (<s>gamya</s>), not the specific properties; and of the effect too, only the specific properties are the indicators, not the universal properties, because of the regularity of being effects of those [universal properties]. But those specific properties of the cause, by which there is a regularity of being an effect [only] of the effect in general — they are not what is indicated. And those universal properties of the effect — substance-ness and the like — since they too lack the regularity of being effects of those [specific cause-properties], they have no indicative capacity. Therefore, when indicative capacity is through the cause-effect relation, how could there be an all-encompassing indicated-indicator relation, as the opponents would have it?

body.translated_text: Thus, having established the ascertainment of positive and negative concomitance — which is grounded in the establishment of essential identity (<s>tādātmyasiddhi</s>) — regarding the essential-nature reason (<s>svabhāvahetu</s>), [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>] now, with respect to the effect-reason (<s>kāryahetu</s>) — since the establishment of the cause-effect relation is its basis, and since that [cause-effect relation], which is grounded in direct perception and non-apprehension, has already been shown previously — in order to remove yet another cause of error on the part of opponents regarding that [topic], shows its subject matter and says:

body.text: section: 2. janyajanakabhāvasya sarvathā sattve 'pi gamyagamakabhāvasya na tathātvam |
body.translated_text: Section: 2. Even when the producer-produced relation exists in all respects, the indicated-indicator relation does not similarly exist in all respects

children.translated_text: 'Partially' —

children.text: ityādi | yadi hi kāraṇasya sāmānyadharmā eva gamyāḥ kāryasyāpi viśeṣadharmā eva gamakāḥ tatkāryatvaniyamād iṣyante, hanta tarhy aṃśena janyajanakabhāvaḥ prāptaḥ | kāraṇasya sāmānyadharmā eva janakā na viśeṣadharmāḥ, kāryasyāpi viśeṣadharmā eva janyā na sāmānyadharmā iti syāt | sarvathā ca janyajanakabhāvo 'bhimata [T. 314a.] ity abhyupagamavirodhaḥ | etat pariharati -- nāṃśena janyajanakabhāvaprasaṅgaḥ, niraṃśatvena vastunaḥ sarvātmanā tadabhyupagamāt, gamyagamakabhāvasyāpi sarvathā 'bhimatatvāt | tad āha --
children.translated_text: and so forth. For if only the universal properties of the cause are what is indicated and only the specific properties of the effect are the indicators, because of the regularity of being effects of those — well then, a partial producer-produced relation has been arrived at! [Namely:] only the universal properties of the cause are the producers, not the specific properties; and only the specific properties of the effect are the produced, not the universal properties — this would follow. But the producer-produced relation is accepted in all respects — so there would be a contradiction with what is accepted. He resolves this: there is no consequence of a partial producer-produced relation, because the entity, being without parts, is accepted as such in its entirety, and because the indicated-indicator relation too is accepted in all respects. He says:
'The specific [feature] produced by that' —

children.text:
-- ityādi | yadi hi kāryasya taiḥ kāraṇagatair viśeṣadharmair janyo yo viśeṣaḥ sa grahītuṃ śakyate, tadā tajjanyaviśeṣagrahaṇe 'bhimatatvāt [S. 147a.] kāraṇagataviśeṣadharmāṇāṃ gamyatvasya | tathā liṅgaviśeṣo dhūmatvādiḥ upādhir viśeṣaṇaṃ yeṣāṃ dravyatvādīnāṃ sāmānyānāṃ kāryagatānāṃ
teṣāṃ cābhimatatvād gamakatvasya | tathā hi -- agurudhūmagrahaṇe bhavaty eva tadagner anumānaṃ dhūmatvaviśeṣaṇena ca dravyatvādinā 'gner anumānam | na hi sarvathā janyajanakabhāvo 'stīty eva tathaiva gamyagamakabhāvo bhavati, tasya jñānāpekṣatvāt | tathā hi -- na sattāmātreṇa liṅgasya gamakatvam, tasya jñāpakatvāt[582]| jñāpako hi svaniścayāpekṣo jñāpyam arthaṃ jñāpayati, nānyathā | kathaṃ {p. 153.1} tarhy uktaṃ
children.translated_text: and so forth. For if the specific [feature] that is produced by those specific properties belonging to the cause can be grasped, then since it is accepted that in grasping the specific [feature] produced by that, the specific properties belonging to the cause are what is indicated; and similarly, since the indicative capacity of the specific form of the logical mark (<s>liṅga</s>) — smoke-ness and the like — which qualifies the universals belonging to the effect — substance-ness and the like — is also accepted. Thus: in the apprehension of <s>aguru</s>-smoke, there is indeed the inference of that [particular] fire; and through the qualifier of smoke-ness, there is also inference of fire along with substance-ness and the like. For it is not the case that just because the producer-produced relation exists in all respects, the indicated-indicator relation exists in exactly the same way, since the latter depends on cognition (<s>jñāna</s>). Thus: the logical mark is not an indicator merely by existing, since it has the nature of making known. For what makes known does so only in dependence on one's own ascertainment of the object to be made known, not otherwise. How then was it said:
'In the absence of that, because of the absence of the regularity of its production' —
thus? Since the producer-produced relation is accepted in all respects, in the absence of that [cause]

children.text: iti? | sarvathā janyajanakabhāvābhyupagame [T. 314b.] tadabhāve bhāvasyaivābhāvād ity ata[h13]āha --
children.translated_text: , there would be the absence of the entity itself — therefore he says:
'Undistinguished' —

children.text: ityādi | yadi hi tajjanyaviśeṣagrahaṇarahitam aviśiṣṭaṃ kāryamātram upādīyate liṅgaviśeṣopādhirahitaṃ vā dravyādikaṃ tadā
children.translated_text: and so forth. For if the undistinguished mere effect — devoid of grasping the specific [feature] produced by that — is taken [as the logical mark], or if substance and the like devoid of the qualifier of the specific form of the logical mark [are taken], then
'when the intention is of the undistinguished universal' —

children.text:
kāraṇagataviśeṣābhāve 'pi dhūmamātrasya bhāvāt tadaviśiṣṭasya ca dravyatvāder agnyabhāve 'pi bhāvād vyabhicāra iti sarvathā [S.
147b.] janyajanakabhāvo neṣyate, tadabhāvād gamyagamakabhāvaś ca | na tu viśeṣavivakṣāyām, tatra vyabhicārābhāvāt | tathā hi -- yadi nāma dhūmamātraṃ tārṇapārṇādiviśeṣābhāve bhavati, na tu tajjanyo viśeṣaḥ, sa yadi grahītuṃ śakyate, tadā viśeṣasya gamyatvam asty eva, niścitasyaiva liṅgatvāt | tathā yady api dravyatvasattvamātram agnyabhāve 'pi bhavati na tu dhūmātmakam iti tadviśiṣṭasyāvyabhicārād gamakatvam api na vāryata iti |
children.translated_text: since even in the absence of the specific [property] belonging to the cause, mere smoke exists, and since the undistinguished substance-ness and the like exist even in the absence of fire — there would be deviation (<s>vyabhicāra</s>). So the producer-produced relation is not accepted in all respects, and due to its absence, neither is the indicated-indicator relation. But [there is no such problem] when the intention is of the specific, because there is no deviation there. Thus: even if mere smoke exists in the absence of the specific [properties] such as fuel-twig, leaf, and the like, the specific [feature] produced by those does not [exist without them]. If that can be grasped, then the specific is indeed what is indicated, since only what is ascertained has the nature of a logical mark. Similarly, even though mere substance-ness and existence exist in the absence of fire, [they do] not [exist] as having the nature of smoke — therefore, since the qualified [substance-ness] does not deviate, its indicative capacity too is not precluded.

body.translated_text: Anticipating the undesirable consequence for the opponent, he says:
because of depending on what makes known — T.
Section: 3. Refutation of the apprehension that cognition of the cause-effect relation is extremely difficult to obtain

children.translated_text: 'Of something' —
of smoke and the like,
'at some time' —
at some particular time,
'from something' —
from fire and the like,
'even when there is existence' —
when there is,
'every' —
smoke and the like,
'of that kind' —
of the same class as the one observed at one time arising from fire and the like,
'born of that kind [of cause]' —

children.text: yathāvidhāt sa eko bhavan dṛṣṭaḥ tādṛśād eva janma yasya sa |
children.translated_text: the one from which kind [of cause] that single [smoke] was observed to arise — [born] from exactly that kind — that is one whose birth is of that kind.
'How is it [known that it is] born of that kind?' —

children.text:
pramāṇād avasitam? yenocyate [T. 315a.] `kāryahetau kāryakāraṇabhāvasiddhinibandhanāv anvayavyatirekau' iti | tathā hi -- yadi nāma pratyakṣānupalambhābhyāṃ kasyaciddhūmasyāgnyādisāmagrīkāryatvam avagataṃ kim etāvatā 'nyasyāpi [S. 148a.] tādṛśasya tādṛśakāryatā sidhyati, tatra tannibandhanayoḥ[584]pratyakṣānupalambhayor avyāpārāt | tatraiva hi tayor vyāpāras tasyaiva tatkāryatā bhavatu, tad anyasya tu kim āyātam? yena tathāvidhād asya janma syāt | evaṃ hi kasyāściddhūmavyakter agnyādijanyatā dṛṣṭeti kinna ghaṭāder
api sā 'bhyupagamyate? {p. 154.1} anyatvena viśeṣābhāvāt | ka evaṃ sati doṣaḥ? iti cet; tathā ca pramāṇābhāvena tathāvidhajanmatvāniścayād atādṛśād api janmāśaṅkāyāṃ tādṛśasya dhūmāder agnyādinā 'nvayavyatirekau na niścitāv iti kutaḥ kāryahetor ggamakatvam? | na hi yo 'smāv eko deśakālāvasthāniyato 'gniviśeṣahetuko dhūmo 'dhigataḥ pratyakṣānupalambhābhyāṃ tasyaivānvayavyatirekau pratipattavyau | tasya deśāntarādāv asambhavāt | kiṃ tarhi? | tādṛśasya sāmānyātmana eva liṅgatvāt tasya cātathāvidhād api janmāśaṅkāyāṃ kutas tathāvidhenānvayo vyatireko vā? | tad uktam -
children.translated_text: from what <s>pramāṇa</s> is this ascertained? — by which one says 'positive correlation (<s>anvaya</s>) and negative correlation (<s>vyatireka</s>) are the basis for establishing the cause-effect relation with respect to the causal ground (<s>kāryahetu</s>).' Thus: even if the nature of some smoke as an effect of a fire-aggregate is ascertained through direct perception and non-apprehension, how does this establish that another [instance] of that kind is also an effect of that kind [of cause], since those [means of valid cognition] — direct perception and non-apprehension — do not operate with respect to that [other instance]? For their operation pertains only to that [particular instance] — let only that have that effect-nature; but what does this accomplish for another? By which [reasoning] its birth would be from that kind [of cause]. For thus, the fact that some particular instance of smoke is produced by fire and the like has been observed — why should it not be accepted for a pot and the like too? Because there is no distinction by way of otherness. 'What is the fault in this?' If so: since, due to the absence of <s>pramāṇa</s>, there is no certainty that it is born of that kind, and since there is the apprehension that it might be born from something not of that kind — the positive and negative correlations of such smoke and the like with fire and the like are not ascertained. So whence the indicative capacity of the causal ground? For it is not the case that the positive and negative correlations are to be understood of that very smoke which we have ascertained, through direct perception and non-apprehension, as caused by a specific fire restricted to a specific place, time, and condition — because that [specific smoke] is impossible at another place and the like. What then? Since the logical mark is of the nature of a universal — of that kind — and since there is the apprehension that it might be born from something not of that kind, whence the positive correlation or negative correlation with that kind? As stated:
'Given that entities have different powers due to differences of condition, place, and time,
cognition through inference
is extremely difficult to obtain.' ||
<s>Vākyapadīya</s> 1.32

Thus.
The proponent (<s>siddhāntavādin</s>) says:
'No, because of [the smoke] not having its nature from that [non-fire source]' —

children.text: ityādi | evaṃ manyate -- ihaikadā dhūmāder agnyādisāmagrījanyatayā [S. 148b.] pratyakṣānupalambhābhyāṃ niścitarūpatve 'pi tādṛśasyātādṛśād api bhāvaḥ samāśaṅkyate yathāparidṛṣṭād anyatvena | tatra yo 'sāv agnyādisāmagrījanyo dhūmaviśeṣa ekadā niścitas tadapekṣayā yathā 'nyo dhūmaviśeṣas tādṛśo yo 'nyādṛśād api -- bhāvānāṃ vicitraśaktitayā -- bhaved iti śaṅkyate, tathā so 'py ekadā 'gnyādisāmagrījanyatayā niścitas tadanyāpekṣayā tādṛśa eva | tatra yadi tad anyasya tādṛśasyātādṛśāj janma syāt
children.translated_text: and so forth. He thinks thus: here, even though the nature of some smoke as an effect of a fire-aggregate has been ascertained through direct perception and non-apprehension at one time, the existence of such [smoke] from something not of that kind too is apprehended, since it is other than what was observed. There, that specific smoke which was once ascertained as produced by a fire-aggregate — relative to that, just as another specific smoke of that kind is suspected to arise even from something of a different kind — due to the varied powers of entities — so too that [other smoke], once ascertained as produced by a fire-aggregate, is of that very kind relative to the other [smoke]. There, if the birth of that other one of that kind were from something not of that kind,
then of that kind of essential nature —

children.text:
nāgnyādisāmagrījanyasvabhāvateti paridṛṣṭasyāpi[588]dhūmasya nā 'gnyādisāmagrī kāraṇam ity āyātam | tādṛśasya svabhāvasyā 'gnyādisāmagrīvilakṣaṇakāraṇajanyasvabhāvatvāt | tataś cāgnyādisāmagryā akāraṇatvāt yo mayaikadā
tato bhavan dṛṣṭo dhūmaḥ so 'pi na bhavet | na hi yad yasya kāraṇaṃ na bhavati tat tataḥ sakṛd api jāyate, tasyāhetukatvaprasaṅgād iti |
children.translated_text: it would follow that [it] does not have the essential nature of being produced by a fire-aggregate — and so even the observed smoke would not have the fire-aggregate as its cause. Because that kind of essential nature would have the essential nature of being produced by a cause dissimilar to the fire-aggregate. And consequently, since the fire-aggregate is not its cause, even the smoke that was once observed to arise from it would not arise [from it]. For that which is not the cause of something never produces it even once, because of the absurd consequence of it being without a cause.
'Not having its nature from that' —

children.text: iti tacchabdena vivakṣitam agnyādikāraṇaṃ parigṛhyate, na tat atat, tadvilakṣaṇaṃ atādṛśaṃ śakramūrddhādikam, atasmād[589]bhavituṃ [T. 316a.] śīlaṃ {p. 155.1} yasya tasyātadbhāvinas tādṛśasya tallakṣaṇasya dhūmavastunaḥ
children.translated_text: the word 'that' refers to the intended cause — fire and the like; 'not-that' is what is dissimilar to that, not of that kind, such as the peak of <s>Śakra</s>'s [mountain] and the like; that whose character is to exist from that [non-fire source] — of such a smoke-entity bearing that characteristic, which has the nature of arising from that [non-fire source],
'even once' —
even at one time,
'from that' —
from fire and the like,
'because of [its] absence' —

children.text:
bhāvavirodhāt | bhavati ca tādṛśo 'gnyādisāmagrītaḥ tatas tādṛśasya svabhāvasya tādṛśam eva kāraṇam ity avagamyate sakṛtpravṛttābhyām eva pratyakṣānupalambhābhyām iti kuto vyabhicārāśaṅkā? | tena yādṛśo dhūmo 'gnyādisāmagryā bhavan dṛṣṭaḥ sakṛt tādṛśasya tasya tajjanyasvabhāvatayā tādṛśād eva bhāvāt `yatra dhūmas tatrāgnyādisāmagrī' ity anvayavyatirekaniścayaḥ |
  athavā 'nyathā vyākhyāyate -- iha pratyakṣānupalambhanibandhanā kāryakāraṇabhāvasiddhiḥ prāguktā tannibandhanāv anvayavyatirekau
children.translated_text:
because of the contradiction with [its] existence. And since such [smoke] does arise from a fire-aggregate, therefore it is understood that such an essential nature has such a cause alone — by direct perception and non-apprehension operating even once. So whence the apprehension of deviation? Therefore, of whatever kind the smoke was observed once to arise from a fire-aggregate, since that of that kind has the essential nature of being produced by that and exists only from that kind [of cause] — the ascertainment of positive and negative correlation: 'wherever there is smoke, there is a fire-aggregate' [is established].
Alternatively, [the passage] is explained differently: here, the establishment of the cause-effect relation based on direct perception and non-apprehension has been stated above. [To use] that as the basis for positive and negative correlations
to demonstrate — but that is unreasonable. Thus:
'Of something' —
of the first smoke that exists immediately after the fire-aggregate,
'at some time' —
at the time of first production,
'from something' —
from the fire-aggregate,
'even when there is existence' —
even when there is production,
'every' —
'of that kind' —

children.text: yādṛśaḥ[591]prathamakṣaṇabhāvī dhūmo dvitīyādikṣaṇeṣv api tādṛśaḥ pratyakṣata eva tasya pūrvakṣaṇāvilakṣaṇatayā pratīteḥ |
children.translated_text: of the kind that the smoke existing at the first moment is — even in the second and subsequent moments it is of that kind, since it is cognized through direct perception as not differing from the prior moment.
'Born of that kind [of cause]' —

children.text: iti yathāvidhād agnīndhanasāmagrīlakṣaṇāt kāraṇād ādyo dhūmakṣaṇa utpannas tathāvidhāj janma yasya sa
children.translated_text: thus: from whatever kind of cause characterized as the fire-fuel aggregate the first smoke-moment arose, that whose birth is from that kind —
'how is it [known that it is] born of that kind?' —

children.text: naiva tasya dhūmāder abhāvāt [T. 316b.] | evaṃ ca yadyato dṛṣṭaṃ tasyānyato 'pi bhāvasya darśanāt sarvatrānāśvāsa [S. 149b.] iti anyamāna āha --
children.translated_text: this is not [known] at all, because of the absence of that smoke and the like [in a subsequent moment]. And thus, since what has been observed from one source is seen to exist from another too, there is no confidence anywhere — thinking thus, the [opponent] says:
'And thus' —

children.text:
anagnito dhūmād api dhūmasya
bhāve śakramūrddhāder api tasya bhāvāvirodhād agninā dhūmasya nānvayavyatirekāv iti cen manyasa iti pūrvapakṣāśaṅkā |
  taduktam -
children.translated_text:
since even from non-fire smoke, there is the existence of smoke, and since even from the peak of <s>Śakra</s>'s [mountain] and the like, the existence of that is not contradicted — 'there is no positive and negative correlation of smoke with fire' — if you think thus, this is the prima facie objection.
As stated:
'If [things are] momentary, how can entities have their existence dependent on anything?'

children.text: prathamadhūmakṣaṇajanito dhūmakṣaṇas tādṛśo 'paraprathamadhūmakṣaṇajanita eva dvitīyo dhūmakṣaṇo na tṛtīyādiḥ | evaṃ tṛtīyakṣaṇādiṣv apy aṅkurādiṣu ca sarvatra vācyam | kutaḥ punar ayaṃ vibhāgaḥ? iti cet, āha --
children.translated_text: The smoke-moment produced by the first smoke-moment is of that kind; the second smoke-moment is produced only by another first smoke-moment, not by the third and so on. The same should be said for the third moment and so on, and for sprouts and the like everywhere. But whence this distinction? If asked, he says:
'Not having its nature from that' —

children.text: atasmād -- anagnīndhanādirūpād dhūmād [T. 317a.] bhavanaśīlasya prathamakṣaṇāvilakṣaṇasya dhūmasya
children.translated_text: of smoke that has the character of arising from that [non-fire source] — from smoke that is not of the nature of fire-fuel and the like — of smoke that does not differ from the first moment,
'even once' —
even at one time,
'from that' —
from the fire-aggregate,
because of [its] absence —

children.text: bhāvāyogād | yathā hi prathamakṣaṇāpekṣayā dvitīyas tādṛśas tathā tadapekṣayā prathamo 'pīti tādṛśatvāviśeṣāt tādṛśasyānagnito bhāve tādṛśo nāgnijanyasvabhāvaḥ iti sakṛd api tato na bhavet | bhavan vā tajjanyasvabhāvatām ātmanas tādṛśaḥ khyāpayatīti kuto 'nyādṛśād bhavet? tasmād anyādṛśād bhavann anyādṛśa eva tato na vyabhicāraḥ |
children.translated_text: because of the impossibility of the existence [of such]. For just as the second [moment] is of such a kind with respect to the first moment, so too the first with respect to that — and since there is no distinction in being of such a kind, if what is of such a kind does not arise from fire, then what is of such a kind does not have the essential nature of being fire-produced — and so not even once would it arise from that [fire]. Or if it does arise, it — being of such a kind — demonstrates the essential nature of being produced by that — so how could it arise from something of a different kind? Therefore, arising from something of a different kind, it is indeed of a different kind from that — so there is no deviation.

body.translated_text: Anticipating an opening for the opponent's words, he says:

body.text:
kāryakāraṇabhāvani-

[586] iti cet -- T.
[587] tadā 'tādṛ- -- T.
[588] -tety apa- -- T.
[589] tasmāt -- T.
[590] -tum iṣṭau ta- -- T.
[591] -śo na yādṛ- -- T.
[592] kāraṇaśaktibhedena svayaṃ -- T.
body.translated_text:
cause-effect-nature-deter-
[585] established- — Vākya-
[586] if so — T.
[587] then not-of-such- — T.
[588] -thus refu- — T.
[589] therefore — T.
[590] -to be intended those- — T.
[591] -kind not of-what- — T.

body.text: section: 4. bhinnakāraṇajanyānāṃ dhūmānāṃ atādṛśatve 'pi sādṛśyāt tādṛśatvābhimānaḥ |
body.translated_text: Section: 4. The supposition that smoke-moments of different causes are 'of such a kind' due to similarity

children.text:
dhūmakṣaṇānāṃ kaṇṭhakṣaṇanākṣisrutikālīkaraṇādikāyām[593]arthakriyāyām upayogāt kathaṃ tādṛśasvabhāvatā na syāt? | na, tasyā apy arthakriyāyāḥ kṣaṇabhedopadhīyamānarūpāyāḥ tādṛśatvābhāvāt tatrāpi tulyadoṣatvāt | kathaṃ tarhi loke sarvatra dhūmavyavahāraḥ iti cet; sadṛśāparabhāvanibandhanaikatvādhyavasāyavaśāt kṣaṇair vyavahārāyogāc[594]ca | sādṛśye sati kathaṃ na tādṛśatā? iti cet | tādṛśād anyatvāt sadṛśasya | tathā hi -- gosadṛśo bhavati gavayaḥ na tu tādṛśaḥ, gor evāparasya tādṛśatvāt | paramārthenātādṛśe 'pi tādṛśābhimāno [S. 150b.] mandamatīnāṃ bhavan kathaṃ nivāryeta? | tathā hi -- tattvādhyavasāyo 'pi tāvad -- atasminn arvāgdṛśāṃ [T. 317b.] vinivārayituṃ na pāryate, kim aṅga punas tādṛśatvādhyavasāyaḥ? yathoktam -
{p. 157.1.}
children.translated_text: smoke-moments, since they are useful in the causal efficacy of making the throat smart, making the eyes water, blackening, and the like — how could they not be of such a nature? No, because that causal efficacy too, being differentiated in form by the difference of moments, does not have the nature of being 'of such a kind' — so the same fault applies there too. 'Then how is the designation of smoke universally applied in the world?' — because of the force of the determination of unity based on the arising of successive similar [moments], and because moments are not [practically] viable for ordinary usage. 'If there is similarity, how is there not being-of-such-a-kind?' — because what is similar is different from what is of such a kind. For thus: a <s>gavaya</s> (wild ox) is similar to a cow but not of the same kind, because only another cow is of the same kind as a cow. Even though in ultimate reality [it is] not of such a kind, how could the supposition of being-of-such-a-kind among those of dull minds be prevented? For thus: even the determination of reality — i.e., [the superimposition of identity] on what is not that — cannot be prevented for those of ordinary vision; how much less the determination of being-of-such-a-kind? As stated: {p. 157.1.}
'In a continuum of similar color and configuration, there arises in what is not that' |
'the cognition of that among people — how much more so within a single continuum?' ||

children.text:
iti |
  tattvacintakās tu tādṛśātādṛśakāraṇabhedāt tādṛśātādṛśatāṃ bhāvānāṃ anumanyante na tādṛśatām | tad yady atādṛśād api tādṛśo bhavet tadā tasya tajjanyaḥ svabhāva ity atadbhāvinaḥ sakṛd api tato bhāvo na syāt | amum evārthaṃ samarthayamāna āha --
children.translated_text: Thus. | But those who contemplate reality infer the being-of-such-a-kind and not-being-of-such-a-kind of entities from the difference of causes that are of such a kind and not of such a kind — not [merely] being-of-such-a-kind [from similarity]. Therefore, if what is of such a kind were to arise even from what is not of such a kind, then that essential nature would be produced by that [dissimilar cause] — and so, since it would not exist in the absence of that, not even once would it arise from that [fire-assemblage]. Establishing this very point, he says:
'With respect to each other' —

children.text: ityādi | kāraṇāpekṣayā hi janyasvabhāvaṃ kāryam, kāryāpekṣayā ca janakasvabhāvaṃ kāraṇam | yato hi kāraṇād yad bhavad dṛṣṭam tasya tajjanyasvabhāvaḥ, itarasya ca tajjanaka iti pratīyate | anyathā tasya tato bhāvāyogāt, itarasya ca tajjananāyogāt | yadi nāmaivaṃ tataḥ prakṛte kiṃ siddham? ity ata āha
children.translated_text: and so forth. For the effect is of the nature of being produced with respect to the cause, and the cause is of the nature of producing with respect to the effect. For of that which is observed to arise from a particular cause, the essential nature is 'produced by that,' and of the other [i.e., the cause], it is understood as 'the producer of that.' Otherwise, because of the impossibility of that [effect] arising from that [cause], and because of the impossibility of the other [cause] producing that [effect]. If so, then in the present case what is established? — to this he says:
'There' —
given this logical principle —
'if the smoke' —
of such a kind as the second and subsequent moment-instances, being of the same kind as the first [moment] produced by the fire-and-the-like assemblage —
'from the fire-and-the-like assemblage' —
determined as having the nature of producing that, from the causal aggregate of fire, fuel, and the like —
'from another' —
from the first smoke-moment produced by the fire-fuel-and-the-like assemblage — were to arise, then
'of that' —
of that smoke-nature which is of such a kind —
'the essential nature produced by that' —
produced by the fire-and-the-like assemblage —
'does not exist' —

children.text: kintu dhūmajanya eveti kṛtvā sakṛd api
children.translated_text: rather, it is produced by smoke alone — and hence, not even once
'from that' —
from the fire-and-the-like assemblage —
'would it arise.' —

children.text: | tādṛśasya hi [T. 318a.] svabhāvasyānyato bhāve tajjanyasvabhāvatā, nāgnyādijanyasvabhāvateti kutaḥ sakṛd api tato
children.translated_text: | For if the essential nature of such a kind arises from another, then it has the essential nature of being produced by that [other], not the essential nature of being produced by fire and the like — so how is even a single arising from that [fire]
tenable? Here the example is:
'like a different kind of thing' —

children.text:
iti | yathā hy arthāntaram[597]atajjanyābhimatam anyato bhavat na tajjanyasvabhāvaṃ nāgnyādisāmagrījanyasvabhāvam iti sakṛd api tato na bhavati tadvat tādṛśo dhūmo 'pīti tato bhavann anyādṛśa evāsāv iti gamyate |
 syānmatam -- agnyādisāmagryā 'sāv atajjanyasvabhāvo 'pi tādṛśo balāj janyate kas tasya tapasvino 'parādhaḥ? ity ata āha --
children.translated_text: thus. For just as a different kind of thing, which is regarded as not produced by that [fire], arising from something else, does not have the essential nature of being produced by that [fire], and not the essential nature of being produced by the fire-and-the-like assemblage — and so not even once does it arise from that — similarly, smoke that is of such a kind too [would be so]. Thus it is understood that [what] arises from that [other cause] is indeed of a different kind. | One might think: 'Even if it does not have the essential nature of being produced by that [fire], the fire-and-the-like assemblage forcibly produces it as being of such a kind — what is the fault of that poor [fire]?' To this he says:
'Nor even' —

children.text: na kevalaṃ svayam atajjanyasvabhāvatayā tato na bhavet, kintv agnyādisāmagry api taṃ tādṛśaṃ dhūmaṃ -- yādṛśo dvitīyādikṣaṇabhāvī {p. 158.1} -- na janayet | kutaḥ ? | atajjananasvabhāvatvāt | tādṛśasya hy anyato bhāve sa eva tajjananasvabhāvo nāgnyādisāmagrīti tajjananasvabhāvavikalā kathaṃ taṃ janayet ? | atrāpy udāharaṇam --
children.translated_text: not only would it, by virtue of not having the essential nature of being produced by that, not arise from that — but the fire-and-the-like assemblage too would not produce that smoke of such a kind — of the kind that exists as the second and subsequent moments. {p. 158.1} Why? Because of not having the essential nature of producing that. For if what is of such a kind arises from another, then that very [other] has the essential nature of producing it, not the fire-and-the-like assemblage. Being deficient in the essential nature of producing that, how would [the fire-assemblage] produce it? Here too the example is:
'like another assemblage' —

children.text: | yathā sāmagryantaram atajjananasvabhāvābhimataṃ [S. 151b.] na janayati tadvad agnyādisāmagry api | tathā hi -- sā ātmīyaṃ svabhāvam anusṛtyaiva pravarttate, tataḥ kuto 'sau sāmagrībalāj jāyeta ? |
children.translated_text: thus. Just as another assemblage, regarded as not having the essential nature of producing that, does not produce [it] — so too the fire-and-the-like assemblage. For thus: that [assemblage] operates following only its own essential nature — so how could that [smoke] arise by the force of the [wrong] assemblage?

body.translated_text: But [the opponent says:] of all —

body.text:
-nāṃ varṇakālīkaraṇādi- -- T.
[594] -hārayo- -- T.
[595] nivāritā- -- T.
[596] bhāvo na yu- -- T.
[597] aṅkurādyarthā- -- T.
body.translated_text:
-of blackening color and the like- — T.
[594] -usage-tenable- — T.
[595] prevented- — T.
[596] existence not ten- — T.
[597] sprout and other object- — T.
Section: 5. When produced by a cause of such-and-such and not-such-and-such a kind, the effect too is of such-and-such and not-such-and-such a kind

children.text: dhūmo dhūmajanyasvabhāvo[598]'pi yathā sa eva dhūma indhanajanyasvabhāvo 'gnijanyasvabhāvaś cobhayato [T. 318b.] bhavati | tathā tādṛśo 'pi dhūma ubhayasāmagrījanyasvabhāvatayobhayato bhaviṣyatīty ata āha --
children.translated_text: also has the essential nature of being produced by smoke — just as that very smoke has the essential nature of being produced by fuel and also the essential nature of being produced by fire, arising from both. Similarly, the smoke of such a kind too, by having the essential nature of being produced by both assemblages, will arise from both. To this he says:
'And not' —
not at all —
'of smoke' —
of that which is of such a kind —
'having the essential nature of being produced by that and not by that' —
produced by the fire-and-the-like assemblage and produced by smoke —
'is the essential nature tenable' —
consistent with reason. Why?
'Because of being of a single essential nature' —

children.text: | tādṛśasya dhūmarūpasya bhedābhāvāt | na hi tasya kālabhede 'pi tādṛgrūpatā bhidyate |bhede hy anyādṛśasyānyādṛśād bhāve vivādāyogāt | tasya yadi tādṛśātādṛśakāraṇajanyatā syāt tatas tādṛśātādṛśasvabhāvataiva syāt | tad eva darśayann āha --
children.translated_text: | Because of the absence of difference in what is of such a kind, namely the smoke-form. For even with temporal difference, its being-of-such-a-form does not differ. For if there were difference, the dispute about what is of a different kind arising from what is of a different kind would not be tenable. If it had the nature of being produced by causes of such-a-kind and not-such-a-kind, then it would indeed have essential natures of such-a-kind and not-such-a-kind. Showing precisely this, he says:
'Smoke and not-smoke' —

children.text:
ityādi | dhūmaśabdena yādṛśo 'gnyādisāmagrījanyas tādṛśaḥ svabhāvo 'bhipretaḥ, adhūmaśabdenānyādṛśakāraṇajanyo dhūmajanito
'nyadṛśaḥ | tayoś ca tādṛśātādṛśakāraṇajanyatayaiva tādṛśātādṛśasvabhāvatā 'vagantavyā vakṣyamāṇanītyā | tenāgnidhūmalakṣaṇāt
children.translated_text: and so forth. By the word 'smoke,' the essential nature of such a kind as is produced by the fire-and-the-like assemblage is intended; by the word 'not-smoke,' [the essential nature that is] of a different kind, produced by a cause of a different kind, produced by smoke. And their being of such-a-kind and not-such-a-kind is to be understood precisely from their being produced by causes of such-a-kind and not-such-a-kind, by the principle to be stated. Therefore, from the fire-smoke — having the essential nature of producing smoke and not-smoke —
'having the essential nature of producing smoke and not-smoke' —

having the essential nature of producing what is of such a kind and not of such a kind — its being of such-a-kind and not-such-a-kind would make it of the nature of smoke-and-not-smoke, i.e., of such-a-kind-and-not-such-a-kind. So how is it of such a kind only? How so? He says:

children.text: tādṛśātādṛśajananasvabhāvāt [S. 152a.] tādṛśātādṛśatayā 'sya bhavato dhūmādhūma[svabhāva]s tādṛśātādṛśasvabhāvaḥ syāt kutas tādṛśa eva? | kuta etat? ity āha --

children.translated_text: 'Of the essential natures of effects' —

children.text: ityādi | kāryāṇāṃ hi ye svabhāvāḥ parasparāsaṃbhavinaḥ te parasparavilakṣaṇakāraṇasāmagrīsvabhāvakṛtā na svābhāvikā ahetukatvaprasaṅgāt | [T. 319a.] tatas tādṛśātādṛśād bhavato dhūmasya
children.translated_text: and so forth. For the essential natures of effects, which are mutually impossible, are produced by the essential natures of mutually dissimilar causal assemblages — not inherent — because of the absurd consequence of being uncaused. [T. 319a.] Therefore, of the smoke that arises from what is of such-a-kind and not-such-a-kind,

children.text:
tādṛśātādṛśasvabhāvataiva syāt[600]|
  {p. 159.1.} syānmatam -- naiva tādṛśātādṛśasvabhāvatāyāṃ tādṛśātādṛśakāraṇāpekṣā, kāryāṇām utpattimātra eva
children.translated_text: the essential nature would be precisely of such-a-kind and not-such-a-kind. | {p. 159.1} One might think: there is no requirement of causes of such-a-kind and not-such-a-kind for the being-of-such-a-kind and not-such-a-kind [of effects], since effects require causes only for their mere arising —
to this he says:
'And if there is no requirement of causes' —
if for the being of such-a-kind and not-such-a-kind form there is no requirement of causes of such-a-kind and not-such-a-kind — the being-of-such-a-kind-and-not-such-a-kind would be —
'because of the absurd consequence of being uncaused.' —

children.text:
| na hi tādṛśātādṛśasvabhāvayor abhūtvā bhāvavyatirekeṇānyā kācidutpattiḥ yatra[602]tādṛśātādṛśasvabhāvakāraṇanirapekṣāṇām api tadapekṣā syāt | tasmād utpattiśabdena tādṛśātādṛśasvabhāvataivocyata iti | [S. 152b.] tatra kāraṇāpekṣopagame kathaṃ tādṛśātādṛśatāyāṃ kāraṇāpekṣā na syāt | tasmāt sāmagrīṇāṃ tādṛśātādṛśatvād eva kāryāṇāṃ tādṛśātādṛśasvabhāvavibhāga iti kuto 'nyādṛśāt tādṛśasambhavaḥ? iti |
  yat tūktaṃ `yathaiko dhūmo 'gnīndhanābhyāṃ vilakṣaṇābhyāṃ janyate tathaikalakṣaṇam api kāryaṃ vilakṣaṇād api sāmagryantarād bhaviṣyati' iti | tad ayuktam | yato nāsmābhir vilakṣaṇānāṃ janakatvaṃ vāryate janayanty eva parasparavilakṣaṇā api svahetupariṇāmopanidhidharmāṇas tadavasthāniyatāḥ tad ekaṃ kāryaṃ, tasya tu teṣāṃ ca parasparāpekṣayā [T. 319b.] janyajanakasvabhāvatāniyamāt tādṛśasya tādṛśād eva janmocyate nānyādṛśāt, tasyātajjananasvabhāvatvāt, tadabhāve 'py anyato bhavatas tadutpattiniyamābhāvāt | aniyame ca [S. 153a.] kāryakāraṇabhāvāyogāt | yadi tv agnir ivendhanopādānopakṛtas tadupādānopākṛtaṃ cendhanam iva tadavasthāniyatam atādṛśam api
children.translated_text: | For there is no arising other than the coming-into-being-from-not-having-been of the essential natures of such-a-kind and not-such-a-kind, for which those not requiring causes of such-a-kind-and-not-such-a-kind essential nature would [nonetheless] require that [arising]. Therefore, by the word 'arising,' the very being-of-such-a-kind-and-not-such-a-kind essential nature is denoted. Therein, if the requirement of causes [for arising] is accepted, how could there not be a requirement of causes for the being-of-such-a-kind-and-not-such-a-kind? Therefore, precisely because of the being-of-such-a-kind-and-not-such-a-kind of the assemblages, the division of effects into those of such-a-kind and not-such-a-kind essential nature [obtains] — so whence the possibility of what is of such a kind [arising] from what is of a different kind? | As for what was said — 'just as a single smoke is produced by fire and fuel, which are dissimilar, so too an effect of a single character will arise even from a dissimilar alternative assemblage' — that is untenable. For we do not deny the producer-status of dissimilar [causes]; indeed, mutually dissimilar causes having the property of the transformation of their own causes, restricted to that [particular] state, do produce that one effect. But because of the restriction of the produced-producer essential nature through the mutual reference of those [causes and effects], it is said that what is of such a kind arises from what is of such a kind only, not from what is of a different kind — because that [different kind] does not have the essential nature of producing it, and because in its absence, the restriction of the arising of that [effect] from something else [does not hold]. And without such restriction, the cause-effect relation would be untenable. But if, like fire assisted by fuel as material cause, and like fuel assisted by fire's material-cause contribution, something restricted to that state — even though not of such a kind —

children.text:
dhūmādikaṃ tādṛśaṃ[603]dhūmaṃ janayet pratyakṣānupalambhābhyāṃ ca tathā 'vagamyeta tadā 'gnyādivat so 'pi tajjananasvabhāvatāniyamāt tādṛśajanakaḥ kena nānumanyeta | tadabhāve[604]'pi
tu tādṛśasya bhāve tayor janyajanakasvabhāvatāniyamābhāvāt kutaḥ kāryakāraṇatety ahetutaiva tādṛśasyānyādṛśād bhavataḥ syāt | yata evaṃ
children.translated_text: like smoke and the like, were to produce smoke of such a kind, and if this were ascertained through perception and non-apprehension — then, like fire and the like, it too, because of the restriction of the essential nature of producing that, would be an acknowledged producer of what is of such a kind — who would not infer [it to be so]? But if what is of such a kind exists even in the absence of that [cause], then because of the absence of restriction of the produced-producer essential nature of those two, how could there be a cause-effect relation? — and so the being-of-such-a-kind of what arises from what is of a different kind would be without cause. Since it is so,
'therefore' —
that particular fire-fuel-and-the-like assemblage should be regarded —
'which' —
is the first —
smoke-producer,
'not another.' —
'That' —
first smoke —
'by the particular fire-and-the-like assemblage' —

children.text: janito nānya {p. 160.1} iti kṛtvā kāryakāraṇayor evaṃ yathoktena nyāyena janyajanakarūpasya svabhāvasya
children.translated_text: is produced, not by another — {p. 160.1} and therefore, because of the restriction of the essential nature of the produced and the producer — of cause and effect — by the principle as stated,

children.text: niyamād yādṛśaṃ yasya[605]karaṇam ekadā pratyakṣānupalambhābhyām evāvadhāritaṃ
children.translated_text: the production of a particular [effect] by a particular [cause], once ascertained through perception and non-apprehension —
'from what is of a different kind from that' —
from a cause of a different kind —
'the arising' —
of an effect of such a kind —
'does not occur' —

children.text:
anyādṛśasya eva na vāryata iti |
  tad evaṃ tādṛśātādṛśakāraṇakṛtakatvaṃ tādṛśātādṛśakāryasvabhāvasya pratipādyopasaṃharann āha --
children.translated_text: but [the arising] of something of a different kind is not denied. |
'Therefore' —

children.text: tasmāt yādṛśaṃ [T. 320a.] kāryaṃ yādṛśāt kāraṇāt dṛṣṭaṃ pratyakṣānupalambhābhyāṃ niścitam ekadā tat ta
children.translated_text: therefore, whatever effect is observed from whatever cause, ascertained once through perception and non-apprehension — that
'does not deviate' —
what is of such a kind does not arise from what is of a different kind. Since this is so,
'by that' —
by that reason —
when the cause-effect relation is established,
'of what is of such a kind' —
of the effect —

children.text: tādṛśam eva kāraṇam iti niścaye sati yathoditena nyāyena
children.translated_text: when there is the determination that the cause is precisely of such a kind — by the principle as stated,
'the pervasion of the effect by the cause' —
in the form of co-presence and co-absence (<s>anvayavyatireka</s>) — is established.
'There is no arising from what is of a different kind' — thus

children.text: dṛṣṭakāraṇavijātīyāt kāraṇād anyādṛśān notpattir ity amum artham apratipadyamānaḥ kāryasya {na
children.translated_text: not understanding the meaning that 'there is no arising from a cause of a different kind from the observed cause' — thinking that the meaning intended here is 'there is no arising of the effect from a cause of a different kind at all,' the opponent, raising an objection, says:
(? see p. xxxv)

children.text: } vijātīyāt kāraṇān notpattir ity ayam atrārtho 'bhimata iti manvānaḥ paraś codayann āha --

children.translated_text: 'But' —
'of its own accord' —
'even from a cause of a different kind' —
from a cause —
'some' —
effect —
'is observed to arise' —

children.text: tat [S. 154a.] kathaṃ na vijātīyād utpattir ity asya na dṛṣṭavirodhaḥ syāt | kathaṃ yathā[606]ity āha --
children.translated_text: so how would 'there is no arising from what is of a different kind' not be contradicted by observation? How so? He says:
'For example, from cow dung and the like' —
by the word 'and the like,' from buffalo horn, moonstone (<s>candrakānta</s>), and the like —
'lotus root (<s>śālūka</s>) and the like' —

children.text: ādigrahaṇāc charodakādi | tathā hi -- gomayāc chālūkasya bhāvaḥ śṛṅgāc charasya candrakāntādapām | na ca gomayādikaṃ śālūkāder na vijātīyam tat kim ucyate na vijātīyād utpattiḥ iti | siddhāntavādī parasya bhrāṃtatāṃ darśayann āha --
children.translated_text: By the word 'and the like,' arrow-water (<s>śarodaka</s>) and the like. For thus: from cow-dung arises a lotus-root (<s>śālūka</s>); from a horn [arises] an arrow (<s>śara</s>); from moonstone [arises] water. And cow-dung and the like is not of a different kind from the lotus-root and the like — then why is it said that 'there is no arising from what is of a different kind'? The proponent (<s>siddhāntavādin</s>), showing the confusion of the opponent, says —
'There is no arising from what is of a different kind' —

children.text:
iti | yato hi kāraṇād yad bhavad dṛṣṭaṃ tat tato 'nyādṛśyān na bhavati ity ayam
atrārtho vivakṣitaḥ, na tu kāryavijātīyād iti | na ca tasya[607]vyabhicāraḥ | tad āha --
children.translated_text: thus. For the intended meaning here is: that which is observed to arise from a certain cause does not arise from another [cause] different from that — but not [that it does not arise] from what is different from the effect. And there is no deviation of that [principle]. To that he says —
'For precisely that kind' —
the form of cow-dung and the like,
'of such' —
of lotus-roots and the like,
'is the initial cause' —
of the series of lotus-roots and the like,

children.text: ya ādiḥ prathama ārambhakṣaṇaḥ tasya kāraṇam iti kṛtvā śālūkādipabandhasyāder
children.translated_text: the 'initial' means the first moment of origination — thus it is the cause of the beginning of the series of lotus-roots and the like,

children.text: na {p. 161a.} kāraṇabhedo 'nyādṛśād utpattiḥ [T. 320b.] sarvasya tadā ''der ggomayādinimittatvāt | yadā tu prabandhena pūrvakṣaṇanimittānām uttarottarakṣaṇānāṃ santānenotpattilakṣaṇā vṛttir bhavati śarasya tadā
children.translated_text: there is no difference of cause, i.e., no arising from something different, since at that [initial] time everything has cow-dung and the like as its cause. But when through the series, there is the operation characterized by the arising of successive moments caused by the preceding moments in the continuum of the arrow, then

children.text: śarād bhāvaḥ[609]| tad evaṃ yasya prabandhādeḥ śṛṅgādibhyo bhāvo na tādṛśasya śarādeḥ yasya ca [S. 154b.] śarādes taduttarottarasya bhāvo na tādṛśasya
children.translated_text: there is arising from the arrow. Thus, of the series and the like whose arising is from horns and the like, the arrow and the like is not of that kind [as the initial series]; and of the arrow and the like whose arising is of each successive [moment], the horn and the like is not of that kind —

children.text:
śṛṅgāder iti[610]na dṛṣṭakāraṇavijātīyāt kāraṇāt tādṛśasya sambhava iti kāryahetor anvayavyatirekaniścayaḥ |
  yadā 'pi śālūkādayaḥ pūrvapūrvasvajātinibandhanā[611]anādisantānapravṛttā iṣyante tadā 'pi gomayādibhyaḥ keṣāñcidbhāve 'pi tādṛśatvābhāvān na vyabhicāra iti darśayann āha --
children.translated_text: thus, from a cause different from the observed cause, there is no arising of something of that kind — and so the ascertainment of positive and negative concomitance (<s>anvayavyatireka</s>) of the cause of the effect [is established]. Even when lotus-roots and the like are accepted as having a beginningless continuum grounded in their own kind in each preceding [moment], showing that there is no deviation even though some [lotus-roots] arise from cow-dung and the like, because they are not of that kind, he says —
'And there is' —

children.text: ityādi | yasya śālūkasantānasya gomayādi kāraṇaṃ yasya ca sarvadā svajātinimittatvaṃ tayor gomayetarajanmanoḥ śālūkayor asty eva svabhāvabhedaḥ parasparam anyādṛśatvaṃ
children.translated_text: and so forth. Of the lotus-root continuum whose cause is cow-dung and the like, and of that [lotus-root] whose cause is always its own kind — between these two lotus-roots, one born from cow-dung and the other born otherwise, there is indeed a difference of essential nature, a mutual otherness,
'even though there is no difference of form' —

children.text: sati | tulyākāratve sati katham anyādṛśatvam? iti cet,[h15]āha --
children.translated_text: even when there is similarity of appearance. If [you ask:] 'when there is similarity of appearance, how can there be otherness?' — he says —
'For not' —
and so forth. Because the mere similarity of appearance of entities is not
'the ground of their reality' —

children.text: tādṛśatve nimittam yato gomayetarajanmanoḥ śālūkayor ākārasāmyāt tādṛśatvam eva syān na jātibhedaḥ | kuta etat ? ity āha --
children.translated_text: the ground of being of that kind — such that, of lotus-roots born from cow-dung and born otherwise, there would be sameness of kind rather than a difference of kind, merely from the similarity of appearance. Whence is this [known]? He says —
'Even of those with non-different appearance' —

children.text:
ityādi | yeṣām api hi samānākāratā [S. 155a.] keṣāñcid bhāvānāṃ teṣām api yata ākārād anyato [T. 321a.] viśeṣāj jātibhedo dṛśyate tato nākārasāmyam eva jāty ekatve nibandhanam | tathā hi -- ākārasāmye
'pi kvacit puṣpād bhedo dṛśyate nīletarakusumayor iva sūryayoḥ, kvacit phalāt vandhyetarayor iva karkkoṭakyoḥ, kvacid rasād van{dh}yetarayor iva trapuṣayoḥ, kvacid gandhād vṛkṣetaraprabhavayor iva campakayoḥ, kvacit prabhāvāt sparśopayogasraṃsinyor iva haritakyor iti | tasmād ākārasāmyanibandhanaṃ yady api `tad evedam' iti pratyabhijñānaṃ sajātīyatāṃ gomayetarajanmanoḥ śālūkayor upakalpayati tathāpi vilakṣaṇasāmagrījanyatayā tayor jātibheda evāvagantavyaḥ, naikajātitā | tata eva pratyabhijñānasya bhrāntatayā tatkalpitasya tādṛśatvasyālīkatvāt |
children.translated_text: and so forth. For even those entities that have similar appearance — even among some of those, since a difference of kind is seen from some other distinguishing feature beyond appearance, therefore similarity of appearance alone is not the ground of unity of kind. For thus: even when there is similarity of appearance, difference is seen sometimes from the flower — as with a blue [lotus] and another flower resembling the sun; sometimes from the fruit — as with a barren and a fertile <s>karkoṭakī</s> (bitter melon); sometimes from the taste — as with a barren and a fertile <s>trapuṣa</s> (cucumber); sometimes from the smell — as with [campaka flowers] produced from a tree and produced otherwise; sometimes from the potency — as with two yellow myrobalan (<s>haritakī</s>) fruits, one having a loosening effect on touch and the other not. Therefore, even though the recognition [expressed as] 'this is the very same' — grounded in similarity of appearance — attributes same-kindness to lotus-roots born from cow-dung and born otherwise, nevertheless, because they are produced from a different aggregate, a difference of kind alone is to be understood, not unity of kind. Precisely because of the erroneousness of the recognition, the sameness attributed by it is false.
