By this, he states that even the bare spot is of the nature of <s>prasajyapratiṣedha</s>. 'How can a positive entity have a void form as its essential nature? — because of contradiction.' No, because even that [positive entity] is of a void form with respect to another's form. For just as <s>prasajyapratiṣedha</s>, not involving contact with another entity, appearing in a void concept, is of a void form with respect to the thing to be negated due to the absence of that form — so too the existence of another, having a form unmixed with the thing to be negated [is of that void form]. So how could its void form with respect to the thing to be negated be contradicted? In its own form,

children.text:
hy ayam atuccharūpaḥ[660]syān na pararūpeṇa,
anyathā katham asyānyabhāvatvaṃ parasya vā tatrābhāvaḥ syāt? | yo hi yadabhāvarūpo na bhavati sa evāsau bhavati, tatsvarūpavat | tataḥ sarvasya jagataḥ parasparātmatāprasaṅgaḥ | tasmāt sarvabhāvāḥ pararūpeṇa niḥsvabhāvaḥ svarūpeṇa rūpavattve 'pīty anavadyam |
  kas tarhi prasajyapratiṣedhāt paryudāsasya bhedaḥ? | na kaścit, kevalam anapekṣitarūpāntaram abhāvamātraṃ prasajyapratiṣedha iti loke kathyate | rūpāntaraṃ tu pararūpaśūnyaṃ paryudāsa iti | na tu rūpāntaraṃ pararūpatucchātmakaṃ na bhavati | anubhūyata eva ca rūpāntaraṃ {p. 180.1} tadrūpaśūnyatayā, kathaṃ tasya prasajyapratiṣedhātmatā na syāt pararūpeṇa? | sāmarthyāt tatas[661]tatpratītir[662]iti cet; na akāraṇapratītau[663]sāmarthyāsambhavāt[664]| tādātmyābhāve hi prasajyapratiṣedhasya paryudastāt [S. 171b.] pratītau tatkāraṇatve sati syāt pratipattiḥ nānyathā | tasya tadanyāsaṃsṛṣṭarūpasya yat tattvaṃ tasya pratiṣedhyatuccharūpatāyā vyavasthāpakaṃ pramāṇaṃ pratyakṣarūpam tat eva -- na taduttarakālabhāvino [T. 335a.] `nāstīha ghaṭaḥ` iti vikalpāt, tasya gṛhītagrāhitayā smṛtitvenāpramāṇatvāt -- anyasya ghaṭādes tatrāsato vyavacchedasyābhāvasya siddhes tadabhāvātmakasyaiva
pradeśasya tena grahaṇāt | dvividho hy ayaṃ pradeśo ghaṭāsaṃsṛṣṭarūpas tadvyāvṛttarūpatayā tato 'nyo ghaṭavān api, kevalaś ca ghaṭaṃ prati apratipannādhārabhāvaḥ[665]|
children.translated_text: this would be of a non-void form, not in another's form — otherwise, how could it be the existence of another, or how could the other be absent there? For that which does not have the form of the absence of something is that very thing, like [having] the form of that [thing]. And so there would be the absurd consequence of everything in the world being mutually identical. Therefore, all entities are without essential nature in another's form, even while possessing form in their own form — and this is faultless. | What then is the difference between <s>prasajyapratiṣedha</s> (non-implicative negation) and <s>paryudāsa</s> (implicative negation)? There is none whatsoever. It is merely that what is the mere absence [of something], without reference to another form, is called <s>prasajyapratiṣedha</s> in the world. But another form, empty of another's form, is called <s>paryudāsa</s>. But it is not the case that another form, having a void nature with respect to another's form, does not exist. And since another form is indeed experienced as being empty of that form — how could it not have the nature of <s>prasajyapratiṣedha</s> in another's form? | 'Because of the capacity, from that, the cognition of that [arises]' — if so, no, because the capacity is impossible for the cognition of what is not a cause. For only when there is identity, and when the <s>prasajyapratiṣedha</s> is the cause of the cognition distinguished from the <s>paryudāsa</s> — [only] then would there be the apprehension [of one from the other], not otherwise. That reality of that [existence of another], which has a form unmixed with that, is also what establishes its void-form-ness with respect to the thing to be negated — and the <s>pramāṇa</s> for this is of the nature of perception — not from the subsequent conceptual cognition 'there is no pot here,' because that [concept], being of the nature of memory since it grasps what has already been grasped, is not a <s>pramāṇa</s> — because of the establishment of the exclusion, i.e., the absence, of the other, such as a pot, which does not exist there — because the spot, which is itself of the nature of the absence of that, is grasped by that [perception]. For this spot is twofold: having a form unmixed with the pot, and also being different from that [pot] by virtue of having a form excluded from it, and [the spot] that possesses the pot too, and also the mere [spot], in which the substratum-relation to the pot is not apprehended.

children.text:
tasya tadvivekena[666]pratyakṣeṇa grahaṇe ghaṭād anyatvaṃ ghaṭavirahaś ca gṛhīta eva bhavatīti na vastvasaṃkarasiddhyarthaṃ, `ihedaṃ nāsti` ity evam arthaṃ ca pramāṇāntaram anveṣaṇīyam | vistaraś caitad uttaratra vakṣyata iti āstāṃ tāvat | yataś cānyabhāvasiddhyaiva tadabhāva uktena nyāyena siddhyati tato nānyabhāvaḥ pratiṣedhyābhāvasya liṅgam |
  dvitīyaṃ kāraṇaṃ vyācakṣāṇa āha --
children.translated_text: When that [spot] is grasped by perception as distinct from that [pot], its otherness from the pot and its being devoid of the pot are already grasped — so there is no need to seek another <s>pramāṇa</s> for establishing the non-intermixture of real entities and for the meaning 'this is not here.' And the elaboration of this will be stated later — so let this suffice for now. And since, by the very establishment of the existence of another, the absence of that is established by the stated principle — therefore the existence of another is not an inferential mark for the absence of the thing to be negated. | Explaining the second reason, he says:
'And because of the absence of a relation' —

children.text: iti | anyabhāvatadabhāvayor na [S. 172a.] kaścit sambandho 'sti tataḥ kuto liṅgaliṅgibhāvaḥ iti | etac ca kadocyate? | yadā tadabhāvarūpatā
children.translated_text: thus. Between the existence of another and the absence of that, there is no relation whatsoever — so whence the relation of inferential mark and mark-bearer? And when is this said? When the nature of the existence of another as being the absence of that

children.text: 'nyabhāvasya parānabhyupagatā[667]'pekṣyate | tadanyabhāvāt[668]pṛthag eva tadabhāvas tuccharūpa iṣyate paraiḥ | anyathoktena nyāyenānyabhāvasyaiva tadabhāvarūpatve tādātmyāt kathaṃ sambandhābhāvaḥ? | pratyakṣasiddhatā ca[669]tadaiva[670], na pakṣāntareṇa[671]abhihitā |
children.translated_text: is not accepted by the opponent, is in question. For the opponent accepts the absence of that as separately established from the existence of another, of a void form. Otherwise, by the stated principle, when the existence of another itself has the nature of the absence of that, due to identity (<s>tādātmya</s>), how could there be an absence of relation? And the establishment through perception too has been stated precisely in that [context], not in the alternative position.
'And that, of that' —
and so forth, is an explanation of that very [point] through the method of exclusion (<s>vyatireka</s>).
'Co-inherence in a single object' (<s>ekārthasamavāya</s>) —

children.text:
iti[672][T. 335b.] paradarśanenoktaṃ | pareṣāṃ hinaiyāyikādīnāṃvyatiriktāv eva kṛtakānityatvākhyau dharmāv ekasminn eva dharmiṇi samavetāv iti kṛtakasyānityatvenaikasminn arthe dharmiṇi samavāyaḥ sambandhaḥ dhūmasya veti {p. 181.1} sambandha evodāharaṇāntaram | atraikarthasamavāya iti saṃyogaḥ sa eva samavāyaśabdenoktaḥ
| saṃyogasamavāyayoḥ kalpitatvād bhedena vyapadeśe 'nādarāt | pareṣāṃ tv agnidhūmau svāvayaveṣv eva samavetāv iti na tayor ekārthasamavāya ādhārādheyabhāvo veti dhūmasyāgner upari darśanāl laukikaḥ sambandha uktaḥ |
children.translated_text: thus, is stated in the opponent's doctrine. For the opponents — <s>Naiyāyikas</s> and the like — [hold that] the two properties called 'produced' and 'impermanent' are indeed distinct, yet inhere in one and the same property-bearer — thus the co-inherence (<s>samavāya</s>), i.e., the relation, of the produced with impermanence in one and the same object, the property-bearer, or [the relation] of smoke [with fire] — is another example of relation. Here, 'co-inherence in a single object' means conjunction (<s>saṃyoga</s>) — that very thing is denoted by the word <s>samavāya</s>,
'Or the relation of product and producer' —

children.text:
iti pāramārthikaḥ sambandho 'bhihitaḥ, paramārthato 'gner janakatvāt itarasya ca janyatvād iti |
  nanu ceśvarasenena saha vicāraḥ prakrāntaḥ tat kim itinaiyāyikābhimatasyāpi sambandhasyānyabhāvatadabhāvayor abhāva ucyate | satyam, [S. 172b.] prasaṅgena tu tanmatasyāpi niṣedhārtham uktam | pūrvaṃ hy anyabhāvagrāhipratyakṣasiddhatvāt pratiṣedhyābhāvasya na tadarthaṃ pratyakṣāntaraṃ `nāstīha ghaṭaḥ` ity evamākāraṃ kalpanīyam iti prasaṅgataḥ kathitam | adhunā tu prasaṅgād idam ucyate -- yadānyabhāvagrāhipratyakṣasiddho 'yaṃ tadabhāvo na bhavati tadā pratyakṣāntaraṃ `nāsti iha ghaṭaḥ` ity evam ākaraṃ viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāvalakṣaṇāt
children.translated_text: Thus the ultimate relation has been stated — because in ultimate reality fire has the nature of being a producer, and the other [smoke] has the nature of being produced. But the investigation was undertaken with <s>Īśvarasena</s>, so why is the absence of the relation accepted by the <s>Naiyāyika</s> too — of other-existence and its absence — stated? True, but it is stated incidentally for the purpose of negating that [Naiyāyika] view as well. For previously, since the absence of the negated [entity] is established through perception that grasps other-existence, it was stated incidentally that another perception of the form 'there is no pot here' need not be postulated for that purpose. But now this is stated incidentally: when this absence of that [entity] is not established through perception that grasps other-existence, then another perception of the form 'there is no pot here' is accepted by you [the Naiyāyika] on the basis of a contact characterized by the relation of qualifier and qualified —

children.text:
sannikarṣād iṣṭaṃ bhavatā[673]| na cāsati sambandhe 'nyabhāvatadabhāvayor viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāvo yuktaḥ, atiprasaṅgāt | tataḥ [T. 336a.] kutas tallakṣaṇāt sannikarṣāt tadabhāve[674]pratyakṣaṃ bhaved iti |
  evaṃ sambandhasvarūpam ākhyāya tasyehāsambhavam āha --
children.translated_text: and when there is no relation between other-existence and its absence, the relation of qualifier and qualified is not tenable, because of over-extension. Therefore, how could there be perception of that absence from a contact characterized by that [qualifier-qualified relation]? Having thus explained the nature of the relation, he states its impossibility here —
'Not so' —

children.text: , yathā kṛtakatvānityatvayor agnidhūmayor vaikārthasamavāyādilakṣaṇaḥ sambandho naivaṃ kaścid bhāvābhāvayoḥ sambandho yena
children.translated_text: just as the relation characterized by same-object inherence (<s>ekārthasamavāya</s>) and the like obtains between being-produced and impermanence, and between fire and smoke — no such relation of any kind obtains between an existent and a non-existent, by which
'of this' —

children.text: tadabhāvasyānyabhāvaḥ sādhanaṃ syāt | yāv ekatrārthe dharmirūpe pravarttete tayor ekārthasamavāyo bhavati | anyabhāvaś ca pradeśākhyaḥ svāvayaveṣu yeṣu varttate na tatra ghaṭābhāvaḥ | evaṃ hi pradeśāvayaveṣu ghaṭo nāstīti syāt na pradeśe | na cāsya pradeśavayavair ārambhaḥ | te hi dravyātmāno dravyāntaram evārambhante | na ca ghaṭābhāvo dravyam | navaiva hi dravyāṇīṣyante | na ca kriyāvadādikaṃ dravyalakṣaṇaṃ [S. 173a.] tatrāsti | na ca guṇarūpatayā tatra varttate | caturviśatir eva hi {p. 182.1} guṇā iṣyante | na cāyaṃ teṣām anyatamaḥ | nāpi karmarūpatayapañcasu karmasvanantarbhāvāt[675]tallakṣaṇavirahāc ca |
children.translated_text: its absence could be the means of establishing other-existence. For the same-object inherence obtains between two [things] that operate in a single object having the form of the property-bearer. And other-existence, called 'location' (<s>pradeśa</s>), subsists in its own parts — in those, the absence of a pot does not [subsist]. For thus it would follow that the pot is absent in the parts of the location, not in the location [itself]. And this [absence] is not produced by the parts of the location. For they, being of the nature of substance, produce only another substance. And the absence of a pot is not a substance. For only nine substances are accepted. And the defining characteristic of substance — such as possessing action and the like — is not present in it [absence]. Nor does it subsist there in the form of a quality. For only twenty-four qualities are accepted. And this [absence] is not one of them. Nor in the form of action — because it is not included among the five actions, and because it lacks their defining characteristic.
'[That which subsists] in a single substance' —
<s>Vaiśeṣikasūtra</s> I.1.15

children.text:
ity ādikaṃ
hi tallakṣaṇam | na caitad abhāve sambhavatīti | nāpi sāmānyādirūpatayā, tadrūpavirahād eva | nāpy anyabhāvatadabhāvayoḥ saṃyogo 'gnidhūmayor iva, dravyayor eva tadabhyupagamāt | na ca tadabhāvo dravyam ity uktam | nāpy ādhāra(rā)dheyabhāvo, yataḥ so 'pi saṃyoganimitta ucyate `iha kuṇḍe badarāṇi` iti | samavāyanimitto vā, `iha tantuṣu [T. 336b.] paṭaḥ` iti | na cābhāvasyādravyātmanaḥ saṃyogaḥ samasti[676]| nāpi samavāyaḥ, pañcānām eva hi dravyādīnāṃ padārthānāṃ samavāyitvam iṣyate; na cābhāvaḥ pañcasv antarbhavatīti | na ca tadātmānupakāre saty ādhāravyapadeśaḥ sambhavati | upakāre vā janyajanakabhāvaḥ | na ca tadabhāvo janyaḥ; kāryatāprasaṅgāt | kāryatā cāsyāsambhavinī[677], [S. 173b.] yataḥ svakāraṇasamavāyaḥ, sattāsamavāyo vā kāryatocyate bhavadbhiḥ | anyabhāvas tu pradeśākhyo 'sya na kāraṇam, trayāṇām eva hi dravyaguṇakarmaṇāṃ dravyaṃ kāraṇam iṣṭam | na cābhāvo
dravyādilakṣaṇaḥ iti | sattāsamavāye 'pi satpratyayaviṣayatā tadabhāvasya syāt, nābhāvapratyayaviṣayatā | pradeśābhāve 'pi ca ghaṭābhāvasambhavāt kutas tatkāryatā | na cāsya prativiṣayaṃ bhedaḥ, ekākārajñānaviṣayatvāt | sambandhibhedād bhede vā sāmānyādiṣv api tatprasaṅgaḥ | samavāyopy asyānantaram eva nirasta iti kutaḥ svakāraṇasattāsamavāyarūpā kāryatā tadabhāvasya syāt? | etena janyajanakabhāvaḥ pratyuktaḥ | tataḥ sarvathā sambandhābhāvān nānyabhāvaḥ tadabhāvasya sādhanam iti |
  paraḥ sambandhāntaraṃ darśayann āha --
children.translated_text: and so forth — for that is its defining characteristic. And this is not possible in the case of absence. Nor [does it subsist] in the form of a universal (<s>sāmānya</s>) and the like, because of the absence of that form. Nor is there conjunction (<s>saṃyoga</s>) between other-existence and its absence, as between fire and smoke — because conjunction is accepted only between substances. And the absence of that [pot] is not a substance, as stated. Nor is there a container-contained relation (<s>ādhārādheyabhāva</s>), because that too is said to be caused by conjunction — as in 'here in the pot are the jujube fruits.' Or caused by inherence (<s>samavāya</s>) — as in 'here in the threads is the cloth.' And for absence, which is not of the nature of substance, there is no conjunction at all. Nor is there inherence, for inherence is accepted as obtaining only among the five categories beginning with substance; and absence is not included among the five. And without assistance to it from that [container], the designation of 'container' is not possible. And if there were assistance, there would be a producer-produced relation. But that absence is not produced, because of the absurd consequence of being an effect. And its being an effect is impossible, because inherence in one's own cause, or inherence of existence (<s>sattā</s>), is what you [Naiyāyikas] call being an effect. But other-existence, called 'location,' is not its cause, for only substance is accepted as the cause of the three — substance, quality, and action. And absence does not have the characteristics of substance and the like. And even in the case of inherence of existence, the absence of that [pot] would be an object of the cognition 'existent,' not an object of the cognition 'absent.' And because the absence of a pot is possible even when the location is absent — whence would that [absence] have the status of being its effect? And there is no differentiation of this [absence] relative to each object, because it is the object of a cognition of a single form. And if there were differentiation due to difference of the relatum, the same consequence would apply to universals and the like. And inherence too has been just now refuted — so how could the absence of that [pot] have the status of being an effect, in the form of inherence in one's own cause or [inherence of] existence? By this, the producer-produced relation is also answered. Therefore, because of the absence of any relation whatsoever, other-existence is not the means of establishing its absence.
The opponent, showing another relation, says: 'There is, with respect to the object' —

children.text: ty ādi | yathā hi artho viṣayaḥ śabdo viṣayīti tayor viṣayaviṣayibhāvaḥ sambandhaḥ, [S. 174a.] evam anyabhāvatadabhāvayor viṣayaviṣayibhāvaḥ sambandho bhaviṣyati [T. 337a.] pradeśākhyenānyabhāvena ghaṭābhāvasya pratyāyanād iti pūrvapakṣāśaṅkā | śabdārthayoḥ sambandhaḥ {p. 183.1} syād ity abhisambandhaḥ | kiṃ rūpaḥ? |
children.translated_text: and so forth. Just as an object is the <s>viṣaya</s> (referent) and a word is the <s>viṣayin</s> (that which has a referent), and their <s>viṣayaviṣayibhāva</s> (referent-possessor relation) is the relation — so there will be a referent-possessor relation between other-existence and its absence, because the absence of a pot is made known by other-existence called 'location' — this is the objection of the <s>pūrvapakṣin</s>. The relation between word and meaning should be — that is the connection. Of what kind?
'Characterized as cause and effect' —

children.text: | kathaṃ punar arthakāryatā śabdasya? | tatpratipādanābhiprāye sati arthapratipādanavivakṣāyāṃ satyāṃ tatprayogāc chabdoccāraṇāt | tenārthena vivakṣāviparivarttinā śabdasya kāryakāraṇalakṣaṇaḥ sambandhaḥ syāt | yady api ca śabdārthayoḥ buddhiparikalpitasāmānyarūpatā tathāpy arthapratibhāsinyā vivakṣayā śabdasāmānyotprekṣānibandhanasya śabdasvalakṣaṇasyotthāpanāt tanmukhena kāryakāraṇabhāva ucyate |
children.translated_text: How then is the meaning the effect of the word? When there is the intention to convey that [meaning] — when there is the desire to communicate the meaning — from the employment of that, i.e., from the utterance of the word. So, between the word and the meaning that varies with the desire to express — there would be a relation characterized as cause and effect. And even though word and meaning have a universalized form constructed by the intellect, nevertheless, since the particular instance of the word — which is grounded in the projection of the word-universal — is produced through the desire to express that manifests the meaning, the cause-effect relation is stated through that medium.
'Or characterized by invariable co-occurrence (<s>avinābhāva</s>)' —

children.text: iti paraprasiddhyocyate | paro hy avinābhāvalakṣaṇaḥ śabdārthayoḥ sambandha iti vyavaharati | tataḥ sambandhanibandhanaḥ pratipādyapratipādakarūpo[678]viṣayaviṣayibhāvo yuktaḥ | tadabhāvānyabhāvayor apy evaṃ bhaviṣyatīti cet, āha --
children.translated_text: this is stated according to the opponent's accepted [view]. For the opponent speaks of the relation between word and meaning as characterized by invariable co-occurrence. Therefore, the referent-possessor relation in the form of what-is-to-be-communicated and what-communicates, grounded in the relation, is tenable. If [one says:] 'The same will obtain between absence-of-that and other-existence' — he says —
'And this' —
of the kind just stated,
'here' —
between absence-of-that and other-existence,
'is not possible.' —

children.text:
| na hi ghaṭābhāvapratipādanābhiprāye [S. 174b.] sati anyabhāvasya pradeśalakṣaṇasya prayogo[679]niṣpattir bhavati, ghaṭābhāvapratipādanābhiprāyāt prāg api pradeśasya svahetubhya eva niṣpatteḥ | saty api tadabhiprāye 'nyabhāvasyābhāvāc ca | tataś ca kathaṃ tayoḥ kāryakāraṇabhāvaḥ? taddvārako 'vinābhāvo vā syāt? yato [T. 337b.] viṣayaviṣayibhāvaḥ kalpyeta |
  syān matam -- yathā śabdārthayoḥ sādhyasādhanabhāvanimitto viṣayaviṣayibhāvaḥ tathā anyabhāvatadabhāvayor api ity etāvanmātreṇa śabdārthayor dṛṣṭāntatety ata āha --
children.translated_text: For when there is the intention to communicate the absence of a pot, it is not the case that other-existence, characterized as location, comes into being — since even before the intention to communicate the absence of a pot, the location comes into being from its own causes alone. And also because of the absence of other-existence even when that intention obtains. Therefore, how could there be a cause-effect relation between those two? Or an invariable co-occurrence mediated by that? — such that a referent-possessor relation could be postulated. One might think: just as between word and meaning there is a referent-possessor relation caused by the relation of what-is-to-be-proved and what-proves, so too between other-existence and its absence — and to just that extent, word and meaning serve as the example — to this he says —
'For when established' —

children.text: ityādi | śabdārthayor hi kāryakāraṇabhāvanibandhanaḥ sādhyasādhanabhāvaḥ anyathā 'rthāntaratve tadayogāt tathehāpi yadi tadabhāvānyabhāvayoḥ sādhyasādhanabhāvaḥ sidhyet tadā tanmukhena sādhyasādhanabhāvadvāreṇa viṣayaviṣayibhāvaḥ syāt | yāvatā sa eva sādhyasādhanabhāvo 'sati sambandhe
children.translated_text: and so forth. For between word and meaning, the relation of what-is-to-be-proved and what-proves is grounded in the cause-effect relation — otherwise, if they were different things, that [relation] would not obtain. Likewise here too, if the relation of what-is-to-be-proved and what-proves between absence-of-that and other-existence were established, then through that medium — through the relation of what-is-to-be-proved and what-proves — there would be a referent-possessor relation. But that very relation of what-is-to-be-proved and what-proves, in the absence of a relation

children.text:
kāryakāraṇabhāvādike na sidhyati[680], sarvasya sādhyasādhanāprasakteḥ |
  katham indriyaṃ svaviṣayasiddhinibandhanam iti cet; parasparopasarppaṇādyāśrayāt pratyayaviśeṣād indriyaviṣayayor ekavijñānotpādanayor {p. 184.1} udayāt tathā vyapadeśaḥ, naivam iha, anyabhāvatadabhāvayos tadayogāt | liṅgaliṅgibhāvalakṣaṇasya [S. 175a.] ca sādhyasādhanabhāvasya prakṛtatvāt, tasya ca sambandham antareṇāyogāt |
  naiva sambandhāntaranibandhano 'nyabhāvatadabhāvayoḥ sādhyasādhanabhāvo 'pi tu viṣayaviṣayibhāvanimitta eveti cet; āha --
children.translated_text: characterized by cause-effect and the like, is not established — because everything would absurdly be the prover of everything [else]. 'But how is the sense-faculty the ground of establishing its own object?' — Because, from the particular condition based on mutual approach and the like, there is the arising of both the sense-faculty and the object as producing a single cognition — therefore that designation [of object and possessor-of-object]. It is not so here, because that [relation] is untenable between other-existence and absence-of-that. And because the relation of what-is-to-be-proved and what-proves, characterized as the mark (<s>liṅga</s>) and what-is-marked (<s>liṅgin</s>), is what is under discussion — and because that is untenable without a relation. If [one says:] the relation of what-is-to-be-proved and what-proves between other-existence and absence-of-that is not grounded in another relation, but is caused precisely by the referent-possessor relation — he says —
'Otherwise' —

children.text: yadi [T. 338a.] sambandhāntaraṃ neṣyate kin tu viṣayaviṣayibhāvāt sādhyasādhanabhāvaḥ tasmāc ca viṣayaviṣayibhāvaḥ, tata itaretarāśrayam idaṃ syāt | tathā caikāsiddhau dvayor apy asiddhir bhaved iti | kiñcānyabhāvāc ca liṅgabhūtād abhāvasya liṅginaḥ siddhāv anumitāv
children.translated_text: if another relation is not accepted, but rather the relation of what-is-to-be-proved and what-proves [is derived] from the referent-possessor relation, and the referent-possessor relation from that [prover-proved relation] — then there would be mutual dependence (<s>itaretarāśraya</s>). And thus, when one is unestablished, both would be unestablished. Moreover, when the inference is desired — in which absence, the thing-marked, is established from other-existence, the mark —

children.text:
iṣyamāṇāyāṃ asamudāyaś[681]ca sādhyaḥ syāt, anyabhāvena tadabhāvasya kevalasyaiva sādhanāt na kevalasambandhābhāvāt sādhyasādhanabhāvāyogaḥ | samudāyaś ca viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāvāpanno dharmadharmilakṣaṇaḥ sādhyo ya iṣṭas tadabhāvadoṣaś ceti `ca` śabdaḥ |
  sarvatra samudāyasya sādhyatā naiveṣṭeti cet, āha --
children.translated_text: the non-aggregate would be what is to be proved, because other-existence establishes only the bare absence-of-that, not [the conjunction of absence with location]. And it is not because of the mere absence of the relation that the relation of what-is-to-be-proved and what-proves is untenable [in the case of the aggregate]. And the aggregate — characterized as property and property-bearer, endowed with the relation of qualifier and qualified — is the desired thing to be proved. And the fault of the absence of that [aggregate as proved] and also [the fault of absence of relation between mark and marked] — that is [the meaning of] the word 'and.'
If [one says:] 'Not everywhere is the aggregate what is to be proved' — he says: 'And so' —

children.text:
dharmamātrasyāpi svatantrasya sādhyatopagame `ghaṭābhāvas tadanyabhāvāt` ity evaṃrūpe prayoge ghaṭasya sarvatra deśe sarvadā cābhāvaḥ prasajyeta | dharmiṇi hi kvaciddharmasya guṇabhūtasya sādhane tatraiva tatkāla eva ca bhāvo yukto nānyadeti sarvatra samudāya eva sādhyo 'bhyupagantavyaḥ na kevalo dharma iti |
  atrāha paraḥ -- nāsamudāyasya [S. 175b.] sādhyatā
children.translated_text: even if the independent establishment of the bare property alone were accepted as what is to be proved, then in a formulation of the form 'absence of pot, because of other-existence' — the absence of the pot in every place and at all times would absurdly follow. For when a property that is subordinate [to a property-bearer] is proved with respect to a property-bearer at some [place], it is tenable that it obtains there alone and at that time alone, not elsewhere — so everywhere the aggregate alone is to be accepted as what is to be proved, not the bare property.
Here the opponent says: 'Not the non-aggregate as what is to be proved' —
'nor the absence of relation between other-existence and absence-of-that. Why?'

children.text: ityādi | `iha pradeśe ghaṭo nāsti` ity evaṃ ghaṭābhāvena pradeśādir dharmī viśeṣyate saghaṭāt [T. 338.b.] pradeśāder bhedenāvasthāpyata iti tadviśeṣaṇatvaṃ prāptaḥ sādhyate na tu ghaṭo nāstīty evaṃ
children.translated_text: 'Location and the like' — and so forth. When [one says] 'there is no pot in this location,' the property-bearer — location and the like — is qualified by the absence of the pot, [and] is established as different from a location-and-the-like that has a pot — thus it has attained the status of being its qualifier. It is proved [as an aggregate], but not [merely] 'there is no pot' — thus
'the bare [property]' —

children.text: dharmiṇaḥ kasyacidguṇabhāvamanāpannaḥ | tato nāsamudāyasya sādhyateti kutas tadbhāvī doṣaḥ? |
children.translated_text: not having attained the status of being subordinate to any property-bearer. Therefore, there is no [fault of] the non-aggregate being what is to be proved — so whence the fault that would arise from that?
'And not' —
not in this thesis,
'of the mark' —
having the nature of other-existence,
'and of the thing marked' —
having the character of the property-bearer — location and the like —
'does the fault of absence of relation obtain.' —
Why?
'Of other-existence' —
characterized as the location and the like that is devoid of the pot,
'with the location and the like' —
with the property-bearer,
'because of the relation' —

children.text:
tādātmyasadbhāvād iti | tathā hi -- śabdādidharmiṇā kṛtakatvādes tādātmyalakṣaṇa eva sambandha iṣyate bhavatā | sa ihāstīty abhiprāyaḥ | tataś ca `sambandhābhāvāc
ca` ity ayuktam iti manyate |
  siddhāntavādī tu sādhyadharmalakṣaṇasya liṅgino ghaṭābhāvākhyasyānyabhāvena liṅgena sambandhābhāvaḥ prāg ukto na dharmiṇā tataḥ kvadam uttaraṃ saṃbadhyata iti manyamāno dharmiṇā 'py anyabhāvākhyasya liṅgasya sambandhābhāvaṃ darśayann āha --
children.translated_text: because of the existence of identity (<s>tādātmya</s>). For thus: just as the relation of identity alone is accepted by you between the property-bearer — sound and the like — and being-produced and the like, so it exists here too — this is the purport. Therefore 'because of the absence of relation and also...' is untenable — so he thinks. But the proponent (<s>siddhāntavādin</s>), thinking that the absence of relation — previously stated — is between the mark, namely other-existence, and the thing marked, namely absence-of-pot — which is the property to be proved — not with the property-bearer; so where does this reply connect? — and showing that even between the mark called other-existence and the property-bearer there is no relation, says —
'Not' —

children.text: liṅgaliṅginor asambandho na ceti sambadhyate | tathā nāsamudāyasādhanam iti | kin tu liṅgaliṅginor asambandha evāsamudāyasādhanam eva ca evam api bruvataḥ | kutaḥ? | pradeśāder eva dharmitayā 'vasthāpyamānasyānyabhāvatvād anyabhāvalakṣaṇaliṅgatvāt | etad eva [S. 176b.] darśayati -- yatraiva hi pradeśādau dharmitayā tvayā kalpyamāne yad [T. 339a.] ghaṭādikaṃ nāstīty ucyate lokena sa eva pradeśādis tena ghaṭādinā 'saṃsṛṣṭas saṃsargarahitaḥ
children.translated_text: the absence of relation between mark and thing-marked — this connects with 'and not.' Likewise, 'not the non-aggregate as proof.' Rather, there is precisely the absence of relation between mark and thing-marked, and precisely the non-aggregate as proof — even when speaking thus. Why? Because what is being established as the property-bearer — the location and the like itself — is of the nature of other-existence, i.e., has the nature of the mark called other-existence. This itself he demonstrates: for the very location and the like that is postulated by you as the property-bearer — of which it is said by the world that 'such-and-such a pot and the like does not exist [there]' — that very location and the like, being unconnected with that pot and the like, devoid of association,
'is the other-existence' —
that is desired as the mark, and nothing else — because
'from the observation of that alone' —

children.text:
ghaṭāsaṃsṛṣṭapradeśādidarśanād evāsya pratipattuḥ `ghaṭo nāsti` iti vikalpo liṅgijñānatayopagato
bhavati | tataḥ sa evānyabhāvaḥ | yad eva hi dṛśyamānaṃ liṅgijñānaṃ janayati tad eva liṅgam ucyate | ghaṭāsaṃsṛṣṭaś ca pradeśādir evam | tasmāt tadevānyabhāvalakṣaṇaṃ liṅgam upeyam | tataḥ kathaṃ tasyaivānyabhāvasya vyāvṛttito 'pi bhedam ananubhavato liṅgaliṅgibhāvo liṅgatvaṃ liṅgitvaṃ vā? | na hi liṅgam eva dharmī bhavitum arhati, dharmipratipattāv eva sādhyapratipatter anvayādyanusaraṇāyogāt | tataś cānyasya dharmiṇo 'bhāvāt katham anyabhāvātmano liṅgasya tatsambandhaḥ, samudāyasādhyatā vā? | śabdakṛtakatvayos tu paramārthatas tādātmye 'pi vyāvṛttibhedanibandhano 'sty eva bhedaḥ | tataḥ śabdādidharmipratipattāv apy anityatvādyapratītau kṛtakatvādinā tat sādhyata iti yuktam |
  syān matam -- sāmānyaviśeṣakalpanayā [S. 176b.] liṅgaliṅgitaikasyāpi bhaviṣyatīty ata āha --
children.translated_text:
from the very perception of a location and the like not connected with a pot, the conceptual cognition 'a pot does not exist' arises for this cognizer, having the status of an inferential cognition.
Therefore, that very other-existence [is the reason]. For that which, being perceived, generates the inferential cognition — that alone is called the reason (<s>liṅga</s>). And the location and the like not connected with the pot is just such. Therefore, that alone — characterized as other-existence (<s>anyabhāva</s>) — should be accepted as the reason. Then how can there be the reason-probandal (<s>liṅgaliṅgibhāva</s>) — the status of being a reason or a probandum — for that very other-existence which does not experience any distinction from its own exclusion [of the pot]? For the reason cannot itself be the subject (<s>dharmin</s>), since the cognition of the probandum [occurs] only upon the cognition of the subject, and [otherwise] the pursuit of positive concomitance and the like would be untenable. And therefore, since there is no other subject, how can there be a connection of the reason — having the nature of other-existence — with that [subject], or the status of the probandum being [something to be] proved by the aggregate [of subject and property]? But in the case of sound and produced-ness, even though they are ultimately identical in essence (<s>tādātmya</s>), there is indeed a distinction grounded in the difference of exclusion. Therefore, even in the cognition of the subject — sound and the like — when impermanence and the like are not yet cognized, it is proper that they are proved by produced-ness and the like.
  One might think: 'Through the postulation of universal and particular, there will be a reason-probandum [relation] even for a single [entity]' — therefore [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>] says:
'And here there is no' —
in the present case of other-existence,
'possibility of postulating a universal-particular relation' —

children.text: , yena [T. 339b.] sāmānyaviśeṣavikalpena sāmānyaṃ hetur bhaved viśeṣo dharmī, yataḥ {p. 186.1} samudāyasādhyatā liṅgaliṅginoḥ sambandho vā syāt | kuto na sambhavatīty āha --
children.translated_text: by which, through the conceptual distinction of universal and particular, the universal would be the reason and the particular the subject — such that there would be the status of the probandum being proved by the aggregate, or the connection of reason and subject. Why is it not possible? — he says:
'Because of the cognition of that particular alone' —
because of the cognition of precisely the particular location distinct from the pot —
'of the absence of that' —

children.text: ghaṭābhāvasya pratīteḥ | yataś ca viśeṣa eva ghaṭābhāvapratītinibandhanaṃ tataḥ kiṃ tatra sāmānyakalpanayā kriyata iti | sa eva viśeṣo 'nyatra varttamānaḥ sāmānyarūpatāṃ pratipatsyata iti cet, āha --
children.translated_text: of the absence of the pot. Since it is the particular alone that is the ground for the cognition of the absence of the pot, what is accomplished by postulating a universal therein? [If one says:] 'That very particular, occurring elsewhere, will attain the status of a universal' — he says:
'Of that' —
of the particular location distinct from the pot —
'elsewhere' —
in a similar [instance] —
'of continuity' —

children.text: anuvṛtter abhāvāt kutaḥ sāmānyātmatā? | na hy asau deśakālāvasthāniyato viśeṣo 'nyam anvetīti | atraivopacayahetum āha --
children.translated_text: because of the absence of recurrence — how could there be the status of a universal? For that particular, restricted to a [specific] place, time, and condition, does not recur in another [instance]. Here he states the reason for the accumulation [of the argument]:
'In the object of the thesis (<s>pratijñārtha</s>)' —

children.text:
tyādi | yadi hi ghaṭavivikta
eva pradeśaviśeṣo dharmī, tasyaiva ca hetuteṣyate, tadā pratijñāyā yo 'rtho dharmadharmisamudāyas tadekadeśa eva dharmilakṣaṇo hetuḥ syāt, pratijñārthaikadeśasya ca vyāvṛttito 'pi bhedam anu(na)nubhavato hetutvam asiddham iti | atha mā bhūt [S. 177a.] eṣa doṣa iti na ghaṭavivikta eva pradeśaviśeṣo hetur iṣyate, kin tu pradeśamātraṃ ghaṭaviviktatāviśeṣarahitam ity ata āha --
children.translated_text: and so forth. For if the particular location distinct from the pot alone is the subject, and its very [existence] is accepted as the reason, then the reason would be a portion of the object of the thesis — which is the aggregate of property and property-bearer — that very portion characterized as the subject. And the status of being a reason for a portion of the object of the thesis that does not experience any distinction from its exclusion is unestablished. But if, lest this fault obtain, it is not accepted that precisely the particular location distinct from the pot is the reason, but rather the mere location, devoid of the specific feature of being distinct from the pot — therefore he says:
'And where there is a mere location, there the absence of the pot [does not follow]' —

children.text:
| saghaṭe 'pi pradeśe pradeśamātrasya bhāvād anaikāntiko hetuḥ syāt |
  paro 'nyathā sāmānyaviśeṣabhāvaṃ [T. 340a.] darśayann āha --
children.translated_text:
| since even in a location with a pot, the mere location exists — the reason would be inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>).
  The opponent, showing the universal-particular relation in another way, says:
'In one of such a kind' —

children.text: yādṛśo ghaṭaviviktaḥ kevalaḥ pradeśo 'grataḥ sthitas tādṛśe sarvatra pradeśe ghaṭasyābhāva iti kuto 'nekāntaḥ? | tathāvidhapradeśaviśeṣapratītir eva ghaṭābhāvapratītis tato 'nyabhāvatadabhāvayoḥ liṅgaliṅgitā 'nupapannety upadarśayann āha --
children.translated_text: the absence of the pot obtains in every location of such a kind as the bare location standing before [one] that is distinct from the pot — so how can there be inconclusiveness? Showing that the very cognition of a particular location of such a kind is the cognition of the absence of the pot, and therefore the reason-probandum relation between other-existence and its absence is untenable, he says:
'But surely of that very [thing]' —

children.text: ityādi | yo 'sau kevalaḥ pradeśaviśeṣo dharmitayā 'vasthāpitas tasyaiva yat kaivalyaṃ kevala ity anena viśeṣaṇenocyate bhavatā, tad eva ghaṭaviraho ghaṭābhāva iti kathyate | sa ca ghaṭaviraho liṅgabhūtasya kevalasya pradeśasya
children.translated_text: and so forth. Of that very bare particular location established as the subject — its very bare-ness, which is expressed by you with the qualifier 'bare' — that itself is said to be the absence of the pot, the separation from the pot. And that separation from the pot is established in the very cognition of the bare location that is the reason —

children.text: pratipattāv eva[683]siddho na tūttarakālaṃ tato 'nya eva ākārāntareṇa dhūmādivāgniḥ[684]sidhyati | tataḥ kasyedānīṃ
children.translated_text: not [in such a way] that subsequently, something different from it is proved in another form, like fire from smoke and the like. Therefore, for whom now, when
'in that very cognition' —

children.text:
sādhyapratītau satyāṃ talliṅgam[685]? | na {p. 187.1} kasyacit | jijñāsitasya ghaṭābhāvasya siddher anyasya kasyacid ajijñāsitatvāt | kevalapradeśapratipattāv eva ghaṭavirahapratītau
ca yad etad uttarakālaṃ `yatra yatra kevalaḥ pradeśas tatra tatra ghaṭavirahaḥ` iti [S. 177b.]
children.translated_text: when the cognition of the probandum already obtains, [can there be] its reason? For no one. Since the absence of the pot, which was desired to be ascertained, is [already] established, there is nothing else that is desired to be ascertained. And when, upon the cognition of the bare location, the cognition of the separation from the pot [also obtains] — the subsequent
'pursuit of positive concomitance' —

children.text: anu)saraṇam, tac ca nirarthakam ādāv eva sādhyapratīteḥ | yata evaṃ tasmād anyabhāvaḥ kevalapradeśalakṣaṇaḥ sādhyasādhanayor bhedābhāvān na sādhanam abhāvasyeti sthitam | tad evaṃ [T. 340b.] samudāyasādhyatāṃ
children.translated_text: [i.e.,] the tracing [of the rule] 'wherever there is a bare location, there is separation from the pot' — that too is pointless, since the probandum is cognized at the very outset. Since it is thus, therefore other-existence — characterized as a bare location — because of the absence of a distinction between the probandum and the means of proof, is not a means of proving absence. This is established. Thus, the status of the probandum being proved by the aggregate,

children.text:
liṅgasya ca dharmiṇā sambandhaṃ[686]pratipādayituṃ yad uktaṃ pareṇa -- `pradeśādidharmiviśeṣaṇasyābhāvasya sādhanāt`[687]iti tadapṛthaksiddhidūṣaṇenaiva nirākṛtam |
  viṣayaviṣayibhāvena tu sambandhapratipādane niraste paro 'nyathā sambandhaṃ sādhyasādhanayor darśayann āha --
children.translated_text:
and the connection of the reason with the subject — what the opponent stated for the purpose of establishing [these] — 'because [other-existence] proves absence which is a qualifier of a subject such as location and the like' — that has been refuted by the very objection of non-separate establishment (<s>apṛthaksiddhi</s>).
  When the establishment of a connection through the relation of object and its cognizer is refuted, the opponent, showing the connection of probandum and means of proof in another way, says:
'There is' —

children.text: anyabhāvatadabhāvayoḥ sambandho virodhākhyaḥ | tataḥ sambandhasadbhāvād anyabhāvād abhāvasya siddhir bhaviṣyatīti | siddhāntavādī tu sādhyasādhanayor virodham evāsambhāvayan pṛcchati --
children.translated_text: a connection between other-existence and its absence, called contradiction (<s>virodha</s>). Therefore, from the existence of the connection, the establishment of absence from other-existence will follow. But the proponent (<s>siddhāntavādin</s>), considering the very contradiction between probandum and means of proof to be impossible, asks:
'What is contradicted by what?' —

children.text: iti | na hy atra sādhyasādhanayor virodhaḥ saṃbhavatīty abhiprāyaḥ | paro virodham abhiprāyānabhijñātayā darśayati --
children.translated_text: thus. For here, contradiction between the probandum and the means of proof is not possible — this is the intent. The opponent, unaware of the intent, demonstrates the contradiction:
'By the other-existence' —
having the nature of the bare location —
'of the counter-correlate (<s>pratiyogin</s>)' —

children.text:
yasyābhāvaḥ pramātum iṣṭo ghaṭādes tasyeti |
  parasyaivaṃvādino asambandhābhidhāyitām ādarśayann āha --
children.translated_text:
of the pot and the like, whose absence is desired to be ascertained.
  Showing that the opponent who speaks thus is stating a non-connection, [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>] says:
'Is it indeed the counter-correlate' —

children.text: ghaṭādiḥ pramātum iṣṭo yena pratiyogināḥ prameyatvena liṅgaliṅginor virodhaḥ sambandho 'bhidhīyate? | naiva pratiyogī pramātum iṣṭaḥ kin tu tadabhāva iti cet, āha --
children.translated_text: the pot and the like, that is desired to be ascertained — by which it is said that the contradiction, which is the connection between the reason and the probandum, is with the counter-correlate as the object to be ascertained? It is not the counter-correlate itself that is desired to be ascertained, but rather its absence — if so, he says:
'But the absence' —

children.text:
pratiyogino yaḥ sādhyaḥ [S. 178a.] ................................................................................................................ [S. 178b.] ........................................................................................................................
  [kumārilas tu manyate bhāvāṃśād bhinno '] [S. 179a.] yam abhāvāṃśas tato nānyabhāva eva tadabhāva iti kathaṃ tatpratipattir eva tadabhāvapratipattir iti | tathā hy ayam abhāvaḥ {p. 188.1} prāgabhāvādibhedabhinnaḥ, na cāvastuno bhedaḥ sambhavati ato 'yaṃ vasturūpa eva | yad āha --
children.translated_text:
of the counter-correlate, which is the probandum, ................................................................................................................
  [<s>Kumārila</s>, however, thinks:] this aspect of absence, being different from the aspect of positive existence — therefore it is not the case that the other-existence itself is the absence of that, [and] how can the cognition of that [other-existence] itself be the cognition of that absence? For thus: this absence, being divided into [types such as] prior absence (<s>prāgabhāva</s>) and the like, [has divisions]; and divisions are not possible for a non-entity; therefore this [absence] is of the very nature of a real entity. As [<s>Kumārila</s>] says:

children.text: na cāvastuna ete syur bhedās tenāsya vastutā||
children.translated_text: 'And these [divisions] would not be possible for a non-entity; therefore it has the nature of a real entity.' ||
ŚlV <s>abhāva</s> 8ab

children.text: iti | na ca bhāvāṃśa evābhāvāṃśo yuktaḥ, tasyendriyasaṃyogabalena pratīteḥ, itarapratīteś ca tadasaṃyogahetukatvāt | yad āha --
children.translated_text: Thus. And it is not proper that the aspect of absence is the same as the aspect of positive existence, because the latter is cognized through the force of sense-contact, while the former cognition has as its cause the non-contact with that [sense faculty]. As [<s>Kumārila</s>] says:
'Through contact with that, [the cognition] "it exists" — thus the nature of a positive entity is cognized;
"this does not exist here" — but that is caused by the non-contact with that.' ||
ŚlV <s>abhāva</s> 26

children.text: iti | tat kathaṃ tatpratipattir evāparasya vyavacchedanam iti tannirāsārtham āha |
children.translated_text: Thus. So how can the cognition of that [other-existence] itself be the exclusion of the other? In order to refute this, [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>] says:
'Of that' —
other — of the bare location — that which [is]
'bare-ness' —
alone-ness, the state of being without a companion — that itself [is]
'of the other' —
of the counter-correlate, the pot and the like —
'the deficiency' —
the absence.
'Thus' —
'therefore'
'the other-existence itself' —
the very aspect of positive existence accepted by you —
'is the absence of that' —

children.text: pratiyogyabhāvāṃśo na tataḥ pṛthagbhūtaṃ dharmāntaram ity ucyatesugatasutaiḥ| tataś ca
children.translated_text: the aspect of absence of the counter-correlate — not a different property existing separately from it — thus say the sons of the <s>Sugata</s> (Buddhists). And therefore,
'and the cognition of that itself' —
the cognition of that other-existence itself —
indeed
'is the non-cognition of that' —

children.text:
tasya pratiyogino 'pratipattir abhāvapratipattir iti yāvat | evaṃ manyate -- yo 'yam abhāvāṃśo bhāvāṃśāt pṛthagbhūto vastuno dharmaḥ parikalpyate sa ghaṭādyabhāvātmakatāṃ [S. 179a.] tadrūpavaikalyād evānubhavati nānyathā | tac ca tadrūpavaikalyam anyavastuno bhāvāṃśasyāpi
vidyata eva | tadabhāve hi tasyānyavastutaiva hīyeta | na hi yad yadrūpavikalaṃ na bhavati tat tato 'nyatvam anubhavati, yathā tasyaiva svarūpam, tathā cābhāvāṃśo 'pi tasya na sidhyet, sarvaṃ ca viśvam ekaṃ dravyaṃ prasajyeta, tataś ca sahotpattyādiprasaṅgaḥ, sarvasya ca sarvatropayogaḥ syād ity avaśyam anyavastuno bhāvarūpatā tadanyābhāvātmikaiva | tathā ca tatpratipattir eva tadanyābhāvapratipattiḥ[689]| tatsaṃyoga eva cendriyasya tadanyabhāvābhāvasaṃyoga [T. 342b.] iti kim ucyate --
children.translated_text:
the non-cognition of that counter-correlate, i.e., the cognition of absence — thus the meaning. [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>] thinks thus: this aspect of absence that is postulated as a property of a real entity, existing separately from the aspect of positive existence — it experiences the nature of being the absence of a pot and the like precisely because of the deficiency of that form, and not otherwise. And that deficiency of that form belongs to the very aspect of positive existence of the other real entity as well.
For in the absence of that [deficiency], it would lose its very other-entity-ness. For that which does not lack the form of something does not experience otherness from it — just as its own form [does not]. And thus the aspect of absence too would not be established for it; and the entire universe would be a single substance — and hence the absurd consequence of simultaneous arising and the like; and everything would be useful everywhere. Therefore, necessarily the positive-entity-nature of the other real entity is itself of the nature of the absence of that other. And thus, the cognition of that [other-existence] itself is the cognition of the absence of that other. And the very contact of the sense faculty with that [other-existence] is the contact with the absence of the other-existence — so what is [the point of] saying:
'"This does not exist here" — but that is caused by the non-contact with that' —
ŚlV <s>abhāva</s> 26cd

children.text:
iti? | vikalpāpekṣayoktam iti cet, tadetadabādhakam eva | pratyakṣeṇa tadākārotpattyā tadanyābhāvātmake[690]eva vasturūpe pratipanne pāścāt yasya {p. 189.1} yathāgṛhītābhilāpino vikalpasyopagamāt | vistarataś cāyam abhāvavicāraḥpramāṇadvitvasiddhāv abhāvaṃ prameyaṃ pramāṇaṃ ca vicārayatā vihita iti tata evāvadhārya iti |
  avaśyaṃ ca tadanyabhāvapratipattir eva tadabhāvapratipattiḥ | tato na vastvasaṅkarasidhyarthaṃ, `nāsty atredam` ity abhāvavyavahārārthaṃ [S. 180a.] cābhāvapramāṇaparikalpanā yukteti darśayann āha --
children.translated_text:
? If [<s>Kumārila</s>] says 'this was said with reference to conceptual cognition' — that is simply without force as a defeater. Because, when through direct perception, by the arising of that form, the very nature of the real entity — having the nature of the absence of that other — has been cognized, the subsequent conceptual cognition conforms to what was previously grasped. And this examination of absence has been presented in detail in the proof of the two <s>pramāṇas</s> — [the section] examining absence as the object of knowledge and the [absence as a] means of knowledge — so it should be ascertained from there.
  And necessarily, the cognition of that other-existence is itself the cognition of that absence. Therefore, the postulation of a separate means of knowing absence is not proper — neither for establishing the non-confusion of real entities, nor for the convention 'this does not exist here' — showing this, [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>] says:
'Otherwise' —

children.text: yadi tatpratipattir eva tadabhāvapratipattir iti neṣyate[691]tadā
children.translated_text: if it is not accepted that the cognition of that [other-existence] itself is the cognition of that absence, then
'of that' —
of the other real entity, through the determination of its own form, of the other — which lacks that form —
'without exclusion' —
without elimination — when there is no cognition of the absence of that —
'the very determination of that would not obtain' —

children.text: -- tasya tadanyavastunaḥ svarūpapratipattir eva na syāt | kiṃ kāraṇam?
children.translated_text: — the cognition of the own form of that other real entity itself would not obtain. What is the reason?
'Of the having-that-form and the not-having-that-form' —

children.text: tasya tadanyavastuno yadrūpaṃ pratiniyataṃ sakalatrailokyavilakṣaṇaṃ yac cātadrūpaṃ tadrūpaṃ na bhavati pararūpaṃ tayoḥ
children.translated_text: of that other real entity — the form that is restricted [to it], distinct from the entire triple world, and the not-having-that-form, which does not have that form, [but has] the form of others — of those two,
'because of non-discrimination' —

children.text:
avivecanād vivekenāvyavasthāpanād asāṅkaryeṇāprasādhanāt | sakalapararūpāsaṅkīrṇaṃ hi tadrūpam tac cet [T. 343a.] tatsāmarthyabhāvinā pratyakṣeṇa tathā nānukṛtaṃ kevalaṃ sammugdhākāram[692]eva tadutpannaṃ tadā kathan tena tatparicchedaḥ
syāt? | na hi yadrūpaṃ yadvastu tadrūpānanukāriṇā jñānena tatparicchedo yukto yathā -- śuklaśaṅkharūpānanukāriṇā kāmalinaḥ pītaśaṅkhāvabhāsinā jñāneneti | pratiniyatarūpānukāre vā tatparicchedasya katham anyā 'vyavacchedo nāma? | tataḥ pratiniyatarūpānanukārād eva tadanyāvyavacchedaḥ | tathā ca tatparicchedābhāva iti |
  bhavatv evaṃ tataḥ ko doṣaḥ? ity ata āha --
children.translated_text:
because of non-discernment, because of non-establishment through discrimination, because of non-accomplishment without confusion. For that form, unmixed with the forms of all others — if it is not thus reproduced by direct perception arising through the capacity of that [object], [but] only a confused image arises from it — then how could there be determination of that by it?
For it is not proper that a cognition that does not reproduce the form of an entity can determine that entity — just as the cognition of one with jaundice, which presents a yellow conch, [cannot determine] the form of a white conch. Or if there is reproduction of the restricted form, how can there not be the exclusion of the other? Hence, from the very non-reproduction of the restricted form, there is non-exclusion of the other. And thus there would be absence of determination of that.
'This convention' —
recognized by all people —
'of some' —
from perceiving a real entity such as fire and the like,
'in some place' —
connected with that
[is] for the purpose of attaining (<s>prāptyarthaḥ</s>)
what is seen and what is unseen,
and for the purpose of avoiding (<s>parihārārthaḥ</s>)
— characterized as engagement and disengagement —
that would not be [possible].
| What is the reason? |
'For' (<s>na hi</s>)
— because
'this' (<s>ayaṃ</s>)
— the cognizer —
'even though seeing fire' (<s>analaṃ paśyann api</s>)

children.text: saṅkīrṇatadatadrūpapratibhāsinā pratyakṣeṇa, anyathā 'sya darśanarūpatāhāneḥ, tathā hi -- asaṅkīrṇasyādarśane saṅkīrṇam api yadi na paśyet tadā loṣṭādiprakhyaṃ kathaṃ kasyacid etaddarśanaṃ syāt? | sa evaṃbhūtaḥ saṅkīrṇadarśanavān {p. 190.1} pratipattā katham
children.translated_text: — through a direct perception that presents a mixed appearance of both its form and what is not its form — otherwise there would be a loss of its nature as seeing. For thus: if, in the non-seeing of what is unmixed, one would not see even what is mixed, then how could anyone have this seeing [of fire] as resembling a clod of earth and the like? That [cognizer] of such a nature, possessing mixed seeing,
sees fire alone (<s>analam eva paśyati</s>)
and not water and the like? |
Rather (<s>kin tu</s>)
— by virtue of having a cognition that presents a real entity of mixed form —
he sees water and the like too.
Then how would
'one desiring water, there' (<s>salilārthī tatra</s>)
— in a place possessing fire —
'not proceed' (<s>na pravarteta</s>)
Anticipating the opponent's occasion for a reply, [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>] says:
'By non-apprehension' (<s>anupalambhena</s>)

children.text: ityādi | analapratibhāsinā hi jñānenānalasvarūpan eva pratīyate | yas tu salilābhāvaḥ sa tatra salilasyānupalambhena | tato jñānadvayena tadatadrūpayor vivekāl loke pravṛttinivṛttilakṣaṇaḥ pratiniyato vyavahāraḥ sidhyatīti | siddhāntavādy āha --
children.translated_text: and so forth. For by a cognition presenting fire, only the essential nature of fire is apprehended. But the absence of water there [is established] by the non-apprehension of water. Therefore, through the pair of cognitions, because of the discrimination of what has that form and what does not, the restricted conventional usage (<s>vyavahāra</s>) characterized as engagement and disengagement is established in the world. | The <s>Siddhāntavādin</s> (proponent) says —
'What is this so-called non-apprehension?' (<s>ko 'yam anupalambho nāma</s>)

children.text: iti | kadācit paro brūyāt salilopalambhavirahamātram ity ata āha --
children.translated_text: | Perhaps the opponent might say: 'merely the absence of the apprehension of water' — to this [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>] says —
'If [the non-apprehension] of water' (<s>yadi salila</s>)

children.text: ity ādi |kumārilasya tu salilopalambhanivṛttimātraṃ tuccharūpam abhāvapramāṇatayā nābhimatam eva |
children.translated_text: and so forth. For <s>Kumārila</s>, the mere cessation of the apprehension of water, which is of a void nature, is indeed not accepted as a means of cognizing absence (<s>abhāvapramāṇa</s>).
'The non-arising of perception and the like is called the absence of a means of valid cognition (<s>pramāṇābhāva</s>);
or the non-transformation of the self, or cognition directed at another object.' ||
<s>ŚlV</s> <s>abhāva</s> 11

children.text:
iti vacanāt | kin tu yo 'bhāvātmanaḥ pratiṣedhyavastupratibhāsijñānātmanā 'pariṇāmaḥ sa tadanyavastupratibhāsijñānasahacarito 'bhyupagantavyo na kevala iti param abhyupagamayitum asyopanyāsaḥ | tathā cānyavastuvijñānam evābhāvapramāṇam astu, kim apramāṇakasyātmano 'pariṇāmākhyena dharmeṇa parikalpitena? | na ca tadanyavastuvijñānapariṇāmād anya eva tasyāpariṇāmo nāma bhavato 'bhimato bhāvāntarasyaivābhāvatvenopagatatvāt | tulyayogyatārūpasyaikajñānasaṃsarggiṇa eva cānyavastuno vijñānaṃ tathopeyaṃ nānyasya, tajjñānāt pratiyogyabhāvasiddheḥ | na hi rūpajñānād rasādyabhāvapratītir yuktamatī [T. 344a.] deśādiviprakarṣavato vā | anyavastuvijñānaṃ ca pratiniyatarūpapratibhāsyeva | rūpāntarāvabhāsitve hi tasya salilopalambhābhāva eva na sidhyet | evaṃ ca pratiyogyabhāvaḥ pratyakṣāvabhāsita[693]eva | tadabhāvavyavahāre tv asmadabhimataivānupalabdhir āyāteti pratipādayitum asyopanyāsaḥ | tatra yadi salilopalambhābhāvaḥ
[S. 181b.] tuccharūpo 'nupalambhas tadā katham {p. 191.1} abhāvaḥ kasyacit pratipattiḥ pariccheda iti yāvat, paricchedasya jñānadharmatvāt | atha na tasya pratipattirūpateṣyate kin tu taddhetubhāva ity āha --
children.translated_text: — because of this statement. Rather, the non-transformation — which is of the nature of the self that is not cognition presenting the negandum — should be accepted as accompanied by cognition presenting another object, not alone — this presentation is to make the opponent accept [this]. And so let the cognition of another object alone be the means of cognizing absence — what need is there for the contrived property called 'non-transformation of the self,' which is not a means of valid cognition? Nor is the non-transformation of the self something different from the cognition presenting another object, since you accept it as nothing but the absence of an alternative entity. And the cognition of another object should be so accepted only of an object connected with a single cognition and having the form of equal fitness (<s>tulyayogyatā</s>), not of anything else, since the absence of the counter-correlate (<s>pratiyogin</s>) is established from the cognition of that [equally fit other object]. For the cognition of absence of taste and the like from the cognition of form is not reasonable, nor [from cognition of something] remote in place and the like. And the cognition of another object presents only a restricted form. For if it presented another form, the very absence of the apprehension of water would not be established. And thus the absence of the counter-correlate is not manifested by direct perception itself. But for the conventional usage of the absence of that [counter-correlate], the non-apprehension accepted by us has arrived — this presentation is to demonstrate [this]. Therein, if the absence of the apprehension of water, being of a void nature, is non-apprehension, then how can it be the apprehension — i.e., determination — of anyone's absence, since determination is a property of cognition? Or if it is not accepted as having the nature of apprehension, but rather as having the status of a cause of that [apprehension] — [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>] says —
'Or [is it] a cause of apprehension?' (<s>pratipattihetur vā</s>)

children.text:
iti | na hi sarvasāmarthyavirahalakṣaṇasyābhāvasya pratipattiṃ prati hetubhāvo yuktaḥ | hetubhāve vā tasyānapekṣitasahakāriṇo nityaṃ tajjñānajananād abhāvajñānam evaikaṃ pratipattuḥ syāt, jñānāntarasyāvakāśa eva na bhavet |
  na cājñātasyāsya nāstitājñānajananaṃ yuktam ity āha --
children.translated_text:
| For it is not reasonable that the absence characterized by the complete lack of all capacity should have the status of a cause with respect to apprehension. Or if [it has] the status of a cause, since it does not require cooperative causes, it would always generate cognition of that [absence] — so the cognizer would have only one cognition of absence, and there would be no occasion at all for any other cognition. |
  And it is not reasonable that this [absence], being unknown, should generate the cognition 'it does not exist' — [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>] says —
'Of that too' (<s>tasyāpi</s>)

children.text: salilopalambhābhāvasya kathaṃ pratipattiḥ? | athāyaṃ salilopalambhābhāvaḥ svayam apratīta eva salilābhāvapratītiṃ janayati tadā kasyacid api | tad evāha --
children.translated_text: — of the absence of the apprehension of water — how can there be apprehension? Or if this absence of the apprehension of water, itself unapprehended, generates the apprehension of the absence of water, then of anything whatsoever [it could do the same]. That is what [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>] says —
'Of that' (<s>tasya</s>)

children.text:
salilopalambhābhāvasya tato vā salilād anyasyānalādeḥ `vijñānaṃ vā 'nyavastuni` ity ata ātmano 'pariṇāmasya pṛthag avasthāpanāt, tatrāpi tadaṅgīkaraṇe cātmano 'pariṇāmasya [T. 344b.] tadātmakatvān na tato bhedena vyavasthāpyeta | tataś ca kasyacid api [S. 182a.] tasya tadanyasya vā 'pratipattāv api yady abhāvaḥ salilādeḥ pratīyate tadā svāpādyavasthāsv api salilādyabhāvaḥ kiṃ na pratīyate? | tadāpi tadabhāvaḥ pratīyetety etadvicāritampramāṇaviniścaye, tata evāvadhāraṇīyam | vyavadhānādigrahaṇena caitaddarśayaty anyavastuno 'pi anyatvaṃ tattulyayogyatārūpāpekṣam eva, na tadanapekṣam upeyam | tathā cāsmad upavarṇitānupalabdhisiddhir iti | yadā caivam uktena
prakāreṇānupalambhena salilābhāvapratītir na yujyate 'nalapratibhāsinaś ca jñānasya pratiniyatākāratā nābhyupagamyate
children.translated_text: — of the absence of the apprehension of water, or of something other than water such as fire and the like — since the non-transformation of the self is established as separate from 'or cognition directed at another object,' and since even if that [non-transformation] is accepted therein, the non-transformation of the self, being identical with that [cognition of another object], would not be established as different from it. And therefore, if even without the apprehension of any of those [items] — whether that [absence of apprehension] or that other [object] — the absence of water and the like is apprehended, then why is the absence of water and the like not apprehended even in the states of sleep and the like? At that time too the absence of that would be apprehended — this has been examined in the <s>Pramāṇaviniścaya</s>, so it should be ascertained from that very [text]. And by the inclusion of 'obstruction and the like,' [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>] shows this: the otherness of the other object too is to be accepted only with reference to the form of equal fitness (<s>tulyayogyatārūpa</s>) with that [negandum], not without reference to it. And thus the establishment of non-apprehension as described by us [is achieved]. | And when thus, by non-apprehension in the stated manner, the apprehension of the absence of water is not tenable, and when the restricted-aspect nature of the cognition presenting fire is not accepted —
'therefore this' (<s>tasmād ayam</s>)
— this cognizer who sees fire —
'even seeing fire' (<s>paśyann api</s>)

children.text: saṅkīrṇarūpapratibhāsinā jñānena `analo 'yaṃ na salilam` iti nādhyavasyati anadhyavasyaṃś ca salilarūpasyāpi pratibhāsanāt tadarthī
children.translated_text: — through a cognition presenting a mixed form — does not determine 'this is fire, not water'; and not determining [thus], because of the appearance of the form of water too,
'he would not stand still' (<s>na tiṣṭhet</s>)
— he would proceed [toward it] —
'nor would he refrain' (<s>nāpi pratiṣṭheta</s>)

children.text: salilārthī na pravarteta | tathā hi -- salilaṃ nāma tad ucyate yat sarvodanyāsantāpādyapanayanakṣamaṃ[694]sakalatadanyarūpāsaṅkīrṇapratiniyatākārajñānāvabhāsi | idaṃ tv anyad eva śabalarūpaṃ kim apy avabhāsata iti | {p. 192.1}
children.translated_text: — one desiring water would not fail to proceed. For thus: that is called 'water' which is capable of removing all thirst, burning sensations, and the like, and which appears in a cognition of restricted aspect that is unmixed with the form of anything other than it. But this [object] appears as something else entirely — of a variegated form — some indeterminate [thing]. |
'And therefore' (<s>tataś ca</s>)
— because of the impossibility of simultaneously performing engagement and disengagement, which are contradictory —
'an insuperable predicament would befall the cognizer' (<s>dustaraṃ vyasanaṃ pratipattus syāt</s>)

| |
  Here, anticipating the opponent's occasion for a reply, [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>] says —
'From that very' (<s>tata eva</s>)

children.text:
ityādi | na mayā [T. 345a.] salilopalambhanivṛttimātrāt tuccharūpāt tadabhāvagatir ucyate, yathoktadoṣaprasaṅgāt | kin tu yad etad ekasya kevalasyānalasya darśanaṃ tata evānyasya tatrāpratibhāsamānasya salilasyābhāvagatir bhavati `vijñānaṃ vā 'nyavastuni` iti vacanāt |
  siddhāntavādy āha --
children.translated_text:
and so forth. 'I do not say that the understanding of the absence of that [water] [arises] merely from the cessation of the apprehension of water, which is of a void nature, since the stated faults would follow. Rather, from the very seeing of fire alone, by itself, the understanding of the absence of water — which does not appear there — arises, because of the statement: or cognition directed at another object.' |
  The <s>Siddhāntavādin</s> (proponent) says —
'How does a single [cognition]?' (<s>katham ekam</s>)
and so forth. But by what capacity does the seeing of that one [fire]
convey the absence of the other (<s>anyābhāvaṃ pratyāyayati</s>)?

children.text: | tathā hi -- tasmin dṛśyamāne tadevāstīty avagacchatu, tadanyat tu nāstīti kim iti pratyetīti |
children.translated_text: | For thus: upon its being seen, let one understand that it alone exists — but why does one understand that the other does not exist? |
'Of that very' (<s>tasyaiva</s>)
— of fire and the like that is being observed —
'alone' (<s>kevalasya</s>)
— of [fire] whose form is unmixed with water —
'from the seeing' (<s>darśanāt</s>)

children.text:
analajñāne pratibhāsanāt `salilaṃ nāsti` iti niścayaḥ sañjāyate | tathā hi -- anala iva salilam api yadi tatrābhāviṣyat tadapy analavad darśane pratyabhāsiṣyata tayoḥ svajñānaṃ pratyaviśiṣṭatvād yogyatāyā naikasya pratibhāso yuktaḥ | tasmād ekapratibhāsanam anyābhāvanāntarīyakaṃ ity anyābhāve tato jñānam utpadyate anyavastuni ca vijñānaṃ nāstīti jñānaṃ janayati | tathā 'nyad vastu pararūpāsaṃkīrṇasvabhāvatayaiva tathocyate | tadrūpatayaiva[695]ca tajjñānam anyat[696]pratiyad evaṃ vyapadiśyate 'nyathā[697]tadayogād[698]ity anyapratipattir eva tadabhāvavikalpahetur iti siddhāntavādy āha
--
children.translated_text: — from its appearing in the cognition of fire — the determination 'water does not exist' arises. For thus: just as fire [appears], if water too were to exist there, it too would have appeared in the seeing, just like fire, since the fitness of both with respect to generating their own cognition is undistinguished — so the appearance of only one is not reasonable. Therefore, the appearance of one is inseparable from the absence of the other — so from that, a cognition regarding the absence of the other arises, and the cognition of another object generates the cognition 'it does not exist.' Likewise, another object is called so precisely by virtue of having an essential nature whose form is unmixed with the form of another. And the cognition of it is called 'other' precisely by virtue of having that form — it is so designated because it apprehends that [unmixed form]; otherwise, that [designation] would be impossible — so the apprehension of the other itself is the cause of the conceptual determination of the absence of that [negandum]. | The <s>Siddhāntavādin</s> (proponent) says —
'This very [thing]' (<s>idam eva</s>)

children.text: ityādi | nanv asmābhir idam eva prāg abhihitaṃ
children.translated_text: and so forth. But this is precisely what we have previously stated —
'When both of those exist, the apprehension of a single form alone is not possible because of [its] impossibility' (<s>tayoḥ satoḥ naikarūpaniyatā pratipattiḥ asambhavāt</s>)

children.text:
ity ādibhir vacanaiḥ | tato yad evānyāsaṃsarggiṇaḥ kevalasya [T. 345b.] pratibhāsanaṃ tad eva tadanyābhāvasyāpi, tasyaiva kevalasya tadanyābhāvātmakatvād anyasya cābhāvāṃśasya nirastatvāt | tataḥ pratyakṣāvabhāsitatvāt tadabhāvasya tadbalāt pāścātyaṃ vyavahārapravartanarūpaṃ nāstitājñānaṃ {p. 193.1} vikalpakam ājāyate | na tu tenāpratipannaṃ kiñcid avagamyate, yatas tadanyavastuni vijñānaṃ pratyakṣātmakam apy anavagate tadanyābhāve jñānaṃ janayat pṛthag abhāvapramāṇatayā vyavasthāpyeta | tathā hi -- tadanyākāraśūnya eva tadekajñānākāraḥ saṃvedyate | tatas tatsaṃvedanam eva tadabhāvasaṃvedanam | na hi vikalpajñānasyāpi tadākāraśūnyarūpasaṃvedanād anyat tadabhāvasaṃvedanaṃ nāma | kevalam asya vikalparūpataivātiricyate | tato yathā nirvikalpajñānāvasite kvacid
anale `analo 'trāsti` iti pāścātyo vikalpo vyavahārapravartanamātraṃ na tataḥ pṛthak pramāṇaṃ yathoktaṃ prāk, tathā nāstitājñānam api vikalpakaṃ tatphaladvāreṇa vā 'nyavastuvijñānaṃ na pratyakṣāt pṛthag abhāvākhyaṃ [S. 183b.] pramāṇam iti | tasmād yad evāsmābhir abhihitaṃ tadanyābhāvapratītiṃ prati, tad eva tvayā 'py abhidhīyata iti kasmāt puruṣam ivābhāti yatas tadanabhyupagamena pṛthagabhāvākhyaṃ pramāṇam abhyupagatam ity upahasati | tathā hy agaty edānīṃ tvayocyate na madhyasthatayā anyathedam eva kiṃ na pūrvam evābhihitam?, yata ālajālābhidhānena ''tmā parikleśita [T. 346a.] ity upasaṃharann āha --
children.translated_text: — by these and other statements. Therefore, the very appearing of the isolated [object], unmixed with the other, is itself [the ground for understanding] the absence of that other as well, since the isolated [object] alone is of the nature of the absence of that other, and the negative aspect — the absence of the other — has been excluded [from the perception]. Therefore, since the absence of that [negandum] is manifested by direct perception itself, a subsequent conceptual cognition in the form of the conventional usage 'it does not exist' arises by the force of that [direct perception]. But nothing unapprehended [by perception] is understood by that [conceptual cognition] — therefore the cognition of another object, even though of the nature of direct perception, would not be established as a separate means of valid cognition called 'absence-cognition,' [as if it] generates cognition of the absence of that other which has not been understood [by perception]. For thus: the aspect of the single cognition [of fire] is experienced as utterly devoid of the aspect of that other [water]. Therefore, the experience of that [single aspect] is itself the experience of the absence of that [other]. For even of conceptual cognition, there is no 'experience of the absence of that' other than the experience of a form devoid of the aspect of that [other]. It is only that its conceptual nature is additional. Therefore, just as the subsequent concept 'fire exists here' regarding fire determined by non-conceptual cognition is merely the functioning of conventional usage and is not a separate means of valid cognition from that [perception] — as was stated before — so too the conceptual cognition 'it does not exist,' or the cognition of another object through the door of its result, is not a separate means of valid cognition called 'absence' distinct from perception. | Therefore, what we have stated regarding the apprehension of the absence of the other — that very thing is being stated by you too — so why does it appear as if [you are] another person?, since by not accepting that, a separate means of valid cognition called 'absence' has been accepted — [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>] ridicules [the opponent]. For thus, being at an impasse, you now say it — not as a neutral party — 'why was this very thing not stated before?', since through the verbal web the self has been tormented — [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>] concludes saying —
'Therefore, like one who sees no shore' (<s>tasmāt tīrādarśinā iva</s>)

children.text:
ityādi | yathā kila vahanārūḍhair vaṇigbhiḥ śakunirmucyate api nāma tīraṃ drakṣyatīti | sa yadā sarvataḥ paryaṭaṃstīraṃ nāsādayati tadā vahanam evāgacchati tadvad etad api draṣṭavyam | yataś cāvaśyābhyupagamanīyo 'yaṃ pakṣas tasmān na kiñcid anayā 'vidyamānapratiṣṭhānayā
diśaḥ pratipattyā prayojanam |
  tad evaṃ parasyānyabhāvatadabhāvayor liṅgaliṅgibhāvam icchataḥ sambandhābhāvād[700]asāv ayuktaḥ iti pratipādite pareṇa `asati sambandhe 'nyabhāvagatyā 'pi tadabhāvagatir na syāt` iti codite `na vai kutaścit sambandhād` ity ādy abhihitam | tataḥ `anyabhāva eva tadabhāvo 'nyabhāvagatir eva ca tadabhāvagatiḥ` iti prasādhayatākumārilaparikalpitaḥ kasyacid abhāvaniścayārtham abhāvapramāṇavādaḥ prasaṅgato nirastaḥ samprati tu --
{p. 194.1}
children.translated_text:
and so forth. As they say, merchants aboard a ship release a bird [to see if] 'perhaps it will see the shore.' When that [bird], roaming in all directions, does not reach the shore, it returns to the very ship — similarly, this [argument of the opponent] is to be viewed. And since this position must necessarily be accepted, there is no purpose in this direction of understanding that has no existing foundation. |
  Thus, having demonstrated that the opponent's desire for an inferential-mark-and-inferable relation (<s>liṅgaliṅgibhāva</s>) between the existence of another and the absence of that [negandum] is untenable because of the absence of a connection — when the opponent objected: 'if there is no connection, then even from the understanding of the other's existence, there would be no understanding of the absence of that [negandum]' — the statement 'not indeed from any connection' and so forth was made. Then, while establishing that 'the existence of the other is itself the absence of that, and the understanding of the other's existence is itself the understanding of the absence of that,' the doctrine of a separate means of cognizing absence (<s>abhāvapramāṇa</s>) conceived by <s>Kumārila</s> for the purpose of ascertaining anyone's absence has been incidentally refuted. But now —
'And the establishment of the non-confusion of entities is dependent on the validity of that [means of cognizing absence]'
<s>ŚlV</s> <s>abhāva</s> 2cd.

children.text: ity etad āhatya nirākartuṃ [S. 184a.] pūrvapakṣam utthāpayann āha --
children.translated_text: — striking at this [position], in order to refute it, [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>], raising the prima facie objection, says —
'If from the determination of one alone' (<s>yady ekaparicchedād eva</s>)
and so forth. If indeed
'of one' (<s>ekasya</s>)
— of the isolated — from the determination, the exclusion of the other
'the exclusion' (<s>vyavacchedaḥ</s>)
— the negation — is established, then without distinction of all that is other,
'there' (<s>tatra</s>)

children.text:
deśe yatrāsāv ekaḥ paridṛśyate tatrābhāvasiddhir bhavet, na tu viśeṣaparigraheṇa [T. 346b.] tulyā svajñānajananaṃ prati yogyāvasthā yasya tasyaiveti | tathā hi -- asau yathā tulyayogyatārūpapadārthaviviktarūpa upalabhyate, tadekākārapratiniyamāt tajjñānasya, tathā tadatulyayogyatārūpapadārthaviviktātmako 'pi | tataś ca tadviviktākāratayā tadanyābhāvasādhane viśeṣābhāvāt pradeśarūpajñānaṃ ghaṭābhāvam iva rasādyabhāvam api sādhayet, na vā ghaṭābhāvam apīti |
  kiñ ca, yad etad `upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptasyānupalabdhir abhāvasādhanī` iti viśeṣaṇam uktaṃ tac ca na vaktavyam | kiṃ kāraṇam? yato ye 'py anupalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptās teṣām api tatra deśe tadekākāratayā jñānasya vyavacchedo bhavaty eva | tathā hi -- yathopalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptās tadekākāravati jñāne na pratibhāsante tataś ca vyavacchidyante [S. 184b.] tathā 'nupalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptā apīti kim
children.translated_text:
in a place where that single [object] is perceived, the establishment of absence would follow, but not [in a manner] that is equivalent, through the grasping of a specific [qualification], to the capable state for generating its own cognition of only that [particular object]. Thus: just as it is apprehended as having a form devoid of objects of equal capability — since its cognition is restricted to that single form — so too it is also of a nature devoid of objects of unequal capability. And consequently, since there is no distinction in proving the absence of what is other [from it] through a form devoid of that [object], the cognition of the form of a place would prove the absence of taste and the like just as [it proves] the absence of a pot — or alternatively, it would not prove even the absence of a pot.
Furthermore, the qualifier that has been stated — 'non-apprehension of what meets the conditions of apprehensibility is the proof of absence' — that too need not be stated. Why? Because even those that meet the conditions of apprehensibility — of them too, in that place, there is the exclusion by means of that cognition having that single form. Thus: just as those meeting the conditions of apprehensibility do not appear in a cognition having that single form and are consequently excluded, so too those not meeting the conditions of apprehensibility — so what [use is the qualifier]
'of what meets the conditions of apprehensibility'? —

children.text:
ity anena viśeṣaṇeneti | evaṃ pūrvapakṣe vyavasthite yadi tadanyavyavacchedaḥ -- tataḥ pṛthakkaraṇam anyatvena vyavasthāpanam abhimataṃ tadabhyupagamyata eva | atha taddeśakālayor abhāvaḥ, tad ayuktam, yena hi sāmarthyena tulyayogyatārūpasyopalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptasya cābhāvaṃ sādhayati na tatsāmarthyam atulyayogyatārūpe 'nupalabdhilakṣaṇaprāpte vā sambhavati | `tayoḥ sator naikarūpaniyatā pratipattiḥ asambhavāt`[701]ity evaṃ hi tadabhāvasādhanam | na [T. 347a.] caitad
anyatra sambhavatīti pratipādayitum
children.translated_text: [what use is] this qualifier? When the prima facie position is thus established: if the exclusion of what is other than that [is intended] — then the intended separate treatment, establishing [non-apprehension] as otherness, is just what is conceded. But if [what is intended is] the absence in that place and time — that is wrong, because the capacity by which [non-apprehension] proves the absence of what has the form of equal capability and of what meets the conditions of apprehensibility is not possible with respect to what does not have the form of equal capability or does not meet the conditions of apprehensibility. For thus is the proof of absence [made]: 'when both of those exist, the cognition restricted to a single form does not occur — because it is impossible.' And this does not obtain elsewhere — demonstrating this, he begins with:
'From the determination of a single self' —

children.text: ity ādinopakramate | yat puro 'vasthitaṃ pratyakṣe 'vabhāsate tasyaikasyātmanaḥ pratiniyatasya rūpasya paricchedāt tadākārotpattyā vidhivikalpotpādanena ca yaḥ
children.translated_text: and so forth. From the determination of the self — the restricted form — of that single [object] that is situated before [the cognizer] and appears in direct perception, [i.e.,] through the arising of that form [in cognition] and through the production of a positive conceptual cognition — of whatever
'is other than that' —
is different from that, distinct from that — of all of that, the
'self' —
the essential nature — from that,
'exclusion' —
