children.text: bhedanaṃ pṛthakkaraṇam anyatvasādhanam asaṅkīrṇarūpatāpratyāyanaṃ bhavati | kathaṃ punar ekātmaparicchedād eva tasya[702]tadanyātmano vyavacchedaḥ pratyakṣeṇa kriyate?, yāvatā pratyakṣaṃ puro 'vsthitapadārthasāmarthyabhāvi [S. 185a.] tadrūpam eva pratipadyatām | yat tu tadvyatiriktam aśeṣapadārthajātaṃ tadātmanas tasya puro 'vasthitasya kathaṃ tadvyavacchedakam? ataḥ tadvyavacchedārtham abhāvapramāṇam abhyupeyam, yato --
children.translated_text: differentiation, separation, establishment of otherness, demonstration of non-intermixed nature — occurs. But how does the exclusion of what is other than that self occur through direct perception from the determination of a single self alone? — since direct perception, arising from the capacity of the object situated before [the cognizer], cognizes only its form. But the entire class of entities distinct from that — of its self, of that which is situated before [the cognizer] — how can it exclude that? Therefore, for the purpose of excluding that, an absence-<s>pramāṇa</s> must be accepted, since —
'And the establishment of the non-intermixture of entities depends on that <s>pramāṇa</s> [of absence].'
ŚlV <s>abhāva</s> 2cd.

Thus.
Therefore he says:
'From the cognition whose appearance is restricted to the self of that [object]' —

children.text: iti | yataḥ puro 'vasthitasyaikasya vastunaḥ pararūpāsaṅkīrṇa ātmā, sarvabhāvānāṃ svabhāvata eva svasvabhāvavyavasthiteḥ pararūpeṇāsaṅkīrṇasvabhāvatvāt | anyathā katham abhāvapramāṇato 'py asāṃkaryam eṣāṃ sidhyet? | saṃkīrṇarūpāṇām asāṅkaryasādhane tasya [T. 347b.] bhrāntatāprasaṅgāt | tasmin pararūpāsaṃkīrṇe svabhāvata eva tadātmaniyato yaḥ pratibhāsaḥ pararūpapratibhāsāsaṃkīrṇaḥ tadekapadārthasāmarthyabhāvini pratyakṣe pararūpapratibhāsāyogāt tasya bhrāntatāpattyā pratyakṣatāhāneḥ | tad uktam --
children.translated_text: thus. Because the self of a single object situated before [the cognizer] is not intermixed with other forms, since all entities by their very nature are established in their own essential natures and have essential natures not intermixed with other forms. Otherwise, how could their non-intermixture be established even through an absence-<s>pramāṇa</s>? — since in proving the non-intermixture of things whose forms are [actually] intermixed, the absurd consequence of [that <s>pramāṇa</s>] being erroneous [would follow]. In that [object] which is not intermixed with other forms, the appearance that is restricted to its self by its very nature — not intermixed with the appearance of other forms — because in direct perception, which arises from the capacity of that single object, the appearance of other forms is impossible, and [if it occurred,] the consequence of its being erroneous [would entail] the loss of its direct-perception nature. As stated:
'For that [cognition], arising from the capacity of the object, would replicate only its form' —
[PVin I 40.12f.:

children.text: gaṅ gi phyir de don gyi nus pa las skyes pa na de 'i raṅ bḥzin kho na'i rjes su byed pa'i phyir ro ||
children.translated_text: <s>gaṅ gi phyir de don gyi nus pa las skyes pa na de 'i raṅ bḥzin kho na'i rjes su byed pa'i phyir ro</s> ||

children.text: iti | tasya tadātmaniyatapratibhāsasya jñānāt pratyakṣeṇa svasaṃvittyā saṃvedanāt | tatsaṃvedanam eva [S. 185b.] hi pratyakṣasyātadrūpād
children.translated_text: thus. From the cognition whose appearance is restricted to the self of that [object] — from the awareness through direct perception, through self-awareness (<s>svasaṃvitti</s>). For the awareness of that [restricted appearance] itself is the direct perception's
'exclusion' —

children.text:
pṛthakkaraṇaṃ tadbalenaiva ca pāścātyaḥ `anyātmakam etan na bhavati` ity asāṃkaryavyavasthāpratyayo vikalpakaḥ saṃjāyate gṛhītagrāhī | na tenāpūrvaṃ kiñcit pratīyate, pararūpāsaṃkīrṇasyātmanaḥ pratyakṣeṇaiva tadākārānukāriṇā paricchedād iti |
  yadi nāma tadātmaniyatapratibhāsajñānaṃ tathāpi katham anyātmanaḥ tasya pṛthakkaraṇam? ity ata āha --
children.translated_text:
separation — from what does not have that form. And by the force of that [direct perception] alone, a subsequent conceptual cognition arises — 'this does not have the nature of another' — a determinative cognition that establishes non-intermixture, apprehending what has been grasped [by direct perception]. Nothing new is cognized by it, since the self — not intermixed with other forms — has already been determined by direct perception alone, which replicates that form.
Even if the cognition has an appearance restricted to the self of that [object], how does it effect the separation of the other's self from that? To this he says:
'For that self is not' —

children.text:
ityādi | yasmāt tasya vastuno ya ātmā pararūpāsaṃkīṛṇnaḥ sa tadanyasya śeṣasya vastuna ātmā na bhavati, sarvasya tato 'nyasvabhāvatvāt, anyathā tadanyatvahāner iti | tasmāt {p. 196.1} tadātmaniyatapratibhāsajñānam eva tadanyebhyo nivarttanam | na hi jñānenārtho haste gṛhītvā 'nyato nivarttanīyaḥ | kevalam anyarūpāsaṃkīrṇasyaikasātmano 'nukaraṇam evāsyānyato [T. 248a.] nivarttanam ucyata iti | athānyātmanaḥ svaviṣayaṃ na nivarttayet, tadā 'sya viṣayasyānyātmanaḥ sakāśād avyavacchede pṛthag avyavasthāpane parātmano 'pi tatra paricchedaḥ syāt, anyathā[703]tadaparicchedasyaivaikātma[704]paricchedātmanas tannivarttanarūpatā[705][S. 186a.] syāt | tataś cāvyavacchede 'nyātmanas tatparicchedaprasaṅgāt pravṛttinivṛttyor abhāva iti pūrvaḥ prasaṅgo `na hy ayam analaṃ paśyann
api`[706]ity ādikaḥ |
  na kevalam anyātmanas tannivarttayati tadātmano 'py aśeṣam anyad iti darśayann āha --
children.translated_text:
and so forth. Because the self of that entity — not intermixed with other forms — is not the self of the remaining other entity, since everything other than that has a different essential nature; otherwise, [that thing's] otherness would be lost. Therefore, the very cognition whose appearance is restricted to the self of that [object] is the exclusion from what is other. For cognition does not have to grasp the object by hand and remove it from another. Rather, the mere replication of the single self not intermixed with other forms is itself called its exclusion from others. But if [the cognition] were not to exclude its own object from the self of others, then — since its object would not be excluded from the self of others, not separately established [from them] — the self of others too would be determined there [in the cognition]. Otherwise, the non-determination of that [other self] itself, being of the nature of the determination of a single self, would have the nature of exclusion from that [other]. And consequently, in the non-exclusion of the other's self, since the absurd consequence of the determination of that [other self] [would follow], there would be the absence of purposive activity and cessation — thus [we get] the earlier absurd consequence stated in 'for one who sees fire and the like, even so.'
Not only does [the cognition] exclude the other's self from that [object]; [it excludes] all else of its own self too — showing this, he says:
'And that' —

children.text: agrataḥ sthitaṃ deśākālasvabhāvāvasthāniyataṃ tadanyadeśādibhyo vyāvṛttātmanaḥ svahetubhyaḥ evāsya bhāvāt,
children.translated_text: [object] situated before [the cognizer], restricted by place, time, essential nature, and condition — having a self that is excluded from other places and the like, since its existence is from its own causes alone —
'by that self' —
the cognition (<s>buddhi</s>) that apprehends [it] by a self restricted to place and the like, replicating only such an essential nature,
'the deviation from that-ness' —
[i.e.,] the state of having another place, time, essential nature, or condition —
'of this [object]' —
of its own object —
'excludes' —

children.text: tataḥ pṛthakkaroti | kasmāt punar anyadeśāditāṃ tataḥ pṛthagavasthāpayati ity ata āha --
children.translated_text: separates from that. But why does it separately establish the state of other-place and the like from that? To this he says:
'For thus' —

children.text: yasmād anyadeśatādes tataḥ pṛthakkaraṇe sati taddeśādiniyataḥ padārthaḥ [T. 348b.] paricchinno bhavati, tadrūpasyaivānukārād | yady anyathābhāvo 'nyadeśāditā tadrūpānanukārād vyavacchinnaḥ -- bhavati tathātvaṃ ca taddeśādiniyatatvaṃ ca, tadā tasyaiva dṛśyamānasya bhavati nānyasyānyadeśādimataḥ | yata evam
children.translated_text: because when the state of other-place and the like is separated from that, the object restricted to that place and the like is determined, since only its form is replicated. But if the otherwise-being — the state of other-place and the like — were not excluded due to non-replication of its form, then both the being-thus and the being restricted to that place and the like would [apply], then that [being-thus] would belong to the very [object] being seen and not to another possessing other-place and the like. Since this is so,
thus —
therefore, from what is otherwise — possessing other-place and the like — [it] excludes what is thus — possessing that place and the like —
'it certainly excludes' —
it certainly turns away, it determines — this is the conclusion of the first [point]

children.text: nivarttayanty eva tat paricchinattīti pūrvakasyopasaṃhāraḥ | tathā
children.translated_text: . Similarly,
'from what is thus, it certainly excludes what is otherwise' —
this is the conclusion of the second [point] that should be drawn.
'Thus' —
by the stated reasoning,
'of a single' —

children.text: pramāṇasya pratyakṣasyānumānasya vā tasyāpy evam eva svaviṣayaparicchedād
children.translated_text: <s>pramāṇa</s> — whether direct perception or inference — its operation too, from the determination of its own object in exactly this way,
'operation' —
activity — [establishes] all entities
'in the two classes' —
'in identity and otherness' —
'establishes' —

children.text:
| tatas tatparicchedakapramāṇabalenaivāsāṅkaryasiddhiḥ | kiṃ tadarthikayā 'py abhāvakalpanayeti? |
  {p. 197.1} nanu ca vikalpavyāpāra eṣa `idam anyātmakaṃ na bhavati anyathaitad ātmakam` iti | pratyakṣaṃ ca nirvikalpakam iṣyate tat katham asāṃkaryasiddhis tataḥ? ity ata āha --
children.translated_text:
therefore, by the force of the <s>pramāṇa</s> that determines that [object] alone, the non-intermixture is established. What need, then, for the supposition of an absence-[<s>pramāṇa</s>] even for that purpose?
But [the opponent argues]: this is the operation of conceptual thought — 'this does not have the nature of another; otherwise it has this nature.' And direct perception is accepted as non-conceptual — so how is the establishment of non-intermixture from that [direct perception]? To this he says:
'When that [<s>pramāṇa</s>] is present' —

children.text:
tyādi | tad dhi pratyakṣaṃ vidhipratiṣedhavikalpau yadā svaviṣaye janayati tadaivāsya sāphalyam, tadaiva ca pramāṇam iṣyate [T. 349.a] nānyadā | ata evaikasyārthasvabhāvasyāpratipannāṃśābhāvāt[708]sarvātmanā paricchede 'pi bhrāntikāraṇasadbhāvāt kṣāṇikatādāvanvayavyatirekabuddhī janayitum asāmarthyāt tatrāsya prāmāṇyaṃ neṣyata iti |
  syān matam -- dvairāśyasādhane 'py asāṃkaryasiddhyarthā mā bhūd abhāvapramāṇakalpanā kin tu prakārāntarābhāvasiddhyarthā bhaviṣyati | na hi tadabhāvasiddhau pratyakṣasya kaścid vyāpāraḥ [S. 187a.] pratipādita iti ata āha --
children.translated_text:
and so forth. For that direct perception has its fruitfulness only when it produces the positive and negative conceptual cognitions with respect to its own object, and only then is it accepted as a <s>pramāṇa</s>, not at other times. For precisely this reason, since there is no uncognized aspect of a single essential nature of an object — even though it is determined in all respects — because of the existence of a cause of error, [direct perception] is not capable of producing positive and negative correlative cognitions with respect to momentariness and the like, and therefore its <s>pramāṇa</s>-validity with respect to that is not accepted.
One might think: even if the supposition of an absence-<s>pramāṇa</s> is unnecessary for the purpose of establishing non-intermixture in the two classes, it will be [needed] for the purpose of establishing the absence of any other alternative. For no operation of direct perception has been demonstrated in establishing that absence — therefore he says:
'In what is distinct from that' —

children.text:
tyādi | tasmāt paridṛśyamānād vyatiriktasyāśeṣasya vastuno vyavacchedena tataḥ pṛthakkaraṇenānyatvena yā vyāptis tatsādhanād eva prakārāntarasya tattvānyatvabahirbhūtasyābhāvaḥ sidhyati | tatas tadartham api nābhāvapramāṇakalpanā yukteti |
  atha matam -- sarvasyāparidṛṣṭasya dṛśyamānād anyatayā vyāptiṃ naiva pratyakṣaṃ sādhayati tat kutas tṛtīyarāśyabhāvaḥ pratyakṣata eva syāt, yato 'bhāvaprāmāṇyakalpanā vyarthā bhaved ity ata āha --
children.translated_text:
and so forth. From the exclusion of all entities distinct from what is being perceived — i.e., by separating [them] from that, [establishing them] as other — through the proving of that very pervasion, the absence of any other alternative beyond identity and otherness is established. Therefore, the supposition of an absence-<s>pramāṇa</s> is not appropriate even for that purpose.
But if [one thinks]: direct perception does not establish the pervasion of everything unperceived as other than what is being perceived — then whence the absence of a third class from direct perception alone, such that the supposition of the <s>pramāṇa</s>-validity of absence would be pointless? — therefore he says:
'Of that [hypothetical entity]' —

children.text: tṛtīyarāśitayā kalpyamānasya tato dṛṣṭād anyatayā vyaptyabhāve
children.translated_text: of what is being supposed as belonging to a third class — in the absence of pervasion as other than what is seen,
'by that' —
by direct perception —
from that —
from its own object —
'because of non-exclusion' —

children.text: d apṛthakkaraṇāt, tadarthasya ca rāśyantaratvena kalpyamānasya svaviṣayād avyavacchedāt apṛthakkaraṇāt punar api bhāvasya svaviṣayasyāparicchedaprasaṅgāt | [T. 349b.] sa hi tadviṣayaḥ sakalapararūpāsaṃkīrṇātmā yadi tenātmanā na paricchinnaḥ kathaṃ tena tasya paricchedaḥ? | tenātmanā paricchede vā kathaṃ sarvasya tadanyatayā vyāptyasādhanam? anyathāikasyāpi tadanyatvaṃ na syāt, nimittasya samānatvād iti | yata evaṃ
children.translated_text: because of non-separation — and because of the non-exclusion from its own object of that which is supposed as belonging to another class for that purpose — again, the absurd consequence of non-determination of the positive entity [which is] its own object [would follow]. For if that object — whose self is not intermixed with any other form — is not determined by that self [through direct perception], how could there be its determination by that? Or, if it is determined by that self, how could the establishment of pervasion of everything as other than that not be [achieved]? Otherwise, the otherness of even a single [thing] from that would not obtain, since the ground [for the distinction] is the same. Since this is so,
therefore —

children.text: kvacid vastuni pramāṇaṃ {p. 198.1} pratyakṣādikaṃ [S. 187b.] pravṛttaṃ tadvastu
children.translated_text: a <s>pramāṇa</s> such as direct perception and the like, operating with respect to some entity,

children.text: pratiniyatenātmanā paricchinatti, tato 'nyat tadrūpavikalaṃ vyavacchinatti, tadanyatvena vyavasthāpanāt | tṛtīyasya ca tattvānyatvabahirbhūtasya prakārasyābhāvaṃ sūcayati, sarvasyānyatayā vyāptisādhanāt, tadviruddhasya[710]vā sarvavastuno dvaividhyasya sādhanād iti |
children.translated_text: determines that entity by a restricted self, excludes what is other — deficient in that form — from that, by establishing [it] as other. And it indicates the absence of a third alternative beyond identity and otherness, by proving the pervasion of everything as other, or by proving the twofold nature of all entities as contradictory to that [third option].

children.text: evam ekasya pramāṇasya vyāpāra eṣo 'nantarokta iti tam evopasaṃhṛtya sukhapratipattaye darśayannāha --
children.translated_text: Thus, this operation of a single <s>pramāṇa</s> has been stated just now — summarizing and showing it for ease of understanding, he says:
'Thus' —
'with respect to some entity' —
'a <s>pramāṇa</s>' —
'direct perception and the like, operating' —
'that very' —
'entity — from what is other than it' —
'from other forms, excludes' —

children.text: tataḥ pṛthakkaroti tadasaṃkīrṇarūpatayā pratipadyate, paramārthatas tasya tadrūpatvāt yathāvastu ca pratyakṣeṇa rūpānukārāt | kim iti pararūpād vyavacchinatti? | tasyaiva pararūpavikalasyaikarūpasya paricchedāt | tathā
children.translated_text: separates from that, cognizes it as having a non-intermixed form — because in ultimate reality its form is such, and because direct perception replicates [its] form as the entity [actually] is. Why does it exclude from other forms? Because it determines a single form deficient in other forms. Similarly,
'and what is other than it, too' —

children.text: tasmād dṛśyamānād anyad eva ca vyavacchinatti | kutaḥ? |
children.translated_text: Therefore, it excludes precisely what is other than the perceived [object]. Why?
'From that' —

children.text: svaviṣayāt | na kevalaṃ svaviṣayaṃ parato vyavacchinatti, param api svaviṣayād iti | kuta etad? | anyasya pararūpasya tatra svālambane 'paricchedād avaśyam evāparicchinnasya [S. 188a.] paricchinnād anyatvaṃ bhavati | yata evam ataḥ
children.translated_text: from its own object. Not only does it exclude its own object from others, but others too from its own object. How so? Because another form — a different form — is not delimited there, in its own object (<s>svālambana</s>). Necessarily, what is not delimited is different from what is delimited. Since this is so, therefore,
'that' —

children.text:
eva pramāṇam ekavastuparicchedakaṃ prakārāntarābhāvaṃ sādhayati, nābhāvākhyam | kuta etat? | tasmiṃ dṛśyamāne
vastuni dṛṣṭatadanyatvena tasyānyasya tatrāparicchidyamānasyānyatvaṃ tadanyatvaṃ dṛṣṭāt tadanyatvaṃ
children.translated_text: that very <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid cognition), delimiting a single entity, establishes the absence of another form, not [an absence] called 'abhāva.' How so? When a real entity is perceived, by virtue of the otherness of that other — which is not delimited there — from the perceived [entity], its otherness from the perceived,
'otherness from the perceived' —

children.text:
tena sarvasya tadvyatiriktasya vyavasthāpanān na a(-panena a)tad anyasyaiva ca yad anyan na bhavati puro 'vasthitaṃ sakalaparabhāvavyāvṛttaṃ tasyaiva tattvena dṛśyamānaprakāratayā vyavasthāpanād iti |
  amum eva nyāyam anyatrāpy atidiśann āha --
children.translated_text: by establishing thereby [the otherness] of everything distinct from that — and that which is not other [from the perceived], standing directly before [one], excluded from all other forms of being — by establishing precisely that, in its reality, as the mode of the perceived. | Extending this very principle to other cases too, he says:
'By this [principle], successive and simultaneous, and the like' —

children.text:
ityādi | etena anantaroktena nyāyena pratiniyataikapadārtharūpānukāriṇī buddhir upajāyamānā tadviparītarūpaṃ sarvaṃ svaviṣayād vyavacchindatī dvairāśyaṃ tṛtīyaprakārābhāvaṃ ca sādhayatīti[711]ye kecid anyonyavyavacchedarūpāḥ kramākramanityānityādayaḥ te vyākhyātāḥ | {p. 199.1} tathā hi -- kāryasya kramamananyasahāyatāṃ pratiyaty eva buddhis tasyākramaṃ kāryāntarasāhityaṃ [T. 350b.] tataḥ pṛthakkaroti | tataḥ kramākramatayā dvaitasiddheḥ tṛtīyasya prakārasya sambhavo nirasto bhavati | kramabhāvavyatirekiṇaḥ sarvasya kāryajanmanaḥ tadanyatayā dvitīyaprakāratayā 'vasthānāt | evam udayānantaradhvaṃsitā [S. 188b.] kṣaṇikatocyata iti pratīyatī vyavasthāpanākāla eva buddhis tadviparītarūpatāyāḥ svaviṣayād apākaraṇāt tato 'nyatvena prakārāntare 'vasthāpanād rāśyantarābhāva[712]iti |
  tad evam ekapramāṇanibandhanām asāṅkaryasiddhiṃ pratipādyopasaṃharayann āha --
children.translated_text: and so forth. By this just-stated principle, a cognition that arises replicating the form of one restricted particular entity, [thereby] excludes from its own object everything of the opposite form, and establishes [both] the twofold division and the absence of a third mode. Thus whatever [pairs] — successive and simultaneous, permanent and impermanent, and the like — are of the nature of mutual exclusion, they are explained. {p. 199.1} For thus: the very cognition that apprehends the successiveness of an effect — its not being accompanied by another — separates from it its simultaneity, its being accompanied by another effect. [T. 350b.] Therefore, through the establishment of the duality of successive and simultaneous, the possibility of a third mode is negated — because everything pertaining to the production of effects that differs from successive existence is established as the second mode, in virtue of its being other than that. Similarly, 'being destroyed immediately after arising is called momentariness' — when this is cognized, the very cognition at the time of establishing [this] removes the opposite form from its own object and establishes [it] as another mode by virtue of being other than that — [hence] the absence of another class.
'Thus' —
by the stated principle —
'of a single [entity]' —

children.text: pratiniyatātmana upalambhāt tasyopalabhyamānasya yas tato 'nyas tattulyayogyatārūpas tadviparīto vā tadrūpavikalas tadātmano
children.translated_text: from the apprehension of one that has a restricted self — of that which is apprehended, whatever is other than it, having the form of equal fitness or being the opposite of that, or being deficient in that form — of that self —
'the exclusion' —

children.text: pṛthakkaraṇaṃ tasyopalabhyamānasyānupalabhyamānasvabhāvād rūpāntareṇa pratibhāsanāt | tathā tasya svaviṣayasya tadanyātmatāyā bhāvapradhānatvān nirdeśasya
children.translated_text: the separation — because of the appearing of the apprehended [entity] with a form different from the non-apprehended essential nature. And because the description of the otherness of that, its own object, from other natures is predominantly [in terms of] positive entity,
'the exclusion obtains' —

children.text:
asāṅkaryaṃ sidhyati |
  tad yady etad aviśeṣaṇānyasya sarvasya tatrābhāvasiddhiḥ syād ity atrābhimataṃ tadā siddhasādhanam, yataḥ sarvam aviśeṣeṇaiva tad ekākārayā budhyā tadrūpavikalaṃ svaviṣayād avacchidyate, sarvasyānyarūpasya tatrāprati-bhāsanāt | atha taddeśakālayor abhāvaḥ sarvasya [T. 351a.][S. 189a.] tadviparītarūpasya vyavacchedo 'bhimataḥ sa na yukta iti darśayati --
children.translated_text: the non-intermixture (<s>asāṅkarya</s>) is established. | Now, if the intention here is that the establishment of the absence of everything else whatsoever without qualification is achieved there — then this is the fallacy of proving what is already established (<s>siddhasādhana</s>), since everything whatsoever, without qualification, being deficient in that form, is excluded from one's own object by a cognition of a single aspect, because nothing of another form appears there. But if the intended exclusion is the absence of everything of the opposite form at that place and time, he shows that this is untenable:
'Not at that place and time' —

children.text: yatrāsau pratiniyatātmā sakalatrailokyavilakṣaṇaḥ padārtha upalabhyate tatra sarvasyānyasya bhāvasya tattulyayogyatārūpasyetarasya vā vyavacchedaḥ pratiṣedhaḥ | yena hi kāraṇena tattulyayogyatārūpasya tatrāpratibhāsamānasya pratiṣedhas tasmin sati tad ekarūpaniyatāyāḥ pratipatter asaṃbhavāt tad[713]abhāvanāntarīyikā
children.translated_text: where that entity of restricted self, dissimilar from the entire triple world, is apprehended — there, the exclusion, i.e., the negation, of every other entity, whether of the form of equal fitness with that or otherwise. For by the very reason that what is of the form of equal fitness with that, not appearing there, is negated — when that [negation] obtains, since the cognition restricted to one form would be impossible, [that cognition]

children.text:
sā bhavantī tatpratiṣedhaṃ[714]gamayatīti tatkāraṇam anupalabdhilakṣaṇaprāpte tadatulyayogyatārūpe ca na sambhavatīti kathaṃ tadabhāvaḥ sidhyet |
  {p. 200.1} etad evopasaṃharann āha --
children.translated_text: becoming one that necessarily entails the absence of that, indicates the negation of that — [and] that reason amounts to [what is] arrived at by the defining characteristic of non-apprehension. But [this negation] is not possible with respect to what does not have equal fitness with that — so how would the absence of that be established? | Concluding this very [point], he says:
'Therefore, what is not of that nature' —

children.text: ca sarvas tadviparītarūpas tadekākārayā buddhyā prasādhitaḥ syāt
children.translated_text: and everything of the opposite form would be established by a cognition of a single aspect of that —
'and [what is] at that place and time' —

children.text: tasya pratibhāsamānasya yau deśakālau tau yasya, sa ca syāt | kiṃvat? | rasarūpādivad iti | na hi rūpapratibhāsinā jñānena tadrūpavikalasya rasasya svaviṣayāt pṛthakkaraṇe 'pi tad asāṃkaryasādhane 'pi taddeśakālayor abhāvaḥ [S. 189b.] sidhyati | tataś ca kathaṃ sarvasyātulyayogyāvasthasyāpi tatrābhāvaḥ syāt?, upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptasyeti viśeṣaṇaṃ vā nocyeta | yata evaṃ
children.translated_text: would also [be established], namely that which is at the place and time of the appearing [entity]. Like what? Like taste and color, and the like. For a cognition in which color appears, even when separating taste — which is deficient in that color-form — from its own object, even when establishing that non-intermixture — does not establish the absence [of taste] at that place and time. Therefore, how could the absence of everything, even what is not in a state of equal fitness, be [established] there? — or the qualifier 'arrived at by the defining characteristic of apprehension' (<s>upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāpta</s>) would not need to be stated. Since it is so,
'therefore' —

children.text: kvacit kadācit kasyacid abhāvasiddhir yathoktād evānupalambhād upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptasya [T. 351b.] tattulyayogyatārūpopalambhātmanaś cety evaṃrūpāt, na tu sāmānyena yathā ''huḥpare --
children.translated_text: the establishment of the absence of something, somewhere, at some time — is from non-apprehension of precisely the stated kind only — [i.e.,] of what is arrived at by the defining characteristic of apprehension, and having the nature of the apprehension of what has the form of equal fitness with that — of such a form, and not in general, as the opponents have stated:
'Where the fivefold <s>pramāṇa</s> does not arise regarding the form of an entity,' |
'there, for the purpose of cognizing the being of the entity, there is the validity of the <s>pramāṇa</s> of absence.' ||
ŚlV <s>abhāva</s> 1; TS 1647.

children.text:
iti |
na hy anupalabdhilakṣaṇaprāpte pramāṇapañcakāpravṛttāv api tadabhāvaḥ sidhyati, saty api tasmin svabhāvādiviprakarṣeṇa pramāṇapañcakāpravṛttisambhavād iti |
  tad evaṃ prāsaṅgikaṃ parisamāpayya yad uktaṃpareṇa `sa evānyabhāvas tadviṣayā copalabdhiḥ tadabhāvasya kiṃ na sādhanam`[715]iti tatrānyabhāvasya tadabhāvaṃ prati liṅgatve niraste tadviṣayāyā upalabdher nirākurvann āha --
children.translated_text: Thus. For even when the fivefold <s>pramāṇa</s> does not operate with respect to what is arrived at by the defining characteristic of apprehension, the absence of that is not established, since even when that [object] exists, the non-operation of the fivefold <s>pramāṇa</s> is possible due to remoteness in essential nature and the like. | Thus, having concluded the incidental [discussion], regarding what the opponent said — 'that very existence of another, and the apprehension directed at it — why is it not a means of proof for the absence of that?' — having negated the mark-status of the existence of another with respect to the absence of that, refuting [the mark-status of] the apprehension directed at it, he says:
'[The apprehension] directed at the existence of another' —

children.text:
tyādi | yat punar uktam -- anyabhāvaviṣayopalabdhis tadabhāvasya kinna sādhanam`[716]iti sā tadabhāvasya sādhikeṣṭaivāsmākam, [S. 190a.] na tu liṅgatvena yathoktavānasi | kiṃ kāraṇam? | yataḥ tatrāpy anyabhāvaviṣayāyām[717]upalabdhāv 'bhāvasya pṛthag anyabhāvāt sādhyatve kalpyamāne sambandhābhāvasya tadabhāvena tulyatvāt | na hi tasyā api anyabhāvarūpāyāḥ tadabhāvena kaścid ekārthasamavāyādirūpaḥ sambandho 'stīti |
  apṛthak siddher ity asyāpi tulyatāṃ darśayann -- āha
children.translated_text: and so forth. As for what was again stated — 'why is the apprehension directed at the existence of another not a means of proof for the absence of that?' — that [apprehension] is accepted by us as indeed establishing the absence of that, but not as an inferential mark as you have stated. For what reason? Because even in the case of the apprehension directed at the existence of another, when the separate establishment of absence — separately from the existence of another — is postulated, the same [objection] of the absence of a relation applies equally as with the absence of that. For there is no relation of the form of co-inherence in a single object and the like between that [apprehension] too, which is of the nature of the existence of another, and the absence of that. | Showing that the [objection of] non-separate establishment also applies equally, he says:
'At the manifestation of the inferential mark' —

children.text: tyādi | yeyam anyabhāvaviṣayā upalabdhir lliṅgatayocyate tasyās {p. 201.1} tadviviktapradeśākārāyā [T. 352a.]
children.translated_text: and so forth. This apprehension directed at the existence of another, which is called the inferential mark — of that [apprehension], which has the form of the spot devoid of that [negated entity], {p. 201.1} [T. 352a.]
'at the very time of manifestation' —

children.text: janmakāle pratītikāla eva[718]vā tadabhāvasiddheś ca | tathā hi -- tatpratibhāsaviviktānyabhāvapratibhāsabuddhisaṃvedanam eva tadabhāvasaṃvedanam iti | tad eva sādhayati -- na hy anyasya tadviviktasya bhāvaṃ pratipadya pratipattā punar uttarakālaṃ tatpratipatter anyabhāvapratipattes tadabhāvenānyavyatirekau prasādhya pratibindhasādhakena pramāṇena tadabhāvaṃ pratipadyate | kiṃ tarhi? | tadanyaṃ tadviviktarūpaṃ pratipadyamāna eva tasya
children.translated_text: at the time of birth, or at the very time of cognition, the absence of that is [already] established. For thus: the self-awareness of the cognition whose appearance is the appearance of another devoid of the appearance of that — that very thing is the awareness of the absence of that. That alone establishes [it]. For it is not the case that having apprehended the existence of another devoid of that, the apprehender subsequently, at a later time, by ascertaining the exclusion from and co-presence with the existence of another through the non-cognition of that, apprehends the absence of that through a <s>pramāṇa</s> that establishes invariable concomitance. Rather, the very [person] apprehending another — of a form devoid of that —

children.text:
pratiyogino 'bhāvaṃ[719]pratipadyate, tasyaiva tadabhāvātmakatvāt | tathā hi -- saghaṭapradeśāsaṃkīrṇarūpasya [S. 190b.] kevalapradeśasya darśanam eva ghaṭābhāvadarśanam | na hi `ghaṭo 'tra nāsti` `ghaṭavānayaṃ na bhavati` `saghaṭād anyaḥ` ity arthabhedaḥ
kaścit | tataḥ saghaṭād anyatayā kevalapradeśasya darśanam eva ghaṭābhāvadarśanam iti | `ghaṭo 'tra nāstī`ti jñānaṃ gṛhītagrāhitayā smṛtir eveti | kathaṃ jñāyata iti cet | darśanānantaram anvayavyatirekasādhanalakṣaṇena vyavadhānena vinā `idam ghaṭaviviktaṃ pradeśavastv asti` `idaṃ tu ghaṭavastu nāsti` iti pāścātyena vikalpadvayena vyavasthāpanāt[720]| tato nānvayavyatirekānusaraṇam atrāstīti [T. 352b.] |
  kiñ ca -- dṛṣṭāntarāsiddhe svātmanyabhāvaviṣayopalabdhis
children.translated_text: apprehends the absence of that counter-correlate (<s>pratiyogin</s>), because that [existence of another] is itself of the nature of the absence of that. For thus: the very seeing of the bare spot, whose form is unmixed with that of a spot-with-pot, is the seeing of pot-absence. For there is no difference in meaning between 'there is no pot here,' 'this is not one possessing a pot,' and 'this is other than [a spot] with a pot.' Therefore, the seeing of the bare spot as being other than [a spot] with a pot is itself the seeing of pot-absence. And the cognition 'there is no pot here' is merely memory, since it grasps what has already been grasped. How is this known? Because immediately after perception, without the intervening [process of] establishing through co-presence and co-absence, [the content] is determined by the subsequent pair of concepts: 'this is a spot-entity devoid of pot' and 'but this pot-entity does not exist.' Therefore, there is no following of co-presence and co-absence here. | Moreover: when a different example is not established, the apprehension directed at the existence of another, in its own self,

children.text: tadabhāvasya sādhanaṃ[721]| tad eva vyatirekamukhena darśayati --
children.translated_text: is the means of proof for the absence of that. He shows this very [point] through the method of exclusion (<s>vyatireka</s>):
'And that, of that' —

children.text: ityādi | ihāpy asty evānvaya iti cet, āha --
children.translated_text: and so forth. 'But there is indeed co-presence (<s>anvaya</s>) here too.' To this he says:
'For it cannot be shown thus' —

children.text: ityādi | kasmān na śakyaṃ darśayitum? | tad ekopalabdheḥ tasyaikasyānanyasaṃsarggiṇo yopalabdhir viśeṣarūpā tasyāḥ kvacid apy anyatrābhāvāt | atha tadviviktopalabdhisāmānyaṃ hetur ucyate -- yatra yatra ghaṭaviviktabhūtalopalabdhis tatra [S. 191a.] tatra ghaṭābhāvo yathā pūrvānubhūte ghaṭavivikte pradeśa ity āha --
children.translated_text: and so forth. Why can it not be shown? Because of the absence, anywhere at all, of that [particular] apprehension — the specific apprehension of that one [entity] unmixed with another. But if the generality of the apprehension-of-what-is-devoid-of-that is called the reason — 'wherever there is the apprehension of a ground devoid of pot, there is pot-absence, as in a previously experienced spot devoid of pot' — he says:
'When the demonstration is made in general terms' —

children.text:
dṛṣṭānte 'pi pūrvānubhūtaghaṭavivikte pradeśe ghaṭābhāvasya prasādhakaṃ pratyakṣādikaṃ pramāṇāntaram anyabhāvaviṣayopalabdher nāsti, kiṃ tu saiva tadanyabhāvopalabdhiḥ sādhyadharmasya tadabhāvalakṣaṇasya {p. 202.1} sādhikā | sā ca yathā sādhyadharmiṇi tadabhāvasiddhaye dṛṣṭāntam apekṣate tathā
dṛṣṭānte 'pi | tathā, tatrāpi tadanyatrāpītyanavasthā dṛṣṭāntānām iti | anavasthāyāṃ cāpratipattiḥ sarvatra tadabhāvasya | yata evaṃ
children.translated_text: even in the example — the previously experienced spot devoid of pot — there is no other <s>pramāṇa</s> such as perception and the like, apart from the apprehension directed at the existence of another, that establishes pot-absence. Rather, that very apprehension of the existence of another establishes the property to be proved — characterized as the absence of that. And just as that [apprehension] requires an example for the establishment of the absence of that in the property-bearer to be proved (<s>sādhyadharmin</s>), so too in the example. And thus, there too [an example is required], and in that [further example] too — and so there is an infinite regress of examples. And with the infinite regress, there is non-apprehension of the absence of that everywhere. Since it is so,
'therefore not' —

children.text: kutaścil lliṅgāt tadanyabhāvāt tadupalabdher vā tadabhāvasiddhir iti | yadi tadanyabhāvas tadabhāvaṃ na sādhayati, kiṃ
children.translated_text: from any inferential mark — from the existence of another, or from the apprehension of it — is the absence of that established. If the existence of another does not establish the absence of that, what

children.text: punar lliṅgatayā [T. 353a.] sādhayati[722]?, ity ata āha --
children.translated_text: then does it establish as an inferential mark? To this he says:
'That existence of another' —

children.text: pratyakṣalakṣaṇena -- pratyakṣasyaiva vivakṣitopalambhād anyatvenānupalambhatvāt | tallakṣaṇenānupalambhena siddhaḥ sann abhāvavyavahāraṃ sādhayet,[723]karmasthakriyāpekṣāyāṃ[724]tadanyabhāvasyānupalabdhirūpatvāt | kva punar asāv abhāvavyavahāraṃ sādhayet? | mūḍhapratipattau sādhyāyāṃ | yas tv amūḍho [S. 191b.] viṣayapratipattau viṣayiṇaṃ smaraty eva tasyābhāvavyavahāraḥ pratyakṣanibandhana eveti na tatrānupalabdher liṅgateti sucarccitam evānyatretīhālaṃ prasaṅgeneti |
children.translated_text: by the defining characteristic of perception — because of being non-apprehension (<s>anupalambha</s>), in the sense of being other than the intended apprehension of that very thing [i.e., perception]. Being established through non-apprehension of that defining characteristic, it would establish the practice of absence — because the existence of another has the nature of non-apprehension when there is the requirement of an action with respect to the object of [that absence]. And where would it establish the practice of absence? When the apprehension of a confused person is to be corrected. But one who is not confused in the apprehension of the object simply remembers the object-possessor [i.e., the locus] — for such a person, the practice of absence is grounded in perception alone — so non-apprehension is not an inferential mark there. This has been well-discussed elsewhere — enough with this digression.

[724] 'Other-existence, which is established through non-apprehension — how is it [itself] non-apprehension?' — to this he says:
Section: 3. Dividing non-apprehension threefold and its examination.

body.text: tad evam anupalabdher aśeṣavipratipattinirākaraṇena svarūpam avasthāpya prabhedanirddeśārtham āha --

children.translated_text: 'This very <s>anupalabdhi</s> (non-apprehension), as stated, is threefold' —

children.text: | katham? | siddhe tatprasādhakena pramāṇena kāryakāraṇabhāve sati kāraṇasyānupalabdhiḥ | kīdṛśasya? | siddhābhāvasya | tathā, vyāpyavyāpakabhāvasiddhau satyāṃ tatprasādhanapramāṇabalenaiva siddhābhāvasyaiva vyāpakasya nānyasya vyāpakānupalabdher evāsiddhatāprasaṅgād | yathoktā svabhāvānupalabdhiś ceti | evaṃ trividhā 'nupalabdhiḥ | kathaṃ punaḥ kāraṇavyāpakayor abhāvavyavahāraḥ sidhyati yatas tayoḥ siddhābhāvatocyata [T. 353b.] ity āha --
children.translated_text: How? When the cause-effect relation is established by the <s>pramāṇa</s> that proves it, there is the non-apprehension of the cause. Of what kind? Of that whose absence is established. Likewise, when the pervader-pervaded relation is established, by the very force of the <s>pramāṇa</s> that proves it — because only the non-apprehension of the pervader whose absence is established [is relevant], not of another, since otherwise there would be the absurd consequence of unestablishedness — and the non-apprehension of essential nature (<s>svabhāvānupalabdhi</s>) as stated. Thus non-apprehension is threefold. But how is the convention of absence for cause and pervader established, such that their absence is said to be established? — he says —
'Of cause and pervader too' —

children.text: na kevalaṃ yasya sākṣād abhāvavyavahāraḥ sādhyate | svabhāvānupalabdhau
children.translated_text: not only [for] that whose absence-convention is directly proved; in the case of non-apprehension of essential nature,
the establishment of the absence-convention of essential nature — which is the establishment of the existence of another,

children.text: tadviviktasya bhāvasiddhir yā saivāsadvyavahārasiddhihetutvād evam ucyate | [S. 192a.]
children.translated_text: of what is distinct from that — that itself is said to be the cause of the establishment of the absence-convention.
'That' —
the absence of cause and pervader,
'thus established' —

children.text: 'nyabhāvasiddhyā pratyakṣarūpayā siddho 'bhāvavyavahāraḥ kāryavyāpyayoḥ pratiṣedhyayoḥ | yadā 'nayor virūpaviṣayatayā {p. 203.1} saviśeṣāṇām upalabdhir na sidhyati
children.translated_text: the absence-convention established through the establishment of other-existence, in the form of perception, is [the absence-convention] of effect and pervaded — what is to be negated. When the apprehension of those [cause and pervader], having objects of a different kind, qualified [apprehension], is not established,
'then it does not establish absence or the absence-convention' —

children.text: | samuccayārtho vāśabdaḥ | atha kiṃ svabhāvānupalabdhāv apy abhāvo liṅgatayā sādhyata ity āha --
children.translated_text: The word 'or' has the sense of conjunction. Now, is absence established as a mark (<s>liṅga</s>) even in the case of non-apprehension of essential nature? — he says —
'But in the case of non-apprehension of essential nature' —
and so forth.
'The absence-convention alone' —

children.text:
, nābhāvo 'pi tasya pratyakṣasiddhatvāt |
  atra parasya vacanāvakāśam āśaṅkyāha --
children.translated_text: not absence itself, because that [absence] is established by perception. Here, anticipating an occasion for the opponent's statement, he says —
'If' —
'then' —
'cause and pervader' —
those for which the absence-convention is established — [they are such] existing. By what?
'Of what is other than that' —

children.text:
karaṇavyāpakaviviktasya bhāvasya siddhir yā pratyakṣātmikā tadrūpayā 'nupalabdhyā, anyasya kāryasya vyāpyasya vā 'bhāvam abhāvavyavahāraṃ ca sādhayataḥ | sā cānyabhāvopalabdhis tayoḥ kāraṇavyāpakayor upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptāv eva satyām asadvyavahārasya sādhikā nānyathā ity evam iṣyamāṇe [T. 354a.][S. 192b.] sati kathaṃ tayoḥ kāraṇavyāpakānupalabdhyoḥ parokṣe 'rthe viṣaye prayogaḥ | yadā kāryasvabhāvahetvor vyatirekaprayogaḥ kriyate -- yatra yatrāgnir nāsti tatra tatra dhūmo 'pi nāsti, tathā yatra yatra vṛkṣo nāsti kṣaṇikatā vā tatra tatra śiṃśapā nāsti sattvaṃ vā ity aśeṣapadārthaparigraheṇa vyatirekaprayoge sati | na hi tadāgnivṛkṣavyatiriktāḥ sarve 'rthāḥ pratyakṣatā(kṣā) akṣaṇikatā vā | tataś ca kathaṃ
tadviviktopalabdhilakṣaṇānupalabdhiḥ[725]pratiyogino nopalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptatā siddhā? | tathā ca katham aśeṣopasaṃhāreṇa vyāptyā kāryasvabhāvahetvor vyatirekaḥ sidhyet? | tadasiddhau vā katham anayor ggamakatvam? | tasmāt kvacid adarśanamātrād eva vyatireka eṣṭavyaḥ, kvacic ca darśanamātrād anvayaḥ | tathā ca pratibandhaghoṣaṇā 'narthiketi manyate paraḥ |
  siddhāntavādy āha --
children.translated_text: the existence of an entity distinct from the cause and pervader — through non-apprehension in the form of that [perception]; [which is the non-apprehension] that establishes the absence and the absence-convention of another — namely the effect or the pervaded. And that apprehension of other-existence establishes the absence-convention of those [cause and pervader] only when they have attained the defining characteristic of being apprehensible — not otherwise. When this is accepted, how is the employment of those — the non-apprehension of cause and pervader — [possible] with respect to a non-manifest object? When the negative concomitance of effect-nature and essential-nature reasons is formulated — 'wherever there is no fire, there too there is no smoke'; likewise 'wherever there is no tree or momentariness, there too there is no <s>śiṃśapā</s> or existence' — with the comprehensive inclusion of all objects in the negative concomitance. For at that time, not all objects other than fire, tree, and the like are perceptual, or non-momentary. And so, how is the non-apprehension characterized as the apprehension of what is distinct from the counter-correlate — the [non-]attainment of the defining characteristic of being apprehensible by the counter-correlate — established? And so, how could the negative concomitance of effect-nature and essential-nature reasons be established through comprehensive inclusion? Or, if that is not established, how could these two have the capacity to indicate? Therefore, negative concomitance must be accepted from mere non-observation in some cases, and positive concomitance from mere observation in some cases. And so the proclamation of invariable connection (<s>pratibandha</s>) is purposeless — so thinks the opponent. The proponent says —
'Not at all' —
of the non-apprehension of cause and pervader with respect to a non-manifest object,
'the employment' —
at the time of demonstrating the negative concomitance,
'as <s>pramāṇa</s>' —

children.text: kāraṇasya vyāpakasya vā 'nupalabdhiḥ pramāṇabhūtā naiva prayujyate | kasmāt? |
children.translated_text: the non-apprehension of cause or pervader is not at all employed as <s>pramāṇa</s>. Why?
'Of the mark' —
characterized as non-apprehension of cause or pervader, or characterized as the absence of that,
'because of non-ascertainment' —

children.text: tadanupalabdhyoḥ sandeharūpatvāt tadabhāvasya ca [T. 354b.] sandigdhatvāt | kathaṃ tarhi tadā 'nayoḥ prayoga iṣyate? ity āha --
children.translated_text: because those non-apprehensions have the nature of doubt, and because the absence of that is also doubtful. Then how is their employment at that time accepted? — he says —
'Merely' —

children.text:
ityādi | kāraṇavyāpakayor hi {p. 204.1} kāryakāraṇabhāvaprasādhakena pūrvoktena pramāṇena vyāpyavyāpakabhāvasādhakena ca tadutpattilakṣaṇe tādātmyalakṣaṇe ca sambandhe sādhite siddhasambandhayor yady abhāvo yatra yatrābhāvaḥ syāt parasyāpi kāryasya vyāpyasya vā 'vaśyaṃ niyamenābhāvo 'nyathā 'hetukatvaprasaṅgāt, niḥsvabhāvatāprasaṅgāc ca | taddvāreṇa pratibandhaprasādhake pramāṇe smṛtiḥ kathaṃ nāma
syād ity etasyārthasya darśanārtham ete kāraṇavyāpakānupalabdhī prayujyeta iti | darśanādarśanabalena tu sādhane yatraivaikadarśane paro dṛṣṭo 'darśane vā na dṛṣṭaḥ tatraiva tasya bhāvo 'bhāvo vā bhavatu sarvatra tu kasmād bhavati? | na hy apratibaddhātmanāṃ gavāśvādīnāṃ kvacit tathābhāvadarśane 'pi sarvatra tathābhāvo bhavati, puruṣasya tu sarvadā kvacid ekabhāvābhāvayor aparasya [S. 193b.] bhāvābhāvadarśanaṃ yadṛcchāsaṃvādaḥ sambhāvyeta asati pratibandhe | tathā cāha --
children.translated_text: and so forth. For when, regarding cause and pervader, the relation — characterized as arising-from (<s>tadutpatti</s>) or as identity (<s>tādātmya</s>) — is established by the previously stated <s>pramāṇa</s> that proves the cause-effect relation and the <s>pramāṇa</s> that proves the pervader-pervaded relation, then of the two whose relation is established — if there is absence, wherever there is absence, there must necessarily be the absence of the other too — the effect or the pervaded — otherwise there would be the absurd consequence of causelessness, and the absurd consequence of being without essential nature. Through that [relation], the remembrance of the <s>pramāṇa</s> that proves the invariable connection — 'how could it possibly be [otherwise]?' — for the purpose of showing this meaning, these non-apprehensions of cause and pervader are employed. But in a proof by the force of observation and non-observation — where the other [entity] is seen only in one [instance of] observation, or not seen in [one instance of] non-observation — only there would there be the existence or absence of that [entity], but why should it obtain everywhere? For of cows, horses, and the like — whose selves are not invariably connected — even when such existence is observed somewhere, there is not such existence everywhere. And for a person, the observation of the existence and absence of one thing whenever there is the existence and absence of another might be supposed to be a coincidental agreement, in the absence of invariable connection. And so he says —
'Because of differences of place and the like, distinct capacities are seen in substances.' ||

children.text: pramāṇasiddhe saty avaśyam eva yatra yatra kāryaṃ tatra tatra kāraṇam, yatra yatra tadabhāvaḥ tatra tatra ca kāryasyāpy abhāvo 'nyathā kāraṇam antareṇa kāryasya bhāve tasyāhetutaiva syāt | tataś ca nityaṃ sattvādiprasaṅgaḥ | tathā yatra yatra yatsvabhāvas tatra tatra tadbhāvaḥ[726]anyathā tasya nairātmyam eva syād iti vyāptyaivānvayavyatirekopadarśane pratibandhaḥ khyāpayituṃ śakyate nānyatheti prāg eva vistarato vipañcitam |
children.translated_text: When [the cause-effect relation] is established by <s>pramāṇa</s>, necessarily wherever there is an effect, there is a cause; and wherever there is the absence of that [cause], there is also the absence of the effect — otherwise, if the effect existed without the cause, that [cause] would simply not be its cause. And so the absurd consequence of permanent existence and the like [would follow]. Likewise, wherever there is what has a certain essential nature, there the existence of that [essential nature obtains] — otherwise its very selflessness would follow. Thus, through pervasion (<s>vyāpti</s>) alone, the demonstration of positive and negative concomitance can make known the invariable connection — not otherwise. This has been elaborated in detail earlier.

body.translated_text: Thus, having established the nature of non-apprehension (<s>anupalabdhi</s>) through the removal of all objections, for the purpose of indicating its divisions, he says —

agnivṛkṣa-
[726] tatsvabhāvaḥ — T.
Section: 4. Conclusion regarding the three characteristics of the reason, its threefoldness, and the pseudo-reasons.

body.text: evaṃ kāraysvabhāvānupalabdhilakṣaṇe eva pakṣadharme tatsādhakapramāṇasadbhāvād anvayavyatirekasadbhāvo nānyatreti pratipādyopasaṃharann {p. 205.1} āha --
body.translated_text: Thus, having demonstrated that positive and negative concomitance obtain only when the property of the thesis has the character of effect-nature, essential-nature, or non-apprehension — because only there does a <s>pramāṇa</s> that proves [the invariable connection] exist, and not elsewhere — concluding the demonstration, he says —
'Thus' —

body.text: eṣa eva [S. 194a.] svabhāvakāryānupalabdhilakṣaṇaḥ pakṣadharmo 'nvayavyatirekavān pratibandhasadbhāvāt[727]| yataś cānvayavyatirekavān pratibandhaprasādhakapramāṇasadbhāvād uktena nyāyena
body.translated_text: this very property of the thesis — characterized as essential nature, effect, or non-apprehension — possesses positive and negative concomitance because of the existence of an invariable connection. And since it possesses positive and negative concomitance — because of the existence of a <s>pramāṇa</s> that proves the invariable connection, by the method stated —
'thus' —
'therefore' —
'pervaded by that aspect' —

body.text: 'nvayavyatirekaniścayenaiva tadaṃśavyāpter niścayād yathoktaṃ prāk, [T. 355b.] tataś ca tadaṃśavyāptivacanāt trilakṣaṇa eva
body.translated_text: precisely because the pervasion by that aspect is ascertained through the ascertainment of positive and negative concomitance — as stated before — and therefore, because of the statement of pervasion by that aspect, only the one with the three characteristics —
'only the one with the three forms' —

body.text: trividha eva hetur ggamako nānyalakṣaṇo 'nyo vā yathoktatrairūpyasadbhāve rūpāntarasya vaiyarthyāt yathoktatrairūpyābhāve ca rūpāntarakalpanāyām apy avyabhicārābhāvenāgamakatvāt | kasmāt trilakṣāṇa eva trividha eva hetur ggamako nānyalakṣaṇo 'nyo veti darśayati
body.translated_text: only the threefold reason is the indicator — no other characteristic or other [reason] — because when the stated three characteristics exist, another form would be purposeless; and because even when imagining another form in the absence of the stated three characteristics, there would be no indicative capacity due to the absence of non-deviation. Why is it that only the three-characterized, threefold reason is the indicator, and no other characteristic or other [reason]? He shows —
'Because of non-deviation from one's own property to be proved' —

body.text:
iti trilakṣaṇasyaiva svasādhyadharmāvyabhicārāt
| svasādhyadharmāvyabhicāra eva ca gamakatvam iti rūpāntarakalpanā vyarthā | pratibandhanibandhanānvayavyatirekāpagame ca rūpāntarakalpanāyām api svasādhyadharmāvyabhicārābhāvāt | tad anena
body.translated_text: because of the non-deviation of the three-characterized alone from one's own property to be proved. And since the indicative capacity is precisely the non-deviation from one's own property to be proved, the postulation of another form is purposeless. And because when the positive-negative concomitance grounded in invariable connection is removed, even in postulating another form, there would be the absence of non-deviation from one's own property to be proved. Therefore, by this —
'Only threefold is it' —
this means: only three-characterized,
that reason, of the invariable co-occurrence —
of the non-deviation from one's own property to be proved —
'because of the restriction' —

body.text: avaśyan tayā sadbhāvāt [S. 194b.] pratibandhanimittatadaṃśavyāptyanabhyupage(game) ca rūpāntarakalpanāyām api
body.translated_text: because of the necessary existence [of the three marks], and because of not accepting the pervasion of the relevant aspect grounded in the restriction — even in postulating an additional form,
'the pseudo-reasons are others beyond those' —

body.text: yathoktatrilakṣaṇād apare rūpāntarayogitayā vikalpyamānā hetvābhāsā [T. 356a.] avinābhāvasya svasādhyadharmāvyabhicārasya teṣv abhāvād ity aparo 'rtho darśita iti |
body.translated_text: others, being conceived as possessing an additional form beyond the stated three marks, are pseudo-reasons (<s>hetvābhāsa</s>), because of the absence in them of inseparable connection (<s>avinābhāva</s>), i.e., the non-deviation from one's own probandum-property — thus an additional meaning has been shown.
-sadbhāvāt asyaiva svabhāvakāryānupalabdhilakṣaṇāśraya(ṇās pada)tvāt — T.
Section: 5. Refutation of those who assert additional marks in the definition of a valid reason

body.text: yaduktaṃ `trilakṣaṇa eva hetur nānyalakṣaṇaḥ` iti tatra pareṣāṃ vipratipattiṃ darśayann āha --

children.translated_text: 'The reason has six marks — so say others' —

children.text: naiyāyika-mīmāṃsakādayo manyante | kāni punaḥ ṣaḍrūpāṇi hetos tair iṣyaṃte? ity āha --
children.translated_text: <s>Naiyāyikas</s>, <s>Mīmāṃsakas</s>, and the like think so. What then are the six forms of the reason accepted by them? — he says:
'These three' —

children.text: pakṣadharmānvayavyatirekākhyāni | tathā 'bādhitaviṣayatvaṃ caturthaṃ rūpam | abādhitaḥ pramāṇenānirākṛto viṣayaḥ sādhyadharmalakṣaṇo yasya sa tathoktaḥ tasya bhāvaḥ tattvam aparaṃ rūpam | tathā vivakṣitaikasaṃkhyatvaṃ rūpāntaraṃ, ekā saṃkhyā yasya {p. 206.1} hetudravyasya tadekasaṃkhyaṃ vivakṣitam ekasaṃkhyaṃ hetudravyam āśrayatvena yasya hetusāmānyasya tadvivakṣitaikasaṃkhyaṃ tadbhāvo 'paraṃ rūpam | yady ekasaṃkhyāvyavacchinnāyāṃ pratiheturahitāyāṃ hetuvyaktau hetutvaṃ bhavati tadā gamakatvaṃ na tu pratihetusahitāyām api
children.translated_text: called property-of-the-thesis, positive concomitance, and negative concomitance. Likewise, 'having a non-contradicted subject-matter' is the fourth form. [That reason is called thus] whose subject-matter — characterized by the probandum-property — is non-contradicted, i.e., not refuted by a <s>pramāṇa</s>; the state of that [non-contradictedness] is another form. Likewise, 'being of a single enumeration as intended' is another form: that reason-substance which has the enumeration of one, and that single-enumeration is intended — [that is,] the reason-substance of single enumeration is the locus of the reason-universal having the character of being of a single intended enumeration — the state of that is another form. If the status of being a reason obtains in a reason-instance isolated by the enumeration of one — [i.e.,] devoid of a counter-reason — then there is indicative capacity, but not in [an instance] accompanied by a counter-reason and

children.text:
dvisaṃkhyāyuktāyām iti[728]| [S. 195a.] yadi viruddhāvyabhicāryaparaṃ
hetvantaraṃ nopadarśyata iti yāvat | tathā jñānatvaṃ ca jñānaviṣayatvaṃ ca | na hy ajñāto hetuḥ svasattāmātreṇa gamako yuktaḥ [T. 356b.] iti | tatraiteṣu rūpāntareṣu yad etad abādhitaviṣayatvaṃ nāma tat tāvat pratibandhanibandhanānvayavyatirekātmakā 'vinābhāvasambhave sati tataḥ pṛthag anyallakṣaṇaṃ na bhavati | tadātmakaṃ tu tadvacanenaivoktam iti na vaktavyam iti | kasmāt pṛthag lakṣaṇaṃ na bhavati? bādhāyā avinābhāvasya ca virodhād iti | tathā hi -- saty apy avinābhāve yathokte bādhāsambhavaṃ manyamānair abādhitaviṣayatvaṃ rūpāntaram ucyate | sā ceyaṃ tatsambhāvanā na sambhavati, bādhāyā avinābhāvena
children.translated_text: joined with the enumeration of two — as long as another reason that is contradictory and non-deviating is not shown. Likewise, the status of being cognized [is another form], i.e., being the object of cognition. For an unknown reason is not reasonably an indicator by its mere existence. Among those additional forms, that which is called 'having a non-contradicted subject-matter' — to begin with, when the inseparable connection (<s>avinābhāva</s>) — having the nature of positive and negative concomitance grounded in the restriction — is possible, it does not exist as a separate additional mark. But that it is stated by that very expression [of inseparable connection] — this should not be said. Why does it not exist as a separate mark? Because of the contradiction between contradiction (<s>bādhā</s>) and inseparable connection. For thus: those who think that even when there is inseparable connection as stated, contradiction is possible — they state 'having a non-contradicted subject-matter' as an additional form. But this supposition is not possible, because of the
'contradiction' —

children.text: sahānavasthānalakṣaṇāt | tam eva virodhaṃ sādhayann āha --
children.translated_text: characterized by the impossibility of co-existence — between contradiction and inseparable connection. Establishing that very contradiction, [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>] says:
'For the inseparable connection' —

children.text:
ityādi | saty eva hi sādhyadharme bhāvo hetor avinābhāva ucyate | pramāṇabādhā tu tasminnasati | yadi hi saty eva tasmiṃs tadabhāvaviṣayaṃ pramāṇaṃ pravartteta tadā 'sya bhrāntatvād apramāṇataiva syāt
iti kuto bādhā? | tataḥ
children.translated_text: and so forth. For the inseparable connection of the reason is said to consist in [the reason's] existing only when the probandum-property exists. But <s>pramāṇa</s>-contradiction [occurs] when that [probandum-property] is absent. For if a <s>pramāṇa</s> whose object is the absence of that [probandum-property] were to operate even when that [probandum-property] exists, then, being erroneous, it would simply not be a <s>pramāṇa</s> — so how could there be contradiction? Therefore,
'that' —
reason —
'having that character' —
being inseparable from the probandum —

children.text: dharmiṇi syāt | atra ca sādhyadharmaḥkathaṃna bhavet
children.translated_text: 'would be in the subject, and how could the probandum-property not exist there' —

children.text:
? yato [S. 195b.] bādhāvakāśaḥ syāt | tasmād avinābhāvasya pramāṇabādhāyāś ca sahānavasthānam avinābhāvenopasthāpitasya dharmiṇi sādhyadharmabhāvasya pramāṇabādhopasthāpitasya ca tadabhāvasya parasparaparihārasthitilakṣaṇatayā virodhenaikatra dharmiṇy asambhavād iti |
  tam eva virodhaṃ saṣṭīkartuṃ paropahāsavyājenāha --
children.translated_text:
? — such that there would be occasion for contradiction. Therefore, the inseparable connection and <s>pramāṇa</s>-contradiction cannot co-exist, because of the contradiction — having the nature of mutual exclusion — between the existence of the probandum-property in the subject, which is presented by the inseparable connection, and the absence of that [probandum-property], which is presented by the <s>pramāṇa</s>-contradiction, [they] being impossible in one and the same subject.
  To make that very contradiction vivid, [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>] says, under the guise of ridiculing the opponent:
'For direct perception and inference' —
and so forth. For when direct perception and inference contradict the probandum-property,
'seizing it by the neck' —
from its own locus, i.e., from the subject —
'expelling [it]' —
| And the reason, since it exists only when that probandum-property exists — because of being inseparable from it —

children.text: | tasmiṃś ca sādhyadharme saty eva tadavinābhāvitvād dhetur bhavaṃ

children.translated_text: 'that' —
{p. 207.1} the probandum-property being expelled — seizing [it] by the throat, by force —
'right there' —
'establishes [it] in the subject' —
truly
extreme indeed
'of the entities' —

children.text:
sādhyadharmalakṣaṇānāmasvāsthyaṃ vartate | tathā hi -- yantradvayaniyantritānāṃ nirucchvāsitayā maraṇam eva prāptam iti |
  paro bādhā 'vinābhāvayor viṣayabhedād avirodhaṃ darśayann āha --
children.translated_text: characterized as probandum-properties — 'is the distress.' For thus: being constricted by two machines, death has arrived through suffocation.
The opponent, showing the non-contradiction of contradiction and inseparable connection through the difference of their domains, says:

children.text:
sādhyadharmiṇaṃ parihṛtya dṛṣṭāntadharmiṇi sādhyadharmeṇāvinābhāvī hetur na punaḥ sādhyadharmiṇy eva | tataḥ [S. 196-7a.] kuto bādhā 'vinābhāvayor virodho 'nyatra bādhayā sādhyadharmābhāvasādhanād anyatra ca hetunā tadbhāvasādhanāt | tathā caivaṃvidhe saty api avinābhāve bādhāsambhavād abādhitaviṣayatvasya rūpāntarasya sambhava iti |
  evaṃvidhāvinābhāvopagame saty apy abādhitaviṣayatvādike rūpantare
children.translated_text: 'Elsewhere' —
'the pseudo-reasons are others beyond those' —

children.text: rūpāntarasambhavina ity āpāditāṃ hetvābhāsatāṃ vivarītuṃ paropahāsapūrvakam āha -- tat kim
children.translated_text: possessing the additional form — in order to unravel the charged pseudo-reason-status, [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>] says, preceded by ridicule of the opponent: 'Then what —'
'this' —
the probandum-subject,
'the ascetic' —
'the wretched one' —
having married a eunuch, [i.e.,] having taken in that [reason] —
a reason deficient in the capacity to prove the probandum-property —
'seeks a son' —
characterized as the probandum-property? | He explains this very [point]:
'Of which' —
of which reason, even when the probandum-property is absent in the subject,
'existence' —
is accepted, because of accepting inseparable connection elsewhere [in the example] than the probandum-subject —
'that' —

children.text:
tathāvidhaṃ sādhyadharmiṇy upadarśya kathaṃ dharmī sādhyadharmavān ity ucyate? | na hy 'mbhastvasya[730]samudre[731]lavaṇatvenāvinābhave 'pi tadvyatirikte 'mbhasi lavaṇatayā sādhyatveneṣṭe 'mbhastvabhāve 'pi lavaṇatvasiddhir iti |
  parasya vacanāvakāśam āśaṅkhyāha --
children.translated_text:
presenting such a [reason] in the probandum-subject, how can one say 'the subject possesses the probandum-property'? For it is not the case that, even though the inseparable connection of water-ness with salt-ness in the ocean [obtains], when salt-ness is desired to be proved in water other than that [ocean], the establishment of salt-ness [follows] from the absence of water-ness [in that other water].
  Anticipating an opportunity for the opponent's response, [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>] says:
'For this very reason' —
and so forth. He explains this very [point]:
'This may be' —

children.text:
bhavato matam | yata eva hetur anyathā 'pi sādhyadharmam antareṇāpi dharmiṇi bhaved ambhastvādiṣu tathādarśanāt, sādhyadharmiparihāreṇa cāvinābhāopagamāt ata eva kāraṇāt pramāṇābhyām abādhitadharmā dharmīty ucyate | yadi {p. 108.1} pratyakṣānumānābhyāṃ sādhyadharmiṇi [s. 196-7b.] hetor viṣayaḥ sādhyadharmo na bādhyate yathā 'mbhastvasya lavaṇatvam, tadā tasya gamakatvam, nānyatheti | tato 'nyatrāvinābhāvamātreṇa sādhyasiddher anabhyupagamāt na yathokto doṣa iti |
  siddhāntavādy āha --
children.translated_text:
your view. Since the reason may exist in the subject even otherwise, i.e., even without the probandum-property — because such is observed in water-ness and the like — and because inseparable connection is accepted excluding the probandum-subject — for this very reason, the subject is said to have a property not contradicted by <s>pramāṇas</s>. {p. 108.1} If the subject-matter of the reason in the probandum-subject — the probandum-property — is not contradicted by direct perception and inference, as salt-ness is not [contradicted] for water-ness, then it has indicative capacity — not otherwise. Therefore, since the establishment of the probandum is not accepted merely from the inseparable connection elsewhere, there is no fault as stated.
  The proponent (<s>siddhāntavādin</s>) says:
'Then what —'

children.text: idānīṃ [T. 358a.] yadā hetor dharmiṇy avinābhāvitānabhyupagamāt sādhyasiddher abhāvāt tatsiddhaye rūpāntaram abādhitaviṣayatvam ucyate tadā hetor na kiñcit sāmarthyam | kasmāt?
children.translated_text: now, when — since, because of not accepting the inseparable connection of the reason in the subject, there is no establishment of the probandum, the additional form 'having a non-contradicted subject-matter' is stated for its establishment — the reason has no capacity whatsoever. Why?
'By non-contradiction alone' —
'even without the reason' —
'since the probandum is established' —

children.text: akiñcitkara eva hetuḥ | tathā hy atra kalpanādvaiyam -- bādhakapramāṇavṛttau sādhyābhāvo niyato vā syād? aniyato vā? | tatra yadi pūrvo vikalpas tadā sādhyābhāvo hi bādhakapramāṇasya vṛttau niyataḥ, tadaiva bhāvāt tadabhāve cābhāvād iti | tasmād
children.translated_text: the reason is entirely ineffectual. For thus, there are two possible conceptions: when the contradicting <s>pramāṇa</s> operates, is the absence of the probandum determinate or indeterminate? In the first alternative: since the absence of the probandum is determinate upon the operation of the contradicting <s>pramāṇa</s> — existing at that very [time] and not existing in its absence. Therefore,
'when there is non-contradiction' —
when there is no operation of the contradicting <s>pramāṇa</s>, because of the absence also of the absence of the probandum that is determinate upon that [operation] —
'the probandum is established' —

children.text:
bhavaty eveti vyartha eva hetur iti nopanyasanīya eva | tataḥ kasyābādhitaviṣayatvaṃ rūpāntaraṇ bhavet? | syān matam -- mā bhūd bādhakapramāṇavṛttyabhāve hetoḥ sāmarthyam, yadā tu sādhyasya bādhakaṃ pramāṇaṃ dharmiṇi varttate tadā hetoḥ sādhyasādhane
sāmarthyaṃ bhaviṣyatīty ata [S. 198a.] āha --
children.translated_text: it is established indeed — so the reason is entirely pointless and should not even be adduced. Then for what [reason] would 'having a non-contradicted subject-matter' be an additional form? One might think: let there be no capacity of the reason in the absence of the operation of the contradicting <s>pramāṇa</s>; but when the <s>pramāṇa</s> that contradicts the probandum operates in the subject, then the reason will have the capacity to prove the probandum — therefore he says:
'Even when there is contradiction' —

children.text: iti | yadi bādhakaṃ pramāṇaṃ varttate tadā tena sādhyābhāvasya dharmiṇi sādhanāt punar brahnaṇāpi tadbhāvasya karttum aśakyatvāt kim aṅga
children.translated_text: thus. If the contradicting <s>pramāṇa</s> operates, then since it has established the absence of the probandum in the subject, even <s>Brahmā</s> himself could not bring about its presence — so what then

children.text:
punaḥ śaṣṭhena hetuneti[732]kutaḥ sādhanasya hetoḥ sāmarthyam? | ata [T. 358b.] eva hi bhavadbhir abādhitaviṣayatvaṃ rūpāntaram ucyata iti |
  atha bādhakapramāṇavṛttau sādhyābhāvo na niyataḥ tadabhāve 'pibhāvād iti dvitīyaḥ pakṣa iṣyate tad apy abādhāyāḥ sāmarthyaviraha iti darśayann āha --
children.translated_text:
can the feeble reason do? — so how can the means of proof, the reason, have any capacity? It is for this very reason that you state 'having a non-contradicted subject-matter' as an additional form.
  But if it is accepted that the absence of the probandum is not determinate upon the operation of the contradicting <s>pramāṇa</s> — existing even in its absence — [this is] the second alternative. Showing that even then non-contradiction has no capacity, he says:
'When there is indeterminacy' —

children.text: bādhakapramāṇavṛttau sādhyābhāvasyeṣyamāṇe satīdam āpatitam | na ca -- bādhakaṃ pramāṇaṃ syāt
children.translated_text: when the absence of the probandum upon the operation of the contradicting <s>pramāṇa</s> is being accepted, this consequence has arrived: even though the contradicting <s>pramāṇa</s> may exist,
'and the absence of the probandum is possible' —
thus,
'there is no' —
'capacity to prove the probandum' —
'of non-contradiction' —

children.text:
satyām api sādhyābhāvasya smbhavād iti tadyogino 'pi hetvābhāsataiveti |
  yad uktam --
children.translated_text:
since the absence of the probandum is possible even when [non-contradiction] obtains — thus the pseudo-reason-status of even that which possesses it [obtains].
  Regarding what was stated —
'by non-contradiction alone the probandum is established, so the reason is pointless' —

children.text:
iti tatrānyathārtham abādhāyā darśayan hetusāmarthyaṃ pratipādayann āhaparaḥ-- na bādhāyā abhāvo samābādhā 'bhimatā | kiṃ tarhi? | bādhāyā anupalabdhiḥ | sā ca tadanupalabdhiḥ puruṣasya śaktivaikalyāt kvacid deśādau bādhāyā sambhave 'pi syāt | tato bādhā 'nupalabdhimātreṇa sadhyasiddher abhāvāt tatsiddhye 'vaśyaṃ [S. 198b.] hetur abhidhānīya iti sa hetuprayogasya viṣayaḥ. tadā hi hetuḥ svasādhyaṃ sādhayan katham asamarthaḥ syād iti.
  siddhāntavādy āha -- kiṃ nu vai hetur bādhāyā yā upalabdhis tasyāḥ bibheti na punar bbādhāyā yena bādhāṃ sambhavantīm apy anādṛtya tadanupalabdhau satyāṃ prayoktavya iṣṭo bhavataḥ |
  kadācitparo brūyāt -- kiṃ kariṣyati vidyamānā'pi bādhā tapasvinī, [T. 359a.] tadupalabdhir eva rākṣasī | tasmāt tata eva hetor bhayaṃ tadabhāve hetuḥ prayoktavya evety ata āha --
children.translated_text:
therein, the opponent, showing the purpose of non-contradiction as otherwise [than stated], establishing the capacity of the reason, says: 'It is not the absence of contradiction that is regarded as non-contradiction. What then? The non-apprehension of contradiction. And that non-apprehension may occur even when contradiction exists in some place and the like, due to the deficiency of the person's capacity. Therefore, since the probandum is not established by the mere non-apprehension of contradiction, for its establishment the reason must necessarily be adduced — so this is the domain of the deployment of the reason. For then, when the reason proves its own probandum, how could it be without capacity?'
  The proponent (<s>siddhāntavādin</s>) says: Does the reason fear the apprehension of contradiction, and not contradiction itself — that you wish it to be deployed when, even though contradiction exists, its non-apprehension obtains, disregarding the existing contradiction?
  The opponent might say: 'What can the poor existing contradiction do? It is its apprehension that is the demoness! Therefore, the fear of the reason is from that alone; in its absence, the reason should indeed be deployed' — therefore [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>] says:
'In that case, then' —

children.text: ityādi | evaṃ tarhi paramārthena bādhā kim asti nāstīty etadanapekṣya bādhāyā anupalabdhau satyāṃ prayoktavya iti kākvā pṛcchati | kadācit paro brūyāt -- uktam evaitat kim arthaṃ pṛccyate? ity āha --
children.translated_text: and so forth. Then — [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>] asks with irony — in ultimate reality, without regard to whether contradiction exists or not, [is the reason] to be deployed when there is non-apprehension of contradiction? The opponent might say: 'This has already been stated — why is it being asked?' He says:
'For what purpose is it deployed' —

children.text: iti | bādhā 'nupalambhe 'pi tatsambhave sādhyasdhanāyogād ity abhiprāyaḥ | paro 'navagatābhiprāya āha --
children.translated_text: thus. Even when contradiction is not apprehended, if it exists, there is no possibility of proving the probandum — this is the intent. The opponent, not having grasped the intent, says:
'For the establishment of the probandum' —

children.text: iti bādhakapratyayābhāve prāmāṇyasyeṣṭatvāt tataḥ sādhyasiddhir avirūddhaiveti manyate | siddhāntavādī satyāṃ bādhāyāṃ tadanupalambhe 'pi sādhyasiddhim asambhāvayan pṛcchati
children.translated_text: thus — he thinks: since validity is accepted in the absence of a contradicting cognition, therefore the establishment of the probandum from that is quite uncontradicted. The proponent, considering the establishment of the probandum impossible even when contradiction, though existing, is not apprehended, asks:
'Does it [prove] anywhere?' —

children.text:
ityādi | kiṃ [S. 199a.] punar asau hetuḥ satyām api bādhāyāṃ sādhyaṃ sādhayed iti sambhavyate bhavatā yenāsyā bādhāyā abhāva viniścayaṃ prati yatno na kriyate
hetuś ca prayujyata iti | evam etat iti cet; tathā satyām api bādhāyāṃ sādhyasādhanasāmarthyopagame saty abādhitaviṣayatvaṃ na bhavati | kiṃ kāraṇam? | bādhāyām api satyām asya hetoḥ
children.translated_text:
and so forth. Is it supposed by you that the reason would prove the probandum even when contradiction exists — that no effort is made toward the definitive ascertainment of the absence of this contradiction,
and the reason is deployed? If so — then, when the capacity to prove the probandum is accepted even when contradiction exists, 'having a non-contradicted subject-matter' does not obtain. What is the reason? Because, even when contradiction exists, of this reason's
'capacity' —

children.text: sāmarthyopagamāt | tad dhi hetor lakṣaṇam ucyate yena vinā sādhyaṃ na sādhayed iti |
children.translated_text: because of the acceptance of capacity. For that is said to be the definition of a reason: that without which it would not establish the probandum. |

children.text: syan matam -- anupalabhyamānabādhatvaṃ hetulakṣaṇaṃ [T. 359b.] paramārthena, nābādhitaviṣayatvam ity ata āha --
children.translated_text: One might think: the definition of a reason is, in ultimate reality, having an unapprehended contradiction (<s>bādha</s>), not having an uncontradicted subject-matter — to this [Dharmakīrti] says —
'And so' (<s>tathā ca</s>)

children.text:
ityādi | evaṃ sati bādhāyāḥ sadbhāvasambhave 'pi tām abhyupagamya tadanupalambhamātreṇa hetoḥ prayogaḥ prāptaḥ | yadi hi bādhām abhyupagamya hetuprayogo nābhimataḥ syāt tadā 'nupalambhamātreṇa bādhāyāṃ saṃśayāt -- satām api keśāñcit kathañcidanupalambhasambhavāt -- saṃśayitasya hetuprayoge pravṛttir eva na yujyeta | tasmād yo yatsaṃśaye 'pi pravartate sa tasya bhāvapakṣam abhyupetyaiva pravarttate | tathā ca yathā bādhānupalabdhau tām abhyupagamya hetuḥ prayujyate tathā tadupalabdhāv api prayujyatām, bādhāyāḥ sadbhāvābhyupagame sati tadupalambhānupalambhayor viśeṣābhāvād iti nānupalabhyamānabādhatvam api [S. 199b.] hetulakṣaṇaṃ yujyata iti kuto bādhakapratyayavirahe 'py asati pratibandhe prāmāṇyasya sambhava iti |
  parasya vacanāvakāśam āśaṅkhyāha --
children.translated_text:
and so forth. This being so, even when the existence of a contradiction is possible, having accepted that [possibility], the employment of the reason would follow from the mere non-apprehension of that [contradiction]. For if the employment of the reason were not accepted when a contradiction is accepted, then from mere non-apprehension of the contradiction — since non-apprehension is possible even for some things that exist, somehow — employment in the application of the reason, when [contradiction] is doubtful, would simply not be tenable. Therefore, one who proceeds even in doubt about something proceeds only by accepting the possibility of its existence. And so, just as when contradiction is not apprehended, the reason is employed by accepting that [contradiction may exist], so too let it be employed even when that [contradiction] is apprehended, since there is no distinguishing feature between the apprehension and non-apprehension of contradiction when the existence of contradiction is accepted. Thus, even having an unapprehended contradiction is not a tenable definition of a reason — so whence the possibility of validity even in the absence of a contradicting cognition, when there is no necessary connection (<s>pratibandha</s>)? |
  Anticipating the opponent's occasion for a reply, [Dharmakīrti] says —
'Not when contradiction [exists]' (<s>na bādhāyām</s>)

children.text: ityādi | naiva hi bādhāyāṃ satyāṃ hetoḥ sāmarthyam iṣyate tat kathaṃ tadupalambhe 'pi prayogaḥ syāt? | siddhāntavādy āha --
children.translated_text: and so forth. For when contradiction exists, the capacity of the reason is simply not accepted — so how could there be employment even when that [contradiction] is apprehended? | The Siddhantavadin (proponent) says —
'If so' (<s>yady evaṃ</s>)

children.text: bādhāyāṃ satyāṃ hetur asamartho yadīṣyate tadā 'nirṇīto adhāyā asaṃbhavo yasya hetoḥ sa tathāvidhaḥ prayogaṃbādhā 'nupalambhamātreṇa nārhati | kiṃ kāraṇam? | mā bhūd bādhāyāḥ sambhasvapakṣe
children.translated_text: — if the reason is accepted as incapable when contradiction exists, then a reason for which the impossibility of contradiction has not been ascertained — such a [reason] does not deserve employment merely from the non-apprehension of contradiction. What is the reason? Lest there be
'even of the employed [reason]' (<s>prayuktasyāpi</s>)
— in the establishment of the probandum —
incapacity, due to the possibility of contradiction in one's own thesis. |

| The prima facie objector says: 'If you think that when contradiction is not apprehended, because of the absence of contradiction, and when a cognition apprehending its existence is absent, the capacity of the reason [is established]

children.text: | [T. 360a.] pūrvapakṣavādy āha -- bādhānupalambhe sati bādhāyā ābhāvāt[734]sadupalambhakapratyayābhāve[735]saty avaśyam arthānām asattvād dhetoḥ sāmathyam iti cen manyase siddhāntavādy āha --
children.translated_text: because the things necessarily do not exist' — the Siddhantavadin says —
'Does apprehension [establish] contradiction?' (<s>kim upalambho bādhām</s>)

children.text:
ityādi | upalambho hy arthānāṃ kāryaṃ, na ca kāryaṃ kāraṇaṃ vyāpnoti | na hy 'vaśyaṃ kāraṇāni kāryavanti bhavanti, pratibandhavaikalyasambhavāt[736]| tat katham avyāpakasyopalambhasya
nivṛttau bādhāyā nivṛttiḥ?, yato hetor bbādhāyāḥ sambhavakṛtam asāmarthyaṃ na sambhaved iti | etac ca parair apīṣyata eva; [S. 200a.] pramāṇatayopagatasyāpy udayakāle 'nupalabdhabādhasya {p. 211.1} kālāntareṇa bādhakapratyayotpāde saty aprāmāṇyopagamāt | athāvyāpakasyāpy upalambhasya ivṛttau bādhā nivarttate --
children.translated_text: and so forth. For apprehension is the effect of things, and the effect does not pervade the cause. For causes do not necessarily have effects, because of the possibility of obstruction or deficiency. So how, upon the cessation of apprehension — which does not pervade [its cause] — would there be a cessation of contradiction?, such that the incapacity of the reason due to the possibility of contradiction would not obtain. And this is accepted even by the opponents — since when a contradicting cognition arises at another time for something that was accepted as valid at the time of its arising because contradiction was not apprehended, [they accept] its invalidity. Or if, even upon the cessation of apprehension — which does not pervade [its cause] — contradiction ceases —
'For falsity ceases due to the effort [arising] from the knowledge of the defect' ||
SlV Su 2.52

children.text: iti anenaiva nyāyena jñānanivṛttyā bādhānivṛtter ity āha -- tathāpi vyartho hetuḥ | kutaḥ? |
