children.text: bhinnasvabhāvānām apy athānām ekavākyena pratipādanāt | ekenaiva ca lakṣaṇavākyenobhayagatāv api yat
children.translated_text: because even things of different essential natures are taught by a single sentence. And the
'separate statement' —
that [occurs] in the single definitional sentence, covering both [positive and negative concomitance],
'is for the purpose of regulating the deployment' —

children.text:
| sādharmyaprayoge [T. 373b.] vaidharma(rmya)vacanaṃ na karttavyam, vaidharmyaprayoge ca sādharmyavacanam iti na punar ekābhidhānenānavagatasya rūpāntarasya pratipādanārtham | na ca tathā trairūpyavacanena jñānanibandhanena jñeyasattāvyavasthāyāḥ paropalakṣaṇāthena ca śāstrapraṇayanenāśritajñānasyaiva trairūpyasya [S. 214b.] pratipādanāl
labdhasya jñānasya punarvacane na kiñcit prayojanam astīti nāsya pṛthagvacanaṃ yuktam iti |
  syānmatam -- kevalāv api tarhy ekavākyārthānantarbhūtau parasparama'bhinnasvabhāvau bhaviṣyataḥ tata evaikavākyārthāntarbhāvād ity ata āha --
children.translated_text:
| In the deployment through agreement (<s>sādharmya</s>), the statement of disagreement (<s>vaidharmya</s>) should not be made; and in the deployment through disagreement, the statement of agreement [should not be made]. But it is not for the purpose of teaching an additional form not understood by a single statement. And thus, since through the statement of the three marks — which is grounded in cognition, [and] since from the establishment of the existence of the knowable being grounded in the existence of knowledge, and since the composition of the treatise, whose purpose is the guidance of others, teaches the three-mark-ness that is already grasped along with cognition —
there is no purpose at all in re-stating what has already been obtained through cognition. So a separate statement of it is not proper.
  One might think: even when considered alone, [positive and negative concomitance], though not included in the meaning of a single sentence, would still be of mutually non-different essential natures, precisely because they are included in the meaning of a single sentence — therefore [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>] says:
'But not alone' —

children.text: ekavākyārthānapekṣau tadantarbhāvamātreṇa sapakṣāsapakṣayoḥ bhāvābhāvau parasparam ākṣipato 'ntarbhavataḥ bhinnarūpāṇām apy arthānām ekavākyāntarbhāvadarśanāt | nanu ca niyamavantāv api bhāvābhāvau kevalāv eva, tayoḥ parasparākṣepe kevalayor api tatprasaṅga ity ata āha --
children.translated_text: the presence and absence [of the reason] in the homologue and heterologue, independent of the meaning of a single sentence, do not mutually entail each other merely by being included in that [single sentence], since even things of different natures are seen to be included in a single sentence. But [one might say:] even the presence and absence that are subject to restriction are [merely] alone; and if those two mutually entail each other, the same consequence [would apply] to even [those considered] alone — therefore [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>] says:
'And when subject to restriction' —
taught by a sentence containing a restrictive particle —
'not alone' —
but rather combined. Why? |
'Of the restriction' —
of the sentence containing the restrictive particle —
'because it has both natures' —

children.text:
bhāvābhāvapratipādanātmakatvāt |
  tad evaṃ sāvadharaṇena [T. 374a.] vākyena naiva kevalo 'nvayo vyatireko vā 'bhidhīyate | tadantarbhāvāt tu dvitīyagatiḥ kintu parasparānantarbhūtāv eva sahitāv ekena vākyenābhidhīyeta iti pratipādyopasaṃharann āha --
children.translated_text:
because it has the nature of teaching both presence and absence.
  Thus, by a sentence containing a restrictive particle, neither positive concomitance alone nor negative concomitance alone is expressed. And the second [consideration is] because of inclusion in that [sentence]; rather, the two, not mutually included, are expressed together by a single sentence — concluding the thesis to be established, [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>] says:
'Therefore' —

children.text:
tatraiva [S. 215a.] sapakṣa eva bhāva {p. 228.1} ity anena vākyena na sapakṣe bhāva evocyate | kiṃ tarhi? | asapakṣe 'bhāvo 'pi, tathā cetareṇāpy asapakṣe 'bhāva eveti vacanena nābhāva eva kevala ucyate kintu sapakṣe bhāvo 'pi, yena kevalavacanena bhāvo 'bhāvo vā tadātmakatayā dvitīyam ākṣiped yato 'nayoḥ pṛthagvacanaṃ na syāt | tasmād yadā 'nvayavyatirekau bhāvābhāvāv abhipretau tadā tau bhinnarūpāv eveti kathaṃ tayoḥ na pṛthaktvam? | atha niyamavatā vākyenābhihitau tadaikavākyād evobhayagateḥ pṛthagvacanaṃ na karttavyam eva | tat tu kṛtaṃ nāpratipannapratipattaye kintu prayoganiyamārtham ity uktam etad iti |
  syānmatam -- yathā 'nvayavyatirekau bhāvābhāvalakṣaṇau na parasparātmakau tataś ca tayoḥ parasparato rūpāntaratvam, evaṃ paropalakṣaṇaśastrapratipāditāt trailakṣaṇyād bhidyata eva jñānam, na tatrāntarbhūtam, tato rūpāntaraṃ bhaviṣyatīty ata [T. 374b.] āha --
children.translated_text:
by that very [sentence] 'there is presence in the homologue alone' — by this sentence, it is not the presence in the homologue alone that is stated. What then? The absence in the heterologue too. And likewise, by the other [sentence] 'there is absence in the heterologue alone' — by this statement, it is not the absence alone that is stated, but also the presence in the homologue. [This is] so that by a statement of either alone — of presence or absence — [one might think that] it entails the second by identity, such that there would be no separate statement of the two. Therefore, when positive and negative concomitance — presence and absence — are intended, those two are of different natures indeed — so how can they not be separate? But when expressed by a sentence containing a restrictive particle, since the understanding of both [follows] from that single sentence alone, a separate statement should not be made at all. But that [separate statement] was made — not for teaching what was not understood, but for the purpose of regulating the deployment — this has been said.
  One might think: just as positive and negative concomitance, characterized by presence and absence, are not of each other's nature — and therefore they are of an alternative nature from each other — so too cognition is indeed different from the three-mark-ness taught by the treatise whose purpose is the guidance of others, [and is] not included therein — and so it would be an alternative form. Therefore [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>] says:
'Not so' —

children.text: , yathā 'nvayavyatirekau bhāvābhāvalakṣaṇau parasparam anantarbhūtau, na tathā jñānaṃ paropalakṣaṇaśāstrapratipādite trailakṣaṇye 'nantarbhūtam | kutaḥ? |
children.translated_text: it is not the case that, just as positive and negative concomitance, characterized by presence and absence, are not mutually included, so too cognition is not included in the three-mark-ness taught by the treatise whose purpose is the guidance of others. Why? |
'Because of [its] being for the guidance of others' —

children.text: -- pare upalakṣyante [S. 215b.] upalakṣaṇa(ṇaṃ) trairūpyaviṣayāṃ pratītiṃ kāryante yena śāstreṇa tato yat trailakṣaṇyaṃ pratīyate āgṛhītajñānaṃ tasmād avyatirekād āgṛhītajñāne trailakṣaṇye 'ntarbhāvād iti yāvat,
children.translated_text: — others are guided — i.e., [the treatise], by which they are made to produce cognition regarding the subject of the three marks — from that treatise, the three-mark-ness that is cognized — because of the non-difference from the cognition already grasped, i.e., because of the inclusion in the three-mark-ness of the cognition already grasped — this is the meaning.
'Thus' —

children.text:
tasmān na lakṣaṇāntaraṃ trairūpyād iti | tad ayam atra samudāyārthaḥ -- yadi jñātatvaṃ jñānaśabdapravṛttinimittaṃ uktena prakāreṇa jñānam evocyate tadā talliṃgasyānātmabhūtam iti
na tallakṣaṇam | athāvi(pi )jñānāpekṣaḥ karmabhāvo jñātatvam ucyate tadā 'pi jñeyasattāvyavasthāyā jñānasattānibandhanatvāt trairūpyavyavasthaiva tatsattāvyavasthāpakaṃ jñānam ākṣipati | tatas tadapekṣo 'pi karmabhāvo 'nuktasiddha iti na tadvacanaṃ pṛthakkarttavyam | tathā paropalakṣaṇārthaśāstrapratipāditāgṛhītajñānāt trailakṣaṇyād avyatirekād iti |
  tad evam abādhitaviṣayatvādikaṃ rūpatrayaṃ nirākṛtya nigamayann āha --
children.translated_text:
therefore it is not an additional mark distinct from the three marks. This then is the combined meaning here: if the status of being cognized — the ground for the application of the word 'cognition' — is, in the manner stated, called 'cognition' itself, then since it is not [something] other than the self of that reason,
it is not a mark of it. But if the status of being an object — dependent on cognition — is called 'the status of being cognized,' then too, since the establishment of the existence of the knowable is grounded in the existence of knowledge, the very establishment of the three marks entails the cognition that establishes the existence of that [knowable]. Therefore, even the status of being an object, which depends on that [cognition], is established without being stated — so a separate statement of it should not be made. Likewise, because of the non-difference from the three-mark-ness of the cognition already grasped, taught by the treatise whose purpose is the guidance of others.
  Thus, having rejected the three forms — non-contradicted-subject-matter and the like — [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>] concludes:
'Therefore, the reason does not have six marks.' |
What then? | It has three marks alone. |
{p. 229.1} 'This [teaching], which has destroyed the entire path of sophistry,
a lamp of tranquil reasoning from the lord of sages —
having spread it, may the merit thus acquired
bring about the supreme purification of the world.' ||

body.translated_text: Regarding what was stated — 'the reason is the three-marked alone, not of any other mark' — showing the disagreement of opponents on that, [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>] says:

The <s>Hetubinduṭīkā</s> is complete. |
..... May those of such a form always [strive]
for the welfare of the three worlds. Of the bridge of men... the instructor of the doctrine of the <s>Tathāgata</s> || 2 ||
....... 74, <s>Mārgaśira</s>, dark half, 7th, Sunday. May there be auspiciousness and great prosperity. ||

body.text:
na guror upadeśam agrahīt bubudhe vastu tato ... ... dhīḥ |
  yatato sma na tasya vṛddhaye na parispanditum apy apārayat || [1 ||]

children.text: jīvātmakaṃ cāndramasaṃ ca tejaḥ kṛtāspadaṃ tasya tai ...t |
children.translated_text: The life-force and the lunar radiance, having found a place in that... |

children.text: tad eva śaktā ...thā paratra citrā hi viśvaprakṛti...nāḥ || 2 ||
children.translated_text: That very [radiance], capable... elsewhere, wonderful indeed... the nature of the universe... || 2 ||

body.translated_text:
He did not receive the teacher's instruction, [yet] understood the real from that... ... intelligence |
  [Despite] striving, it did not grow for him; it was not even able to stir. || [1 ||]

children.translated_text: Lord of the stars! Sovereign of the night! Treasury of nectar!
Among the qualities of the flavor of <s>Kādambarī</s>... ...
one should remember the moon, who has offered his body. || 3 ||

body.translated_text: O beloved of <s>Rohiṇī</s>! Abode of all arts!

In the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> lineage, [the work of] <s>Abhayakumāra</s>:
  the <s>Hetubindutarka</s> ||
